reviews.excerpt: Metacritic user score 5.4/10 (27335 ratings).
98.8% of OpenCritic critics recommend this game (90 reviews).

Few games have carried this much hype. For every big swing that pays off, plenty of ambitious games have either launched broken or strained under the weight of their own open worlds... Grand Theft Auto VI is a masterpiece, and it was worth every one of those 13 years.

GTA VI is not only the best game of 2026, but also represents the pinnacle of the current console generation. It is not simply a bigger game than its 2013 predecessor, but a better and more refined experience in virtually every aspect. Its incredible level of detail and the entire ecosystem built to bring the game world to life make it one of the most complex and meticulously crafted games ever released. GTA VI is fun, memorable, and raises the bar for the entire gaming industry.

GTA VI is Rockstar's best game yet, and one that will go down in gaming history. It's a breathtaking, incredibly ambitious experience with a world so immersive that you can't help but feel like you're truly part of it.

Grand Theft Auto VI, against all odds, has somehow managed to not only meet but surpass all my expectations. The story is a huge standout, delivering an emotional rollercoaster that had me sitting on the edge of my seat for over seventy hours. Not to mention a killer soundtrack and phenomenally tuned gameplay that made every second a joy to play, I can’t wait to dive back in.

Eight years after its last game Rockstar is back to raise the bar even
higher. GTA VI is an attempt to create the best game in its category –
and to say that this attempt was successful is an understatement.

GTA 6 is an absolute masterpiece. Rockstar delivers a story of rare emotional power, with top-notch storytelling, deep and complex characters, masterful direction, a frenetic pace, and a profoundly alive world of unparalleled richness. I've never seen anything like it! Visually, it's a true revolution: to be honest, I've never seen anything so impressive in a video game. Add to that fantastic music and this incredible ability to make us feel so much emotion and adrenaline simultaneously… Simply exceptional. It's a true lesson in video game design, a monumental work that pushes the boundaries of the medium and reminds us why I love video games so much. Ultimately, there's Rockstar, and then there's everyone else.
Grand Theft Auto VI is everything I wanted it to be and more. If I could only pick one game to play for the rest of my life, this would be it. One of the true masterpieces of our time.

If you asked me whether the 13-year gap for Grand Theft Auto 6 was worth the wait, it is a resounding yes. What Rockstar Games has done is craft one of the most incredible and exciting living worlds I've ever had the pleasure of playing in. Each region of Leonida is hand-crafted and filled with memorable places to explore. Whether I was in the Keys, where I could scuba dive for treasure, drink at the Rusty Anchor with my friends, or in the Grassrivers, where I'd hunt for backwater drug deals, or in the city centre of Vice City, where I'd hit up a club then rob a boutique, there's an abundance of life unfolding each day…Jason and Lucia's story quickly shifts from the mundane to a thrilling Bonnie & Clyde survival story. The characters even become two of the most memorable protagonists in the series, with incredible performances from their respective actors. It quickly becomes clear that everybody in this cast came to play and have a good time.

Grand Theft Auto VI is an astonishing video game, a masterclass in game design, engineering, visuals, sound, writing and everything between. It's the inevitable product of more time, money and human labour than has ever been afforded to a project like this, and so it's unsurprising in its scope and scale, but also pleasingly grounded, matured and focused in ways I wasn't expecting. I fear that the industry may never recover from this game.
Worth the wait? Maybe. But it only takes about 5 minutes to realise that Rockstar has changed the game once again with Grand Theft Auto VI.

The wait was truly worth it. GTA 6 is a game that keeps drawing you back in, making you feel like part of its city and its story. Its customization options and hundreds of activities are downright addictive. It manages to bring together the best of GTA and Red Dead in a single experience, offering a little bit of everything: racing, adrenaline, heists, romance, shootouts, pursuits, and exploration. There’s a detail to discover everywhere you go, and every little detail makes you feel part of the wealth and misery of a Vice City ready for crime.

Funny, sad, euphoric… GTA 6 is the most entertaining and emotionally engaging open world I’ve played. Rockstar has taken the sandbox freedom of Grand Theft Auto and the environmental storytelling of Red Dead Redemption 2 and made something that feels lived-in. The characters, humour, and systems are all wonderfully written, and the attention to detail makes Leonida a place I want to stay in long after I’d finished the story. The set pieces rival Hollywood, but I'll remember the small, unplanned moments.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is part criminal come-up tale, part love story, and part life sim all wrapped up in an impossibly deep and detailed Rockstar Games open world that may never run out of things to do. For the last three-plus weeks, I have been gleefully vacationing in Vice City: robbing banks, fighting drug dealers, stealing cars, and enjoying the view while not coming close to finishing everything it has to offer. GTA 6 is finally here now, and it was well worth the wait.

Rockstar’s highly anticipated new crime epic is set to steal our hearts—and a good chunk of our free time—for at least the next ten years. It’s a colossal, dazzling masterpiece that elevates the series to an even higher echelon within the industry—if that was even possible. Leonida is all the rage, and it’s undoubtedly the place to call home if you love action, driving, and open worlds brimming with possibilities and surprises.

GTA 6 is still the same GTA we all grew up playing and loved, but it's GTA elevated to the next level, where every part of its DNA has been innovated to be the best it can be. Every aspect of its design builds on the years of experience Rockstar has accumulated with its previous titles, and the result is a tightly-crafted generational masterpiece…Even after playing the game for over 200 hours, we're still loading it up and making incredible discoveries and encountering surprising moments. Exploration has never felt as rewarding as it does in GTA 6, with every curiosity being compensated with memorable and unique experiences.

Like all videogame protagonists, Jason and Lucia are ciphers through which the player exerts their will on the digital world. And yet, through the co-authored interplay of the characters Rockstar has written, and the people you personally tune them into becoming, they form one of the great partnerships in entertainment: beautiful and deadly, open to the possibilities of their world and, despite the violence they inflict on those beyond their circle, driven forward not by fear, but by love.

While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time.

Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar firing on every conceivable cylinder. Whether or not it lands in the same emotional resonance as Red Dead Redemption 2 will be up for the world to decide, but for now, there's absolutely nothing better on the market to just create the chaos, wonder and immersion that only Rockstar can manufacture. Grand Theft Auto VI is a miracle. See you in Leonida.
Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content.

Grand Theft Auto VI is one of the most ambitious video games ever created, somehow living up to the almost impossible expectations surrounding it. Rockstar Games has delivered one of the best games of this generation.

GTA 6 is the wholly unique experience it was promised to be, and that includes setting it apart from Rockstar’s own history with the series.  If nothing else, this is the most impressive video game world I’ve ever played and with the most impressive citizens to occupy that world in both animation and never-ending dialogue.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the kind of game that doesn't come around very often. Rockstar has created an impressive open-world experience, not just in terms of graphical fidelity and the sheer amount of things to do, but also when it comes to character development, world-building and, above all, pure fun. The game does suffer from some familiar open-world flaws, but these rarely detract from the overall experience. It has been a long wait, but Rockstar has delivered a product that can become one of the defining games of this generation.

Grand Theft Auto VI is everything we hoped for and more: Rockstar blends the best of GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 with countless new details that make its world more immersive and alive, and it stands firmly on its own identity. After a 13-year wait, it was absolutely worth it.
A grounded and deeply affecting story that makes you care about the protagonists in ways the series has never managed before. Rockstar has done it again.

After many years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here, and despite the extremely high expectations surrounding it, the game manages to meet them. The county of Leonida is a living, breathing place, a kaleidoscope of Americana that comes to life as though it were an actual destination to visit. Additionally, Jason and Lucia are among the most naturally developed characters in Rockstar's history, sharing great chemistry and proving highly likeable in their respective anti-hero, criminal personas. Add to this some truly memorable action sequences and an overall grandiose, well-written story that can easily stretch beyond 60 hours of gameplay, and you have one of the greatest entries in the series, one that also sets new standards for the open-world genre, particularly in terms of the believability of its world design.

Grand Theft Auto VI continues Rockstar’s tradition of unparalleled excellence, once again pushing the boundaries of video games in terms of content, visuals, and narrative. From deeply emotional storytelling to intense action, it delivers an extraordinary experience unlike anything else.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the greatest video game ever made.

GTA VI is the most ambitious game we have seen from Rockstar Games, shattering the mold of anything released to date. Every single detail is a rich, high-quality visual treat, set inside an open world that gives players countless hours to enjoy it. Without a doubt, this is the best game we have played in recent years.

Believe the hype: Grand Theft Auto VI supersedes Red Dead Redemption 2 as Rockstar Games' magnum opus. It's the ultimate crime simulator, with a world so alive that even if you choose not to follow the story or engage in any wrongdoing you'll still find hours upon hours of fun things to see and do. And however you play, your jaw will frequently be making contact with the floor at the outstanding level of detail Rockstar has lavished on us.
Rockstar hasn't just set a new benchmark for the open-world genre, it has delivered the highest-fidelity sandbox of the generation

What can I say? GTA VI is finally here, and despite expectations having long since gone through the roof, Rockstar has still managed to surprise us. Having essentially invented the modern action open-world formula, Rockstar has now brought it close to perfection with GTA VI, setting it within a digital world that, in terms of naturalism, vitality, lighting and animation, simply has no equal in the industry today. The theory that the reality we live in is a simulation suddenly doesn’t seem so absurd anymore (and finding a Mango song in the OST strikes me as a pretty obvious clue).

Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realising such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.

Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar’s magnum opus, and nothing else comes close to what they’ve created here. This is without a doubt the most immersive world ever created, and it’s filled to the brim with story missions, side quests, secrets, and thousands of things to see. There are a lot of new systems, but you’re never forced to use them all. This is your story, and you can shape it however you want. Combine this with the most cinematic and touching story to date, and you’ll understand why this is a masterpiece. We had to wait a long time for it, but in the end, it was worth every second. This is the new blueprint for a lot of games to come, but it will take years before we see something like this again. Grand Theft Auto VI is a true evolution of the franchise and easily one of Rockstar’s greatest achievements. Prepare to lose yourself in Leonida.

With impossible production values, details that matter, and an
interconnected set of world systems that bring this world to life, GTA
VI is unlike anything we’ve ever seen.  Jason and Lucia are the
beating heart of this game, and the story they tell is worth living.
This isn’t just a good game, or a great game, it’s the kind that comes
just once a generation.
Rockstar overdelivers on the most hyped video game of all time.
GTA VI cherry-picks some of the best qualities from previous Grand Theft Auto entries and the eternal masterpiece Red Dead Redemption 2 to create a truly impactful video game.

Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar Games at its absolute best. With an outstanding story, unforgettable protagonists, a remarkably detailed open world and exceptional technical polish, it surpasses GTA V in virtually every way while capturing the narrative depth of Red Dead Redemption 2. A genuine masterpiece.

As always, you’ll carjack your way through the city and work your way up in the criminal underworld. But this time around, it definitely makes a difference whether you use your weapon merely to threaten someone, to immobilize them, or to actually kill them. What reinforces this even more is the fact that everything has been rendered with almost terrifying realism: the way you move and handle weapons feels lifelike. In addition, Leonida is a lively and vibrant city where you’ll enjoy spending time, full of characters who, although sometimes exaggeratedly caricatured, don’t feel like cardboard cutouts. However, the massive hype that has built up is sure to spark polarizing reactions and reviews. Thirteen years of waiting for a sequel may have set the bar so unrealistically high for some that nothing will ever be good enough. Let them keep complaining; in the meantime, we—undoubtedly along with tens of millions of others—will continue to enjoy life in Leonida for weeks—if not months—to come.

Thirteen years in the making, Grand Theft Auto 6 lives up to the hype and then some. Rockstar has created the most immersive and unpredictable open world we’ve ever seen and has transformed the action game into a life sim.

I say without a hint of hesitation: Grand Theft Auto VI is the best game to be released this console generation and a genuine watershed moment for the industry. Boasting sky-high production values, an astonishing sense of scale, and a gripping, emotionally resonant narrative paired with Rockstar’s signature biting social commentary, it’s an experience that will keep you glued to your controller from beginning to end throughout its sprawling, 80-plus-hour runtime. Quite simply, if you enjoy video games at all, then you can’t afford to miss GTAVI.
The scale of Grand Theft Auto 6 is undeniably vast, but it’s above all the underlying systems that bring it to life. This is a revolution for the medium of video games.

Grand Theft Auto VI more than lives up to the huge expectations. The game is groundbreaking and is packed with characters you’ll gradually come to love. Together, these characters weave a compelling story set in a world I’m in no hurry to say goodbye to.

Rockstar Games has done it again. Grand Theft Auto VI delivers one of the most ambitious open-world experiences ever created, refining the franchise's gameplay while offering a breathtaking world filled with activities, secrets, and rewarding exploration. Its stunning audiovisual presentation pushes current-generation consoles to their limits. While its story may not be the series' best, it remains among its strongest. Whether it will live up to every player's enormous expectations remains to be seen, but GTA VI is an exceptional experience that no open-world fan should miss, even before the arrival of the new GTA Online.

By focusing on its main narrative without sacrificing the vibrant open world we've come to expect from the series, it delivers the best of both worlds. The tightly woven story of its two protagonists is compelling, with seamless shifts between their perspectives adding to the experience. A refined open-world adventure that proves great design is about more than sheer scale.

There are games and works that transcend the scores assigned to them in reviews, because reducing them to a single number will never do them justice; and among those works is GTA 6. View this 10 as merely symbolic and dive headfirst into Leonidas’s world.

GTA VI is, in many ways, the greatest game of all time, but be careful not to expect that same level of quality, polish, and detail from other games. GTA VI isn’t here to set the standard—it’s here to show that it’s pushing the boundaries of the medium to the limit—so enjoy every moment of this new Rockstar ego trip; we don’t know if we’ll still be around for the next one.

GTA VI has turned out to be the masterpiece everyone was hoping for. Rockstar has surpassed itself technically and created an open world that is more immersive, believable and meticulously detailed than anything anyone has ever done before. But in terms of storytelling too, this is, in my opinion, the studio’s best game yet. Lucia and Jason are clearly morally dubious characters, but their motivations are so fundamentally likeable and clearly presented that you can’t help but take them to your heart straight away. Above all, the chemistry between this duo carries the game through the extensive, grippingly told main campaign, whilst the sheer variety – both in terms of mission design and the freedom to explore this world – is unique. I can’t wait to delve even deeper into this wonderfully chaotic, beautiful Leonida until I’ve explored every last nook and cranny, robbed every bank and witnessed every random event, no matter how crazy.
Rockstar Games has combined the best of all its games and taken it to the next level by creating the largest, wildest, and most realistic open world ever seen in a videogame.

Rockstar makes up for the 13-year wait with one of the most entertaining, varied and ambitious entries in the series. Visually and technically breathtaking, and overflowing with content, Leonida is the best open world we've ever seen.

Rockstar Games has created a monumental masterpiece that elevates action, freedom, and attention to detail to an extraordinary scale. GTA 6 is an experience that will define this generation and cast its influence over much of the next.

GTA VI is definitely like a flower in a hurricane. After being postponed,
leaked and doubted my many, it survives the chaos and stands out as the
biggest videogame of all time. Welcome to Vice City, Bienvenidos a Vice
City. Believe the hype. It's well worth the 13 year wait.

Grand Theft Auto VI feels like Rockstar at the height of its powers, and a new benchmark in open-world game design. Yet it is the more grounded, compelling story that steals the show here. Those quiet moments define GTAVI for me - and it’s an experience I can’t wait to relive again and again.

GTAVI is a game that's constantly impressing you. The level of detail and immersion that Rockstar has achieved is unprecedented; combined with a love story that will definitely shed a lot of tears, this one is nothing short of a masterpiece.

Despite its compelling story and brilliantly written characters, the true highlight of GTA 6 lies elsewhere: its breathtaking open world. Rockstar has created an incredibly dynamic world that will be talked about for years to come. In the end, GTA 6 was well worth the 13-year wait.
A masterpiece that seamlessly weaves drama and entertainment with nuance on one hand, while on the other prompting the question, 'What else is left that Rockstar wanted to achieve but hasn't yet?'

Grand Theft Auto 6 is an engrossing Bonnie and Clyde crime thriller that delivers social and political commentary as only Rockstar can. Not only has Rockstar retooled all of the mechanics core to the “Grand Theft Auto” experience, but it has also delivered a level of immersion in Leonida never before seen. Vice City is still destination gaming after more than two decades with its unbelievably dense, coked-to-the-gills sandbox where there’s something must-see on every street. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a generation-defining instant classic.

A truly generational video game in every palpable sense,
Grand Theft Auto VI is easily the most impressive game this console
generation and easily Rockstar Games finest hour. Nobody does
open-worlds like they do and when taken in tandem with masses of
razor-sharp writing, a fully reactive world stuffed with exciting things
to do and some of the most downright enjoyable and epically ridiculous
action sequences this side of Hollywood, it becomes an undeniable fact
that Grand Theft Auto VI is an absolute must-play and sets an impossibly
high bar for other studios to follow.

I think this is a more mature Grand Theft Auto, a game that, even if you bounced off the questionable characters in the past, you should find joy here. That said, it still feels like a Grand Theft Auto game, there is still the trademark humour, crazy characters and set pieces, they have just been taken to the next level. Tie this in with the amazing technical achievements, brilliant writing, and a map that begs you to stick your nose into every corner, and GTA VI exceeded my already high expectations.

GTA VI is finally here, and it’s everything. This whole experience… I still can’t fully wrap my head around it. Let’s all savor this moment, because I’m having a hard time imagining any entertainment product coming close to what GTA VI has accomplished for years to come...What a game. Wow.

There are great games, there are games that define a console generation, and then there are games that make you reconsider what you expect from the medium altogether. Grand Theft Auto VI belongs in that last category.

The video game equivalent of HBO's The Wire, Grand Theft Auto VI is the most immersive game ever created, with a spectacular, unprecedented marriage of narrative and gameplay. It is a watershed moment not just for this console generation, but for gaming as an art form.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a modern work of art and the best experience in the franchise to date. Perfect in virtually every possible department, the game shows that the developer's obsession raises the bar once again for what is possible to achieve in open-world games. Just like Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA VI is another product that is difficult to surpass, something that perhaps can only happen again in another Rockstar Games project.

GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time. Crucially, despite the 30fps cap, the gameplay feels responsive and you have much more authorship over how you want to approach it. I enjoyed preparing for my robberies and feeling like I was rewarded for the legwork. The audiovisual presentation is a new high for the industry, with a frankly flabbergasting array of art assets bringing it all to life. But I think Jason and Lucia’s ragtag romance, which is central to everything in the game, also demonstrates an unexpected maturity – without completely removing the silly sense of downright dumb humour the series is known for. Despite unprecedented expectations, GTA 6 delivers – and then some.

A masterclass in every facet of its design, Grand Theft Auto VI’s epic scale, immaculate production, astonishing world, and gripping narrative resets the standard it set for open world sandboxes, ensuring it’s in the conversation as one of the best games of all time.

Everyone will leave Rockstar's latest generational masterpiece with a different takeaway. For me, the essence of GTA VI will forever be crystallized in a single snapshot of Jason and Lucia looking out at the sunset over the Vice City skyline, fingers tightly intertwined.

There is genre-defining, and then there is genre-making. GTAVI is the kind of experience that pushes the boundaries of what an interactive world can achieve, while delivering a story and characters that will remain memorable for years to come.
GTA 6 delivers on pretty much everything it promises, and takes a page from Red Dead Redemption 2's book, making it one of the strongest entries in the franchise to date.

A masterpiece of immersive storytelling that perfectly blends the authorship of deep player customization with some of the richest screenwriting, world creation, and voice work in the history of gaming.

Could we really have ever doubted Rockstar Games? For decades, the studio has been operating on a completely different level, constantly pushing the boundaries of gaming.
From GTA 3 to Red Dead Redemption 2, every major release has set new standards for an industry that's still struggling to catch up. And with GTA 6, Rockstar hasn't just outdone its competitors. It's surpassed its own achievements. Of course, the studio has massive financial resources and years of development behind it. But money alone doesn't create a masterpiece, you need talent, vision, and that almost obsessive attention to detail. And that's exactly what makes GTA 6 so extraordinary. Rockstar has created something truly special: a world that's just as enjoyable to live in as it is to play in. A living, breathing universe where everything feels natural, and where Jason and Lucia bring a genuinely human dimension to this incredible adventure. It'll probably take years for the industry to catch up. GTA 6 isn't just a masterpiece, it's the new benchmark for every open-world game to come. And one thing is absolutely clear: Rockstar Games is, now more than ever, the undisputed god of open-world gaming.

Rockstar has exceeded unrealistic expectations, delivering a love story set in the most incredible world, with unrivaled quality and detail. Grand Theft Auto 6 is everything we dreamed it could be and more.

GTA VI delivers one of the most impressive open worlds ever created, with an enormous, richly detailed and dynamic environment, countless activities, and two memorable protagonists, Jason and Lucia, whose romantic relationship adds a new dimension to the story. While the leap in scale, realism and detail is remarkable, the core gameplay remains largely familiar, building on the strengths of GTA V while refining and expanding the experience in nearly every aspect.

Despite its cultural significance taking on an almost mythical guise in the years leading up to launch, the game itself is, luckily, worthy of these lofty expectations. Rockstar delivers its sharpest technical achievement to date, of course, but even more importantly, the game is a masterpiece on an artistic level too, delivering a fantastic story told through memorable characters in an unbelievable world. This is one for the history books in every conceivable way.

That’s the perfect word to sum GTA 6 up: encapsulating. It completely takes over, pulling you into its world in a way I haven’t seen done before. It feels as significant as the leap from GTA 3 to GTA 4, such is the technical mastery of Rockstar’s developers, and takes everything the company learned from Red Dead Redemption 2 to evolve the GTA formula into something refreshing while still maintaining the identity of the series that made Rockstar what it is today. GTA 6 is a generational game and we likely won’t see anything even close to it until Rockstar makes something else in ten years.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the culmination of more than a decade of anticipation; it’s a monumental achievement in video game development. With the best story in franchise history, unforgettable characters, refined gameplay, and the most dynamic and immersive open world ever created, Rockstar Games has surpassed even the loftiest expectations. Despite a few technical imperfections and the absence of a 60fps mode, GTAVI sets a new benchmark for the industry. Simply put, it’s the best video game ever made.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a truly colossal experience, featuring an enormous open world packed with activities and populated by hundreds of NPCs whose unpredictable behavior can lead players into unexpected adventures. Jason and Lucia’s story remains engaging from beginning to end, striking an excellent balance between a more serious tone, outrageous action sequences, and the signature satire that defines the franchise. Combined with stunning visuals and an outstanding soundtrack, GTA 6 delivers an unforgettable experience that is worth every penny and every second of the 13-year wait for a new installment in the series.

Grand Theft Auto VI does not merely meet the immense expectations that surrounded its anticipation—it surpasses them. Rockstar Games has crafted a monumental work, seamlessly blending masterful storytelling, remarkably diverse gameplay, and a game world with a level of credibility unmatched in the gaming landscape. It is a technological, artistic, and interactive achievement destined to serve as a benchmark for the entire industry for years to come. A "perfect" game may not truly exist, but rarely have we come this close to that definition. An absolute masterpiece.

Whether you’re new to the world of GTA or a longtime fan of the series, Grand Theft Auto VI brings an exceptional experience as a whole. Whether it is the jaw dropping graphics fidelity and its hyper attention to the smallest of details without cutting any corners, a wide range of side activities, random encounters that throw you off unexpectedly or a dopamine inducing story from beginning to end keeping you on your toes at all times. All of which takes place in a handcrafted world that is full of life wherever you go. Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto VI will keep players delving deep into it for an incredibly long time.

GTA 6 is a masterpiece that redefines open-world gaming. Leonida has left us speechless, Jason and Lucía are at the center of a fascinating story, and the gameplay possibilities in Rockstar's latest title seem endless. It's the game of our lives.

GTA 6 is a massive, meticulously polished Katamari of everything human, rolling up just as much of our artistry as the gritty detritus of everyday life. It is a collaborative triumph that an AI could never replicate, simply because it is profoundly human down to the marrow. I might not have been waiting for this one since 2013. But even if I had been, I wouldn't be disappointed in the slightest.

With a single-player campaign that showcases the full potential of gaming and an impressive open world, GTA VI manages to justify the high expectations that have built up over the last few years. Furthermore, the foundation laid by Rockstar is primed to evolve, ensuring the title becomes an even more historic experience as time goes on.

GTA VI is a true masterpiece that lives up to the hype, combining a cinematic story, believable characters and a breathtakingly immersive world. With dynamic NPCs, intelligent police and lasting consequences, Leonida feels more alive than ever.

In many ways, Grand Theft Auto VI is more of a sequel to Red Dead Redemption 2 than to GTA5. In its very deliberate-feeling systems and its heavy focus on player choice and consequence in a subtly more grounded world, GTA6 closely resembles its western cousin. With that said, there has been a remarkable threading of the needle here - such focus has been instilled without losing the potential and predilection for chaos, humour, cultural satire, and true sandbox freedom that made GTA famous. It feels like everything people loved before, but it also feels exciting and new. It's my new favourite GTA game, and by quite some way - which is really saying something.

GTA 6 tells a story about two criminals in love that’s as spectacular as it is moving. It brings together the series’ trademark scale, an impressive open world, and a meticulous attention to detail. Jason and Lucia are terrific leads, and the vibrant state of Leonida makes you want to keep uncovering its secrets. Technical issues, a 30 fps frame rate, and dips in performance do little to dull the shine of one of the best and most engrossing games of this generation.
Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered.
A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. Our review.

GTA 6 does everything you’d expect and more, delivering a cohesive experience with a strong story, excellent performance, incredible visuals, an engaging and dense world, and an evolution of the franchise formula to its most advanced iteration yet. It's full of nuance and unpredictability, and of course, offers a healthy dose of freedom to do what you will.
It raises the bar at every level that matters. Grand Theft Auto VI is the most extraordinary game I’ve ever reviewed.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is an absolute triumph, and one of the most complete, most gripping, and downright coolest video games I have ever played, and is an essential must-play experience for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S owners. Every aspect of the game is top-tier, crafted with immense care and detail, and combines into one all-consuming, blockbuster cinematic experience. The story and narrative offer some gripping storytelling complete with bombastic action set pieces; the action is chaotic, and the open world of Vice City is a fantastic sandbox playground that’s as deep as it is wide, with an incredible amount to do and discover. It’s a veritable memory-maker of a video game; it’s everything we’d hoped and waited for, and then some, and the most complete open-world single-player game I’ve ever played.

In every regard, Grand Theft Auto VI is an extraordinary achievement for Rockstar Games. Even with incredibly high expectations coming in, Rockstar found a way to surpass just about everything that I had hoped to see in GTA VI. The final product is one that I’m still spellbound by, as I struggle to understand how the studio was even capable of making such an engrossing and complex experience. Grand Theft Auto VI is unquestionably going to go down as a landmark release in gaming’s history and will continue to consume both my thoughts and free time well into the future.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a modern masterpiece. Rockstar's developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched. Minor performance issues don’t dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait.

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't a perfect game. The story experiences inevitable ups and downs, some missions remain anchored to Rockstar structures that are starting to show their age, certain sections overdo it with gunplay, the geography of Leonidas suffers from a lack of consistency with less biome variety, a true ownership system is missing, and we would have liked to see the PS5 Pro reach 60 frames per second. Yet none of these flaws can undermine what GTA 6 achieves at its core. Rockstar hasn't simply built a bigger, better-looking open world with more activities: it's built a world where systems, characters, environments, and player behavior are in constant dialogue with each other. A heist isn't just a mission, a car isn't just a vehicle, the sea isn't just a border, money isn't just a number, and Jason and Lucia aren't just two characters to switch between. Everything can become part of something else: GTA 6 is an open world capable of generating stories through its systems even more than it can with its script. Some will probably miss the more immediate, anarchic, and rowdy GTA of the past. We, however, believe this is the evolution the series needed.

A display of power and pure talent, GTAVI reaches new heights of immersion. From the summit of Mount Kalaga to the depths of the ocean, passing through the disturbing Vice City, the alchemy between the countless systems is so strong that it overshadows the sporadic inaccuracies and understandable technical compromises. The Leonidas is an inexhaustible source of emerging stories, a ravenous devourer of time, within which the hours slip by without us noticing, sucked in by unique and constant stimuli. We are faced with a colossus of creativity that sets standards, and in this sense, the top rating should be understood as an emblem not of unattainable perfection, but of the grandiose goals that Rockstar's work manages to achieve. Thanks also to its masterful writing, Grand Theft Auto VI represents a concrete evolution for the series, both narratively and playfully. Jason and Lucia move, and we with them, through an incredibly cohesive world, where every corner deserves to be explored and experienced. Perhaps even hand in hand.

GTA 6 is the ultimate expression of everything Rockstar has built over nearly thirty years. And after completing the entire main campaign, I find it hard to imagine what the studio could possibly do to surpass it. Leonida feels like a world that exists independently of whatever you choose to do, Jason and Lucia are two protagonists capable of carrying an entire story, and everything happening around them adds further depth to the experience. Beneath the surface of heists and crime there's a deeper reflection on the pursuit of a better life. Because the path that promises easy money doesn't always lead to happiness. And perhaps that's one of the most interesting contradictions Rockstar has chosen to explore.

A knockout, a gut punch, love at first sight. Call it whatever you like. GTA 6 is something truly special. A remarkable game like no other, with a unique perfection. Its central duo is nothing short of phenomenal. Their chemistry, the bond they share, and the emotional connection we develop with them draw us so completely into their world that we never want to leave. And when the credits finally roll, you're left facing that familiar void: the post-game blues, the feeling of loss, the longing for just one more moment with characters you've grown so attached to. You don't want it to end. Thankfully, GTA 6 is endlessly generous and has plenty more to offer, with an incredible wealth of things to do, see and discover. As for its few rough edges, they're barely worth mentioning when set against the sheer brilliance of the experience as a whole. This is a truly outstanding masterpiece: bold, moving and deeply authentic.

Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best open-world game I’ve ever played, and one of the best games full stop, with only incredibly minute nitpicks barely worth mentioning that do nothing to drag it down from masterpiece status. Its jaw-droppingly detailed world, completely revamped and recontextualised mechanics, and heartfelt narrative with two stellar leads put it far above the rest of the incredible series and set an impossible new bar for the medium as a whole. I'm sure we’ll never see another game with such unreal hype that actually lives up to and exceeds expectations, but you can rest easy knowing that the long road to Leonida was worth walking.
Grand Theft Auto VI sets a new benchmark for open-world crime sandbox – one that will probably only be surpassed by the next Grand Theft Auto.

I keep reaching for something that sums up GTA VI, as much as it’s possible to sum up a game as vast as this, and the closest I come is the nightclubs. These show GTA VI at its most extravagant: hundreds of virtual people under the pulsing lights, all dressed up to go out, dancing to a fastidiously curated soundtrack featuring some of the real world’s most famous artists as the controller pulses to the bassline in your hands. These big nights out are an opportunity for both Vice City’s sleaziest denizens and Rockstar’s developers to flash their cash: they are the game’s most ostentatiously expensive and showy scenarios. But at the centre of it all, there are Jason and Lucia, dancing together, focused on each other in the midst of all this chaos and excess.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a revolution. It’s a game with boundless ambition that manages to surprise you every time you play. It’s a technical marvel, but above all, it’s living proof that Rockstar never fails to create vibrant worlds brimming with charisma.

Temper your dream expectations and GTA 6 – a significant but not superhuman evolution of the franchise – is peak gaming. Dive into a huge, vibrant, semi-living city packed with hundreds of hours of activity, hi-octane missions (once you’re past the early bouts of scene-setting domesticity), countless colourful sidelines into bizarre communities and the most focussed and involving storyline in the franchise. From helicopter rescues to drone surveillance and fighting off a pushy dominatrix, the missions are impressively varied – and the more realistic wanted system encourages better heist planning and smoother getaways, expanding the options for gameplay approach. But for all its realistic cityscape detail and exploration opportunities this is still a cartoonish criminal world of freaks, perverts, gangsters and crooked CEOs where you can wreak massive destruction and speedboat your way to anonymity in minutes. Beyond this deep but not fully comprehensive virtual city experience, ordinary urban life isn’t diverting enough to add much more to a game than this.
Grand Theft Auto VI isn't a game you're invited to simply play, it's a whole other world you're invited to live in. Let Leonida draw you in, and you'll never want to leave.

GTA 6 stands as a remarkable narrative, technological and artistic achievement, featuring an open world of unparalleled density, believability, and richness. Its masterful writing, the emotional depth of Jason and Lucia's relationship, and its spectacular cinematic direction give the adventure exceptional intensity. The sheer variety of activities, organic interactions, and outstanding level of polish reinforce the feeling of exploring a genuinely living world. Its relatively low difficulty, occasionally forgiving AI, lack of a 60fps mode, and absence of French voice acting remain notable shortcomings. Yet by bringing together freedom, cinema, and emotion with such extraordinary mastery, Rockstar Games has created a work that could redefine the ambitions of video games for years to come.

GTA 6 more than delivers on all its promises. A colossal adventure in a vast world, overflowing with detail and so much content that you can finish the story without seeing much of it. And all of this is presented with an audiovisual display that is the best this generation has offered so far. A more than deserving contender for Game of the Year 2026.

It’s been a long wait, and amidst fears that the hype would prove to be all smoke and mirrors, Rockstar has risen to the occasion and lived up to expectations that bordered on the impossible. Narratively and in terms of gameplay, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a far more mature and realistic game than one might expect, yet it never forgets the franchise’s roots, presenting itself as a natural evolution of decades of work. With radically different personalities, Jason and Lucia are charismatic and deeply human, which helps to ground their wildest antics and most daring crimes in reality. As for Leonida, it’s the best experience I have ever had in an open-world game – it’s in a league of its own.

GTA 6 is unbelievably fun, with a world that is a joy to simply exist in. Jason and Lucia’s story might not be revolutionary, even if you have more agency in their relationship, but the individual missions are so incredibly diverse and well-written and acted that it’s all the propulsion you need to keep going. You can race to the finish line, but that would be its own crime. This is an experience that’s meant to be savored – packed with surprises and fun details just waiting for players to discover. If this is what a 13-year wait delivers, then Grand Theft Auto 6 was more than worth it.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a masterpiece. Everything from the core elements of the story to 'little' things such as the musical score or the environments that players will journey through, there's always something to see. Leonida never sleeps, and it clearly shows through every aspect of the gameplay. No matter how you choose to navigate the story of Jason and Lucia, Rockstar provides you with tons to enjoy.

GTA 6 is the biggest blockbuster of the PS5 and Xbox Series generation. It is a game in which Rockstar showcases an unrivalled combination of magnificent visuals, sensational attention to detail and energetic, immersive gameplay. This results in a living, breathing world offering unrivalled immersion.

At its core, GTA VI is an intrinsically human story—a simple tale. A love story about two people desperately reaching out to hold each other’s hands in an otherwise selfish world. I think we can all relate to that.

Grand Theft Auto VI is absolutely worth the wait. The unprecedented realization of its world totally immerses you in Jason and Lucia’s criminal odyssey across Leonida. The story is a roller coaster of emotions that feels distinctly personal thanks to multiple endings and small choices throughout. Robbing everyone and everything is an exhilarating rush with an economy that feels worthwhile, and the high-speed police chases are the best in the series. There is so much to do and discover, so sit back, relax, and enjoy the unforgettable ride.

Grand Theft Auto VI takes its time, settling players into a quiet life in the Keys before slowly pulling Jason and Lucia into something much bigger and darker. Its two leads are grounded, likable, and easy to care about, and its photorealistic world reacts to nearly everything you do, constantly testing your patience and your impulses along the way. GTA VI is astoundingly polished, ludicrously fun, and frequently hilarious, and it's the first GTA that made me feel bad about what I was doing to the people I was playing. With zero hyperbole, this is a masterpiece.

Our journey through Leonida has been one to remember, and I get the feeling that it still has countless secrets and surprises waiting to be discovered, even after dozens of hours of gameplay and, of course, completing its main story. Deciding where to draw the line must have been quite a challenge during the planning stages, as Grand Theft Auto VI is precisely the kind of game whose ambitions seem to know no bounds at times. It's impressive to see how Rockstar continues to push the boundaries and challenge the conventions and paradigms of the industry every time it takes the stage, something that feels even more significant today given the circumstances we've already discussed. There's no need to reiterate the cultural significance this title will have, or how, even before its release, it has already become a worldwide phenomenon that is somehow living up to the enormous expectations surrounding it. The debate over who deserves to be crowned GOTY 2026 is over.

Grand Theft Auto VI lives up to the highest expectations. The game recognizes both the good and bad decisions made by its predecessors. The state of Leonida is a truly massive upgrade compared to the concrete jungle of Liberty City or the enormous mountains that occupied half the map in GTAV. Vice City still shines with its bright lights. This is a game that rekindles a childlike sense of curiosity and brings back pleasant memories. It already offers enormous opportunities for exploration and experimentation, delivering an incredible sense of excitement and wonder.

reviews.excerpt: GTA VI had me chasing trouble across Leonida one moment and slowing down the next just to hear what Lucia had to say. I loved choosing my own way through a heist, but what stayed with me was how Jason and Lucia looked out for each other. Their love story gives even the wildest chase a personal stake.
GTAVI takes a few steps into more serious, adult and realistic direction, but this is all for the better. Exceptionally well written story makes this easily the best game of the year.

Expectations for the game are sky-high, but Grand Theft Auto VI is a masterpiece of game design. Rockstar has clearly put thought into every aspect, from character progression and money to the consequences of Jason and Lucia’s actions and the relationship they build together; the game pulls all of it off flawlessly. It has an incredible amount of depth, both as an open-world title and as a role-playing experience, and it goes far beyond what I thought the series was capable of. Personally, this is the single most immersive game I’ve ever played, and Leonida is a world players could happily spend hundreds or even thousands of hours in. The writing is gripping, and at times heartbreaking, carrying Jason and Lucia’s story from their reunion to the last chapter. Grand Theft Auto VI was a long time coming, and it may be a long time before anything matches it.

GTA VI is work of art. Once again, Rockstar has managed to outdo itself and achieve the impossible. The game set a new standard for what an open world and narrative driven game can be. GTA VI excels across the board and is a once in a lifetime experience.

Very rarely does an entertainment property the size of Grand Theft Auto VI live up to the insane hype that has been forced upon it. However, GTA 6 is not only the best game Rockstar has made to date, but it’s also the most impressive open world game ever released. From its breathtaking map, realistic NPCs, or its groundbreaking gameplay innovations, the latest Grand Theft Auto entry is a technical tour de force. GTA 6 also features Rockstar’s most mature and emotional story, grounded by Jason and Lucia’s deeply moving relationship and their fight to protect it at all costs. Grand Theft Auto VI was worth waiting 13 years for, and will no doubt be one of the most influential games over the next decade.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a landmark open-world achievement. Its exceptionally dense world, interconnected crime systems, and compelling partnership between Jason and Lucia elevate Rockstar’s familiar formula into something that feels genuinely transformative. Some mission rigidity and a 30 fps target remain, but they do little to diminish an extraordinary, generation-defining experience.

Coming into GTA VI without passion, we leave completely charmed (not to say "marked for life") by what could be considered Rockstar's coming-of-age installment. While one might lament the loss of the studio's inherent bratty edge, it comes with an extremely endearing duo of protagonists that you emotionally invest in very easily. The fact that GTA VI allows itself to take its time and create quiet moments throughout its epic journey won't please everyone, but it has to be said that it was the right choice to forge that crucial bond between Jason, Lucia, and the player. When you add to that a sublime open world, extremely rich and detailed, populated by NPCs like we've never seen before, all accompanied by deep overhauls of the series' historical gameplay elements, it seems impossible not to fully enjoy the experience. The driving is so enjoyable and the radio stations so well-stocked that you can easily see yourself extending your stay in Leonida for quite a while longer. And a few minor interface issues aren't going to get in our way.

Rockstar innovated and gave us things that we can’t get from any other developer. In closing one and a bit of a forward looking statement, one of the things that blew my mind about GTA V Online was the existence of roleplay servers and when this entry gets its inevitable online mode, players will have a vast playground to mess around in…hopefully these players will have experienced all the amazing single player content that this title has to offer.

For all the time you'll get from it, it's well worth the price of admission. And we'd wager that it's very much worth the wait. It should be a crime for a game to be this good, honestly, and its influence will be felt for years as developers the world over scramble to raise their game and reach this high new bar for what a game can be. Now, when's GTA 7 coming?

Grand Theft Auto VI is a triumph. It feels like the sum of every lesson Rockstar has learned over the past decade, wrapped around a story with real heart. Leonida is a joy to explore, Jason and Lucia are the best duo the series has ever had, and the systems underneath it all are smarter than ever. Yes, the 30fps cap will disappoint some players, and the story could lose a few hours without anyone noticing. However, those are small marks against a game this generous, this detailed and this much fun.
GTA6 is incredible and, despite many hours put in, I feel like I’ve barely scratched the surface.

The endless wait, the delays, the colossal budget: it’s all led to this moment. Grand Theft Auto VI is the new benchmark for open-world action games – a game which, given the scale of its ambitions, gets very little wrong. Leonida is a vibrant and convincing world, the setting for a grand crime saga featuring virtual characters it’s hard not to grow fond of. What gives it its unmistakable character is the variety of situations and the natural way in which the world reacts to the player’s actions – qualities that make it stand head and shoulders above even its most recent rivals. In the genre that bears its hallmark more than any other, to say that Rockstar is in a league of its own is an understatement: at this point, it almost seems as though it’s playing a different sport altogether – one without rivals. Perhaps it’s a bit tedious being up there all on your own, but then again, it’s only natural to look down on everyone else when you’re the king.

Grand Theft Auto VI has demonstrated just how far one can go in this regard with its characters, storyline and the creation of a living, breathing world. It makes you feel, in every single detail, that it is the final and greatest game created by human hands in the age of artificial intelligence. This title is not merely an extremely entertaining open-world game; it also delivers a highly intelligent and socially critical commentary on modern America, thereby fulfilling the mission it set out to achieve in a truly ingenious manner.
A gangster dream come true. With GTA 6, Rockstar has not only outdone itself, it has exceeded even the high expectations.

GTA VI is not only the best GTA release yet, but a truly exceptional game. The roughly 60-hour-long main story motivates from start to finish and scores points with off-the-wall missions, eccentric characters, brilliant ideas, plenty of humour, a good dose of tragedy, and numerous outcomes that depend on various factors. This very approach also ensures that GTA VI offers great replay value. In technical terms, the title also sets new standards. Those who aren’t bothered by the lack of German audio dubbing can look forward to a true gangster epic. Congratulations, Rockstar!
GTA 6 manages what is almost impossible to pull off. The game not only meets the enormous expectations but even exceeds them in multiple ways.

Grand Theft Auto 6 lives up to its promises and surpasses the series’ legacy after 13 years of increasingly feverish anticipation. This is the franchise at its best, bringing together an unforgettable story, characters worth rooting for, and an open world with seemingly endless exploration. There are a few shortcomings in its combat mechanics, some technical quirks on the PS5, and some missed opportunities that keep it from being perfect, but they do little to diminish the sheer quality of what’s here. GTA 6 successfully delivers a watershed moment, defining the pinnacle of gaming in the modern era, and showing the possibilities for future games to follow.
GTA 6 is a breathtaking open-world masterpiece with unforgettable characters, incredible depth, and endless variety, despite a few minor flaws.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not the second coming, nor is it a revolutionary game. However, it is a brilliant new GTA entry that strives to excel in all areas and almost always succeeds, delivering improvements that range from noticeable to substantial and even, in some occasions, surprising. Its story is poignant and engaging, its world is detailed to an unprecedented degree, its visuals are fantastic and its range of activities absolutely massive. When your franchise's predecessor has sold nearly 235 million units, you don't reinvent the wheel; you refine it, and that's what Rockstar did, delivering one of the best GTAs to date.

GTA 6 is a masterpiece both technically and in terms of content. No video game city has ever felt as alive as Vice City, nor has any been as immersive. Only in terms of story does it fall just short of claiming the throne among Rockstar games.

Put simply, Grand Theft Auto VI feels like the kind of advancement you'd expect to come from a future console generation, not something from today's systems. It's a staggeringly well-crafted title that once again proves Rockstar are leading the industry in countless different ways. Whilst opportunities to be narratively bolder were left on the table, it doesn't stop this game from astonishing the player time and time again. Grand Theft Auto VI is the embodiment of a masterful and abundant sandbox escapade.

Grand Theft Auto VI sets a remarkable new standard for open-world gaming, delivering extraordinary visual fidelity, unmatched attention to detail, and a living world that constantly surprises. Jason and Lucia's compelling relationship anchors an excellent story, while innovative financial progression, sophisticated police mechanics, and outstanding mission variety elevate the experience. Despite simplistic melee combat and repetitive QTEs that occasionally undermine important moments, Rockstar has created an exceptional achievement that pushes the boundaries of interactive entertainment and stands among the most impressive games ever made.

GTA 6 is an incredible, truly memorable journey. Jason—and especially Lucia—are excellent, well-crafted characters, featured in a "rags-to-riches" adventure filled with ups and downs that feel meaningful to the story, culminating in an ending that makes it all worthwhile. That said, the game’s mechanic of forcing you to wait before progressing the main plot led me to complete nearly all the optional missions before the story concluded; this left only secondary activities for the endgame—content that, for me, holds little value. Even so, it is easily one of the greatest games of this generation, one that will undoubtedly live up to the immense expectations surrounding it.

GTA 6 is another great triumph for Rockstar Games. It's a new masterpiece for the developer who managed to combine the overwhelming scale with exceptional quality and dared to experiment with a well-established gameplay formula, ascending it to a whole new level. A level that probably no one will be able to match... as probably no one will be able to invest into one game as much time and money as Rockstar in the foreseeable future.

An incredible experience with absolute cutting-edge design in all aspects, it's just so incredibly enjoyable to get lost in Leonida and Vice City. Rockstar has created a stunning and massive world, with detailed gameplay and heaps of surprising moments, GRAND THEFT AUTO VI redefines what the absolute peak of game development looks like once again.

GTA 6 reaches a pinnacle rarely seen in video games. It presents the most stunning urban open world ever created, brought to life with a level of detail that is truly dizzying. With its solid writing, the unforgettable duo of Lucia and Jason, and a more measured approach to gameplay, the title draws you in for well over 100 hours. Admittedly, it is not entirely flawless—there are occasional frame-rate drops, gang hideouts that feel a bit too formulaic, and moments where exploration offers little in the way of rewards. Yet, these minor shortcomings pale in comparison to the overall mastery on display. Players looking for an instant, consequence-free outlet for chaos may be disappointed; however, those willing to fully immerse themselves in this sprawling crime saga will find one of the most absorbing experiences of their gaming lives.

Waiting more than a decade for a video game inevitably comes with enormous expectations. You imagine it in countless different ways, almost convincing yourself that nothing could ever be good enough. Grand Theft Auto VI had an immense weight on its shoulders, as one of the most anticipated and ambitious entertainment releases in history. And despite a few missteps, it manages to live up to those expectations, turning them into something tangible and deeply satisfying. Not everything is perfect: there are some technical compromises, a few missing features, and some characters who deserved more attention. Yet these shortcomings inevitably fade into the background when faced with the extraordinary quality of the overall experience, the freedom it offers, and a level of ambition and attention to detail rarely seen in video games.

Grand Theft Auto VI feels like a game that was worth the wait, although that may go without saying. If you're interested in GTA 6, you're probably already waiting for the preload as I write this. Its breathtakingly detailed, lively world and engaging plot deliver just about everything people hoped for when the game was announced. The opening may feel a little slow, but once things get going, it offers some of the most fun the series has ever delivered.

GTA 6 wasn't just a game—it was a captivating, living, breathing world. It's the kind of title that constantly leaves you wanting to explore more stories within it. While it might not be a flawless 100/100, it's already a fantastic game in its own right.

Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t reinvent the wheel, nor does it bring anything new to the table. It retains the same sandbox formula and wraps it around unforgettable characters, extreme violence and a compelling main story. It’s hard to make a very good game deeply rooted in real-life when everyone plays games to escape reality, but the GTA franchise is proof that it’s possible.
Despite its minor flaws, Grand Theft Auto VI is a major evolution for the series, one that it was well worth the wait. Rockstar’s GTA VI doesn’t set a new standard for sandbox, open-world gaming because this game is in a league of its own. It’s hard to believe that another game will be able to surpass it, unless it’s another Grand Theft Auto title.

Then again, part of the social and cultural value of a work of art lies in the discussions it generates. I’ve spent much of this nearly 3,000-word essay discussing the artistic merits of GTA VI, the billion-dollar game that is also almost certainly going to be the most discussed game of the year. So perhaps it is good art too, after all.

Grand Theft Auto VI elevates the story of its criminals into a deeply personal experience for the player through its astonishingly dense urban environment and meticulous depiction of everyday life. The main missions are admittedly conservative in their design, and the long drives that account for much of the playtime can detract from the sense of immersion. Yet the more time you spend experiencing the protagonists’ daily lives, the more their criminal deeds become imbued with desperation and guilt, and the more you find yourself rooting for their modest dreams of happiness. By making the player experience the gulf between wealth and happiness through everyday life, Grand Theft Auto VI emerges as a modern work of New Hollywood cinema realized in a form uniquely possible through video games.

Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. While uneven storytelling, pacing issues, and occasional performance drops prevent it from reaching perfection, the richly realized world of Leonida and its extraordinary attention to detail make this an unforgettable crime adventure that largely lives up to its monumental expectations.
Rockstar has created the first truly meaningful interactive relationship between two semi-realistic grown-ass adults in the entire medium.
Grand Theft Auto VI will steal your heart. The series matures beyond its memorable car crashes and stick-ups with a game about love, relationships and nurturing your partner.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a great game that lives up to so much of the hype and expectations. Lucia and Jason are a well-written  and compelling pair of protagonists, and the side characters you meet on their journey are great, even if the need to constantly raise the stakes across such a long story lessens its impact. You do have so much more freedom with how to tackle missions, though, and Leonida is a world filled with things to do and discover that will keep you coming back for a long time.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a technological wonder and I’m confident they used some kind of forbidden magic to make it run on a base PS5. The whole of Leonida is alive and the immersion is indescribable. Every corner of this world will give you new stuff to do, new ways to play or take part in wacky stories that only a GTA game can provide. However, all of this is undermined by a weak, slow and inconsistent story with Jason being a very underwhelming protagonist.

Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't just meet the sky-high expectations of a 13-year wait—it shatters them. Across my 100+ hours on PS5 Pro, I was blown away by Leonida's unmatched level of detail, reactive NPCs, and overhauled police and combat systems. Despite a somewhat predictable narrative and a few frustrating restrictions on bonus content, Rockstar has delivered a true generational leap that sets a brand-new standard for open-world games.

We’ll see a PC release eventually, and if all the RAM in the world doesn’t disappear to feed our AI overlords, it’ll probably make its way to the PS6/next Xbox, too. When it does, and the platform players can experience GTA 6 on matches its sheer technical ambition, we’re looking at a pure 10 out of 10 game, no notes. Until then, GTA 6 is a beautiful, staggeringly detailed, enrapturing sequel that pushes current-gen consoles to their absolute limit.

I could go on and on about Grand Theft Auto VI and not run out of things to say. Not because of the scale of the game. Despite being a lengthy title packed with activities, I came out feeling like GTA VI is a focused, lean, and sharp experience. Each act feels almost like a TV show season with its own stakes and climax, even if it can go on for a bit too long. Rockstar made strides in incorporating all the systems and the open world into the campaign in a satisfying way. But Jason and Lucia are the glue that keeps everything together. It’s their chemistry and complicity that made me want to experience everything, and it’s them that will keep me coming back.

At its core, GTA 6 is a pretty good game. There are large sections where it is an absolutely epic game, and large sections that are boring and too limited. However, after I pushed through the boring parts and it opened up enough to become a proper GTA title, it became worth it. Regardless of whether the game was good, it was always going to be an inescapable cultural moment. Luckily, it’s one largely worth participating in.

Breaking a 13-year hiatus, GTA 6 reclaims its unrivaled standing in the open-world action-adventure genre. Its vastly expanded explorable interiors, unpredictable encounters and events, deeper storytelling centered on Jason and Lucia, meticulously crafted realism, and intricate police pursuit system all make its 99-point critic score feel well-deserved. However, an overly lengthy introductory learning phase, meaningless repetitive actions, and occasional untranslated elements in the Korean localization remain notable shortcomings.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the deepest and most accomplished open-world game Rockstar has ever produced. It takes the familiar foundations of the series. It builds on them with a more detailed environment, stronger systems, and a story that places its characters at the center of the experience. Leonida feels alive, the activities are varied, and the freedom you have during missions makes the experience more rewarding.

Grand Theft Auto VI is an ambitious sequel that knows why players keep coming back to Rockstar's worlds. It gives you a great story to follow, but it also makes the time between missions feel just as important. Whether you're planning a robbery, exploring the countryside, customizing a car, or spending an afternoon fishing, Leonida always gives you something worth doing.
Ken cruises around Leonida and does some crimes.
"You got some balls parking your car around here" reads a text message I received in-game, while visiting the small town of Ambrosia in Leonidas,'...

Grand Theft Auto VI should be seen as Rockstar’s finest ever work. Take into account just how good Red Dead Redemption 2 was, and how previous Grand Theft Auto games redefined the gaming scene, and that’s some going.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not only the biggest release in the history of the industry, but, above all, further proof that Rockstar continues to set standards that the competition can only envy. Despite a few clear shortcomings, we have been given a phenomenal story, brilliantly crafted characters, and the most believable, vibrant open world I have ever seen in a game.
A masterpiece that masterfully blends drama and entertainment with nuance, while also making you wonder, "What is left for Rockstar to achieve that they haven't already?"

Grand Theft Auto VI isn't just another sequel that builds upon its predecessor. It's a game that redefines what an open-world experience can be, pushing the boundaries of what's possible and setting a new benchmark for the genre. Its technical achievements are nothing short of extraordinary, the sheer amount of content can keep you immersed for countless of hours, and the vast, breathtaking world of Leonida is a spectacle in itself. At the heart of it all are Jason and Lucia, two compelling, relatable protagonists whose story makes this incredible journey all the more memorable. Rockstar hasn't simply raised the bar for open-world games. It has set a new standard that the rest of the industry will spend years trying to reach. Grand Theft Auto VI isn't just a game of this generation. It's the game that defines it.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the most ambitious game ever, and it’s not really all that close.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a monumental gaming experience, combining an engaging story, charismatic characters, and unexpected twists with a realistic, richly detailed, and visually stunning world packed with activities. Rockstar's extraordinary world-building brings every corner to life through unique inhabitants, unpredictable encounters, and an outstanding technical polish with no significant flaws. A genuine masterpiece.
GTA 6 is here, and it fully justifies the frenzy it has caused in the gaming and pop culture markets.

A game with the level of technical quality seen in Grand Theft Auto VI does not come along often, given the immense development time, staffing, and budget it requires. It is fair to say that Rockstar Games did not settle for simply replicating the traditional formula in GTA 6; instead, they chose to enhance, refine, and add intricate detail to how players interact with the new open world of Leonida and Vice City. Great emphasis has been placed on the writing team to craft a compelling, well-paced story—one that draws you in so effectively that, before you know it, you find yourself in the midst of some of the most cinematic heists in the entire series. There is plenty to experience right now with Lucia and Jason, long before we even need to think about the future—or the inevitable online mode.
When I sat down to play Grand Theft Auto VI, I knew I was in for a great game. What I didn’t know was that I was about to experience one of the greatest games of all time.

Grand Theft Auto VI is an extraordinary achievement from Rockstar Games. With a world that feels more alive than anything I’ve experienced before, a gripping story carried by Jason and Lucia, and an incredible level of detail across its gameplay and technology, GTA VI sets a new benchmark for open-world games.  After countless hours, I’m still impressed by how naturally its systems, characters and world come together. This isn’t a game that relies on hype or nostalgia to make an impression. It’s a genuinely exceptional experience that far surpassed my expectations.

Grand Theft Auto VI represents the culmination of decades of expertise, delivering a masterclass in storytelling, world-building, and player freedom that sets a new gold standard for open-world experiences.

Rockstar Games has created a world that feels richer, more dynamic, and more rewarding to explore than anything the studio has produced before. Every system, from police pursuits to exploration and progression, contributes to a larger vision that rarely loses sight of the player experience. The few shortcomings that do exist, including occasional pacing issues and some predictable story developments, do little to diminish the overall accomplishment. Grand Theft Auto VI is a game of extraordinary ambition, but more importantly, it is one that consistently delivers.

This review can only hint at what has made GTAVI so wonderful to play over the last few weeks, but if there’s simple take away, let it be this; GTAVI is a masterclass in what can be achieved in gaming technically with all of the time and money, sure, but it’s also a masterclass in redefining a well-worn genre into something that feels genuinely fresh. The updates to the gameplay mechanics, the Wanted system, and bringing a still outlandish crime story down to earth with incredibly realistic and relatable characters all meld into what is simply the best game of the year, and something that will be the new standard bearer for what gaming can be.

"Grand Theft Auto VI not only lives up to the hype; it far surpasses it. It routinely delivers with excellent writing, incredible performances, vast amounts of content, and top-tier gameplay in every facet.
Rockstar has done it again, cementing themselves as masters of their craft, creating a world that players will want to live in for years to come. It’s one of the best video games ever made, and certainly my favorite. As such, it's unlikely to be surpassed for a very long time - until Rockstar Games do it all over again."
Grand Theft Auto VI is a genre-defining crime epic with one of the most mindblowing open worlds in a game to date. Rockstar Games has achieved a nearly impossible feat: it lives up to the hype.

Grand Theft Auto VI is nothing less than a masterpiece. The attention to detail is immaculate, and the world genuinely feels alive with lots of random encounters playing out all the time. The emotional journey that Jason and Lucia take you through will leave you in awe up until the very end.

With an overhaul to just about everything GTAV offered, GTAVI evolves the formula in ways that I didn’t know were needed. The design choice for tougher police initially concerned me, though the new challenge of evading relentless law enforcement made me feel smarter every time I got away. Robberies are tougher and make you think on your feet, with carjacking always a risk-reward gamble. VI is still the GTA sandbox I fell in love with in 2001, but Rockstar made me work and think harder this time; the payoffs and satisfaction are peerless in the genre.

GTA VI makes the 13-year wait feel worthwhile with inventive fun, two leads worth caring about and a world that keeps finding ways to surprise. The story loses urgency at times, and awkward aiming still gets in the way, but it's minuscule compared to the majesty at work.

the-legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)

reviews.excerpt: Call us crazy, but when the final version of Zelda 64 arrived in the IGN64 offices, we stopped working, locked ourselves into a room with a big-screen TV and a surround system and played 17 hours straight. After only a few hours of sleep, we were back for more and we couldn't stop until we finished the game. Then, we started over again to find all the secrets.
10 / 10 / 10 / 10 - platinum [first ever perfect score]
The biggest, most heartpounding and awe-inspiring quest of all. Oh yes, Zelda 64 does indeed own your soul.
Nothing but pure 100% fun, challenging, and lengthy.
A game that can't be called anything other than flawless...This is the masterpiece that people will still be talking about ten years down the road.

[Review Score = 110]  What's significant about this convergence of audio, graphics and gameplay is that you are COMPLETELY IMMERSED in Zelda's world. Why? Because everything is meticulously thought out. Each character and event plays a role in a storyline that sprawls like a J.R. Tolkien masterpiece...It's certainly the game of the decade.
An epic adventure that is among the best N64 games. [Jan 2004, p.189]
Perfect. Epic. Unstoppable. Unbeatable. Irresistible. Sensational...The best videogame I have ever played. It is the crowning jewel of the industry. It is Nintendo's finest achievement.
This is, without a doubt, one of the all-time greatest games made. 50 years from now people will still be playing and enjoying this game... thoroughly.

High praise goes to them for also managing to fit joy, creativity and discovery into the game and doing so without the use of Full-Motion Video (FMV) and the CD soundtrack his critics said was needed. This game is simply the most complete experience of any game ever made making Ocarina Of Time the game I've always dreamed of playing.
This Zelda adventure will undoubtedly withstand the test of time and take its place as one of the best games to ever grace a home system.
