With an amazing focus on adventure and exploration, Breath of the Wild is a fantastic journey, despite some noticeable hiccups.

In Zeiten von 08/15-Open-Worlds, symbol-überladenen Minikarten und Collectible-Wahnsinn setzt Breath of the Wild einen markanten Kontrapunkt und trifft mit seinem Gefühl von Freiheit und Entdeckerdrang einen ganz besonderen Nerv: Dieses Zelda ist ein episches und märchenhaftes Abenteuer, über das in Jahren noch gesprochen werden wird.

While the abundance of content overwhelms and impresses me, with a lot of it being really well polished I find it almost impossible to dislike this game. But that doesn't mean to say it's a perfect game, it has a lot of glaring flaws such as poor combat and lots of frustrating moments that break the immersion. All in all I highly recommend this game, as even with all the cons I found, I still found myself really enjoying almost every second of it and wanting to keep going. It's an astounding game but it doesn't give me the feeling that it's a Zelda game. It holds up really well, but after about 30 hours in the cracks do begin to show, but the game manages to keep holding itself together, something a lot of games fail to do.
All in all it's a great game and I'm loving it, it was worth the £60 price tag. It's not the best Zelda game (I'd give that to Wind Waker) nor is it my favourite (Link's Awakening) but it took an ambitious leap and did a great job of it for the most part.

The very first feeling I got from Breath of the Wild was this in a nutshell. Wow! Starting off with \\\"Hey Link, glad you're alive, now GO!\\\" pretty much made it the greatest intro that I could of asked for from someone who absolutely hates tutorials. Sure they give you little hints here and there, a few popups indicating which buttons do what, how to attack and block, but this game gives you nothing to work off of, and it's amazing.

Breath of the Wild might be the best addition to the Zelda franchise. With game changing additions to the gameplay, open world exploration, challenging puzzles and enemies, and stunning graphics and art, Breath of the Wild will capture your attention and give you the Zelda experience you have always dreamed of.

Even though I can take a sizeable time to complain about Breath of the Wild (and that’s not even talking about performance issues), the game is still a very good one. I would comfortably say that after an extensive period of playing Breath of the Wild, I do believe that it is one of the best Legend of Zelda games that has ever been made.

We got used to The Legend of Zelda as it was and as it has been for thirty years. The previous entries in the franchise can still stand the test of time as some of the greatest games ever conceived. But there hadn’t been a true evolution for the series since Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. Breath of the Wild is that next step in the evolution and blew open the design of what it means to be a Zelda game, and it feels extremely satisfying. I pray that we aren’t in for another six years before the next game, but even if we are, there’s a ton of content here to hold fans over for a long, long time. Hands down, this is one of the best games ever made. Bravo Nintendo, bravo.

The best Nintendo game of all time. It's beautiful, charming, mystifying and intense. Motion controls take some getting used to, but in time only enhance the gameplay. There's occasional lag in TV mode so it's recommended to play in Handheld mode for best performance.

While The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild might not change games as we know it, that it echoes so much of the “I can do that” philosophy found in Nintendo cousins Super Mario Bros./Super Mario 64 in a modern age is nothing less than Nintendo magic at work. The Legend of Zelda is back.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is without question one of the greatest games of all time, we’ll learn in years to come whether it will be heralded as the greatest, but at the very least, it will change the way games are developed in the future. It is without question the greatest game of the past few years, and possibly Nintendo’s finest of all time.
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is definitely a bold advancement for the series taking a darker tone while giving players a world of pure choice.

Play The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and you’ll understand just what the veterans and historians were talking about all those years ago – that Nintendo makes some of the most beautiful and inspiring games that money can buy.

The Legend of Zelda Breath of The Wild is an excellent game and it's the best launch game to date. Everyone who has a Nintendo Switch should buy this game. It’s one of the best Zelda games to release.

Despite a weak performance on the TV and some unimaginative Riddles, The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild presents itself as probably the best launch title of the current console generation.  The enormous open world leaves little to be desired and the main quests will surely entertain you over 10-15 hours.

this addition to the Legend of Zelda series has changed a lot in comparison to the past titles of the series and has evolved Open World genre in general. vast open world and the freedom to do whatever you want will create a memorable experience for you. after playing Zelda you will understand that the past "Open World" games that you've played are just like a joke!
"A whole new world."
This video game is really a piece of art. It very well may become a part of videogame history. Surely that’s something we can all enjoy.
The courses themselves are also graphical masterpieces. The size of the skating environments in THPS3 dwarfs the levels that were found in THPS2 and each level comes to life with rich detail.

Take the same awesome game play from the first two incarnations, pump up the frame rate to a blistering 60 frames per second, add larger more addictive levels that are full of life and imagination, and enhance the graphics.
This is THPS at its best. More fun? Can’t have it.

The introduction of the revert is a handy addition to you stunt arsenal, but it doesn't have the same game-changing effect that the manual had in number two. Which is good, as it adds an extra touch but doesn't meddle with a beautifully balanced control system.
A rare and beautiful thing, a nearly perfect game.

When it's all said and done, when your eyes have completely dried up after spending 7 straight hours obsessing over massive rail grinds, THPS 3 comes through on its promise to do next-gen justice to the series. There simply is no better skating game available, and for that matter, very few other games that compete, period.
The replayability is off the charts. [Dec 2001, p.168]
This game will not be completed in a weekend – this is one of those rare games that will take a lifetime to play. Not a biggie – you won’t soon be bored with it.
Freaking amazing!

You can combo off of everything in this game. Seriously I mean everything! Cars, people, sidewalks, buildings, rails, ramps, stop signs... The list goes on and on. The funny thing about all this is Neversoft's Highest Score screen shows a high score of 9.4 million. Yes, my jaw dropped too.
Strikes a perfect balance between new and old and renders the two previous entries in the series almost completely obsolete in the process.
Neversoft’s conspicuously elite design ability has created some of the most challenging, yet most rewarding levels ever conceived in a skateboarding game. [Dec 2001, p.94]
Not only are the graphics significantly improved, they whisk by at a steady pace and feature larger levels with even more interactive environments.
One of the best console games I have played this year. It is that good. The online gameplay is fast with no lag or hiccups.
I simply know that as a total package there is no game on the planet that can captivate me more than THPS3 and for many hours on end no less.
Fast, smooth, detailed, and colorful...THPS3 simply makes the previous games of the series look like battered stepchildren.
The most rewarding, playable, and addictive game on the Playstation 2. Just wait until you see who the hidden characters are! Skateboarding stalwarts rejoice! [Dec 2001, p.86]

Should go down in history as one of the best twitch-fests on PS2. Yes, TH3 is that good. The perfect skating game remains just a tiny hair's breadth out of reach, but if you are not satisfied with your purchase of this game, head examinations are recommended.

The visuals are dazzling. Normally, you'd probably be frustrated after losing the 58,976 points you just racked up because you landed sideways. But in THPS3, you'll find yourself screaming, "Sweet!!" after marveling at how cool the pane of glass looked as you shattered it with your airborne body because you didn't land that kick flip.
Doesn't only look better; it also offers more realistic and fluid game play, along with a currently unequaled multiplayer mode that will keep gamers coming back for more.
Third grind is the charm.
At least as good as advertised, if not slightly better.
Once you get used to it, however, tricks will come second nature, and you'll enjoy the view of the humongous levels, which explode in dazzling colors and glorified details.
It's blatantly obvious that the guys at Neversoft know exactly what they're doing.
Like so many classics, the fun in Tony Hawk's 3 comes from being given a liberating amount of freedom.
Neversoft must have made a deal with the devil, because this series refuses to cool down. [Dec 2001, p.246]
Tony Hawk himself really likes the game and loves getting online with his PS2. You could end up playing against the "man" himself if you're the lucky type.
If you loved Tony Hawk Pro Skater 1 or 2 on any other system, and you are a PS2 owner, this is a must have.
Everything to love from the first two Tony Hawk games is back, along with more outrageous levels and more outrageous combos thanks to the revert trick.
There's only one major new technique, which might be disappointing to some fans of the series.
What's so great about the game, apart from it looking and sounding so good on PS2, is the course design that you get to sample.
It’s simple if you loved the first two titles you need this one, newcomers may be put off as the game is beginning to get more complex.

Isn’t as well implemented as I’d have liked. Enjoyable, for certain, but lacking that unidentifiable combination of speed and ease of movement that makes games like this great, I can’t say that Tony Hawk was a truly excellent title.

While fans of the last installment may at first be disappointed in the apparent lack of notable new features and improvements, there are plenty of additions to be enjoyed after mastering the new options and levels.
It's a stunning achievement by any measure and stands as one of those rare products that delivers more than you paid for.
So damn close to perfect that it makes me want to cry tears of joy.
Simply the best game I have ever had the pleasure of playing.
Magnificent. Until now, GoldenEye was arguably the best reason for gamers over the age of 16 to own a Nintendo 64. No longer.
Beyond the visual feast and a plethora of features and options, Perfect Dark is a soup of gameplay genius beefy enough to eat with a fork!

No longer are those shooting at you simple targets in a practice range. These guys are smart, evil and ready to battle. Enemies will work together to cover each other, they’ll roll under your gunfire, hide behind corners and even shoot the gun right out of your hands.
Oh yea, oh yea, glory hallelujah -- this is the game we've waited so long for.
It's still by far the finest crafted game of its ilk on the N64 and it positively oozes class from every pore.
Joanna looks good and she knows it, with spectacular Ram-pak enhanced graphics.

With all the gadgets and alternative goals thrown in, "Perfect Dark" is more than just a straight-up blastfest; It's a futuristic spy-thriller that also happens to be the best multiplayer shooter on the console market.
Cool options such as friend/foe identification and threat readings, plus the best graphics ever on an N64 game.
Though it is not without its flaws, "Perfect Dark" is the best game yet for the N64 and among the most fun console games ever produced.
The framerate trouble brought the graphics down to 9.9, and even framerate problems you won't even notice most of the time because this game is so much fun.
The number of things that you can unlock in the game is simply staggering.

Rare's intelligent 3D shooter features amazing graphics, loads of in-game options, a cooperative mode, a counter-operative mode, extensive bot setups, and a the most well-rounded multiplayer mode ever to grace Nintendo 64.
If "GoldenEye" is a bull's-eye, Perfect Dark hits somewhere in the lungs. [Jan 2004, p.189]
With stellar solo and multiplayer action, there are more things to try here than in a stroll through Amsterdam.
Absolutely brilliant.

From superior graphics, which really showcase the capacity of the N64 Expansion Pak, to Dolby Surround Sound, to seemingly unlimited playability potential, "Perfect Dark" is the game of choice for N64 owners.

There are as many different reasons for the gamer to go to bed thinking of simulants, or any of the friends that have been hiding behind walls and popping a cap in your ass with the farsight, as there are peanuts in the box.
Perfect in every way. Except for the manual, which I've burnt along with every other first person shooter in the office games cupboard: there's no point in keeping either now.
It’s multiplayer is, by far, the best on Nintendo 64. The Single Player is epic and addicting.
Its scope and complexity is lightyears ahead of the competition and it sets a benchmark that many, possibly even Rare itself, will struggle to reach in the years to come.
With Joanna Dark, "Perfect Dark's" heroine, Rare succeeds over Bond, the spy at the top of his game, by matching him with somebody who would likely prefer him on the bottom.
So there's no doubt in anyone's mind... there is not now, nor will there ever be a nude code for Joanna Dark. Go get a girlfriend!
There are some nasty frame rate problems at times, which is mostly the factor that keep this from an A grade, but don't let that stop you from picking up Rare's latest.
This is the best action game on the Nintendo 64 and a great follow-up to "GoldenEye."

The new cast of characters created for Perfect Dark is grossly inadequate when compared to the ones from GoldenEye. The lead player-controlled protagonist, Joanna Dark, exhibits few emotions beyond being clueless and bland.

Yes, Rare should have made the gameplay a little more original, pumped up the enemy AI, and definitely fixed the save system. But they gave the people what they wanted, and in that respect they've done a terrific job. There's so much to explore, kill, blow up and maim in this game that it offers hours and hours of bullet-riddled excitement.

Better than "GoldenEye 007" in every aspect, making it the best first-person shooter at the time of its release. With much deeper Solo Missions and a completely customizable Combat Simulator, Perfect Dark definitely was worth the wait.

the-legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time-2026.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026)

reviews.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is, and always was, one of the best pieces in video game history. Period.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a monumental game. It's revered far and wide for its tale of loss, hope, and the future of a kingdom so beloved by our world. As for remakes, I'm happy to say that this one checks a lot of boxes with its updated mechanics, score, and gameplay. Few games have such a reputation, yet even three decades later, people still talk about it.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was one of the best games in history, and now it is once again.

An iconic all-time story has been reborn for a new generation, and it's the best iteration of the classic Nintendo 64 favorite we've gotten yet. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a must-play, whether you're a franchise fan or not, and one of the best examples of how to properly reimagine an enduring masterpiece.
Whether you're a returning player or a newcomer, Ocarina of Time remake is the definitive way to play Link’s legendary adventure.

This remake of the iconic 1998 game brings an ageless masterpiece back into the spotlight. Its beautiful visuals, narrative tone and gameplay improvements elevate a title whose level design and puzzles remain as magnificent as ever, 28 years later.

Hour by hour, dungeon by dungeon, I fell more and more in love with this game, perhaps in part because it comes from another era. You can feel how this remake never needs to prove anything or chase trends. It simply wants to be the best version of itself. With its visuals, audio, game design, scope, complexity, and gamefeel - oh my god, the gamefeel! - all absolutely spot on, the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake is something I truly never expected: a perfect game.

Nintendo proves that it is possible to faithfully remake one of the greatest games ever made while adding the right technical improvements to make it feel right at home today. The love and attention to detail shine through as you rediscover Hyrule accompanied by an incredible soundtrack. However, its faithfulness to the original also means that the adventure rarely manages to surprise.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remake for the ages, blending the charm and whimsy of the original with more digestible gameplay and stunning visuals. It's as timeless as it ever was, managing to recreate one of the most beautiful games to date without compromising the magic of its 1998 predecessor – only adding to it. Between newly voiced dialogue, revamped dungeons, fresh puzzles, and more, Hyrule has never felt so alive.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is an undisputed masterpiece, with the Nintendo Switch 2 remake being the sleeker, sexier new version with a few extra tricks up its sleeve. While I’d have still liked the remake to explore some of that cut content from the Nintendo 64 era, I’m more than satisfied with this upgraded port.

Nintendo has respectfully restored Ocarina of Time, only stepping in where the ravages of time had left their mark. The result is an adventure that lives up to its legendary status and still ranks among the very best.

Having spent at least 20 hours of my life playing it, the Ocarina of Time remake achieves the impossible: it improves upon something that was already perfect. Whether it’s the cutscenes, battles, localization, simple yet heroic story, details, or graphics, this version is the most complete and beautiful iteration of the game, and if I had to choose just one—between this one, the original, and the 3DS version—I’d definitely pick the remake.

This return to the series’ roots is exactly what I feel the franchise needed: an adventure with a meticulously crafted structure, yet one that is incredibly charming and delivers on every level. The whole experience shines brighter than ever thanks to stunning visuals and sound design, alongside some much-needed quality-of-life improvements.

The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the legendary classic touched up to live up to its reputation, making it impossible to put down. It's lucky to be working with such quality material, but Nintendo had the unenviable task of making a near-perfect game even better—and they pulled it off. Not all of its changes are incredible in isolation, but together, they bring a masterpiece up to speed with modern sensibilities. It sounds too good to be true, but a lot of people are going to wake up on 5th November to find that Christmas has come early this year and that the childlike spark in their eyes went nowhere—it was just waiting to see Hyrule once again.
Despite it being almost 30 years on from the original release, this is still one of the greatest games ever made, and the degree to which its core design still holds up is remarkable.

Nintendo hasn’t remade Ocarina of Time on Switch 2: it has restored it like a work of art. It has fixed only what needed fixing, removed all the friction of the original without touching its structure or its essence, and brought it up to Switch 2 standards with animated-film visuals, an orchestral soundtrack and full voice acting. The updated controls make it more accessible than the original, but it’s by no means an easy game. It’s the definitive version of the greatest game of all time, and one of the best games on Switch 2, if not the very best.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) doesn't attempt to drastically change one of the best games ever made. It makes well-timed and safe additions, while trying to maintain at all costs the beauty, the pain, the farewells, and the courage that only the saga of a true Hero of Time could convey.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, is a near-perfect remaking of one of the greatest games of all time. While it's enhanced in ways both big and small, the foundations of Ocarina remain largely untouched, cementing that its excellence is deeply rooted in timeless design and effortless storytelling. Regardless of whether or not you've undertaken the Hero of Time's journey, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time simply can't be missed.

This version meshes best with modern tastes and looks great on today’s hardware. The core classic has aged sublimely, and where it hasn’t it has been gingerly given a respectful facelift. The magic has been preserved for a new generation. It is an effortless recommendation: a wonderful experience, a captivating history lesson, and just all-around brilliant.

A rich, breathtaking world brimming with secrets, alongside an extensive inventory of tools and items that you gradually discover and use to explore, overcome obstacles, and solve puzzles. All of this comes together to create a captivating adventure that embodies what an adventure should be.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and its soaring story return at a time in the world where we need its message – of hope, and the power of the little guy. It was intentionally developed as a game to empower kids, to help them see their power and the impact of their voice. That message is what shines brightest on replay.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a game that laid down many foundations in the video game industry with the release of the Original back in the late 90s and now, almost 30 years later, it makes a powerful return with vast improvements in every aspect. It is indeed an experience gamers would not want to miss. Its gameplay elements remain incredibly unique to this day and this is a golden opportunity for a whole new generation of gamers to engage in an all-time classic experience.
Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake is a remarkable restoration of one of gaming’s most beloved adventures. Rather than reinventing a masterpiece, Nintendo has carefully refined what made it special, creating the definitive way for a new generation to discover it and returning players to fall in love all over again.

Nintendo’s approach to this remake is notably safe and restrained—featuring few changes—yet it succeeds brilliantly in crafting the best version of this classic we have ever seen. I am certain that for those playing it for the first time, it will be an incredible journey, while for those who have played it dozens of times, it will be a truly nostalgic adventure.

As Zelda sits at its 40th anniversary, Ocarina of Time still represents a high point for the series and Nintendo games as a whole, and this remake only further validates as much. The changes Nintendo has made with this new version of the game don’t impede the original in any way, and instead simply amplify the excellent story and gameplay experience in virtually every way. The result is a remake that immediately becomes the defining way to play Ocarina of Time and helps make Link’s legendary adventure all the more timeless.
Essential, magical, wonderful: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a stone cold classic, and something nobody should miss out on.

When teams take on a remake, the task is never easy. They must not only capture the essence of the original game but also introduce enough new elements to prevent it from feeling like a pointless rehash that adds nothing new. In this 2026 version of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, the meticulous craftsmanship of the Nintendo teams shines through from start to finish. We dive back into the iconic quest—which pits Link against Ganondorf to save the Princess and the kingdom of Hyrule—with the same delight as ever. At the same time, we’re pleasantly surprised by the subtle new touches that appear exactly where they’re needed to remind us that, no, we’re no longer in 1998—as much as by the beauty of this world, brought to life on the Nintendo Switch 2. A must-play that really hasn’t aged a bit.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a breathtaking Switch 2 overhaul that elevates a timeless classic into an essential modern masterpiece. With gorgeous visuals, modernized controls, a majestic orchestrated score, and clever QoL additions, it's the definitive way to experience one of gaming's greatest achievements.

If it’s not broken, don’t fix it. Instead, tighten screws. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 2026 sets a new standard for what remakes can be, putting it in line with the best of what studios such as Capcom have accomplished with their own remakes in recent years—changes that improve and capitalize on what’s on offer, rather than disrupting what made the original so revered and revolutionary. As much as I love the original Ocarina of Time and its 3DS remaster, I played them this summer for the last time. This is the definitive edition, a game that fans will be talking about in reverent tones for generations to come.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time returns with an outstanding remake that successfully preserves the magic of the original while modernizing its gameplay. Stunning visuals, improved controls, a freely adjustable camera, and thoughtful quality-of-life improvements make exploring Hyrule more enjoyable than ever. The timeless dungeon design, memorable characters, and beautifully rearranged soundtrack remain highlights. Despite minor technical and audio issues, Nintendo delivers a remarkable remake that proves why Ocarina of Time is still considered one of the greatest video games of all time.

I cannot make any pretence of objectivity about Ocarina of Time. It was one of the most important games of my childhood and indeed my life; a game that showed me the possibilities of the form when the rules of video games were still being written, and cemented my love of games. I cannot play it without the influence of nostalgia, and like Link, I often felt returned to my child self as I played. But even without that powerful attachment, I think anyone would be moved by this game. Nintendo’s modern Zelda team have turned one of the best games of the 1990s into one of the best games of the 2020s, and made time-travellers out of us all.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was a masterpiece in 1998 and twenty-seven years later, it still is. With thoughtful quality-of-life changes and some excellent design rework, it is easily the best entry point into the long-running series.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a lavish remake of the original action-RPG for the Switch 2 with gorgeous visuals and some quality-of-life adjustments. It feels like a lovely update, along with some embellishments to add additional life and opportunities to some areas from the original. I would call it another tribute to perhaps one of the best and most influential entries in the series.

A beautiful, engrossing fantasy adventure that maintains its thrilling combat encounters, clever puzzles, and unique charm. This is the definitive way to experience Ocarina of Time, and know that I envy you if this will be your first time ever playing it. Enjoy it. Few games have ever reached, or will ever reach, the heights it has. Fittingly, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time transcends time and maintains its seat as one of the best video games in the world.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake doesn’t merely preserve a classic. It provides the best possible way to experience one of the most influential games ever made. It smooths rough edges without compromising identity, modernises presentation without losing charm, and reintroduces Hyrule to a new generation without forgetting the fans who have cherished it for decades. This is a masterclass in how to remake a classic. Its stunning visual overhaul, beautifully reorchestrated soundtrack, refined gameplay systems, and enduring dungeon design combine to create a version worthy of its legendary reputation. It’s a powerful reminder that some legends truly are timeless.

Nintendo is bringing back one of its most legendary titles, knowing exactly how to make the most of its source material while making only the meaningful changes. It’s an unforgettable experience for both those who remember it fondly and those experiencing it for the first time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the all-time classics of video games, returning in a new version that strikes a delicate balance between respect for the acclaimed original and technological updates. It is a simple experience by today’s standards, but its thrilling action and adventure are precisely the kind of escapism that this industry really needs right now.

Rather than a cheap cash-in to take advantage of The Legend Of Zelda’s milestone birthday, this remake of Ocarina Of Time feels loving and retains the spirit that made the original so adored. Sure, it’s millennial nostalgia-bait, but the pretty graphics, expanded world and polished soundtrack will help a new generation to see why so many consider this the greatest video game of all time.

I had a lot of questions when they announced this remake, and even a little fear that something so important to me could be changed, or even ruined. Having my time again in Hyrule, though, I can safely say that Nintendo has done something very special here. They haven't tried to reinvent the game, nor have they just given it a fresh coat of paint. They've taken a game that was already special and given the world and the characters in it the detail that our imaginations were filling in all those years ago. Some things really do stand the test of time, and Ocarina of Time is one of them.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is fantastic, and a legendary entry into one of gaming's most iconic franchises. Smashing pots never looked so good, and reliving such a classic tale with new graphics, music, and voice acting is truly stunning.

Far more than a simple graphical facelift, this Switch 2 remake is a deeply respectful reimagining that modernizes a masterpiece. By bringing the 1998 concept art to life and introducing massive quality-of-life improvements—including free jumping and a mercifully quiet Navi—it delivers the definitive way to experience Hyrule. The newfound fluidity slightly diminishes the tension of classic combat and stealth sequences, but the sheer magic of this legendary adventure remains undeniable.

Nintendo has done right by its greatest contribution to global art and culture. I doubt that the Ocarina of Time Remake is going to replace its forebear at the top of the Metacritic rankings, for the simple reason that the entire games industry is in a different place now. But Nintendo has effectively turned its 28-year-old classic into something that will feel modern to a new player, thus ensuring that the game will continue to remain relevant within the general discourse for another few generations yet. And now, between Final Fantasy VII and Ocarina of Time, we have some fascinating and deeply contrasting case studies for how publishers can “remake” their most valuable properties in a way that adds, rather than detracts, from the base provided by the original.

The Ocarina of Time remake is a tremendous game, and I hope that in the years to come, everyone for whom this is their first taste of Ocarina will look back on it with the same fondness and awe that its processor inspires in me.

Bathed in rays of golden sunlight and brimming with life, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time gorgeously reimagines the original game while retaining all that made it so beloved. There’s so much more to it than its beautiful audio-visual overhaul, though: from shrewdly redesigned locations and enemies to new features that add depth to the world of Hyrule. It’s a thoroughly well-thought-out retelling of one of the most loved video games of all time.

While this version of Ocarina of Time looks a million miles away from the blocky original - it maintains the same playability, feel and character that made people fall so deeply in love with the game. A must-buy.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is arguably one of the most legendary titles in gaming history, having been highly influential and revolutionary upon its original release. This excellent remake completely modernises the visuals while introducing numerous quality-of-life improvements, offering the perfect opportunity for older gamers to relive the masterpiece that is Ocarina of Time and for newer generations to experience first-hand how a game that is almost 30 years old can still resonate with players today.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake proves that some designs are truly timeless. Despite a simple plot, straightforward puzzles, and a few archaic elements, the superb music, phenomenal sense of adventure, masterfully modernized gameplay, and stunning visuals ensure that it remains one of the greatest titles in the history of gaming. While the remake does not revolutionize the original, it serves as a reminder of why Ocarina of Time became a legend in the industry.

This should be the gold standard for any remake of any franchise going forward. It not only elevates the original 1998 release, which became one of the most successful games in Nintendo’s history, but takes it to an entirely new level. This new edition goes beyond simply updating a visual presentation that was long overdue for an overhaul: it also introduces significant quality-of-life improvements and localization for virtually every region in the world. All of this makes it, without a doubt, one of the greatest games in the history of the industry.

With an improved control scheme, voiced cutscenes and breathtaking visuals, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time takes the 1998 original to the next level. This is an astounding artistic achievement that will bring immeasurable joy to both newcomers and longtime fans.

Nintendo has completely knocked it out of the park, reminding us why Zelda belongs in the pantheon of the greatest franchises in gaming, and it serves even more to bring new faces and fans to Hyrule. Whether you’re an old fan looking to rekindle your love or a new fan looking to see what all the hype is about, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) is the perfect place to be. This leaves us with one final question: will we see Majora’s Mask?

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake's impeccable core design gives every discovery purpose, exceptional pacing keeps the adventure moving, and detailed graphics and excellent performance make Hyrule a pleasure to inhabit.

Ocarina of Time is a stunning remake, but beneath its enchanting visuals and smoother controls enabled by modern technology, its core remains faithfully intact, reminding us why it still deserves to be regarded as one of the greatest games of all time.

Nintendo players, old and new alike, you no longer have any excuse not to discover this landmark in the history of video games. Long-time fans may regret the lack of a few (genuine) new features, but they’ll rediscover the wonder of yesteryear in 2026.

For those who have never played the original, this is the most accessible version yet of the all-time classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Series fans who primarily enjoy the challenge of overcoming dungeons and puzzles may find it an appealing but somewhat overly conservative remake. However, for players who want to fully immerse themselves in the game world and the everyday lives of its inhabitants, this is a remake that is impossible not to fall in love with. So much so that you may never want to leave Hyrule.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time did not need a remake to remain historically important; it needed one to feel relevant again. Nintendo has modernized nearly every aspect that needed attention without changing what made the original so memorable. The visuals are spectacular, the controls feel natural on modern hardware, the voice acting works remarkably well, and the improvements to dialogue, navigation and sound make Hyrule easier to appreciate than ever...I think this is the best possible version of one of Nintendo’s greatest games, and after playing it again like this, I finally understand why Ocarina of Time has remained so highly regarded for all these years.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has proven, once again, to be a stone-cold classic that makes buying the console it was released on worth it. This is the best version of Ocarina of Time, as the beautiful graphics, sly gameplay additions, and small new pieces of lore build on a timeless foundation to create something that expands on the familiar without losing what made the original special. If you’ve somehow never played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, you can’t miss this new, top-notch remake.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels ripped from the dreams and nightmares of a child, wrapped in whimsy and wonder that draws you in regardless of how old you are.

This Nintendo Switch 2 remake is an absolute masterpiece. Breathtaking art direction, modernized gameplay that stays true to the original, brilliantly designed dungeons, memorable bosses, and beautifully re-orchestrated music…  I rediscovered all the magic of my favorite adventure of all time, with the joy of experiencing it in a whole new light. A timeless masterpiece.

The world we grew up in may no longer exist, but somehow Nintendo has managed to take us back there with an absolute masterpiece. Meticulously crafted to appeal to longtime fans and newcomers alike, Ocarina of Time is a remarkable achievement that understands exactly what made the original so special. The additional story beats and subtle changes enhance the experience without ever deviating from the magic of the original, and somehow, Nintendo has managed to recapture that exact same feeling of stepping out onto Hyrule Field for the first time. That, in itself, is nothing short of perfection.
Nearly three decades later, Ocarina of Time not only stands the test of time but also reminds us why great game design never goes out of style.

Nearly three decades after its original release, the legendary adventure returns with gorgeous new visuals, modernised controls and plenty of thoughtful improvements. Some of its age still shows, but the magic that made it a classic remains remarkably intact.

By retaining its core structure and mechanics, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s remake proves that it is still an enduring masterpiece with some of the best world and dungeon design in the series. Through clever improvements to progression tracking and stunningly reimagined visuals and music, Nintendo has brilliantly reworked one of the greatest games of all time, adding new depth to its whimsical and somber coming of age story.

This is an incredible telling of one of gaming’s best stories. It's an incredible arrangement of some of gaming's best music. It’s one of the most visually impressive games Nintendo has ever made. This is the best way to play one of the best games ever made.
As magical and brilliant today as it was thirty years ago, Ocarina of Time is a spellbinding masterwork that captures the imagination of every generation that is lucky enough to play it.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time looks wonderful on the Nintendo Switch 2. It feels natural to replay a timeless classic with beautiful graphics, symphonic music, and familiar gameplay with some changes and improvements.

Link is the Hero of Time, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the embodiment of Link's courage. A game that does not replace the original but which delivers the most marvellous treatment the original masterpiece could get, Ocarina of Time embraces both veterans and beginners alike with its exquisite work of adaptation that goes from eye-filling gorgeous views to the most subtle orchestral notes, along with the inevitable eavesdropping of fellow Hylians. Whether awakening sages, breaking curses, selling ghosts or just fishing and collecting cuccos, Ocarina of Time is the most worthy game of the Hero of Time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 is not just a successful remake. Nintendo has chosen not to change much, focusing instead on targeted improvements and a sumptuous visual overhaul that further elevates an already masterful and timeless game design. The result is an action RPG that, in 2026, feels more balanced, intelligent, and rewarding than many contemporary AAA titles.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 serves as an excellent example of how a remake should be crafted. Nintendo has succeeded in modernizing a masterpiece without compromising its essence, highlighting a gameplay structure that continues to prove its enduring quality, even nearly thirty years after its debut. This is more than just a nostalgic trip; it is proof that great works can transcend generations, continuing to captivate both those who have known them forever and those discovering them for the very first time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the textbook example of how a remake can elevate an all-time classic. It keeps everything that made the 1998 original legendary while layering in the exact tweaks and quality-of-life updates needed to modernize the experience without losing touch with its roots. The overhauled visuals, updated controls, fully orchestrated soundtrack, and brand-new cutscenes turn this into an essential adventure.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has the courage to introduce countless changes and new features, but it does so with great wisdom , always demonstrating absolute respect for the original game, and that gives it the power to become a pure gold remake; a remake worthy of the best game of all time.

Retaining its nearly 30-year-old structure and direction, this remake stands tall as a modern masterpiece. From marker-free exploration and a poignant seven-year time-travel narrative to Link’s newfound emotional expressiveness, every element clicks effortlessly. Reborn with Switch 2’s top-tier visuals and sound, it remains the definitive bible of the genre—proving what truly makes a game great in an era of oversized worlds.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time emerged as a generation-defining masterpiece, and the remake proves that its greatness transcends time itself. With a finely-tuned balance between reverence for a sacred gaming text and a daring ambition towards improvements, Ocarina of Time has emerged stronger than ever before. The remake now stands as the definitive way to play an all-time classic, and Ocarina of Time still stands as one of the greatest games ever made.

Even today, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels remarkably timeless, thanks to its compact and carefully structured level design, environmental interactions woven together through the melodies of the ocarina, and intricately interconnected dungeon layouts. That said, it is only fair to acknowledge that we have since seen countless excellent successors built upon its foundations, making it much harder for the game to deliver the same groundbreaking impact to modern players that it once did.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is wonderful. Even after nearly twenty-eight years, it still manages to surprise me, move me, and make me fall in love with an adventure that radiates joy and happiness from start to finish. This new version is a feast for the eyes, boasting top-tier artistic and visual design, complemented by gameplay enhancements that make the experience feel more modern and accessible—all without compromising its core identity…Long-time fans might find some changes a bit too simplistic, particularly regarding movement and camera control. Conversely, those encountering the world of Link, Zelda, Ganondorf, and the Triforce for the first time will find an adventure that captivates them from the very first minutes, guiding them through a truly extraordinary Hyrule…I recommend this remake to everyone, regardless of whether they belong to an older or newer generation. For those already familiar with the original, it is a chance to revisit a legend in a new light; for those who have never played it, it is an opportunity to discover one of the most significant chapters in the history of video games.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is, quite simply, the definitive version of the greatest video game of all time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time proves that truly timeless game design can remain just as enjoyable nearly 30 years later. Its enchanting world, memorable characters, clever puzzles and excellent dungeons are brought to life through beautiful visuals and an outstanding soundtrack. Unnecessary loading screens, limited voice acting and the inability to complete side quests after the ending are disappointing omissions, but they do little to diminish what is one of the most joyful gaming experiences of the year.

The praise heaped upon The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time back when it first released was not misplaced. It still stands as one of the best games of all time, the pinnacle of the Zelda franchise, and this gorgeous, technically impeccable, thoughtfully updated version of the game will allow a new generation to fully appreciate Link's greatest adventure. This is the new high-water mark for video game remakes and a note-perfect confirmation that some songs never fade.

The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time demonstrates that one of the most important and influential games of all time can be further improved without altering any of its delicate balance. With its place in industry history already firmly established, Nintendo's primary concern was to modernize a masterpiece that needed to smooth out some rough edges and eliminate the technical limitations it unwittingly carried. Thanks to a cleverly constructed world, precision-designed dungeons, an unforgettable soundtrack, and a story that manages to speak of growth, loss, responsibility, and the passage of time through seemingly simple yet profound language, Ocarina of Time presents itself with renewed strength to modern audiences, who can finally discover why that incredible journey was worth undertaking.
A thrilling remake. A masterpiece that no one should miss and which looks, sounds and plays better than ever.

The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is an essential experience for all Nintendo Switch 2 users. It is an enhanced version of what many consider the greatest video game of all time. It serves as a nostalgia-filled journey for veterans and a magical adventure for new players—a classic in every sense of the word.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a glorious remake that reinvents a classic masterpiece into something worthy of our nostalgia goggles. Freed from the shackles of early 3D adventure jankiness, it's the way Ocarina was meant to be played, and is an encouraging example of what a return to the classic Zelda formula could mean for the franchise.

It's clear that just as much heart was poured into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake as the original with its carefully-crafted modernisations, mind-blowing visual overhaul, astounding orchestral score, and a familiar journey that'll stay with you forever.

Playing this remake reminded me that video games can be much more than the mechanics we praise, the level design we analyze, the technical achievements we celebrate, or framerates that we fear to drop. Sometimes, their greatest power lies in how they make us feel, even decades after we've first experienced them – and Ocarina of Time still has that magic. Now, if you'll excuse me, I still have a few Golden Skulltulas and Heart Pieces to collect. And then? Well, I think I'm ready for another adventure.

Ocarina of Time has always been a timeless game, and this remake proves it by requiring no major changes to remain effective. Nintendo preserved what made the original so special, delivering a more visually appealing version with excellent direction, an even more striking soundtrack, and quality-of-life improvements that address the aspects of the game that hadn't aged well. That said, the game features an excessive number of loading screens, and Link’s face looks incredibly odd when he’s a child—but none of this diminishes the brilliance of the experience.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the platonic ideal of a Zelda game. What it lacks in interesting puzzles it makes up for in a story that’s deeper than you think, deliciously satisfying combat, fantastic music, and a mythical atmosphere that the series has been chasing since 1998. This remake delights in some ways and feels like a step back in others, with a few fantastic changes, some strange controls, and one or two outright bad alterations. It speaks to the quality at the core of the game and this remake that not even those can put a damper on the experience.

It was very clear to everyone that this is a massive game, making a stunning return to the spotlight, but if you still need me to confirm this to you: if you have any affinity for adventure and puzzle games and haven’t played this masterpiece yet, stop everything, buy a Switch 2 (if you somehow don’t own one already), and just play it.

Whether you’re a long-time fan looking to revisit one of gaming’s most iconic adventures or someone experiencing it for the first time, this is an absolutely incredible remake that does justice to the legacy of the original.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake shows that its cleverly designed dungeons and time-travel puzzles can still captivate first-time players. Early backtracking and sluggish horseback controls are minor frustrations, but the beautifully detailed world of Hyrule and its moving story make the adventure memorable even without nostalgia.
The 2026 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a fairly straightforward recreation. But an admittedly very good one.

A spectacular reimagining of one of the greatest video games of all time, which brilliantly modernises its gameplay and proves that, almost 30 years later, Ocarina of Time remains an extraordinary adventure.
Ocarina of Time is a timeless masterpiece that's even more fun to play thanks to the Switch 2 remake.

Ultimately, with this Switch 2 iteration of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo has done exactly what this classic deserved. They have left the diverse gameplay, paired with what is, quite simply, brilliant quest design, essentially untouched, while making subtle refinements to the controls and overall user experience. In terms of atmosphere, the new version benefits from comprehensively overhauled, effectively brand-new visuals; they shine in both style and level of detail, while incorporating a host of modern effects. To top it all off, there is a magnificent soundtrack and high-quality voice acting, which perfectly round out the experience from an audio perspective. This is a game that truly belongs in every Switch 2 collection.
An outstanding remake that appeals to both fans and newcomers alike.

Ocarina of Time is still a wonder of game design and a thrilling adventure. This remake smooths over some rough edges, leaves others intact, and lets what was so special about the original shine through. It can be easy to forget after so many years, but the core structure and design ethos are as strong as they ever were. By approaching this remake with a degree of reverence and respect for the source material, Nintendo has shown that a true masterpiece can stand the test of time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remarkably faithful remake that captures the feel of the original. It’s a game brimming with old-school mechanics and design choices, with all its strengths and a few weaknesses. Finally, it represents the pinnacle of the franchise’s graphical achievements and serves as a true benchmark for the Switch 2’s capabilities. The original Ocarina was a landmark title for the entire gaming industry, but even if you’re not interested in OoT’s influence or the Legend of Zelda series, you should still give it a go. A wonderful adventure awaits you, in a style that is, sadly, becoming increasingly rare.

Nearly thirty years after its original release, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is still a fantastic adventure. The beautifully revamped world, gorgeous music and stronger presentation make Hyrule feel more alive than ever.
A pitch perfect remake of one of the best video games of all time, assuming that you’re behind the idea of a 1:1 recreation that adds and changes nothing of substance.

Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a stellar reimagining of the original, one that completely revamps the experience with stunning visuals, modernised gameplay, and vastly improved audio. Despite some minor blemishes, this is comfortably the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever put out, and it’s unquestionably the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time. That said, it is a very safe remake. Despite lots of minor changes throughout, it’s still essentially the same game you’ve likely already played, and so you might find it offers little challenge if you’re familiar with the N64 original or 3DS remake. This makes the lack of Master Quest — or really any kind of hard mode — particularly glaring, but I’m hopeful it’ll be added in the future.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time needs no introduction, and this Switch 2 remake lovingly reminds us why so many people enjoyed this classic in the first place.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the all-time greatest games, of that there's no doubt, and this remake is a glorious way to re-experience this adventure. Nintendo strikes an excellent balance between keeping much of the original feel and the modern niceties of graphics, controls and design. Sure, it might take a little while to get used to the new look, but we should be used to that with Zelda games by now.

It’s in our nature to pass old stories down, and I think there’s meaning in the ones we choose to revisit. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is both an exceptional remake of an incredible game and a rich adventure that stands on its own. This remake proves there’s still so much value in the traditional Zelda formula: the dense, intimate world of Hyrule is stuffed with charming characters and fascinating secrets. Its intricate dungeons are satisfying to unravel, even if their somewhat streamlined design has slightly dulled the special feeling that comes from solving them. Still, the depth, quality, and attention to detail in every corner match the lofty reputation of this series. Whether you’ve played the original 100 times, once back in 1998, or never at all, I highly recommend this beautiful retelling of a legend.

Nintendo has crafted the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as well as it possibly could: staying fully true to the source material, to avoid confusing or disappointing fans, while at the same time updating it in terms of visuals, technology and gameplay. In the latter area, there are quite a few changes, some essential for modernizing the game, others secondary but still enjoyable and helpful in making the whole experience even more fun and magical. It is no longer the game worthy of claiming the title of “best Zelda ever”, that honor now belongs to the two most recent entries, but it remains an incredible experience suitable for everyone.

Ocarina of Time proves why it has become one of the most important gaming classics. The full-fledged remake not only gives it a beautiful new look, but above all removes a number of period compromises and sensitively adjusts the controls and some puzzles. At the same time, it does not lose the original charm or the clearly guided adventure structure. It is fascinating to watch how the first 3D Zelda learns from its younger followers without trying to be modern at all costs. Some archaic elements and a slower pace remind us of how much time has passed, but otherwise it is an exceptionally well-made journey.

Nearly three decades after its original release, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time still holds a special place in video game history. Its combat system has influenced generations of developers, its dungeons remain outstanding examples of level design, and its narrative continues to stand out for its elegance and emotional depth. This Switch 2 remake delivers a successful visual overhaul, modernised controls that address many of the original's limitations, and several other additions that make an already timeless adventure even more engaging.

Looking back, I think so: modernising Ocarina of Time was an excellent way to crown 40 years of The Legend of Zelda, especially at a time when the series seems keen to open itself up to the world beyond video games. Older players will love playing it and appreciating the care and respect put into the remake, travelling back in time through it. Remember to forgive yourselves for having grown up. Everyone else will get to experience, first-hand, the modern version of a true masterclass in game design and pacing, a seminal work that has influenced different genres throughout video game history.

Overall, this new Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a visual tour-de-force, with a beautiful and intricate game world to explore with updated controls and camera. The character designs are off-putting, but the game is still something to be treasured, and after all these years, I may finally include it in my top five Zelda games.

How do you breathe new life into a legendary game from an equally legendary franchise? Nintendo didn't just give this beloved adventure a fresh coat of paint; they went above and beyond. Everything looks like something straight out of a fairy tale, and the experience feels almost entirely new yet familiar, save for a few minor blemishes.

Not every remake feels properly justified. I don’t know for certain if the Ocarina remake needs to exist, but it’s a pretty excellent game. The visuals are a huge improvement, the controls are nicely upgraded, and the addition of voice acting is a big plus. Also, you can play an actual instrument to use the songs in-game, which is extremely cool. I’m not totally in love with all the new character models. But most of them are awesome. I also wish there wasn’t quite so much waiting around while you fight, but that seems much harder to fix. At least, you couldn’t really do so and still have it feel like Ocarina of Time. If you’re any kind of Zelda fan, this game is a must-buy. Even if you’re not, this is an excellent way to experience a classic for the first time.

Nintendo accepts Ocarina was groundbreaking for its time but needed updating for 2026. Hence the sumptuous visual makeover, smart improvements related to equipment and a smattering of voice-acting in the cut-scenes that add more personality to the characters.

Nintendo has successfully rebuilt one of gaming's most influential classics for a modern audience as a cohesive story. It’s a visual and audio spectacle, stitched together with a nostalgia for the dungeon crawler of old. Cinematics and story beats help expand lore, though some voice work falls flat. A reworked overworld and dungeons are a joy to explore, though Nintendo has missed an opportunity to go further in some areas. The experience is more approachable for a modern audience, though some of the challenge and discovery has been diluted. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a truly excellent adventure for both new and returning heroes to enjoy on Nintendo Switch 2.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is about as good as a remake of perhaps the best game of all-time could've hoped to be. Some sense of discovery and difficulty are a bit lost in the modernization, but it's still an incredibly fun and impressive way to experience Link's greatest adventure.
Nintendo dials up a heavy dose of nostalgia, and teaches a new generation why Ocarina of Time is a mainstay for any discussion of greatest video game of all time.

If you grew up playing Ocarina of Time on Nintendo 64, consider this remake a no-brainer. But even if you're jumping into young Link's adventure for the first time, you'll no doubt appreciate the incredible work that has gone in to making this 1998 classic feel just as relevant and wonderful to play today as any AAA game made in 2026.
Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 is a beautiful adventure that feels retro, while also avoiding feeling dated.

It’s so easy to lose yourself in this fantasy world. Ocarina of Time is truly one of those games that sucks you in, and before you know it, four hours have passed. As far as we’re concerned, it’s clear that even the most nostalgic players will thoroughly enjoy this game. The story feels familiar, yet there are plenty of new elements. The only downside might be that the game leans pretty heavily on Breath of the Wild, so by comparison, it doesn’t feature any major technical breakthroughs. It’s exactly what the fans were hoping for, but nothing more (which, to be clear, is perfectly fine). We already know what we’ll be doing this Christmas break.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time works as a vehicle for preserving one of gaming history’s greatest classics and transports it to the current era by modernising the original game so it can be enjoyed fully by everyone – nostalgia goggles or not. And as a new release, it stands proudly as one of my favourites in 2026, even if some elements are stuck in the past. It’s wonderfully off-beat, charming, gorgeous, musical and, of course, well designed and proof that remakes aren’t just cynical cash grabs, but also a way to breathe new life and relevance into games that truly deserve it.

The Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2 is not the most fully-featured version of the game, but it is still an absolutely incredible recreation of what some would say is Nintendo's magnum opus. If you have already played Ocarina of Time thoroughly before, you may not be quite as blown away by the remake, but if this is your first time experiencing Ocarina of Time, it's easily a 10/10 adventure. No matter which camp you fall in, the Ocarina of Time remake offers enough to make it a must-have for any Switch 2 owner.
Without reimagining anything, Ocarina of Time has reached its definitive version and offers new generations a great way to play one of the most influential video games of all time.

Though I wasn’t there when the original Ocarina of Time released, the long shadow it has cast has made it a part of my life as both a Zelda fan, a fan of video games, and even media in general. While this remake might seem unnecessary to some, I have a hard time seeing it that way. The original was brilliant, yes, but claiming that anything is “timeless” is a failure to acknowledge that technology has made leaps and bounds since 1998. What The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake does so successfully is take the original’s brilliance and modernize the qualities that have aged while outright refusing to compromise on staying true to the original’s vision. It does this so effortlessly and with so little missteps that it’s hard not to recommend, even with the original so readily accessible on Nintendo Switch Online.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 retains the soul of the N64 classic while introducing stunning visuals, detailed animations, and a more vibrant Hyrule. With enhanced music, voiced cinematics, improved combat, and a locked 60fps, this remake delivers a truly magical experience despite a few imperfections.

I’m grateful this version exists. It is still a masterpiece, and its simplicity often makes its best ideas easier to appreciate. While playing, I often thought about how much the medium grew from “Ocarina.” It remains a great tree of ideas. I only wish it allowed itself a little more room to grow.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake breathes new life into a timeless classic with a stunning visual overhaul and more comfortable controls, while preserving the magic of the original adventure. However, its faithfulness also limits its ambition, as the lack of substantial new features and minimal quality-of-life improvements leave the impression that it could have offered much more. It serves as an excellent entry point for newcomers, but remains an overly conservative return for longtime fans who know Hyrule like the back of their hand.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a good remake that successfully brings one of gaming's most influential adventures to a new generation. Its enhanced visuals, refined gameplay, and timeless design make exploring Hyrule as captivating as ever, proving why the original remains a landmark in video game history. However, despite these improvements, the absence of Master Quest and meaningful new content feels like a missed opportunity to expand upon an already extraordinary experience. Ultimately, this remake improves a classic, but could have aspired to become something even greater.

Visually sumptuous, impeccably fluid, and featuring a re-orchestrated soundtrack, Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2 restores the full luster of Link’s seminal epic without compromising its core identity. Looking back from 2026, the game may no longer be the "absolute benchmark that no one could possibly ignore." While its Hyrule Field now feels like little more than a modest crossroads, and its combat reflects a certain naivety typical of its era, these minor structural aging marks pale in comparison to the brilliance of its dungeons and the inclusion of modern quality-of-life features. *Ocarina of Time* fulfills the fundamental promise of a legend: "to keep alive the memory of great heroes and their heroic deeds." It is an essential experience—not just for Zelda fans, but for anyone who owns a Nintendo Switch 2.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was untouchable back in 1998, but 28 years later, it's a different story. Don't get me wrong, the game looks absolutely gorgeous, and its dreamy soundtrack puts many modern productions to shame. The controls are also better, and being able to jump and sprint manually gives you more freedom when playing as Link. But as welcome as these changes are, they come with one major drawback: the game has been dumbed down way too much. And that really hurts two of the things that make Zelda special: exploration and puzzle-solving. You're constantly being told where to go and what to do, to the point where even the Water Temple, once a source of real frustration, feels like a walk in the park. If there's one area that could have used a proper modern touch, it's the combat, which still feels a little stiff and could have been much more fluid and dynamic. It's also a shame there's no new content for longtime fans who've played the original inside out. The series' 40th anniversary was the perfect excuse to add something fresh. As it stands, it feels like a cake without the cherry on top.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake feels designed for new players first and foremost, letting new generations see what made us fall in love with it back in the day, and in that regard, it succeeds with flying colors. While some decisions and directions in this remake may keep me from reaching for it again anytime soon, Ocarina of Time is a classic tale and remains a standout among the pantheon of the Zelda titles, and this remake is a great showing of why, even with its blemishes.

Initially put off by its art direction, this remake of Ocarina of Time eventually wins us over thanks to the contrast between its finely rendered realistic world and the modernized character designs from the original game. It's a gradual but ultimately confident change of heart, undoubtedly helped along by the considerable nostalgia factor of a game that remains thoroughly enjoyable to play today, whether you're a veteran or a newcomer. Rather than going for an extremely faithful remake, Nintendo has chosen to change lots of little things that do nothing to alter the structure or overall pacing of the adventure, but each bring a small added value in their own way. We can nevertheless regret that this modernization also comes with a simplification of the experience that wasn't necessarily needed for a game that wasn't particularly difficult to begin with.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake revitalizes a timeless classic with exceptional controls, satisfying combat, gorgeous visuals, and masterfully designed dungeons. However, questionable modernization choices, underutilized new mechanics, and unnecessary conveniences occasionally undermine the original's sense of discovery. It's a compelling reimagining that newcomers may appreciate more than longtime fans, even if it struggles to establish itself as the definitive version.

Ocarina of Time Remake is a pleasant overhaul of a true classic. At times it tries too hard, redoing things just for the sake of redoing them and going overboard with busy visual details, but the mechanical improvements and smoother gameplay experience really help to offset it. I'm not sure how eagerly I'll return to this version of the game next time I want to play it though, because it just lacks the eerie vibe that made the N64 so memorable for me.

Wondering whether this Ocarina of Time deserves to exist is thus perhaps less interesting than deploying it as a barometer for the state of video games as a whole. The game does exist, and it’s good. It was always good. It’s Ocarina of Time. But it’s another in a long line of worrying indicators that games have not, in fact, grown up.
99.1% of OpenCritic critics recommend this game (118 reviews).
Metacritic user score 9.3/10 (24801 ratings).

Mike BC is here with his thoughts on the recently released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, which brings nostalgia and love for the series to the table as he evaluates Nintendo's lovingly crafted remake.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a wonderful reminder of just how special this adventure was, and still is.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is not just a new remake released to reintroduce a classic game to a new generation of players; rather, it is a revival of one of the greatest legends the gaming industry has ever known. It is an experience that brings together an enchanting story, a diverse world, brilliant level design, a variety of tools and weapons, and bosses with distinctive concepts, alongside an unforgettable soundtrack and a visual and artistic side that re-presents this masterpiece in a way befitting its history. Nintendo has proven that the Nintendo Switch 2 is capable of delivering exceptional experiences, and that returning to the past is not necessarily a step backward, but can be an opportunity to rediscover one of the greatest experiences in gaming history—yet in a better form. Whether you are among the players who experienced the original version on the Nintendo 64, or a newcomer discovering the magic of Hyrule for the first time, this game is an experience worthy of being among the very first titles you play on your new console.

This is the best possible version of a legendary game that has shaped not only the games that came after it, but also the players and developers who first laid their hands on the controller. That we get a polished version of this to introduce a new generation of gamers to the many wonders and creativity Nintendo is capable of is nothing short of magic. This is a generational title, ready to reclaim the throne as one of the finest video games ever.

I felt like a kid again while playing this, and now I’m ready to pass the torch Deku Stick to my own offspring!

“The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” goes beyond simply recreating the original, capturing with today’s eyes the ideas the developers wrestled with and could not express because of the technical limits of the time. In the story, Link moved through time from boy to young adult and back to boy again as his adventure carried on. In the same way, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time takes players who loved the original and, all these years later, sends them back to the days of their youth to set out on an adventure once more.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was always that good then, and it’s still that good now. This new iteration is an interesting case of the visuals doing much of the talking for this version’s merits, and to wonderful effect. It’s a very artistically accomplished game, and from a technical standpoint, potentially Nintendo’s best at this time. When layered on top of Ocarina of Time’s well-aged gameplay, it comes together to form a brilliant experience that stands as one of Zelda’s best. That said, while most of the changes here are for the best, there’s some overcorrections here that stuck out to me as a longtime fan. Even with all of that, a game is more than the sum of its parts, and I believe that this 2026 iteration is just as powerful as the original.
Something about this remake moves me like its predecessor didn't.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a joy to revisit from start to finish thanks to its gorgeous 4K visuals, full orchestral score, and slick modern controls. It may not be a brand-new adventure, but it's the definitive remake fans have always wanted and easily the best way to experience the legendary game that started it all.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a brilliant recreation of one of the greatest video games of all time.
For this 2026 version of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, the masterful work of the Nintendo teams shines through.
The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time demonstrates that one of the most important and influential games of all time can be further improved without altering any of its delicate balance.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, is a near-perfect remaking of one of the greatest games of all time. While it's enhanced in ways both big and small, the foundations of Ocarina remain largely untouched, cementing that its excellence is deeply rooted in timeless design and effortless storytelling. Regardless of whether or not you've undertaken the Hero of Time's journey, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time simply can't be missed.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remarkably faithful remake that captures the feel of the original.
