Finally, it represents the pinnacle of the franchise’s graphical achievements and serves as a true benchmark for the Switch 2’s capabilities. The original Ocarina was a landmark title for the entire gaming industry, but even if you’re not interested in OoT’s influence or the Legend of Zelda series, you should still give it a go. A wonderful adventure awaits you, in a style that is, sadly, becoming increasingly rare.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time proves that truly timeless game design can remain just as enjoyable nearly 30 years later. Its enchanting world, memorable characters, clever puzzles and excellent dungeons are brought to life through beautiful visuals and an outstanding soundtrack. Unnecessary loading screens, limited voice acting and the inability to complete side quests after the ending are disappointing omissions, but they do little to diminish what is one of the most joyful gaming experiences of the year.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a stunning, fairy-tale adventure that, thanks to its refreshed visuals, streamlined gameplay and new features, manages to enchant players all over again. Although the simple combat system and low difficulty level are a reminder of the original’s age, exploring Hyrule and discovering new temples still provide plenty of enjoyment. Nintendo has produced an excellent remake that will delight loyal fans of the series and allow a new generation of players to experience one of the industry’s greatest legends.

Nearly three decades after its original release, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time still holds a special place in video game history. Its combat system has influenced generations of developers, its dungeons remain outstanding examples of level design, and its narrative continues to stand out for its elegance and emotional depth. This Switch 2 remake delivers a successful visual overhaul, modernised controls that address many of the original's limitations, and several other additions that make an already timeless adventure even more engaging.

The Ocarina of Time remake makes exactly the right changes and feels the way we always remembered it, putting it in the same league as Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, a must-play on Switch 2 for veterans and newcomers alike.

Whether you're a veteran who's followed Link's journey since the 8-bit Nintendo era or a newcomer who barely knows the franchise, the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time deserves to be appreciated. Nintendo managed to preserve the charm of the 1998 classic, bringing beautiful graphics, a wonderful orchestral soundtrack, Brazilian Portuguese dubbing, and modernized controls that make exploring Hyrule even more enjoyable.

This remake preserves everything that made Ocarina of Time special and adds new features that enhance the experience without detracting from its identity. For me, it’s one of the best games ever, and this is the best way to play it today, both for those who know it inside out and for those who are about to discover it for the first time. A must-buy for anyone with a Nintendo Switch 2.

The original Ocarina of Time laid the foundations for 3D adventure games and remains one of the greatest video games of all time. The remake on Nintendo Switch 2 offers the best way to experience this legendary title once again. Whether you’re revisiting it after playing the original or exploring Hyrule for the very first time, there’s no doubt you’ll fall in love with it and find plenty to keep you captivated.
Some legends aren’t simply remembered. They’re meant to be experienced again.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) is a perfect remake of a perfect game. It honors everything that made the original 1998 game a classic while updating every aspect of the experience for the modern player. It looks great, sounds even better, and plays like butter. 

The addition of voice acting and new cutscenes provides a cinematic flair befitting Link’s flagship adventure. It doesn’t take many risks, but it doesn’t need to. Nearly 30 years ago, Nintendo showed us what’s possible with great writing, great design, and great heart. Now, in 2026, history has repeated itself.

The original Ocarina of Time was brilliant. Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 is brilliant. It was a world-beating game back then, and it is a world-beating game even now. [...] I cannot recommend the game enough. All told, this is a MUST play.

A remake of a masterpiece could have been an exercise in nostalgia; instead, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has become something that stands on its own—renewing the experience without betraying the original.

A 10 doesn’t mean the complete absence of flaws. It means that, once you consider what the game sets out to do, its minor imperfections become irrelevant in the face of the sheer scale of what it manages to deliver. Ocarina of Time was already one of those experiences in 1998. It is once again in 2026. Not because Nintendo made the most radically different game possible. But because it had the courage to realize it didn't need to. The Hero of Time didn't need a new adventure. He just needed time to finally catch up to the adventure he already had.
The love and care sown deep into this project help make Link's best adventure even more powerful today.

It’s without a doubt that Nintendo knocked this remake out of the park. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time preserves the magic of 1998, but brings it into the modern era. Whether you grew up playing the N64 original or you're stepping into Hyrule for the very first time, this is one of the greatest games ever made, and is an easy must-play.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time breathes new life into the Nintendo 64 classic in a way few remakes have managed to achieve, blending the original game's iconic mechanics with modern action-game innovations. The result is a true testament to Nintendo's excellence in every aspect.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a faithful remake that manages to evoke the same magic, mystery, and awe-inspiring adventure as the original, even if the foundations are a bit shaky today.

As mentioned at the start of this game, most Zelda fans have this game and will love it. Is this game worth trying for new fans? Absolutely. Even if you started with Breath of the Wild, Ocarina of Time is a timeless classic that still holds up today. The new gameplay tweaks are nice, the graphics are fine, and that dungeon in the graveyard is still super creepy. My biggest praise, as with the original, is how concise and relevant the pacing is. There wasn’t a moment where I felt bored or wanted to move on to something else. I was hooked to the end of the final sword thrust, and that’s honestly something so few games even achieve in this age.

Playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was like receiving a welcome home cuddle from a family I haven’t seen for years. They didn’t care where I had been or what I went through. They were just happy to have me. And I was happy to take their warm embrace. Cliché or not, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is still a masterpiece, and whether you enjoy this or the original, I can’t recommend it enough.

Nintendo knew this release would be closely scrutinised, and it certainly doesn’t disappoint: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is an excellent game that will be very hard to dethrone on the Switch 2.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 is everything we have been told for years: a legend brought to life through a video game. Its story, characters, and unforgettable adventure invite us to fall in love with Hyrule in ways we never imagined, while reminding us that everything we do can carry meaning and purpose.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the quintessential Nintendo Switch 2 game. It is by far the best-looking and best-sounding game Nintendo has made, and while there are some slight hiccups in its mechanics (sprinting while moving the camera) and gameplay (nerfing one of the best items in the series), Nintendo succeeded in making one of its best games of all-time really feel like its modern entry holds its own against the best titles of today.

Time may have moved on, but some adventures are simply timeless, and this is one of them. Iconic temples, a whimsical new art style and an emotionally evocative soundtrack. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is, simply put, a masterpiece.

Some games don’t need a remake to be remembered. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the perfect example of this. Yet, with this Switch 2 version, Nintendo proves that a classic can still amaze even after all these years. From the very first seconds, I was once again swept up in an adventure that holds a special place in my gaming history. That unexpected lump in the throat when you start the game, the familiar intro, the music and the many little details: these are moments that remind you why you ever fell in love with video games in the first place. The beautiful world, the revamped soundtrack, the voice acting, the improved controls and the many activities make this a remake crafted with a great deal of love and respect. Of course, the challenge could have been a bit tougher here and there, but that hardly detracts from the overall experience. I literally enjoyed every single second of this game. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is much more than a trip down memory lane. It’s a magical journey where nostalgia and innovation go hand in hand. And sometimes it’s wonderful to be able to be that child from back then again, if only for a moment.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake focuses on faithfully recreating the qualities that earned the original widespread acclaim from both critics and players, while bringing the experience up to modern standards. Significantly enhanced graphics that highlight just how much time has passed, more nuanced facial expressions and smoother animations, a more immersive and lifelike world, and quality-of-life improvements that eliminate unnecessary frustrations all provide an opportunity to revisit this timeless masterpiece in greater comfort. However, the remake offers little in terms of innovation, making it difficult to give high marks for originality. Those hoping for a fresh or fundamentally different experience may also find their expectations unmet.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time handles its large task of passing the torch to a newer generation with ease. What was dated now feels new again, and this journey may be one of the most special remakes ever released with its stunning presentation on the Switch 2.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time revisits the classic with exquisite art direction, an engaging soundtrack, and refreshed, satisfying combat. Its attention to detail and gameplay improvements enrich the experience while preserving the spirit of the original. Although the reduced difficulty may disappoint those seeking a greater challenge, the overall package delivers a memorable adventure capable of captivating veterans and newcomers alike.

Nintendo didn't try to reinvent a classic, and that restraint pays off. This remake sharpens Ocarina of Time with better controls, a far stronger camera and gorgeous new visuals while keeping its identity intact. Some old frustrations remain, but it's still one of Switch 2's standout games.

No doubt The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake reminded me why I love this adventure. Beautifully refreshed Hyrule, smoother controls, and that unforgettable soundtrack make returning worthwhile. Inconsistent voice acting and an easy difficulty hold it back, but neither spoiled my journey. I came back to Hyrule for the memories—and left with new reasons to love it.

Revisiting The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a visual refresh was every bit as special an experience as I had hoped—perhaps even a little bit more so. It’s truly striking to realize that everything I was playing has existed since 1998, yet it still managed to stir up so many emotions in me. It’s not a remake that tries to reinvent the wheel, but… between us? Ocarina of Time isn’t a game that needs that.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: is a beautiful adventure that excels at everything it sets out to do. Stunning visuals, unforgettable music, memorable characters, and rewarding exploration make it a truly special experience. It may not be particularly challenging, but it doesn't need to be. This is a game that reminds us why we fell in love with gaming in the first place.

Ocarina of Time’s remake took me right back to the N64, and it never let go of that nostalgia. The visuals and music are a joy, the new jump, sprint and free camera feel smooth and responsive, and quality-of-life touches like swapping the Iron Boots with one button make the dungeons easier to enjoy without changing what makes them special. The final fight against Ganondorf is impressive and looks imposing in the remake. It ran without any performance drops in both docked and handheld, and it’s easy to recommend to newcomers as well as longtime fans.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 serves as an excellent example of how a remake should be crafted. Nintendo has succeeded in modernizing a masterpiece without compromising its essence, highlighting a gameplay structure that continues to prove its enduring quality, even nearly thirty years after its debut. This is more than just a nostalgic trip; it is proof that great works can transcend generations, continuing to captivate both those who have known them forever and those discovering them for the very first time.

This Switch 2 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is almost as perfect as remakes get. In fact, I can only really cite an abundance of added hand-holding and a lack of difficulty options as negatives – small gripes in light of picturesque locales, a reimagined orchestral score, and faithful upgrades that make arguably the greatest game of all time the most enjoyable it has ever been.

Of course, in terms of technical aspects, it may be difficult to compare it to the impact the original had on the gaming market. But it is also true that even if we subtract 3 to 5 points for innovation from the 99 points the original received at the time, it still scores in the 90s. I believe there is sufficient reason for gamers to rate it highly simply for the fact that it has brilliantly revived an already sophisticated work in a form suitable for the current generation.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 masterfully pairs its timeless 1998 dungeon architecture with a lavish 60 fps visual overhaul and modernized free-jumping controls, delivering the definitive edition of an industry landmark despite slightly overly forgiving combat.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake knows what made the original great and does not confuse modernization with completely changing the game's identity. The new controls make exploring more fun, the extra dialogue adds more emotional weight to the story, and the visual and audio upgrades bring Hyrule to life in a way that couldn't be done on the N64.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time returns transformed into a true masterpiece. Nintendo succeeds in modernizing one of the most influential video games in history with an extraordinary audiovisual presentation, a captivating sense of scale, and gameplay design that proves to be nothing short of brilliant nearly thirty years later. An adventure that not only does justice to its legacy, but keeps intact its power to surprise, move, and inspire new generations of players. An essential masterpiece that transcends time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is, still to this day and for decades to come, a masterpiece. It is legendary in every sense of the word and this remake is more than we could have ever hoped for. The world, its characters, its nuances and its attention to detail – it is superb. I say this with absolutely zero cheek that this is a piece of work that should be studied alongside other famous pieces of art (literature, film, etc.).

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a careful remake that keeps the original design while upgrading everything around it. It's easy and lacks Master Quest, but it looks, sounds, and plays wonderfully, and it suits returning players and newcomers alike.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a magnificent remake of one of gaming's greatest masterpieces. Stunning visuals, beautifully modernized controls, outstanding music, and timeless dungeon design make this the definitive way to experience a true legend.
The rebirth of a timeless classic which proves that real legends never get old.

For newcomers, this is a remarkable opportunity to experience one of gaming’s most important adventures in its best form. For veterans, it’s a respectful and beautifully realised return to Hyrule that understands what made the original so enduring. And for me, it’s another reminder that sometimes a video game can be much more than an escape. It can be a place you carry with you long after the console is switched off.
In the end, with the Switch 2 remake of "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," Nintendo has, in our opinion, done exactly what the classic deserves.

A timeless adventure that returns to remind us why The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is still considered one of the greatest video games ever created. Its unforgettable world, memorable characters, ingenious dungeons and iconic soundtrack come together in an extraordinary journey that captures the magic of the original while making its legacy shine brighter than ever. A must-play adventure for longtime fans and newcomers alike.

By publishing the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo is offering players the opportunity to immerse themselves in a video game landmark that has inspired so much and still inspires many studios today. A design lesson, a hairy artistic direction with a chara-design that transcends the iconic scenes of the game. This remake is more than a tribute, it is a masterpiece that remains timeless and that opens its doors to a new audience, which can only be warmly recommended.

Ocarina of Time proves mostly, that it is timeless fun. Besides the flashy graphics, the more fleshed out cutscenes improve the story and the seamless day-night-cycle boosts the atmosphere. But the empty Hyrule Field connecting everything isn't elevated.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is an absolute masterpiece, in addition to being the best game on the Nintendo Switch 2, and one of the frontrunners for the best game of 2026.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time returns with a stunning visual remake that brings new life to one of Nintendo’s most beloved adventures. The enhanced environments, detailed character models, improved lighting, and Canadian French voice acting make Hyrule more immersive than ever. Gameplay improvements such as free jumping, quick-access item menus, and the beautifully designed Hyrule tapestry modernize the experience while respecting the original. It's a wonderful opportunity to rediscover a timeless classic.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the all-time classics of video games, returning in a new version that strikes a delicate balance between respect for the acclaimed original and technological updates. It is a simple experience by today’s standards, but its thrilling action and adventure are precisely the kind of escapism that this industry really needs right now.

It's an remake that didn't venture into significant changes because they mostly weren't necessary. Even 28 years after the original Ocarina, it is easy to recognize the quality in its gameplay, story, and design, now accompanied by a lavish presentation that feels like a generational leap compared to the original.

It is difficult to overstate the importance of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to the gaming industry and generations of players. A masterpiece since 1998, it helped shape the future of 3D gaming, and this remarkable reconstruction demonstrates Nintendo’s respect for its legacy. From rebuilt environments and expressive characters to refined controls and enhanced exploration, every improvement modernizes the experience without sacrificing its identity. To me, this is the definitive version of Ocarina of Time, a tribute that honors the past while introducing a new generation to its magic. Time may change Hyrule, but it will never erase a legend. Some adventures live forever in our hearts, and Ocarina of Time is eternal.

Ocarina of Time is a beautiful reminder of why I fell in love with gaming. Nintendo has captured the magic of a legendary adventure with a stunning remake that feels wonderfully nostalgic while still fresh. I loved every moment of returning to Hyrule, and this is a heartfelt tribute to one of gaming’s greatest classics.

Nintendo proves once again that it can make gamers fall in love with every one of its consoles. *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* remains exceptional and may well point the way for similar efforts in the future.

The dungeon design still works flawlessly for this. What Nintendo serves up, or rather served up back then, is impressive. Especially the last two thirds as adult Link are truly exciting. Something magical is always happening.
For me, "Ocarina of Time" is no longer a masterpiece. But the fact that I even had to think about it shows how well this game has aged—and how brilliant it must have been back then.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was a fantastic game in its day, and thanks to its consistently excellent gameplay design and very good pacing, it still holds up remarkably well today. A beautiful and horrific game, Phantom Blade Zero has everything to be both the game of the year and to be a gateway to wuxia for new audiences.

Phantom Blade Zero is a stunning action RPG that gives the best of all time a run for their money. Phenomenal combat, a beautiful world, and a confidently original story wrapped up in a package that’s an intricately designed Metroidvania at heart. It’s a special game.

After waiting all these years for Phantom Blade Zero and playing it from front to back, it’s clear that S-GAME put real love into creating this masterpiece. The combat, the storytelling, the world, and the way Chinese culture is woven into this dark fantasy all come together into something special. Phantom Blade Zero is a generational game that anyone who enjoys action and adventure games needs to play. Soulslike fans should give it a shot too, even though it clearly isn’t one.

Giving me the exact same feeling I had with Elden Ring and Street Fighter 6, I ultimately think Phantom Blade Zero deserves the same perfect score. Phantom Blade Zero is a thrilling action game with excellent combat, a huge selection of weapons, and truly spectacular boss encounters. While it has a few issues, they barely affect an otherwise outstanding experience.

Phantom Blade Zero is undoubtedly an exceptional, remarkable, and truly unique game. With an investment comparable to that of a major AAA production, S-GAME has brought its producer's almost obsessive vision to life, creating a work with an unmistakable personal style and creative identity. At the same time, its mature gameplay framework and broad commercial appeal make even its most demanding and unconventional elements accessible and enjoyable to a wider audience.

Phantom Blade Zero’s combat system should be taught in every game design school. It’s rare to see this level of mastery, even from studios with years of AAA experience under their belts. The slightest mistake or hesitation when reading an enemy’s attack patterns can cost you a huge chunk of your health. Beyond the sheer challenge, these encounters really showcase S-Game’s talent for cinematic presentation and sound design. The game has a real sense of spectacle that carries through every part of the experience, with each region receiving an incredible amount of care and attention. One area where Phantom Blade Zero really exceeds expectations is exploration, which is surprisingly well designed. Completionists will have a field day, although the more nitpicky players may prefer to focus on a few rough edges, particularly when it comes to the lock-on system. We don’t know yet whether Phantom Blade Zero will be named GOTY 2026, but it certainly has what it takes.

Phantom Blade Zero delivers the most alive, fluid traversal I’ve felt in years, and a combat system that’s effortless to pick up yet genuinely demanding once the difficulty curve kicks in. Its bosses are bursting with invention, its arsenal gives every weapon real personality, and it runs beautifully even on mid-range hardware. The storytelling is scattered and the lack of map markers can leave you adrift, but neither dents what S-GAME has built here: a serious Game of the Year contender.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the finest action games of this generation, delivering exceptional combat, spectacular boss battles, and breathtaking art direction inspired by Chinese martial arts cinema. Its deep weapon customization, rewarding exploration, and outstanding optional content make the 55-hour adventure consistently exciting. While occasional level design frustrations, some narrative shortcomings, and PC performance issues prevent it from achieving perfection, S-GAME has created an extraordinary experience that stands among the best games of 2026.
When I first saw it, I didn’t think Phantom Blade Zero was possible. After playing it, all I can think is that it's hands-down one of the best action games ever made.

Phantom Blade Zero is hands down the best action RPG this year, and quite honestly, one of the best action games I have played in a very long time. Despite its slight hiccups in performance, there's very little I'd change in S-Game's Phantom Blade Zero and I wouldn't be surprised if it ends up as a nominee for the grand prize at the Game Awards.

Phantom Blade Zero is the definitive action game of the generation, delivering a stylish gameplay loop, larger-than-life boss battles, and a world that begs you to step off the beaten path. S-GAME has achieved the impossible, not only living up to my expectations but surpassing them in nearly every way.

Phantom Blade Zero is pure fun from the very moment you pick up the controller. S-GAME has proven with every preview that it wasn’t just blowing smoke, and the game’s release is the definitive confirmation that we’re dealing with one of the greats of the action genre.

With excellent level design, unique and fluid combat that is, above all, fun, a vast array of weapons, and a deep focus on exploration, Phantom Blade Zero surprises not just through its individual merits, but because the experience as a whole is greater than the sum of its parts — making it one of the best games of 2026.

Phantom Blade Zero turns the spectacle of martial arts cinema into a deep, hugely entertaining action game. Fluid combat, a varied arsenal, and memorable bosses anchor an adventure with a strong identity, superb art direction, and excellent performance.

A standout action game that fuses the atmosphere of traditional Eastern wuxia with an industrial aesthetic in its “Kungfu Punk” world, and delivers refined action mechanics that action fans will want to play.

Phantom Blade Zero was absolutely worth the wait, delivering spectacular action, stunning visuals, and incredibly smooth, varied combat that makes wielding Soul’s sword an absolute blast. The more I played Phantom Blade Zero, the more I fell in love with it. I wish the early story beats set the stage better and that some traversal mechanics and technical issues didn't interrupt the experience. But when I think back on my time with Phantom Blade Zero, what stands out are the incredible fights, the strange characters I encountered, and how often I wanted to keep playing.

It's clear that S-GAME had a strong, singular vision for this project. The team set out to make the best wuxia game we've ever seen, and while there are some design decisions that may not necessarily land for everyone, Phantom Blade Zero is a thrilling action ride you won't soon forget.

Phantom Blade Zero delivers dozens of hours of challenging action, with demanding boss fights and multiple endings that encourage replayability. Despite these shortcomings, it is easily one of the best games of the year and an impressive achievement for S-Game.
Phantom Blade Zero is an elegant, showcase-worthy visual design from top to bottom that supports a convincing martial arts fantasy drama of impressive scale.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve played in a long time, with standout combat that never came even close to feeling old across 50 hours of playing. Phantom Blade Zero is a fantastic action game, underpinned by a combat system that borders on perfection. A martial arts adventure rooted in Chinese tradition, yet with an identity and heart of its own.

Phantom Blade Zero delivers a surprisingly fresh and successful action experience, highlighted by its exceptional motion capture, dynamic combat, and 55 unique weapons. Phantom Blade Zero has many strengths, from its rewarding exploration to its incredible soundtrack. But the main takeaway should be this: Phantom Blade Zero has enough X-factor to make it a must-play for any action-RPG fan, and a definitive leap forward for S-GAME.
Phantom Blade Zero isn't just an excellent new IP, it's an excellent game that not only manages to meet expectations, but surpass them in Kungfu cinema style.

At the end of the journey, Phantom Blade Zero left me with a lingering feeling that’s hard to shake: the sense that I had played something with enormous potential, yet one that currently fails to translate that potential into a truly polished, complete experience. The ideas are there, as is the charisma—in spades—and when the protagonist, Soul, begins to dance amidst blades, parries, and counterattacks, you can easily glimpse what this combat system could eventually become. The issue lies in everything surrounding that promise: combat readability that is far too inconsistent; a camera that struggles to keep up during chaotic encounters; collision detection and invisible walls that constantly disrupt the flow; difficulty balancing that is, at times, baffling; and a technical and artistic execution that swings between magnificent moments and others that feel surprisingly dated. Even the bosses—arguably one of the most compelling aspects of the entire production—often turn what should be a lethal dance of study and precision into a struggle against poorly refined mechanics. And perhaps this is what makes the final verdict so bittersweet: Phantom Blade Zero doesn’t strike me as a bad game—far from it—but rather as a great game still trapped within an iteration of itself that simply isn’t ready. I had hoped for an experience that would draw inspiration from the likes of *Black Myth: Wukong* and the ferocity of Ninja Gaiden, while forging its own unique identity through its "Kungfupunk" aesthetic. Instead, what I found was primarily a promise—fascinating and, at times, spectacular—but one stifled by so many issues that they can no longer be dismissed as mere imperfections.

After several attempts, I was finally able to beat him and was rewarded with a weapon: The Fanatic's Drunken Sword. With The Fanatic's Drunken Sword, I could have Soul, the game's protagonist, fight in that very same style. On top of that, the weapon had a unique mechanic where I could enter a Drunk state where I could automatically dodge incoming attacks. That weapon became a mainstay of my loadout for the rest of Phantom Blade Zero, and is emblematic of the game's greatest strength. The modern era of Call of Duty is a bit weird. The series is still one of the biggest and most recognisable names in gaming, with a F2P battle royale that commands the attention of millions of players. When Microsoft purchased Activision Blizzard, Call of Duty was the game that made rivals at Sony concerned over the acquisition. Not World of Warcraft, not Overwatch, not Diablo or any of the other multiplatform games that ActiBlizz is responsible for. It was Call of Duty. And Call of Duty's name is no longer associated with quality. Games are bigger than ever, more difficult to develop, and more expensive. So it makes sense that – after nearly two decades of churning out annual entries by rotating through a handful of primary and several support studios – the series would end up releasing less consequential entries. 2023's Modern Warfare 3 felt like a phoned-in DLC expansion to 2022's Modern Warfare 2. 2024's Black Ops 6 was a momentous return to form, only for 2025's Black Ops 7 to feel like a parody of Call of Duty. If you can see the pattern, you'll know what I'm getting at.
