Metacritic user score 8.4/10 (265 ratings).

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great revival for a series I’m always a little worried about. Nintendo is one of the only AAA players left that still brings real whimsy to the table, and Resort feels fresh, special, and complete from day one. If you want a sports game with actual substance, rather than a handful of minigames, this is the one. If you’d rather sink into a big story, look elsewhere – and if you hate fun? Honestly, I’m not sure how you ended up reading a review about Wii Sports' cheerful grandchild, but I admire the commitment. Somewhere on Wuhu Island, an Island Champ is waiting for me. I might not be ready yet. But I want to become the Island Legend, so I will keep training.

In an unfair comparison, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort makes every other Nintendo sports game look like a mere tech demo. As of now, it is the only game that has managed to unlock the full potential of the Switch 2’s Joy-Cons, and it is likely to remain the only one that explores their complete range of possibilities for the rest of the generation.

After the stumbling start of its predecessor, it's nice to see the series back on track in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. While some of the 12 different sports might feel a little too safe, most of the classics feel better than they've ever been, and the newbies surprise and delight with some classic Nintendo intuition. Revamped customisation options and a surprising amount of single-player content both feel like open goals, but they also provide a great excuse to keep playing, even once the party is over. This just might be the Nintendo Sports series at its best.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort remains as fun and innovative as seventh generation predecessor and even more reason to make the Switch to the new system.

As someone who played the original Wii Sports when it first released, and was awed by the rudimentary real-life movements being mimicked on screen, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort allowed me to feel that all over again as an adult. And it’s a feeling best felt surrounded by friends. Whether you’re a jaded 36-year-old man with no children (like me), a parent, a grandparent, or a kid, it’s hard to imagine even the most calloused-hearted person not having fun with the game. Get your family together, get your friends, heck–invite your neighbors over, break out the party essentials, and have fun.

Even if Nintendo never releases an update for Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, it's still an easy recommendation for Switch 2 gamers. The extensive local multiplayer options alone make it worth picking up, but add online to the mix and the game's value increases exponentially. The included sports are all mostly fun and the motion controls work perfectly, plus Nintendo Switch Sports Resort gives players plenty of compelling reasons to pop in for at least a few matches every day.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is another fantastic addition to the company’s arsenal of sports games. This title represents the series' most significant advancement to date and sets a new standard for Nintendo’s sports genre.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort mostly nails the casual fun of motion-controlled arcade sports anyone can enjoy. Though a couple of activities are a little too simplified, most are stellar and control perfectly. The character customization and progression system add even more to the package, making it a great pick for family and friends at the holiday gatherings you’ll likely be attending in the coming days.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has improved on previous iterations by adding elements that enhance both play and competition.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an incredibly fun time. The included sports offer consistent fun, and their accessible controls make it easy to understand, regardless of whether you have ever used a Switch 2 before. Further, the customization and single-player options are far more vast than I initially expected. While the lack of many brand-new sports, plus the lackluster Boxing minigame, are a tad frustrating, these are minor nitpicks for a game that managed to make me feel like a kid again.

With its classic sports polished to perfection and its new additions bringing plenty of surprises, Switch Sports Resort celebrates the purest essence of video games: having fun above all else and sharing that joy with those closest to you. It retains the series’ trademark simplicity while offering more content and depth for those who want to take things a step further. Hours upon hours of fun await in a game that will stand the test of time.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort may not reinvent the formula, but it doesn't need to. This is a sequel that perfectly understands what made its predecessor so special and manages to recapture the magic that defined the Wii era. An accessible, addictive, and nostalgia-filled experience that proves that, even after all these years, Wuhu Island remains one of the best places to return to for a good time.

Switch Sports Resort strikes the perfect balance between active family fun and nostalgia, capturing the magic of the Wii era with sharp Joy-Con precision and versatile game modes. Whether introducing young kids to motion gaming or tackling single-player challenges, it lands as an accessible, highly engaging party hit.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great time with friends, or even random opponents online.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has so many excellent sports games that are exceptionally fun whether you're playing solo or with chums and it specifically makes local multiplayer a blast and with such delightful sights and sounds that bring it all together.

This title ends up being an appealing option for those looking for a game that’s accessible, easy to share, and capable of bringing together players with different levels of experience. For those who grew up with Wii Sports, returning to this formula has obvious appeal; for those discovering it for the first time, the combination of intuitive controls, a variety of sports, and exploration may be enough to ensure a good time.

There is a huge number of games available, including many new releases. The classics have been updated—though not too drastically—but, all in all, you’ll have plenty to keep you busy for months and years to come. This is even more true if you play with others; and if you don’t, well, you’ll have the perfect excuse to make some new friends.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a solid entry in the franchise and has more than enough content to keep you entertained. The returning sports offer the perfect excuse for an evening full of mindless fun, while the new additions actually bring something fresh to the table. There’s plenty to explore, and even solo players won’t get bored anytime soon. Sure, a couple of fan favorites are still missing, but overall, this is one of the better entries in the Nintendo Sports franchise. It does exactly what you would hope from a game like this and even adds a few nice surprises along the way. This is definitely the game you’ll want around for those family gatherings this season.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a ton of fun, as good alone as it is with friends or family, and is another fantastic addition to the Switch 2 collection.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort positively surprises with fine selection of sports, lot of different control options and pure sports joy when fighting for the last point or game. Switch 2 users will try a lot of new disciplines, the casual audience and families will simply love this fine package too. Every sport counts which is a great result for creators.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort presents a solid, well-crafted journey on Switch 2 that succeeds in its core ambitions despite familiar ideas. While uneven pacing and minor design limitations hold it back from greatness, dedicated enthusiasts will find plenty of satisfying moments to make the investment worthwhile.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has been a breath of fresh air to jump into. After spending some time on Wuhu Island, I actually feel like I’ve taken a short break from the big AAA titles full of guns and explosions for a more wholesome experience (senior citizen boxing aside) that got me off the couch and moving. Whether I was throwing punches in Boxing, exploring the island, or getting increasingly frustrated with my golf game, I found myself having fun in ways that some of the bigger releases on my shelf haven’t quite managed lately. It’s a game that makes you laugh, encourages you to get moving, and gives you an excuse to spend time with friends or family. That’s really the spirit of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. My arms are tired, I’m sweaty, and yet I have a big stupid grin on my face. In an action-packed release schedule, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort proves to be a great little holiday.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has a couple of ‘lesser-than’ sports in the mix, but the overwhelming majority is exceedingly good. This is Nintendo’s best take on the motion-friendly sports mix yet.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has turned out to be, in essence, exactly what one might have expected: a reasonably substantial and, above all, highly enjoyable collection of minigames. It makes extensive—and generally well-implemented—use of motion controls, while also offering entertaining exploration modes. In terms of audiovisuals, it remains faithful to a now-signature style, though as a title exclusive to the Switch 2, it delivers a significant technical upgrade. Those interested in multiplayer—whether playing locally with friends or online—will certainly find plenty to keep them engaged for the long haul. At the same time, solo players are also well catered for, with twelve different disciplines and additional special modes providing a more-than-adequate amount of content.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an excellent package of sports games. Most of these sports have appeared in previous Nintendo Sports games, so it’s likely you’ve already logged hours of gameplay in similar versions. More sports or more variations of sports, such as 5 pin bowling, would have been appreciated. Hopefully Nintendo has some long-term plans for updating Nintendo Switch Sports Resort with some free downloadable content. The character customization options are really well done. This is a game that will definitely get folks up and moving. Local multiplayer is where this game will really shine, especially given the easy pick-up-and-play controls. If you’ve enjoyed previous Nintendo Sports titles, it’s easy to recommend Nintendo Switch Sports Resort for the Nintendo Switch 2.
Nintendo has refined the Switch Sports formula to deliver its most polished and complete sports experience yet. A fun, accessible game that's just as enjoyable on your own as it is with friends.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a testament to just how revolutionary Wii Sports was; proving there's still a place for motion-controls in the gaming space. This revival doesn't try to reinvent the wheel, and it makes little changes to the classic sports we've come to know and love from the series, but nostalgia works best when the source material had so much charm to pull from. The all-new sports, Thumb Wrestling and Skateboarding, fit right in with the rest, and the remastered Wuhu Island really comes alive in the Sightseeing Tour mode, making it a blast to explore. Modernized with increased resolution, better single-player offerings, and fixing most of the gripes that prevented the original Switch Sports from achieving the perfection of the classics, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is nearly definitive enough to finally move the Wii into storage and crown Nintendo Switch 2 as the champion of motion-controlled sports games. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort launches 22nd October 2026.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has plenty to keep you engaged and active, even if the new additions aren't quite as fun as what's returning.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an excellent continuation of Nintendo’s Sports collections. Across the different sports available, there are likely to be several that you’ll happily jump back into time and time again. Leisure Sports are an enjoyable way to showcase Wuhu Island and provide a more relaxed experience when you’re all sported out. The addition of the offline Island Crown mode and the ability to earn points both online and offline address one of the biggest issues with the previous Switch Sports. If you’ve enjoyed any of the previous Wii/Switch Sports titles, then Sports Resort is an easy buy.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort keeps the fun of motion controls alive with entertaining and accessible sports that are perfect for enjoying with friends and family. Exploring Wuhu Island, along with the progression and customization options, adds depth to a familiar formula that, without reinventing itself, delivers a well-rounded experience equally enjoyable when playing solo, gathering with friends, or competing online.

As the 20th anniversary of Wii Sports approaches, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort delivers the fifth and finest iteration of the series to date. The 12 sports provide a good variety, and while some of them continue to have the same (deliberate) control quirks that have remained for two decades now, the overall package is rammed with content regardless of whether you enjoy local or online multiplayer, or prefer to play alone.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a lot of fun, but it's also a game that's entirely removed from standard gaming. This isn't going to appeal to everyone, but I think it's a slam-dunk for those that have kids who want to get involved, or people who want a convenient way to get themselves moving just a little bit more, even if you're unlikely to be working up a sweat. It's a lot of fun, but it's also a game that's largely more of the same, so knowing that you'll like a few of the sports is a must.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a return to form for the series that revisits the island setting for a range of fantastic to functional sports. Putting aside some disappointments in sports and leisure activities, Switch Sports Resort gives yet another generation a good reason to waggle at the TV together with friends (as long as you keep on the wrist strap).

Phasing out the Miis was a mistake, and the sports lineup doesn’t feel as fresh anymore. Even so, it’s a solid pick for newcomers and tremendously fun in local multiplayer, especially with kids. Veterans who own the previous game are probably better off skipping this round.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort delivers a capable compilation of quick-hit sports minigames that can be easily enjoyed regardless of how many people are holding Joy-Cons. Though I certainly have my destination sports, there’s not a loser in the bunch. Island Crown mode does a great job expanding the single-player options, but this package’s legs are in its multiplayer experience. And since Switch Sports Resort is chock-full of easily approachable minigames, I can see it becoming a cherished inclusion in the rotation of party mainstays.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a considerable improvement over its predecessor, with more events, more single-player depth, and more ways to play. While it would’ve been good to have seen sports such as Football and Chambara at launch, and the visual style still feels a bit lacking, responsive controls and chaotic multiplayer gameplay make this title well worth adding to your library.

While I had been worried about the revival of one of my favorite Nintendo games from my childhood, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort captures the essence of the original enough to be an enjoyable game. With smooth controls, excellent customization, and mostly fun sports, not even Sportsmates' domination over Miis can ruin my fun. That being said, thumb wrestling truly sucks.
On the whole, the majority of minigames feel really fun and engaging, both in solo play or multiplayer modes. The odd game could be stronger but there’s more than enough here to keep players engaged.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great sports game with a variety of options to enjoy yourself in both online and offline play. Not every sport is a hit, but I’ve had an amazing time honing my skills in the ones I enjoy most. Motion controls feel intuitive, and I (mostly) enjoyed getting to design my character with new clothes and gear. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is also a great way to get the body moving, a concept I’m glad to see Nintendo keeping alive all these years after the Wii first made us get off of the couch.
Nintendo's knockabout sports series returns for its most refined outing yet; charming, wonderfully considered, and it doesn't require a room full of friends to be fun.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a triumphant return to Wuhu Island, delivering reliable family-friendly fun and slick motion-control tracking. While it cannot quite recapture the lightning-in-a-bottle magic or iconic hardware feel of the original Wii Sports, its expanded modes, free-roaming exploration, and solid game roster make it an easy recommendation for couch multiplayer.
While not terribly exciting, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is the sort of solid staple that could be pulled out at gatherings of people of all ages.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort recaptures the charm of the series that began on the Wii and brings it to the Switch 2, featuring twelve disciplines and plenty of virtual competition. Some sports are surprisingly intuitive and deep, making excellent use of the Joy-Con 2 controllers, while others are less compelling. Despite the inherent differences between single-player and online/local modes—and a somewhat uneven quality across the various activities—a visit to Wuhu Island is an enjoyable experience, one that comes recommended to all sports fans.

Switch Sports Resort is exactly what it says on the box. It combines new and classic sports, focusing on what’s worked well in the past while adding a dash of fresh ideas. The game’s core mechanics work perfectly, though I would have liked to see more new content. If you haven’t picked up Switch Sports yet, you should definitely grab this one. For everyone else, Resort is a great addition.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an engaging and fun game that masterfully taps into nostalgia while refining an already well-established formula. The result is an experience suited both for those who love to have fun with friends and for those seeking a challenging solo experience.

More than just a simple release, this represents a reclaiming of identity. Here, Nintendo invites players back with a nod and a promise: a blend of great fun and solid technology. The game delivers on these promises masterfully, successfully proving that the motion-based sports formula—when executed well—remains one of the most entertaining ways to share a video game experience.

The vast new open world allows for sports on a scale far greater than anything previously seen in the series. However, however much fun and accessible these motion-controlled games may be, it is only when played with others that they really come into their own.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a lot of fun, and even nearly two decades late, Wuhu Island still offers an eclectic resort setting filled with some great moments. The newly added sports are especially great, and each one shows how versatile the Joy-Con 2 controllers can be. Overall, this new entry has strong momentum heading into the Switch 2’s second holiday period, and I expect many families will enjoy what it offers. I’m just not sure how it’ll do long term. For now, though, catch me climbing the ranks on Wuhu Island.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is the most complete chapter of the series. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel the way the 2006 original did, but it manages to file down its imperfections until the wheel is, almost, perfectly round. The island of Wuhu has never been so enjoyable to explore, and there is a decent number of activities to keep solo players entertained.

One final note deserves to be made regarding the game’s artistic presentation. Whether viewed on a home screen or the console’s own display, the game is a truly delightful spectacle. While the level of polygonal complexity and environmental detail is—understandably—quite basic, the rounded shapes and vibrant colors transform Spocco Resort into a dreamlike setting. The frame rate is also rock-solid, ensuring maximum fluidity in every situation. The soundtrack is equally excellent, featuring catchy tracks that perfectly complement navigating through the menus and various challenges.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a wonderful, rewarding time. With its suite of well-rounded mini-games, designed to be simple, distilled forms of each featured sport, there’s lots to explore and a very neat array of unlockables to keep you swinging, smashing, sliding and gliding through Wuhu Island.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings back the good old Wii Sports Resort days with more sports, intuitive controls, relaxing music, and plenty to do. I would have loved to see a few more sports, but exploring the island, uncovering its secrets, and customizing your avatar offer plenty of fun. So dust off those sports shoes and get ready to play.

With Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, Nintendo has excellently tapped back into this same magic that has been lost in recent years. Playing Nintendo Switch Sports Resort now with my own family, which includes children ages 6 and 11, has resulted in one of the most nostalgic and joyful experiences that I’ve had with a game in 2026. And while there’s plenty of fun to be had in a group setting with Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, there’s just as much for solo players to dive into as well.

After a week of daily play, it has become clear that Switch Sports Resort will not be going back on the digital shelf for some time yet. It is perfect for a Saturday afternoon with friends, but it also has enough going on beneath the surface to sustain the long-term attentions of an enthusiastic child. In other words, it is exactly what you want from a family video game – and as a bonus, it gets everyone off the sofa.

Has Nintendo finally recaptured the magic of Wii Sports, two decades later? Short answer: a resounding yes. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort doesn't reinvent the idea, but it serves a surprisingly content rich package with plenty of mechanical depth and content. The simplicity is still very much at its core, but there's a significant amount more nuance and refinement. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is very much a game that anyone can enjoy, with room for competitive players to push further. Most importantly, it's a lot of fun!

As expected, there are some hits and misses among the summer sports on offer, but at the end of the day, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort will provide hours of fun with friends, which is undoubtedly the best way to enjoy the game.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort manages to be something the previous title wasn’t: fun. It retains plenty of that game’s issues, like the tedious gacha system for collectibles, an uneven art style, a lack of accessibility or control options, and having too many kinds of tennis, but motion controls have been tightened and the selection of sports gives some great variety.
A colourful experience full of party sports that does exactly what you expect from a Nintendo game, but could benefit from more depth and a wider selection.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an enjoyable new entry in Nintendo’s motion-control-based sports collection series. A few of the simplifications of these athletic activities aren’t as good as the others, but the sum of its parts manages to be enjoyable and varied enough to make things fun. The package is even more fun with friends, but even alone it offers enough meat in its various challenges to be worth a chance.

A very good (if pretty safe) installment, Switch Sports Resort should enjoy a fun honeymoon period and endure through family gatherings. Perhaps Nintendo will even add a few more great, innovative events for those of us who feel like we’ve been playing the same sports for years. But even if this entry sacrifices bold innovation for conservative safety, its sheer fun redeems its familiar personality. Its low learning curve and unlockables not tied to online play make it an appealing choice for parents with younger kids, an audience less likely to care that it doesn’t take long to see everything on offer. Buy it, enjoy it, and dream of a Bandai-Namco-collaborated follow-up to give Wuhu Island a Go Vacation makeover.
Switch Sports Resort takes Nintendo's motion-controlled fun to new heights with its richest mix of sports and modes yet.

A vibrant return to Wuhu Island delivers a broader, more polished mix of motion‑controlled sports and playful side activities. While a few events stumble, the island’s cohesive world, clever control ideas and strong multiplayer focus make this an unexpectedly charming holiday getaway.

If you want fun with the family or with friends, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort will give you plenty to tuck into, though you’d be forgiven for thinking that something far greater and more ambitious is ready to be unleashed in the world of Nintendo Switch Sports, and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort can’t quite burst out with it. For now, you’ll have to settle for a good sequel to 2022’s Nintendo Switch Sports, and you won’t be disappointed with that.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is perfect if you have a rotation of friends who enjoy casual gaming.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings back the easy to play nature of Wii Sports and brings the experience up to today's standards thanks to twelve different events that work like a charm, whether on multiplayer or solo. The added bonuses are a delightful addition, and the amount of options available make this one of the most enjoyable party games of the Nintendo Switch 2 catalogue.
Packed with content and representing a significant evolution from its predecessor, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort proves that the series is far from over.

The combination of new and returning sports offers plenty of variety, but the game’s real strength lies in its simplicity. Everyone can join in on the fun, and everyone should want to. After all, who doesn’t love bowling?  [Issue#376, p.52]

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a fantastic game to enjoy with others. Much like it did 20 years ago, it can become the centerpiece of any social gathering, regardless of who’s there or how much experience they have with video games. However, its efforts to make the single-player experience more engaging fall flat.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a solid greatest-hits package, offering a collection of the best events and features from this series’ past, along with a surprising amount of single-player content. Unfortunately, it doesn't deliver much that's truly new or innovative either. If you're just looking to kick back with some motion-controlled favs, this is a worthwhile getaway, but those looking for something a bit more novel may want to book elsewhere.

Nintendo Switch Sports is a product that easily surpasses its predecessor, first, due to the number of sports available, and second, because of the fun they provide. The true gameplay experience really shines when more users join in.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort doesn't revolutionize the formula, but it delivers the essentials: bringing together young and old for fun, immediate, and social activities. While the game is a mixed bag, with sometimes imprecise motion tracking, a single-player component that quickly becomes tedious, and open-world activities that aren't entirely polished, it truly shines when it comes to entertaining a group for an afternoon or evening. The Switch 2 has found its perfect, family-friendly title, ideal for getting the living room moving, even if it doesn't offer the technological leap or the sporting precision one might have expected 17 years later.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort successfully captures the charm of the Wii classic, offering precise motion controls, enjoyable multiplayer and a nostalgic return to Wuhu Island. However, the lack of several beloved sports, occasional performance issues and some underwhelming visuals prevent it from reaching its full potential. Still, it's a fun comeback, especially with friends and family.

Like its predecessors, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a hugely entertaining game full of charm that anyone can easily pick up, regardless of their gaming experience. Playing simplified versions of fun sports with others from the comfort of your living room remains a blast, even if the motion controls don’t always cooperate.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort delivers an accessible and entertaining collection of 12 sports that make clever use of the Joy-Con 2 motion controls. Its intuitive mechanics make it an ideal choice for family gatherings and multiplayer sessions with friends, while its varied activities and return to Wuhu Island capture the charm of Wii Sports Resort. However, limited depth, repetitive gameplay, and a lack of long-term appeal in solo play hold it back. A fun casual experience that shines in company but struggles to remain engaging over time.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an entertaining evolution of Nintendo's sports formula, featuring twelve disciplines that make great use of the Joy-Con 2 motion controls. Each sport stands out as a solid experience on its own, even if they don't all carry the same weight. Its greatest strength remains multiplayer where the shared fun turns every match into the perfect excuse to get together with friends and family.

Overall, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a genuine improvement and upgrade over Switch Sports. It’s an easy recommendation if you’re still into the motion sports game craze – I know I am; I have all five games and still play them semi-regularly. The four new additions are all well designed, and the Leisure Sports are a great change of pace from the competitive options we’ve grown to love over the last twenty years. While the design of the Joy-Cons themselves can pose some awkward logistical issues in some sports, once you get the hang of it, you should be having just as much fun as ever, particularly with a group of friends and family.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort succeeds as an electric, accessible party game that rekindles the nostalgia and competitive chaos of the original Wii Sports, though its solo play and shallow exploration modes mean it doesn’t quite hit the bullseye.
While the quality of its sports varies drastically, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a fun and playful collection overall that shines as the party game it’s meant to be.
A fun but unambitious new sports game collection that features the best motion controls the series has ever seen, but disappointingly few surprises.

No, Switch Sports Resort isn’t going to successfully recreate that unique feeling Wii Sports gave you. It is a fantastic game, though, and everything that a Wii Sports successor on the Switch 2 needs to be. The selection of sports is wide and varied, and most of them feel fantastic to play, including the likes of bowling and boxing that have been around since the series' inception, yet still feel great to play. It also does a better job of building on that Wii Sports foundation than any other entry in the series to have come since that will hopefully keep players coming back for more, especially if Nintendo has post-launch support planned.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an interesting evolution of the formula. It introduces some interesting new features, and while it stumbles with a few of its ideas, it manages to preserve and build upon what makes this franchise absurdly fun to play.

While it doesn’t have the impact Wii Sports had two decades ago, this is still a charming and decently rich collection of fun and intuitive games. While not every game lands, and the single player content is meager, the games are as fun as ever if a bit shallow.
It’s got plenty of sports to enjoy although some of the controls feel a bit off.

As it stands, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a family-friendly party game that fits perfectly into its role and the hardware of Nintendo’s hybrid console. It offers a wide variety of disciplines and carries a significant dose of nostalgia—if you owned a Wii during the golden age of gaming, you’ll feel right at home on Wuhu Island. At the same time, this familiarity raises a valid question: if you already own *Nintendo Switch Sports*—or even a Wii U—is a trip to this resort worth it? Given the conservative approach, the limited number of new sports, and the uncertainty surrounding the "live service" aspect of the hub and its seasonal events, the answer is far from clear-cut. However, if you haven’t played the series since the Wii or Wii U era, if you’re looking to jump into the action—locally or online—without any compromises, or if you’re picking up your first Switch and need an accessible experience to share with family or less "hardcore" gaming friends, then by all means, fuel up your seaplane and head over. It’s safe to say that finding mini-games as intuitive, engaging, and fun as those in the *Sports* series—and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort in particular—is no easy task.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort doesn’t clear the bar set by 2006’s Wii Sports, but it doesn’t try to. It’s the ideal party game to take to a friend’s house or liven up a family evening, with great moments of Archery, Skateboarding and even Thumb Wrestling, options that outshine a package that also includes a light campaign. At a time when almost everything is played with headphones on, each person in their own corner, it’s good to see a console insist on getting people into the same room. We’ll hardly miss it the way we miss the versions of the past, but it has the potential to fuel plenty of memories.

A solid addition to the party game roster that combines some excellent virtual sports with others that are less captivating, relying primarily on highly precise motion controls. Not every discipline is a hit, and it's hard to say how long the initial excitement will last.
Switch Sports Resort demonstrates, once more, that Nintendo can liven up the party in innovative and versatile ways, even though the overall look and feel remains spotty in places.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort sticks closely to the timeless Wii Sports formula: simple, accessible and still at its best with friends in the same room. The Island Crowns and cosmetic rewards add some sense of progression, but not every sport is a winner and inconsistent Joy-Con motion controls in tennis, table tennis and boxing too often feel like an extra opponent.

Don’t get me wrong. The sports on offer here run well, they’re absolutely fine, and people will have fun playing each other in this game. This is why I can’t go any lower than three stars here, although my tone might say otherwise. Nintendo set out to make another sports game, and that’s exactly what the developers did... I just wish they could’ve done more.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is first and foremost a multiplayer game. It packs diverse sports activities using motion control which are fun for the most part. However the Switch Sports series must improve and innovate upon all its aspects in future iterations.

It builds on the ideas of its predecessor, offering more disciplines and a few successful new additions - most notably, a very good archery mode. The problem is that most of the sports remain highly simplified and formulaic, which, in the long run, makes them boring. Many events have been lifted straight from the previous installment. While it remains a solid party game for families and younger players, it is hard to shake the feeling that we have simply received a larger version of the same product.

Playing Nintendo Switch Sports Resorts with friends harkens back to the pinnacle of Wii Sports, and that’s a huge compliment. Whether you play alone or with a group, there’s plenty of fun to be had. This game makes a perfect gift or stocking stuffer when the holidays come around.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a triumphant, motion-controlled return to form that brings Wuhu Island to life in crisp 4K. Despite a somewhat modest sport selection at launch, its engaging single-player Island Crown mode, clever Joy-Con 2 features, and accessible local co-op make it an absolute must-play for families and motion-gaming fans alike.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a delightful collection of sports that make great use of the Switch 2's motion controls.
We can guarantee that minigames as immediate, engaging, and fun as those in the Sports series and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, specifically, are hard to come by.

If you've played one of Nintendo's Sports or Sports Resort games before, whether on Wii or not, this collection isn't likely to excite or inspire as it's all, by now, well worn territory-even if bowling is still a clear standout. Efforts to expand the experience with free roam feel rather strange, and the online helping and infrastructure doesn't feel robust enough to keep the attention of players, or families, when the console has better party options.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is one of, if not the best entry in the series in my opinion. I personally think this title belongs in everyone's library that has family members or local friends to play with.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort positively surprises with fine selection of sports, lot of different control options and pure sports joy when fighting for the last point or game. Switch 2 users will try a lot of new disciplines, the casual audience and families will simply love this fine package too. Every sport counts which is a great result for creators.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a highly enjoyable party game that truly shines when played with family or friends. Nintendo has put together a diverse range of events, and the excellent precision of the Joy-Con controllers ensures that activities like archery, boxing, bowling - and even a simple game of thumb wrestling - can deliver plenty of excitement.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an engaging and fun game that masterfully taps into nostalgia while refining an already well-established formula. The result is an experience suited both for those who love to have fun with friends and for those seeking a challenging solo experience.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brilliantly revives the nostalgia of Wuhu Island in a modern guise, and motion-controlled sports still work wonderfully, though a few more new sports and a freely explorable island would have been welcome.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is definitively a fun, diverse new entry into Nintendo’s sports game family. It boasts improved gameplay and increased replayability compared to its predecessors, making it an easy game to come back to again and again. There is plenty to keep you occupied as a solo player, what with matches against CPUs, Island Crown mode, the leisure sports and the achievements to unlock, but also plenty to enjoy with other players too, whether that’s online, in friend lobbies and or local PvP.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a fully-fledged successor to both Switch Sports and Wii Sports Resort. The combination of classic sports, simple motion controls and the return of Wuhu Island makes for a package with a great deal of charm. Not every sport is a hit. This is a game that proves once again why Nintendo is so good at making party games for the whole family.

Switch Sports Resort is a game that aims to bring back the excitement that millions of players experienced with the legendary Wii Sports. To that end, it features beautiful graphics, 12 playable sports, and even an online mode. However, I can’t help but feel that this is a title that could have been so much more than what it ended up being. Don’t get me wrong—it’s a super fun game and a perfect experience for the whole family. However, I think that among those 12 activities, some add practically nothing to the experience. I would have preferred not to have the option to explore the island but to have new sports as interesting as thumb wars.
A formula that hasn’t really changed much since the Wii, and one that still works just as well.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort has improved and refined the formula, but it remains a niche sports game that will be most enjoyable for players with little or no experience with video games. If you're looking for a challenging solo sports experience, you won't really find it here.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort understands the appeal of its predecessors. The sports are easy to pick up, while table tennis, bowling, and golf, in particular, offer plenty of room for improvement. Wuhu Island provides a sense of cohesion to the collection, making even the moments between matches worthwhile. Furthermore, with free exploration and the "Island Crown" feature, Nintendo has shown greater consideration for players who choose to head off on this virtual vacation solo.

Not everything hits the mark. Tennis is less compelling, the difficulty level can sometimes jump quite sharply, and a few fan-favorite sports are missing. Additionally, several disciplines remain very similar to previous iterations. Yet, a familiar formula hardly needs to prove itself when it delivers this much fun. Within minutes, Sports Resort can give everyone in a living room a shared goal, a sense of rivalry, and, in all likelihood, a plan for a rematch.

Ultimately, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a more substantial and enjoyable package than its predecessor, particularly for players who want something to enjoy alone as well as with friends. The new sports bring some welcome ingenuity, the return to Wuhu Island provides a lovely sense of familiarity, and the improved solo progression gives the experience considerably more staying power. When the motion controls click, there’s still nothing quite like the uncomplicated joy of picking up a controller and getting stuck into a round of virtual sport.

Fantastically presented family sports game. Most games have instantly natural controls making it a true pick up and play experience. Exploration of Wuhu in the leisure sports is both fun and adds great world building. An absolute blast to play in local multiplayer scenario. Single player gamers may vary in their mileage despite a wealth of content and challenges.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort succeeds by preserving the uncomplicated fun that made the franchise so popular, while expanding the possibilities for those who like to try different activities. It's the kind of game that works very well for bringing the family together, challenging friends, and turning a few free minutes into great gaming sessions.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort may not have the same novelty factor as the original Wii Sports, but it's a great way to get everyone together for a bit of friendly competition.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort successfully recaptures the essence of a franchise that had long been in need of an installment like this. The return to Wuhu Island, the variety of disciplines, and the new options for solo play make this a remarkably complete and entertaining experience especially in its multiplayer mode. While some activities could offer more depth, this stands as one of the best possible comebacks for this long-running franchise.

Boxing, Archery and the surprisingly entertaining Thumb Wrestling make this a fun sports collection, especially with friends or family. Motion controls can be unreliable, and some activities lack depth, but there's enough variety to keep multiplayer sessions enjoyable. Solo play and island exploration are far less convincing.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is exactly the kind of game that reminds me why Nintendo won over so many families during the Wii era. You don't need to master elaborate controls or sink dozens of hours into it just to figure out where the fun lies. All it takes is grabbing a Joy-Con, picking an event, and diving right in. The 12 activities offer an engaging mix of traditional sports and lighthearted new additions, while exploring Wuhu Island brings a special layer of charm to the whole experience.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort comes highly recommended because it’s a very well-rounded and fun sports game, featuring a good variety of disciplines and motion controls that are quite accessible. Although some sports have been left out, the addition of new challenges and customization options enhances the experience. It’s an ideal game to enjoy with the little ones at home and, of course, to compete online against players from around the world.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort stands out for the sheer variety of sports and modes on offer. While I certainly enjoyed some more than others, each was a fun time and a great way to stay active. Each sport remains simple enough to pick up and play for casual players, while offering some more challenge for those who become a little more invested.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort understands what makes this kind of game work. You don't need to be good at every sport, and you don't need to take the competition seriously. You can win a tennis match after repeatedly losing at table tennis, take time to explore the island, or challenge friends who can make five shots of basketball in a row. Each activity gives you another reason to pick up the Joy-Con and try again.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort improves on the formula with the Sightseeing Tour, Wuhu Island, Thumb Wrestling, and Leisure Sports, while staying timeless whether you’re playing solo, with friends and family, or against others online, thanks to intuitive controls and a fun collection of sports. This should be every family’s game of the year.

You might think that picking up Nintendo Switch Sports Resorts won’t make much of a difference—especially if your favorite sport is already featured in the previous version—but you couldn’t be more wrong. The gameplay has been significantly refined, representing a massive leap forward in terms of both hardware performance and graphical polish. The new activities, which utilize the Joy-Con controllers in inventive ways, are a highlight all their own; while they may not strictly qualify as "sports," they offer delightful experiences—such as hunting for collectibles across a stunning, immersive landscape that you’ll wish you could visit in the real world.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort offers a wonderful return to classic motion-based sports action – even if there is some mixed quality between each offering.

Bowling, Golf, Table Tennis, and Thumb Wrestling stand out as the real hits of the package, whilst Skateboarding is equally satisfying (once you figure out its tricky learning curve). Things like Boxing and Basketball don’t hit quite as hard, but there’s nothing outright bad here… there are just some sports that are more fun than others.

Still, with a wealth of content to get through, plenty of cosmetics to unlock, and a variety of ways to play (or relax) on Wuhu Island, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort stands out as a real treat for sporting fans who want to bring fun activities into their living room.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a very smart evolution of a formula that defined a generation. It’s polished, the progression and cosmetics give you reasons to keep playing, and it finally works just as well solo. The tutorials, menu and soundtrack still fall short.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an experience that wants to remind you how simple it can be to have fun. It lets you enjoy each of its activities with easy-to-learn gameplay while delivering cheerful and enjoyable moments in every match. It's the kind of game that helps you break away from your routine and puts a smile on your face.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort successfully brings back Wuhu Island with sharp Joy-Con 2 motion precision and a clever mouse-driven skateboarding mode, delivering an infectious local multiplayer party despite a lifeless open world and a frustrating cosmetic lottery.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is not only a fantastic improvement over its predecessor, fixing everything that had it wrong, it’s the best “Nintendo Sports” game, it’s a great casual game, a great competitive game and a great party game. Even with some bumps, I couldn’t recommend it more.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a significant improvement over its predecessor, offering a greater variety of sports and modes alongside intuitive, immersive motion controls. The excellent two-player co-op and family-friendly design make it an ideal party game, although some activities become repetitive, and basketball takes time to master. Despite a few limitations, it delivers an entertaining experience that shines when playing with family and friends.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort represents a natural evolution for Nintendo’s sports series. It retains the immediate fun of its predecessors while offering more content to explore and stronger reasons to keep playing, even solo. For those who miss the simplicity of Wii Sports or want a sports collection that makes good use of the Switch 2’s features, this is a welcome return—and one of the games I’ll likely spend the most time playing on the console.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings back the joy of Wii Sports with charming activities, clever Joy-Con 2 controls, and fantastic local multiplayer. Not every sport hits the mark, but Wuhu Island remains a wonderful place to have fun with friends.

It’s Wii Sports, Pilotwings, and Wave Race all at once. This is the kind of tech demo that should have accompanied the Switch 2 at launch, whether bundled with the console or sold as a launch title. Not only does it showcase some genuinely clever uses of the joycons’ motion controls, but it also builds entertaining game modes around them.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort succeeds fully its bet: to offer fun and challenge to players of all generations. The mechanics of movement are inspired, varied enough not to make us blow with boredom after 3 sessions. On the contrary, the title manages to diversify pleasures, inflate its content in challenge of all kinds, even to keep us captivated by exploration sessions. Everything is not perfect, but we like to master every mechanic and go to the end of every sporting experience offered. A beautiful surprise that will probably please the children, but not only...

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort recaptures the magic of local multiplayer thanks to brilliant motion controls. Despite uneven minigames like boxing and the omission of a few classic modes, it remains a thoroughly entertaining choice for group play.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort takes the classic sports formula and completely reinvents it for the Nintendo Switch 2.

The vast new open world allows for sports on a scale far greater than anything previously seen in the series. However, however much fun and accessible these motion-controlled games may be, it is only when played with others that they really come into their own.

"Nintendo Switch Sports Resort" has ultimately turned out to be pretty much what one would expect: a suitably extensive and, above all, fun collection of minigames that makes comprehensive and mostly effective use of motion controls and also includes entertaining exploration modes.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is fun to play, but missing classic sports, limited customisation and familiar gameplay make it feel more like a repackaged experience than a new game.

«Switch Sports Resort» is a clear improvement over the underwhelming «Switch Sports» (2022), with more sports, more single-player content and plenty of cosmetic items. Best of all, the legendary Wuhu Island is back, and I get to explore it by plane, skateboard and water scooter. Unfortunately, Nintendo doesn't make the most of the idyllic resort. The solid gameplay foundations of several sports deserved more interesting modes, while progression relies too heavily on repetition and largely worthless cosmetic rewards. The graphics are mediocre, and classics like Frisbee and swordplay are missing. If you're looking for a casual party game for local multiplayer, it's worth considering. Everyone else should think twice about returning to Wuhu Island and might prefer to dust off their old Wii.
Good company, plenty of space—and your living room will take on a whole new dimension with Nintendo Switch Sports Resort

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort offers a nice mix of familiar sports with a few minor new additions, as well as the opportunity to explore more of the island itself and compete against challenging opponents both offline and online. However, that is largely where the new features worth buying the game for end. The overall presentation leaves a lot to be desired, and unfortunately, the new modes feel somewhat limited after just a few hours of gameplay, making it difficult to recommend the title to all players. Nevertheless, those looking for a few fun rounds with friends and family can still give it a try.
Metacritic user score 8.4/10 (2235 ratings).

The Coalition has elevated the franchise to new heights, crafting an engaging, brutal, and surprisingly intimate campaign that’s full of smart gameplay mechanics and wonderful surprises. It’s the best Gears has ever felt to play, and the best it’s ever looked and sounded on the big screen. Gears of War: E-Day? It's a f.cking masterpiece.

Gears of War: E-Day is, for me, the best game in the series and The Coalition's finest work to date. Its campaign brings Marcus and Dom back without relying solely on nostalgia, delivering a darker and more brutal take on the origins of the Locust threat.

Gears of War: E-Day is a monumental triumph from a developer that irrefutably understands what’s important to fans: Gears isn’t just about tearing through Locust with a chainsaw, it’s about brotherhood, sacrifice, and grief. The Coalition has delivered an unforgettable campaign packed full of fresh ideas whilst staying true to what makes Gears so special. The Locust are back and more terrifying than ever, and blasting them to bits is incredibly satisfying. This is the best the combat has felt in twenty years, and fighting to survive the fall of Kalona will leave you speechless. Through its stunning locations, characters, and cinematics, E-Day is a visual powerhouse and one of the best-looking games I’ve ever seen on Xbox.

Weapons of all kinds, gadgets, and locations brimming with possibilities form the foundation of a story that excels in every aspect. Marcus and Dom return alongside old and new acquaintances in a prequel that feels fresh and invigorating. The story of Kalona’s downfall on E-Day serves as the starting point for a war-torn odyssey filled with unique situations, memorable scenes, and the feeling of experiencing an iconic moment in a saga that, for many, is a must-play. Gears of War: E-Day marks a turning point for the Xbox catalog with a console and PC exclusive that’s determined to raise the bar for Microsoft.
A campaign executed to perfection in terms of both technical aspects and gameplay. A brutal and intense war spectacle featuring the best Gears story to date.

I have to say that Gears of War: E-Day is an absolute triumph of a game. The maps in the multiplayer and the campaign are big, with things to find in unlikely corners. From there, exploration in the story mode should be seen as its own reward. This is a game full of content, and you’ll spend hours upon hours taking in everything it has to offer.  Whether you’re here for the campaign, or prefer to get invested in the multiplayer, if you have the slightest interest in Gears, you have to play Gears of War: E-Day. It really is that simple.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the franchise's finest, most atmospheric campaign, brilliantly balancing pulse-pounding action with genuine horror roots. By pairing breathtaking Series X visuals and refined combat with a deeply emotional return to Marcus and Dom, The Coalition has delivered a masterclass prequel that restores complete faith in Xbox's future. A triumph from start to finish.

Gears of War: E-Day shines by showing off humanity's perseverance. Every new character stands out, never overshadowed by the legacy of Marcus or Dom. Even with the game taking place in one city over several days, the evolution of that city and its inhabitants has created fleshed-out characters that you're rooting for the success of every step of the way.

E-Day succeeds in telling the story of Emergence Day in a gripping, desperate, and most importantly, fun way. The culmination of 20 years as a franchise, refining everything the series is into a must-play XBOX title that takes you on a gloriously brutal, emotionally-satisfying, and epic, cinematic adventure.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the series’ strongest campaign, combining mature, restrained storytelling with the return of Marcus Fenix’s charismatic presence. Already among the franchise’s finest entries, it could become a serious Game of the Year contender if its content-rich multiplayer matches the campaign’s quality. Regardless, Xbox players should not miss this outstanding return to form.

Gears of War: E-Day proves, once again, that The Coalition was a top choice to handle this emblematic IP. This prequel expands the gameplay thanks to the clever addition of a dedicated jump button, elevating the moveset and tactical possibilities of the cover-based gameplay. The biggest triumph of E-Day, apart from its gorgeous visuals, is its meticulously crafted and numerous action set-pieces, each one offering thrilling battles. All in all, this new chapter proves that the franchise may be 20 years old, but it remains the pinnacle of third-person cover shooters.

Gears of War: E-Day gets it right from start to finish. In the campaign, The Coalition keeps the pure DNA of the series, with brutal action that puts Michael Bay movies to shame. It also successfully works in quieter moments that let the story and atmosphere breathe. The result is not only the most gripping Gears of War game to date, but also a confronting war epic with few equals. On the multiplayer side, E-Day surpasses its predecessors mainly by going bigger.

After all these years, I didn’t expect a Gears prequel to hit me this hard. E-Day takes characters and enemies I know inside out and somehow makes them feel important again, especially because I already know where all of this is heading. By the time I finished the campaign, it felt like I had finally seen a missing part of a story I’ve been following for years. I thought I’d be done after the credits, but Horde Siege quickly proved otherwise. For me, this sits right up there with the best games in the series.

Gears of War: E-Day is as close to a complete package as it gets, effectively rivaling the series’ heyday. Minor quibbles with the story or matchmaking pale in comparison to the frightening tale of humanity’s darkest hours and the intense fallout of the all-out invasion. Seeing Marcus and Dom back in action and in their prime is an exciting prospect for a longtime fan like me, but it would be meaningless if it were just a nostalgia play; instead, Gears of War: E-Day innovates in all the right ways while keeping the core and heart of the franchise intact, stamping the series’ return with one of, if not its best, entries to date.

Gears of War: E-Day is now XBOX’s flagship franchise. The campaign’s brutal and stunning recount of Kalona’s fall is immaculate storytelling, featuring revived gameplay via reworked movement systems and the visceral combat we know and love. Although Versus is well-made, it’s lacking depth to promote engaging with the high learning curve. Horde Siege is the best iteration of the mode we’ve ever seen, with a gameplay loop you want to play again and again. E-Day might be one of the easiest recommendations we'll make all year, for purchase and awards season.

I hope the game comes out with fewer bugs and runs more smoothly, because other than that, I had a simply phenomenal experience with Gears of War: E-Day and I wholeheartedly recommend it. This is definitely the best game in the franchise.

All in all, Gears of War: EDay is the best thing Gears since Gears of War 2, and we say that having very much enjoyed the majority of the franchise. The Coalition have done a superb job making the Locust feel fresh – and frightening – all over again, the combat is easily the best in the series, and despite knowing how the general gist turns out for Marcus and Dom, they’ve crafted a genuinely completing story to follow along with. Excellent stuff all round, and if this is the marker of a new beginning for XBOX’s first party titles – exclusive or otherwise – then we’re in for once hell of a renaissance.

Gears of War: E-Day feels like the first true Coalition Gears of War game. It's a shift away from Gears 4 and Gears 5, and it feels like the game the studio genuinely wanted to make, capturing what made the original trilogy special while finally pushing the series forward in its own way. They've taken the horror, brutality, brotherhood, and incredible gunplay that defined those games and used them as the foundation for something more modern. Expanded movement gives combat more freedom, while perks and modifications add another layer of experimentation, and the larger environments make Emergence Day feel like a genuine catastrophe happening around you. Gears of War: E-Day is incredible. Despite a handful of frustrations keeping it from perfection, it's one of the best games I've played this year.

Gears of War: E-Day is a fantastic experience from beginning to end, regardless of whether you are a fan of the series or not. The storytelling is deeply compelling thanks to the great cast of characters and aptly bleak tone. The gameplay is brought together by satisfying combat and gorgeous visuals. Despite the frame drops, if this is the quality that fans and newcomers can expect from Gears of War going forward, then the future of the franchise is bright.

Xbox couldn't have chosen a better title for its return to exclusives. Gears of War: E-Day is an enviable, outstanding game. It features one of the best campaigns in the series and breathes new life into the formula.

Gears of War: E-Day is The Coalition’s best entry in the series to date. It recaptures the brutality and identity of the original trilogy while evolving its formula through greater mobility, customization, and a more ambitious campaign. Its emotional story gives new weight to an event we have known for decades, while an excellent multiplayer offering and the ambitious Horde Siege provide an equally compelling reason to keep playing. Technical issues prevented it from reaching perfection, but ironically, after years of searching for a way forward, Gears found its best version by returning to the day it all began.

Gears of War: E-Day hits the mark by getting the basics right: embracing its identity as a Gears of War game and elevating the strengths inherent to the series. The game doesn't revolutionize the genre, but it delivers a fun gameplay experience featuring a cinematic narrative and local multiplayer support.

Gears of War: E-Day marks an excellent return for the beloved shooter franchise, introducing enough new ideas to keep the experience fresh without sacrificing its identity. Its story thrusts players into a desperate struggle against an invading force, while its varied and consistently satisfying firefights and stunning visuals make Marcus Fenix’s latest adventure a highly recommended experience for both longtime Gears of War fans and shooter enthusiasts.
Gears of War: E-Day is a return to form for the 20-year-old franchise, offering up a great and beefy campaign, expanded Horde mode, and classic Gears multiplayer action in a really well-made package.
Overall, this is an excellent return to the Gears of War franchise, with well designed, detailed levels an an emotion-packed action storyline as good as a movie.

Yes, Gears of War: E-Day is the best Gears of War game ever made so far. I fully understand that the nostalgia and affection people have for the first three entries is incredibly strong, but objectively speaking, The Coalition has far surpassed what Epic Games delivered back in the day. This applies to everything from the core gameplay and level design philosophy to the technical aspects and storytelling. Xbox desperately needed an achievement of this magnitude in the midst of the worst period the company has gone through in its entire history. The only major question I’m left with is where they will take the franchise in the future, because a big part of the success this new installment has achieved comes from its strong connection to its predecessors, while leaving behind the less successful sequels from a few years ago.

Gears of War: E-Day is a stunning AAA production and the triumphant return the series deserves. The Coalition blends two decades of experience with meaningful experimentation, delivering a polished campaign that works equally well for newcomers and longtime fans. Gorgeous visuals, impeccable technical execution, and refined gameplay make E-Day a standout release and one of 2026’s essential games.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers a spectacular and intense campaign that stays true to the series while feeling slightly faster and more dynamic. Excellent gunplay, strong presentation and varied missions make it one of the most impressive entries in the franchise, despite a few minor control and melee issues.

Gears of War E-Day stands out as the best entry in a very long time and one of Xbox’s most accomplished games in recent years in terms of pacing and production values. Its more open design and improved mobility make up for a somewhat traditional formula. Still, The Coalition delivers its best Gears yet, recapturing the series’ brutality, fury and spectacle while expanding its universe. I really enjoyed this return to its roots. It just lacks that extra emotional impact that could have made it truly incredible.

Between PvP, Horde Siege, and the campaign, Gears of War: E-Day gives players significant bang for their buck. Narrative shortcomings hold it back from reaching the level as some other games in the series, but it's still a blood-soaked thrill ride with nonstop action no matter what mode players choose to dive into. It's a no-brainer for Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers, but E-Day is also an easy recommendation even if you have to pay full price.

Brutal and inspired, despite some repetition and technical issues. With its masterful presentation, visceral combat and excellent soundtrack, it brings the essence of the series back to life. One thing’s for sure: the Gears are back.

Gears of War: E-Day's campaign is an explosive ride, and being boots on the ground on day zero, as the invasion kicks off, is a wild experience. It's dark, it's brutal, and at times, it's shocking. Multiplayer is pretty great too, especially the new Horde Siege mode, but Versus needs more maps.

Gears of War: E-Day is simply phenomenal. A campaign that stands as the best ever made for the series, distinguished by a narrative that is finally deeper, outstanding character development, and level design that manages to intelligently evolve the original formula. The gameplay is a sure thing, but this time it manages to offer something more thanks to a structure that perfectly alternates exploration and linear missions, always keeping the pace of the action extremely high. The multiplayer is packed with content, Horde Siege is addictive, and the Versus component continues to deliver everything fans could want. And then there’s the technical and artistic presentation, which is simply off the charts. On Xbox Series X, we’re looking at an impressive visual spectacle, accompanied by a fantastic soundtrack and top-tier sound design. The Coalition has created a work that doesn’t merely celebrate the past, but manages to breathe new life into one of Xbox’s most important franchises. A production that is polished in virtually every respect, capable of moving players, entertaining them, and above all demonstrating just how much this series still has to offer. For me, the best Microsoft Xbox exclusive at the moment and one of the most successful Gears of War games ever made. A triumphant return, simply unmissable.

Gears of War: E-Day has managed to bring back the feel of the first games in this legendary Xbox series—the ones that sprang from the mind of Cliff Bleszinski at Epic Games. But it does so under the guise of exploring the beginnings of Marcus and Dom’s friendship, the response of a city that becomes a witness to the invasion, and a combat system that introduces new features and tactical possibilities. This return to the series’ origins provides context for the characters and revives a threat that needed to feel unsettling once again.

Ultimately, complementing its already widely acclaimed campaign, Gears of War E-Day also offers a robust multiplayer mode capable of satisfying both competitive players and Horde enthusiasts; it features a substantial, solid, and rewarding content plan that helps define what is, without a shadow of a doubt, one of the year's best titles.

Gears of War: E-Day has a blockbuster campaign that sets a new benchmark for Unreal Engine 5 games, with great audiovisuals, strong performance, and new peaks for the franchise, especially in the gameplay department. Its rock-solid combat, evolved mobility options, and deeper mechanics make for an experience that is difficult to put down. However, the open levels undermine some of what makes E-Day so good while introducing technical issues, and despite strengthening its emotional themes, environmental repetition and some weaker story beats do tire at a certain point. Thankfully, the excellent Horde Siege and Versus multiplayer give it enough reasons to keep playing.
Gears of War: E-Day delivers thrilling combat, varied multiplayer offerings, and impressive level design.

There's a lot I love about Gears of War: E-Day, and I honestly feel like its best moments naturally fit along with the original trilogy. I also had to ignore a lot of the things I greatly disliked about the campaign and get straight to the good stuff. It's as if I was fast-forwarding through the parts of a movie I hated to get to the good stuff. PVP multiplayer has its moments, but ultimately, it'll still turn off those who haven't spent the past two decades perfecting their strategy. That said, Horde Siege more than makes up for those shortcomings. The result is an incredible experience that has me excited for the future of the franchise. I'm honestly quite happy with how E-Day's campaign turned out, even if I'd take the open world sections and leave them on the cutting room floor.

While some small, confusing shortfalls persist throughout, Gears of War: E-Day thoroughly demonstrates, that The Coalition are the right stewards for the franchise, showcasing fantastic gameplay tweaks and additions, and a strong structural foundation on which to build for the future.
A prequel that returns to the heart of this series.

Gears of War E-Day revitalizes a storied franchise without betraying its soul, yet gives it something new to say. It achieves this with a hard-hitting opening act, technical execution that sets new standards for the generation, and gameplay that finally offers greater depth through verticality and loadout customization. Minor flaws—such as a still-nascent open-world design and overly guided exploration—dampen the sense of discovery but do not undermine the experience's beating heart. The result is a rock-solid game that will satisfy the hardcore community while opening the door to newcomers; by the time the credits roll, the feeling is that The Coalition and People Can Fly have laid an excellent foundation for the future. It remains to be seen where the series will go from here—and finding that out will, in all likelihood, take another two or three years.

Gears of War: E-Day is a monstrously large package boasting multiple gameplay modes, a meaty campaign, an infectious Siege PvE mode, and classic versus PvP modes. Boasting some of the most impressive Unreal Engine visuals ever committed to the medium, Gears of War: E-Day is another impressive victory for one of the industry's most consistent dev teams. That "consistency" perhaps holds E-Day back in some ways, with a campaign that could've used more innovation and iteration, but the overall package is undeniably fantastic, fun, and ripe for future success.
Gears of War: E-Day is an excellent return to form for the series, with a fun and engaging campaign, improved movement, and a strong range of multiplayer modes.

Gears of War: E-Day makes an incredibly positive impression with a package that offers tons of intense carnage. The campaign is a thrilling take on Emergence Day, and exploring the town of Kelona getting ravaged in real-time is entertaining, with side missions proving to be worthwhile distractions. Meanwhile, Horde Siege is a standout new cooperative mode that has eaten up lots of my spare time, while Versus is there for the die-hard competitive types. It’s all presented with visually stunning art direction and smart gameplay tweaks that improve on what Gears has always been, while maintaining what we love about it in the first place. This is a blood-soaked, adrenaline-filled adventure you simply can’t miss.

Gears of War E-Day is exactly the return to basics the series needed. After Gears 5 got a little lost in its semi-open areas, The Coalition goes back to the franchise’s strengths: a focused campaign, visceral combat, satisfying cover mechanics and spectacular set pieces. New moves and low cover add some freshness without compromising the series’ DNA. It’s not perfect, though. Some environments and situations are reused too often, while the lack of enemy variety makes their patterns predictable. The biggest disappointment is Marcus and Dom, who should have been at the heart of the story. The game had a great opportunity to explore the beginning of their friendship, but their relationship never gets the attention it deserves. Still, E-Day delivers an excellent solo campaign and a strong reminder of what Gears does best.

Gears of War: E-Day is one of the most brutal, fun, and visually stunning entries in the series, breathing fresh air into a formula that clearly needed a shake-up. It isn't completely flawless due to a few minor hiccups, but at its core, it is pure, unadulterated Gears of War.
Gears of War: E-Day thrills with gripping battles and spectacular staging, but it does drag a bit here and there.

Gears of War: E-Day takes us back to the beginning of the Locust War with an intense and epic campaign. Not everything hits the mark, but spectacular moments, relentless action, and new additions make E-Day a strong evolution of Gears.

Is Gears of War: E-Day the Xbox Series X/S exclusive that PS5 players will envy? Perhaps. The Coalition’s ultra-violent blockbuster delivers a stunning visual punch in 4K/60fps—the most impressive seen on console to date. Classic yet fresh, the gameplay focuses on the essentials rather than spreading itself too thin. With environments that crumble apart, visceral impacts, and fluid enemy movement, the game directs its efforts exactly where a Gears of War title needs them. Had the characters been less one-dimensional and the side quests more varied, the *E-Day* campaign could easily have stood as the series' best—surpassing even the original trilogy. Whether played solo or with others via a highly entertaining multiplayer mode, this Gears of War makes a massive impact.

E-Day carefully modernizes the Gears formula, but never looses sight of what made the series great in the first place. Amazing visuals, high-octane action and a surprisingly decent story all come together in one of the best Gears of War games to date. Some pacing issues aside, you are getting a really strong package here, with a satisfying campaign, co-op, pvp and the new Horde Siege which should keep you busy for quite some time.

Gears of War: E-Day is a brilliant addition to the Gears of War franchise. The story does an excellent job of bridging a gap between the Gears world before the locust invasion and after. The character development is excellent, and you can’t help but feel for the members of Bravo Squad and some of the supporting characters you encounter along the way. The gunplay is as solid as ever and the added weapon and armour mods help make us feel in more control of the outcomes. E-Day is not without it’s issues. There were drops to the dashboard, really stupid CPU-controlled Bravo Squad members, and some cheap deaths along the way. I also had a difficult time enjoying the versus mode as there wasn’t a deathmatch-only playlist. The objective modes just aren’t that fun. Overall, Gears of War: E-Day is an excellent shooter that will be an absolute blast to play alongside friends.

Gears of War: E-Day is the best the series has been in a long, long time. While its campaign is fairly by-the-numbers standard for a third-person shooter, the game’s cast is engaging enough to elevate it. The pacing can be a bit of a slog sometimes, but the fantastic movement, gunplay, and visuals make all-out firefights an experience to behold.

I had a great time with Gears of War: E-Day, even when the campaign started showing its unpolished edges. The combat is still incredibly satisfying, and the free-roam sections gave me some of my favorite moments; it gave me more time with characters I ended up caring about more than I expected to. That made the campaign's weaker points stand out more, though, with the repetition and occasional technical issues becoming egregious at times. Neither was enough to sour the experience fully. I finished it satisfied, thinking I probably could have used a little less Locust shooting, which is about as Gears of War a problem as you can have.

Epic to a fault, Gears of War: E-Day packs in everything but the kitchen sink, almost as if saying goodbye to the franchise, which, considering everything, it just might be. But if this is it, what a way to close up shop. E-Day combines everything Gears fans love about the series into an overwhelming and immensely earnest celebration that stands proudly alongside the original trilogy.
While E-Day’s cover-based third-person shooter gameplay doesn’t break the mold, it’s a finely tuned experience that builds on the mechanics established across the long-running series.

Gears of War: E-Day is a solid prequel that gets a lot of things right. The characters, the combat, and the visuals all mesh together into a must-play adventure for any Gears of War fan, but it’s also an excellent starting point for those new to the series.
While it could be seen as the developer losing faith in what they accomplished with the 4th and 5th entries, it can’t be denied that it makes for a fun & bloody good time.

I’ve really enjoyed my time with E-Day. Series S players have got the raw end of the deal, but everyone else should buckle up for a properly epic showcase of enemy brutality, impressive world-building and jaw-dropping spectacle.
Climbing, collapsing buildings, impressive new tech and build-your-own weapons breathe new life into Gears, though a slightly bloated campaign and sponge-like enemies hold it back.
Gears of War: E-Day is a reminder of just how bloody good this series can be. After twenty years, perhaps Gears didn't need another revolution, it just needed another Emergence Day.
