Yes, the political descriptions of the imaginary, yet not SO imaginary parties sometimes appear a bit blunt and underdeveloped, and some of the socio-political points of the game seem distributed like with a sledgehammer. And although the hand-drawn graphics with their wonderful animation please me personally, they are sometimes somewhat confusing and perspective-straining, if for example many different floors are in the picture. Does this really detract from Esoteric Ebb? At least not for me.

"Esoteric Ebb is a narrative triumph and an absolute masterclass in CRPG design, comfortably standing tall in the genre's elite alongside modern legends. By masterfully converting D&a;D 5e mechanics into an investigative, combat-free political thriller, the game delivers an exceptionally clever and hilarious tabletop experience. The writing is nothing short of brilliant, filled with sharp political satire, rich fantasy lore, and deeply philosophical dialogue. Supported by a gorgeous isometric presentation and incredible player agency where every dice roll shapes the city's fate, Esoteric Ebb is an unforgettable, mind-bending masterpiece that no role-playing fan should pass up."

Esoteric Ebb is the rare game that makes you feel genuinely smarter and significantly stupider at the same time. A few rough edges here and there can't undo the fact that this is one of the most inventive, wickedly funny RPGs in years.

Esoteric Ebb is a balancing act. Between irony and seriousness, between political investigation and fantasy comedy, between player freedom and authorial identity. A CRPG with character, albeit with some flaws.

Is a remarkable achievement — a solo developer’s love letter to the CRPG and tabletop traditions that creates something genuinely new from familiar inspirations. The Disco Elysium comparisons will follow it everywhere and they’re not wrong, but they’re also not the whole story. Norvik is Bodegård’s city. The Cleric is his character. The humour, the warmth, the political earnestness — these are his voice, and by the end of a playthrough they’re entirely recognisable as such.

At $24.99, Esoteric Ebb offers more genuine creativity per dollar than almost any other CRPG on the market. The rough edges and occasional over-reliance on its inspirations are the honest price of a singular creative vision. For fans of Disco Elysium, Planescape: Torment, and narrative RPGs generally — this is absolutely essential. For more RPG coverage, check out our full reviews section.

Esoteric Ebb is a debut of exceptional rarity; an indie title that doesn’t merely fill the void left by its inspirations, but actively contributes to expanding the boundaries of what the genre has to offer. Christoffer Bodegård’s ambition is evident in every aspect of the production, from the complexity of the world-building to the sophistication of the progression system, from the quality of the writing to the art direction. Sudden Snail has delivered a debut of rare maturity to the indie scene. Norvik is a city you’ll want to return to, Snell is a companion you won’t easily forget, and the Quest Tree is a fully realized design concept.

However, if players embrace the game’s pacing and accept the rules of this peculiar “tabletop campaign,” they will discover a surprisingly rich microworld full of humor, melancholy, and strange human as well as non-human stories.

While there are plenty of epic RPGs on the market, there’s never been one that has the bones of a campaign with the meat of a moron. You’ve never seen a game hilariously punishing you, in real time, for being a dink, while simultaneously urging you forward with your stupidity. It’s simultaneously serious and satirical, and both are completely genuine. The tonality, the flow and the atmosphere make this a phenomenal marathon game.

Esoteric Ebb has an incredibly cool art style, a living world I enjoy spending time in, a great and compelling story, a wonderful soundtrack and sound design, a script that is at times hysterically funny, and both a quest, level, and loot system that are excellent. If you're a CRPG fan who enjoys games like Disco Elysium and Citizen Sleeper, Esoteric Ebb is a must-play.

I just wish it had the confidence to be a little more itself, and a little less a copy of Disco Elysium, because when Esoteric Ebb occasionally does step out of its inspiration and brings something entirely new to the table, the game is at its absolute best.

The comparison with its big brother makes the few weaknesses here more visible. At the same time, when those weaknesses only emerge because the game is being measured against one of the greatest games ever made, Esoteric Ebb is still one of the best games of 2026 so far.

Esoteric Ebb is an absolutely worthy successor to its inspirations. It effortlessly manages to be both intellectually rigorous and deeply, humanly messy, blending its philosophical questions with the overarching narrative and tea shop mystery, elevating all aspects in the process.

Make no mistake: Esoteric Ebb is just what the doctor ordered for a quick-witted, choice-heavy, path-altering, and experience-defining RPG title that knows how to tinker with your cerebral mentionables.

Despite the occasional punishing dice roll, Esoteric Ebb is a stunning achievement in narrative and gameplay design that is a sheer joy to play from start to end. It takes a familiar framework and brings it to life with a world that reacts wonderfully to every chaotic choice you make. And sure, it does borrow some ideas from the greats of the genre, but with Esoteric Ebb adding its own unique ideas and sense of flair to the mix, it stands out perfectly alongside them as another must–play release.

Christoffer Bodegård has made an excellent game in Esoteric Ebb, especially for a fantasy RPG and D&a;D fan like me. Even if you don’t know about D&a;D, it’s easy to get into. With a rich world to explore and an intriguing story, there is plenty to do, plus numerous interesting side quests. The satirical humour and colourful characters throughout provide a very fun fantasy world. With many hours of gameplay, the stunning graphics and attention to detail will keep you engaged, partnered with a solid soundtrack.

Amazingly, this is Christoffer Bodegård’s debut game, and I’m beyond excited to see what they develop next. I’m thrilled to give Esoteric Ebb the Thumb Culture Platinum Thumbs Up! I previously reviewed Knights in Tight Spaces, a similar isometric fantasy RPG, so feel free to check that out too.

Esoteric Ebb will delight those who love fantastical tabletop adventures but have been craving a single-player experience, especially if you are remotely into medieval stuff, silly stuff, political stuff, and/or male identity stuff. I am not alone in thinking that it's one of the best successors to Disco Elysium, a game I very much loved. There's strong potential for Esoteric Ebb to get a sequel, or even some DLC, and I'll be lining up to try it. 

I think Esoteric Ebb is an excellent example of the CRPG genre, though it is pretty deep into its systems and those who are new to this style or don't enjoy it will be hard-pressed to click with it. But if you do love a TTRPG, you're gonna love it. I'm confident that, at the end of the year, I'll be putting it on my list of best indie games.

Esoteric Ebb succeeds because it embraces its inspirations with confidence and reverence. It borrows the philosophical backbone of Planescape: Torment and the introspective depth of Disco Elysium, then reshapes those ideas into something playful, political, and unmistakably its own. This “thinking person’s RPG” will surely find a spot in our Best of 2026 list.

A highly competent CRPG in its writing, freedom, and artistic style, delivering a relatively dense load of politically and socially relevant dialogue, but which, for better or worse, clings too much to its original inspirations.

Esoteric Ebb quickly became a favorite game. Its sharp wit, outlandish characters, and endless Cleric choices are magnetic. Early on, I knew it stood out—what’s not to love about a game where fleeing from a goblin queen is on the table, even if I fail spectacularly?

Esoteric Ebb shows that the spirit of Disco-likes can be done in a way that is incredibly potent and resonant with the player in the same way the original game was. It is a game that will inevitably stick with me as the months go on, and although 2026 is far from over, I believe you'll be hard-pressed to find anything else with this level of high quality writing this year.  Games such as this come very rarely and they need to be harbored for how special they are as narrative experiences.
Esoteric Ebb is one of the few games that manages to combine tabletop role-playing, story-driven CRPG mechanics, and player choice into a single, enjoyable experience.
Esoteric Ebb is the Disco Elysium that D&a;D fans wanted, and much more. If you're into fantasy, humor, or just a good story, you'll find that in spades here.

Labeling yourself as a Disco-like is a bold move and following the blueprint this closely is even bolder, as this will surely draw comparisons to what many consider to be one of the greatest CRPG’s of all time. Luckily, Esoteric Ebb can withstand the scrutiny and pressure of the comparison because it’s not a carbon copy and there is a clear line of distinction between the two experiences. It might be a little inconsistent and clunky at times, but with a high level of autonomy, witty writing and satirical tone that balances the heavy themes within, Esoteric Ebb is a dungeon worth plundering.

The Disco Elysium-esque gameplay of Esoteric Ebb provides a blank canvas for a colorful 2D graphic style that feels a bit like an interactive comic and often creates an interesting balancing act between style and content. I have very little bad to say about Esoteric Ebb. The only thing I still find difficult even after many hours of gameplay is navigating the different areas and moving from one to another as well as the questing tree, which is a bit rough in use while looking gorgeous. But those are really just minor things. Recommending such a story-driven game without spoilers is always somewhat impossible though. So to put it simply: the Visuals are awesome, the music is great and the story abolutely wild. Esoteric Ebb is really good. Trust me.

The Bubbly Basin's DLC expands the adventure of Pokémon Pokopia into a previously unimagined zone. It impresses with the introduction of new Pokémon and the endless possibilities for building. Here, the only limit is your imagination.

Pokemon Pokopia: Bubbly Basin expands the game's strongest qualities with engaging underwater exploration, meaningful quality of life improvements, and a substantial collection of new content. Its limited story and steep price hold it back, but the new biome adds welcome depth for players invested in the base game.

Pokémon Pokopia’s Coral Basin expansion adds a refreshing underwater dimension to the experience, expanding exploration and building with intuitive mechanics, new Pokémon and plenty of fan service. While the amount of content is somewhat limited, its new possibilities make it a welcome addition for anyone looking to enjoy Pokopia in a different way.

Bubble Blub Backwater is exactly what we expected from the first DLC for Pokémon Pokopia: an excuse to step back into the shoes of Ditto and relive the bittersweet atmosphere of this unique Pokémon adventure.

Pokémon Pokopia: Bubbly Basin is a great excuse to return to the game’s universe. The new underwater region has enough personality to offer an interesting change of pace, there are plenty of new Pokémon, and fans of building will enjoy a wealth of new items and habitats. The free update accompanying its release also greatly improves the game with the ability to dive and several quality-of-life adjustments. However, it’s important to distinguish these free additions from the content actually included in the DLC. Once that distinction is made, Bubblegum is essentially a new region that follows the main game’s formula almost entirely. Despite this, I had a great time during my playthrough and still wanted to keep playing even after completing the main objectives. We’ll just have to wait for the next installments of the expansion pass to see if the package as a whole manages to take things a step further.

Bubbly Basin is a charming, densely packed extension of Pokémon Pokopia that rewards returning players with more room to create. Its biggest limitation is that many of the game’s most meaningful improvements arrive through the free update instead.

Pokémon Pokopia just keeps getting better with the release of Bubbly Basin – the first of three DLC areas that has set an exceptional standard for those yet to be released. There’s lots to explore and more charming narrative content, as well as a strong selection of Pokémon to befriend. If you enjoyed Pokémon Pokopia’s base game, you’d be missing out by passing on Bubbly Basin, and I can’t wait to see what the next area is like.

A large additional town with a free update that allows players to dive underwater and utilise all the space down there as well. Anyone who loves Pokopia’s base game is going to be ecstatic to explore all of the additional content. With just the Bubbly Basin being released, the price point is very expensive; however, a second town is in the pipeline and an update that looks to add accessories to your town residents. I'm feeling very hopeful for the future of this expansion pass.
Bubbly Basin is a delightful new underwater area to dive into in Pokémon Pokopia, which promises hours of salty fun with your favourite water types.
98.6% of OpenCritic critics recommend this game (144 reviews).
Metacritic user score 8.9/10 (293 ratings).

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve exemplifies “High-Flying Action” and takes it to another level, while also giving new fans options to ease into it. Personally, I say dive into the deep end; flying directly into the ground a few times puts some hair on your chest. If you enjoy exploring an action game in a massive 3D space, love jets and airplanes, or are already a fan of the franchise, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a masterclass in its category.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a bold evolution of the foundation laid in AC7. Its story is more exciting, its presentation is more polished, and most importantly, its gameplay is impeccable, with a variety of missions and combat situations that keep the player engaged, entertained, and wanting more. This is one of the best games not only of the year, but of the generation.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is an improvement in everything that is quintessentially “Ace Combat," bringing back squadron commands and adding a plethora of different aircraft, new special weapons, and more. The cinematic visuals and deep, twisting narrative immerse the player in the fantasy of being an ace pilot in a war between two nations.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve elevates the franchise to new heights with a spectacular campaign that mixes high octane missions with relevant thematic storytelling. The real ace, though, remains the compelling and addictive dogfighting gameplay.
Ace Combat 8 is a love letter to combat aviation in its entirety. It showcases aircraft as bringers of both death and salvation, but from an earnest, human perspective.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve gives you total freedom in how you fly and fight, with plenty of customisation options and visuals that'll blow you away.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a spectacular return for the long-running flight combat series, combining exceptionally responsive controls with stunning audiovisual presentation and a substantial 30-mission campaign. Its blend of accessible arcade action and deeper simulation elements makes every dogfight satisfying, while an engaging story, extensive aircraft customization, and multiplayer provide plenty of longevity. Upgrades can feel unnecessary on standard difficulty, but this is otherwise an impressively complete package and one of the strongest flight combat games of the modern era.

The years roll by—now counted in decades given the series' longevity—yet it is delightful to see Ace Combat endure as a franchise crafted with passion and love for both video games and its loyal fanbase. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve stands as one of the franchise's finest entries, undoubtedly earning a spot in the conversation for the series' greatest title of all time. From the very start, it is a beautiful, fun, and challenging game that captures the true essence of gaming through its focus on design and mechanics. Project Aces—now Bandai Namco Aces—remains true to its vision without compromising its identity. Without a doubt, this is one of the year's best games and an experience not to be missed.

After 30 years of soaring to new heights, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve finally reaches the summit and stands undisputed. Refined in every possible way, it is not only the finest game in the series to date, but arguably one of the greatest air combat simulations ever made.

ACE Combat 8: Wings of the Theve from Bandai Namco Aces Inc. is a marvelous, beautiful dogfighting flight simulator. It offers a solid storyline with real stakes, a good variety of missions to keep the game engaging and fun, and accessible gameplay that should satisfy both newbies and veterans of the series.

Another Ace Combat, another showcase of perfection. Every entry in this series is different, yet at the end of the day, they all manage to evoke the exact same emotions. Those emotions are intense, primal, and impossible to find anywhere else. [Issue#375dye, p.58]

It’s a frenetic, challenging and emotional experience, and if you’re on board (or find yourself on board) with its displays of aerial ballet amongst the chaos, you will find yourself feeling the responsibility of Wings and becoming the hero you need to be.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is, so far, one of the best combat flight simulators out there, and among the finest in the franchise. It masterfully blends intense dogfights, gameplay depth, spectacular visuals, a diverse roster of aircraft, and a well-crafted online mode. It is clear that the series keeps its magic intact and its ability to surprise after 31 years.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve doesn't reinvent the series, but it doesn't need to. With a lengthy campaign, satisfying aerial combat, larger-scale battles, and an impressive technical leap, Project Aces delivers one of the franchise's most complete entries yet. A few frustrating missions and technical issues occasionally disrupt the experience, but after seven years, Ace Combat returns in excellent form.
Turns out fast action, banging music, and big explosions are a good combo

Did this, the ninth game in the series, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, live up to the hype? I dare say you had better believe it. Beautiful skies full of a variety of aircraft and aerial combat are accompanied by a compelling campaign, amazing soundtrack, and a multiplayer I can’t wait to play more of with other fans.

ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE is an impressive culmination of the very best that the series has to offer so whether you're a long-time fan or a rookie pilot, you're going to love soaring through the clouds as you evade incoming missiles and blow up all sorts of targets.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve shines in a unique way and possesses the rare gift of attracting players who have always watched flight simulators from afar, wary that they might be too difficult or overly complex. Its mechanics are accessible, yet there is enough depth for those seeking a true simulation experience. Whether you are a campaign player or someone who enjoys dedicating a significant amount of time to multiplayer, there is plenty here to enjoy.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the leap in quality the series had been waiting for, a chapter able to honour everything that made Ace Combat recognisable across more than two decades of history while still questioning itself exactly where it needed to. Not just the best Ace Combat ever made, but one of the best arcade flight games of the entire generation. The sky, once again, has earned its own legend.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve combines exhilarating simcade flight combat with a spectacularly varied campaign and a surprisingly personal story about war, propaganda, and manufactured heroism. Its occasional excess of melodrama does little to diminish one of the series’ most confident and memorable entries.

The only real criticism is that, with this eighth installment, they played it safe. That is hardly surprising given the success of Ace Combat 7; naturally, they wanted to retain the players who came on board with the previous entry. Even so, this remains an even more refined—yet equally (or perhaps even more) epic—experience.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a well-rounded experience that is hard to find any significant faults with, beyond the resolution issue on consoles and, of course, everything we've discussed regarding the challenge of introducing genuinely new ideas into what has already been done in the past. If you've been eagerly waiting all this time for the next chapter in Bandai Namco's epic series, you'll find exactly what you were looking for here: an air combat game made with a great deal of passion that excels in areas such as its controls, mission design, story, graphics, and audio, which will satisfy even the most demanding players. And yes, we're looking at one of the biggest releases of 2026—one that, at the very least, deserves to be considered among the year's best games.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve shows the jet-fighting franchise at its best, with a fantastic story that expands on Strangereal and a variety of fun multiplayer modes.

Ace Combat 8 Wings of Theve proves that, after more than thirty years, the series can still surprise us! It’s a game that brings the fantasy of aerial combat to life: visually spectacular, with gameplay that’s easy to grasp and instantly exhilarating. Its cinematics make the experience deeply immersive, while the weather adds to the spectacle and changes the way we play. In short, it’s a winning blend of substance and style.

Wings of Theve is a fantastic game worthy of a series that has been going strong for 30 years. With its striking visuals, immersive sense of warfare, and well-written characters, I can confidently say that it manages to take the series one step further in every respect.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve brilliantly captures the romantic thrill of flight through a tightly crafted, movie-quality narrative and an expanded tactical system. Honoring 30 years of franchise history with outstanding polish, it delivers one of the most breathtaking gaming experiences of the year.

On the whole, Ace Combat 8 feels like a genuine extension of everything that came before it. The developers have repeatedly stated in previews that the intention of the game has always been to deliver that feeling of being an ace pilot. Whether it be in the missions that encourage repeated approaches with different loadouts, multiplayer duels with your friends, or just flying high with some music on the radio, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is able to accomplish that mission with gusto.

Ace Combat 8 is still the immaculately crafted flight combat game we have all come to enjoy, but there is a more visceral aspect to the game now. From how you feel massive explosions to repeatedly breaking, as well as surpassing, the sound barrier. So I raise a humble hand of hope that this game will find its audience and that they will have a modicum of sympathy for the nomadic Sotoans even after all the carnage they have caused.

Ace Combat 8 could have reached even greater heights had its story undergone an additional edit or two, but it's hard to complain too much about this when the rest of the package is so aggressively high-quality. Here is a game that will blow your hair back, rewarding you for peeling back the layers of its flight and combat mechanics while still giving you enough room to breathe, and the result of this dynamic is one of the most elegantly designed interactive blockbusters I've ever had the pleasure of enjoying.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a triumph of sheer, thrilling joy. Dogfighting amongst the clouds is an exhilarating ride, one matched by the strength of its mechanics and brilliant presentation. While its story is a mixed success, the overall design of this aircraft is almost unparalleled, with a superbly crafted campaign and fully fledged online offering, it will keep you coming back for ever more takeoffs and engagements.
Taking another step forward for this classic series, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve brings a truly cinematic outlook to its special brand of arcade-infused dogfighting.

We had to wait seven years for the release of Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, but it was well worth it. The story campaign is everything I expected as a fan of the series – its minor flaws in no way detract from the fact that this is a bigger, better and more visually stunning game than its predecessor. It doesn’t break anything that worked before; instead, it takes the already high quality of the previous instalments and raises it even further – I’m absolutely delighted.

Most importantly of all, there’s always an assumption with flight combat games that you’re in for something pretty inaccessible. Either it’ll be an arcade game that will require twitch reflexes to be enjoyable on any level, or it’ll be something that may as well be a training simulation for the real air force for what it demands you learn. Ace Combat is not like that at all. It can certainly be challenging, but it is also clearly aware that, with its production values, it may well be the first dogfighting simulation for many players, and it does a brilliant job of giving them a game they can love.
A new series best, that mixes fantastic graphics with impressively accessible gameplay, that you can play like a straight action game or a more open-ended simulator.

Ace Combat remains the quintessential combat-pilot fantasy in gaming. The eighth instalment brings the largest campaign in the series yet, filled with excellent missions and accompanied by jaw-dropping visuals and satisfyingly arcade-style gameplay that lets us experience thrilling dogfights.
Skies packed with enemies and a soundtrack that makes you feel invincible - Ace Combat is back in a big way.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers thrilling aerial combat, stunning visuals, and accessible controls that reward practice and precision. Its remarkably smooth performance on PS5 makes every dogfight a pleasure. The lack of Spanish voice acting makes radio chatter difficult to follow amid the action, and the steep asking price may deter newcomers, but this remains an outstanding aerial combat experience.

A virtually flawless blockbuster, Ace Combat 8 is breathtaking in the intensity of its missions, exhilarating in its music, and stunning in its visuals. Much longer than its predecessor, the multiplayer extends the experience almost indefinitely.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve elevates the series’ established formula with a dramatic campaign, accessible yet deep aerial combat, and extensive customization that encourages experimentation across every mission. Its spectacular visuals and a multiplayer component with strong long-term potential round out an experience that stands as a must-play for fans of the genre.

Ace Combat 8 delivers the scale and spectacle befitting the culmination of the series' 30-year history. Detailed character portrayals deepen the immersion, while the missions expertly build tension before releasing it in bursts of catharsis. With its online modes rounding out the package, it's hard to imagine a better gift for longtime 'aces.'

Graphically, Wings of Theve is a major step forward, the aircraft are beautifully detailed, and the dogfights are among the best moments the series has to offer. Still, the new Ace Combat contains just a little too much repetition to be truly groundbreaking.

In the single-player campaign, Bandai Namco delivers exactly what one would expect, eschewing any major experiments in modernizing the arcade-style gameplay. It features the familiar high-octane aerial combat and spectacular special missions, such as having to stop a state-of-the-art warship in the middle of a city. While the ultimately conservative approach means there isn't a massive leap forward, aside from the improved graphics, the developers succeed in maintaining roughly the same high standard set dye the previous title.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve makes the seven-year wait worthwhile with
intense aerial combat, accessible controls, and a diverse range of
missions. Piloting both fighter jets and support aircraft adds variety
to the gameplay, while the sense of speed and thrilling aerial
engagements create an immersive experience. With a cinematic campaign
reminiscent of Top Gun, memorable characters, and well-crafted action
sequences, the game offers a compelling and thoroughly enjoyable
experience.

When it's all said and done there remains little better than
turning on a dime right into the sights of an onrushing enemy pilot and
tapping for the release of a locked-on missile before sailing through
the resulting debris. Smart additions, including the debris and chain reaction systems,
coupled with the more realistic weather effects and sense of scale make
it so that Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one such outing that
resoundingly sticks its landing.

For every modern combat aviation enthusiast, living out your own Top Gun story is surely the dream. Ace Combat 8 fulfils this dream to perfection — not just through excellent action, but also thanks to its story and characters. Just remember to don a pair of oversized aviator sunglasses every now and again to overlook the graphical flaws.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is Ace Combat—and that says it all. There is a reason it remains the longest-running and most acclaimed series in the arcade aerial combat genre—a genre that has, unfortunately, been increasingly forgotten over the years. The world of Strangereal is in better shape than ever, offering a dynamic and immersive gameplay experience that appeals to both longtime fans and newcomers alike. In telling its story—a tale of geopolitical intrigue, super-weapons, and, above all, people and their personal struggles—it also reflects something of us and the world we live in today.

Visually, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a feast for the eyes, even accounting for the usual tricks Bandai Namco has long employed to create a striking visual impact. The cloud rendering is spectacular once again. The aircraft models boast an incredible level of detail, while explosions and other special effects do justice to the current generation of hardware. On closer inspection, the environments also feature sharp textures and are packed with buildings, forests, and structures that—while certainly cruder than the rest—do not look out of place. Finally, instances of slowdown are extremely rare—minimal enough to have absolutely no negative impact on the gameplay experience.

Ace Combat doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel to be able to offer a fantastic and thrilling experience. Regardless of whether you are a veteran or just playing the series for the first time, this is a great game that deserves your time.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the newest iteration of the famous flight simulator franchise, and it arrived with a bang. With incredible visuals and a campaign featuring several interesting missions, players will find an adventure in the skies full of excitement. The online multiplayer mode is fun and promises a lot, although we need more time to observe its execution. Whether you're a die-hard fan of the series or a newcomer who enjoys jet planes, this is a great addition to your library.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers on all its promises (or nearly so), offering series fans exactly what they have been waiting seven years for. By combining exhilarating flight mechanics with solid technical execution, Project Aces has delivered a fighter jet built for victory. While the single-player campaign occasionally suffers from pacing issues, the thrill of soaring through the clouds remains undiminished—further extended by an ambitious multiplayer mode. Despite legitimate questions regarding its online business model, this new installment proves that the franchise rules the skies of the "10th Art."

Ace Combat 8 draws you in with its stunning graphics and keeps you hooked with its intense action! The excellent aerial combat will appeal to longtime fans of the series and newcomers alike, with plenty of varied solo missions for everyone to enjoy. There’s a lot on offer, too, with co-op and multiplayer modes adding even more to the experience. Playing offline, however, means having to put up with rather ineffective wingmen and difficulty spikes that can sometimes feel unfair. But none of that really matters, because the sheer thrill of dogfights and air-to-ground attacks makes these shortcomings easy to forgive. If you’re looking for aerial combat that strikes the perfect balance between arcade action and simulation, you’ll be hard-pressed to find anything better.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve reopens the hangar and aircraft carrier doors, bringing comprehensive updates to the formula aimed at lending the series a new sense of maturity. It builds upon the solid foundations of past installments, inheriting mechanics that—while neither new nor revolutionary—remain consistently effective. Not everyone will appreciate this conservative approach, yet it is inherent to the game's nature. Visually, the shift to a new graphics engine and the use of the "Cloudy" system are noticeable, and the plot features interesting twists, even if the narrative pacing is somewhat uneven. None of this, however, should stop flight enthusiasts from climbing aboard and taking to the skies.

While the Ace Combat series often flies under the radar, Wings of Theve is definitely the one you don’t want to miss. It outdoes its predecessor with a wider variety of missions, a more grounded narrative, great characters, and more satisfying gameplay. The presentation is also outstanding, with sound design and its musical score taking center stage, with the former a strong contender for this year’s best. There are problems with its multiplayer features— particularly its monetization and online servers—but thankfully they don’t affect the core single-player experience, which remains unmatched in the combat flight simulation genre.

Ace Combat 8: Wing of Theves is an immensely satisfying entry in the long-running series. Between the tense air battles and great plane roster, there's something so satisfying about picking a fighter jet and rocketing into the skies. Celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, Bandai Namco's latest entry in the series delivers a best of entry with incredible single-player, thrilling multiplayer, and thrill of taking to the the skies wrapped into one game.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers a dizzying thrill ride of a campaign that’s brilliantly paced. I just wish its overall packaging as a product were in any way in line with the messaging it attempts to deliver through its story.

Ace Combat 8 takes the simple, stupid joy of flying a fighter jet, piles an emotionally charged amount of drama on top of it, and somehow convinces you the fate of this anime world genuinely hinges on whether you can get one more target locked.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a fantastic game, offering a spectacular campaign packed with many missions, satisfying progression and some of the best audiovisual presentation the series has seen. The multiplayer takes a step forward and has plenty of potential, although it still needs some tweaking before it truly takes off. It may occasionally lack some legroom and proper in-flight service, but Ace Combat 8 delivers a mostly turbulence-free flight that fans of the series shouldn't miss.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve takes the successful formula of previous games and improves it in almost every way possible. The new cloud technology gives us breathtaking skies and offers players a lot more strategic depth than ever before. The story didn't interest me at all, and the QTE events feel like a drag to push through. However, story aside, the campaign offers plenty of opportunities to experiment with your squadron and customized aircraft, while the online component gives veterans a lot of what they've been asking for. A thrilling new cockpit experience for sure.

Ultimately, when it came time for me to eject from AC8, I was left with the impression of something fun but not flawless. Target-selection nonsense, overcooked dialogue and some not-so-novel decisions that decelerate the pacing keep it from being a perfect sortie. But when Wings of Theve is firing on all afterburners, it delivers exactly the kind of high-speed, high-altitude blockbuster nonsense I wanted from it.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the most sure-footed the series has ever been, confidently refining its punchy aerial gameplay and doubling down on a more cinematic story. While there are some wobbles here and there, the much improved presentation, charming character performances, varied campaign, and deeper multiplayer experience offer up a sequel that makes a textbook landing.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is an incredibly exciting action game that works for both new pilots and veterans. The story, the technical aspects, the progression system... it all works very well, except for a single element that clearly holds it back: its treatment of the protagonist, which doesn’t fit how the story wants to be told.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve feels like the franchise’s final form, offering an experience that feels both familiar and fresh. It brings together the very best elements the series has to offer.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve still has some growing to do on the ground, with a story that never quite lands its biggest ideas and first-person scenes that keep you out of the cockpit longer than they should. Once you’re in the air, though, it’s the best Ace Combat has ever felt.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is yet another brilliant entry in the Ace Combat series, with a lengthy campaign and fun multiplayer. There are some minor annoyances, but once you're in the air dogfighting, they're easy to overlook.

Ace Combat 8 builds on the foundations laid by its predecessor, a game that modernised the franchise. With enhanced graphics, improved technology and a commitment to the essence of the series, these arcade-style flights offer a more immersive experience.

While I didn’t find its story particularly compelling and a few missions don’t work, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is still a thrilling adventure because piloting these planes feels incredible. There aren’t many games released in 2026 that feel better on a moment-to-moment basis.

The Wings of Theve campaign is definitely better than its predecessor. Also the online side has been taken to new heights. Combined with improved technical aspects, Namco takes this long running series to a new level.
One or two dud missions and an uneven story do little to dull the shine of 2026’s most breathless, invigorating action game.

Wings of Theve is above all an entertaining, spectacular, gorgeous, and somewhat ridiculously melodramatic flight arcade. If you embrace that approach, you'll get the most impressive aerial action there is. For veterans of the series, returning to the cockpit is practically a mandatory call of duty, while newcomers needn't worry about attending flight school before taking off.

It's hard to imagine a game like this coming out fully formed without the decades of iteration that got us here, and in some ways it is merely a current-generation update of Ace Combats past. But it's an update that uses the tools at hand to achieve maximum velocity. [Issue#430, p.104]

Seven years since the last release, Ace Combat remains just as much fun. The eighth entry in the main series expands upon and improves almost every aspect, and it is easily among the best combat flight simulators available.

After seven long years away, Ace Combat returns in fine form with a polished, ambitious eighth installment boasting a sublime atmosphere. It accomplishes the impressive feat of satisfying longtime fans and newcomers alike, and it is easy to find an unexpected passion for the majesty of its skies and dogfights. These unique sensations are paired with a single-player campaign that is far denser and more varied than usual, taking the series into the most ambitious territory it has ever flown over...Yet, the package is not without its missteps, and one ultimately wishes that Ace Combat 8 would push its approach further while shedding the issues that continue to hound it. The action still lacks clarity and visibility, there is a distinct lack of endgame content for the single-player mode, and the progression system reveals weaknesses that prevent the experience from reaching the absolute heights it was destined for. Bandai Namco comes tantalizingly close to perfection, but make no mistake: this entry is easily one of the most accomplished in the entire franchise.

In terms of gameplay, it’s good old Ace Combat. Nothing more, nothing
less. Yet no other instalment in the series has given me quite so much
excitement – this virtual war really shook me to the core.

If you’re a fan of the Ace Combat series and don’t mind a bit of Japanese silliness while fighting for your country’s survival in a high-tech fighter jet, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve could very well be right up your alley.
The best aerial combat the series has ever had alongside some of its best mission design.
The arcade air combat series soars to dizzying new heights.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is both one of the strongest entry points for newcomers, and still a treat for longtime fans.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve picks up where Ace Combat 7 left off, underlining that the series is well and truly back to its best

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is everything we could have hoped for. It features a much longer, compelling story, a ton of different fighter jets at your disposal and some of the best combat in any air combat game.
Ace Combat 8 refines what its predecessors did well and introduces an exceptional story and cast of characters to really add depth to this arcade series.
If the other games in this series are even half as good as AC8, then Ace Combat is unquestionably the best game franchise.
The game generates blood-pumping moments as you twist, turn and weave through the skies, while your locked-on missiles speed away to obliterate an enemy plane
Ace Combat is back with Wings of Theve, and although the campaign doesn't hit all the right notes, it's still a classic Ace Combat experience.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve knows exactly what it wants to be and doesn't waste time chasing a realism that isn't its forte.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve captures the intensity of aerial warfare better than any other title.
Ace Combat 8 straddles the line between arcade destruction and military precision, with some melodrama thrown in for good measure.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve has a lot going for it. It's full to the brim with plane customization, a bucket load of missions, and a lengthy story. Despite some pacing and difficulty issues, it's a fine addition to the series.
In Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, you play as a would-be ace pilot who starts out flying in the back seat of a fighter jet, as navigator to a fella na...

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a great action game and one of the best entries in the franchise so far, with the only major caveat being the incoherent and impenetrable story told in the 30-hour-long campaign mode.

I waited years for Ace Combat to come back, and Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve reminded me exactly why I missed it. One minute I’m admiring my plane, and the next I’m dodging a damn railgun while my squad is yelling over the comms and the soundtrack has me ready to take on everything in the sky. The targeting did get on my nerves during a few crucial moments, and some aircraft take longer to unlock than I would have liked, but those complaints barely put a dent in the fun.

Between the combat, story, soundtrack, and sheer spectacle of it all, Ace Combat 8 delivers exactly the kind of experience I had been waiting years for. It’s easily one of the best games in the series, and I loved damn near every moment of it.

For many players, the Ace Combat series means far more than the games themselves. It is hard to find anything else quite like Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, a game that lets you tear through such magnificent clouds with complete freedom. You can move fast enough to outrun sound and wind, yet the sky still feels endless. That romance of feeling both insignificant and extraordinary at the same time is exactly why this series deserves to continue.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve manages to improve over its predecessor, while also offering a host of content for those that enjoy air warfare.

One of the best Ace Combat games, offering dozens of spectacular and exciting missions that keep you coming back. The story isn't the most engaging, and the multiplayer is marred by microtransactions, but flying and shooting are fun, and that's what matters most.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a very good flight-combat game. Its story has surprising depth while still delivering the series' signature dose of action. The arcade-focused controls remain approachable, and additions such as wingman commands, midair refueling, and takeoff and landing sequences give simulation fans a few more mechanics to appreciate without making the game significantly more intimidating. The lengthy campaign is complemented by a multiplayer mode with plenty of staying power, even if its rotating game types can be frustrating. Add in the excellent presentation, strong audio, and impressive visuals, and Wings of Theve delivers an experience that should keep Ace Combat fans occupied until the next entry arrives.
If other publishers looked after their series as well as Bandai Namco looks after Ace Combat, the world would be a better place

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers a truly first-rate and polished fighter jet combat experience. The strong character writing adds considerable value to the story, while the excellent level design makes the campaign consistently enjoyable, allowing you to fully experience the excitement—and at times, the tension—of its intense aerial battles. The game’s high-quality visuals and sound effects, along with its impressive variety of aircraft and upgrade options, further complement these strengths. All of these elements come together to make Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve arguably unmatched within its genre. If you’re a fan of the series or the genre, it’s an experience that is sure to leave a lasting impression.

As a fast-paced, arcade-style action game, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers the adrenaline-fueled experience fans have come to expect and keeps them satisfied all the way to the end. However, it does little to attract players who have never connected with the Ace Combat series over the years, as it doesn’t introduce enough new mechanics or ideas to bring something fresh to the table.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Thrones offers a great story, rock-solid gameplay, and an excellent soundtrack, along with interesting online modes and a very good single-player campaign.
A very competent entry for one of the most respected arcade air combat game series. Particularly of note is the inclusion of choices in gameplay and squadro customization.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is genuinely a phenomenal game that has had such an insane grip on me. 2026 has been an absolutely jam packed year full of amazing games, but you are seriously doing yourself a disservice by not experiencing Ace Combat 8.

Ace Combat series is arguably the sole survivor of a once upon a time thriving genre that spawned from Strike Commander, one that combines cinematic storytelling and exciting air combat. Ace Combat 8 is not just a worthy successor of this pedigree but one of the best games of this year regardless of genre.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers an incredible single-player campaign, thrilling dogfights, and a phenomenal soundtrack, despite its underwhelming multiplayer. It wants you to experience the fantasy of being one of the greatest pilots known to man. And once you get to the credits, it’ll leave a smile on your face, leaving you wishing you could experience it for the first time all over again.

ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE offers superb aerial combat, impressive graphics, an excellent soundtrack and a story that keeps you hooked. Unfortunately, however, these qualities are let down by an underdeveloped PC version, particularly the problematic HOTAS support, unconvincing mouse controls and complications with certain controllers. Add to that technical shortcomings, long loading times for some set-ups and limited customisation options, and you end up with a game that is capable of more than it ultimately delivers. If you’re the proud owner of a powerful PC, everything works as it should, and you have a supported gamepad or HOTAS, you’re in for an epic experience that you won’t want to put down.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the kind of game you either love or you don’t. New installments aren’t released every year, which makes it much easier to see the progress being made with the franchise. Everything looks better in this entry, and the gameplay feels just a bit more refined. In terms of story, not much has changed—but that’s not why you play Ace Combat. The action is solid, and the online mode offers a fantastic experience when it comes to flying and shooting things down.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the most intense games of the year. The developers have pushed the audiovisual experience to its absolute limits, delivering one epic moment after another across 30 hours of gameplay. The only weak point is the lacklustre story, which never manages to match the sheer grandeur of the gameplay.

Overall Ace Combat 8 Wings of Theve is a game that I recommend you go out and play immediately. Whether you’re a fan of arcade style flight sims or not, the game is just so good that you’ll immediately be hooked and want more. Bandai Namco and Project Aces have once again delivered a truly great game and the fact that there’s a thriving online multiplayer community for the game really sweetens the deal too.

ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE is clear proof of how one can remain faithful to one's roots while embracing technical modernity and narrative ambition. Project Aces reaches one of the highest peaks ever reached by the entire franchise, thanks to a work able to charm newcomers to arcade flight with well-calibrated accessibility. At the same time, it is perfectly able to make the hearts of Strangereal veterans beat faster. Despite a slightly measured campaign opening and a multiplayer side that is still a bit immature, the incredible variety of the campaign missions, the depth of the gameplay, a gleaming technical side and a soundtrack that gives you chills make this chapter a must-buy for all fans of the series and beyond. The king of the digital skies is back.

Breathtaking visuals and strategic cloud mechanics make Ace Combat 8 the best in the series. While bogged down by an odd story and frustrating boss fights, the phenomenal core dogfighting easily carries the day.
While the story drags in places and fumbles some heavy themes, that bumpy runway still doesn’t prevent Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve from taking to the skies.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the most polished and confident release in the series
Ace Combat 8 understands that fighter jets are cool. This is probably why it connected with me as much as it did.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve marks a glorious return for the franchise after seven years, one that feels better to play and is more intense than ever before.

Ace Combat 8: Wings Of Theve was one of my most anticipated games of 2026 and it delivered beyond even my lofty hopes and dreams for this game. It’s great story and fantastic characters help compliment the ace of this game, the aerial combat. Flying a fighter jet has never felt more satisfying. Some small pet peeves aside, Ace Combat 8 is one of the years best.
With Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Project Aces has produced a particularly comprehensive instalment, driven by an excellent campaign and flying mechanics that are as impressive as ever.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve really impressed me. Although some of the missions were duds, and the multiplayer is a little light on modes, this is air combat at its best. Fluid controls, incredible visuals, and one hell of a campaign make this a game I can easily recommend. If you’ve been clamouring for something in the air combat genre, then you need look no further!

With all that said, I’ll be giving Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve the Thumb Culture Gold Award!

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is an almost perfect game. The developers have done an outstanding job of implementing new technical features while preserving the series signature atmosphere. As a result, both veterans and newcomers will have a fantastic time playing it.

If you are in the mood to be an ace pilot and want to see what Bandai Namco does best, Ace Combat is where you need to look. When it comes to the series, Wings of Theve is one of the best entries yet, showing that the Aces team isn’t slowing down anytime soon. Instead, it is continuing to push the limits that the series has to offer to new heights.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers thrilling, accessible aerial combat with an interesting story, near-photorealistic visuals at its best and around 30 missions, a great new chapter despite minor stutters and weak ground textures.

From the high-level plot to gameplay that embraces both newcomers and veterans, to an exceptional technical department on PC, Ace Combat 8 represents a huge step forward. For the first time in the series, war isn't told only as a succession of military missions; it also makes room for the psychological consequences of the conflict, the weight of collective expectations, and the construction of heroes. All in all, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is without the slightest doubt the best entry in the series.

This is the best installment in the series to date. Project Aces has managed to create a massive, varied, and spectacular campaign that shines not only for its aerial combat but also for a surprisingly deep story, full of meaningful messages and characters that ultimately leave a lasting impression.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve reaffirms why the franchise continues to lead the aerial combat genre. It is a polished, visually stunning, and immensely entertaining experience that no fan of action and aviation games should miss. It is well worth experiencing.

Ace Combat 8 is absolutely stunning. Even knowing the franchise's history and how talented the team at Project Aces is when it comes to making flight combat games, I don't think anyone expected something THIS good. Responsive controls, masterful mission design, flawless audiovisual presentation, and a multiplayer mode that feels like a complete game in its own right.
Wings of Theve tells the legendary story of an ace pilot who single-handedly carries an entire nation on his shoulders, but the truth is, Bandai Namco is the one carrying the entire aerial combat genre on its shoulders.
This tradition began back on the original PlayStation, and it's wonderful to see that it's still alive and thriving to this day.

Ace Combat 8: Wings Of Theve: Ace Combat 8: Wings Of Theve delivers excellent aerial combat, varied missions, intense dogfights and spectacular boss encounters, while its improved presentation and outstanding soundtrack further strengthen the overall experience. The story and some of its characters have their weaknesses, but it is difficult not to get caught up in the action when you are in the middle of a massive aerial battle trying to outmaneuver an enemy ace. Project Aces has delivered one of the strongest arcade flight shooters in the series and a very successful return after a long wait. – NikolaOtasevic

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers an immersive aerial combat experience with spectacular visuals, accessible controls, and a varied campaign of around 30 missions. Its cinematic first-person sequences and intense dogfights make the conflict feel more personal, while the expanded multiplayer offers plenty of content to keep players engaged. Although the story can be predictable and some missions and dialogue slow the pace, it’s a strong return for the franchise that successfully balances accessibility and excitement.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers a surprisingly gripping narrative about propaganda and war legends without sacrificing its signature, spectacular flight combat. With the great balance of controls that cater to both new players and veterans, Wings of Theve offers some of the best dogfighting in franchise history. Dynamic weather and hefty flight physics push the adrenaline to entirely new heights.

ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE is a must-have title because when you find yourself soaring through its skies, flying through clouds as you search for your next target, or listening to your squadron over the radio, the game manages to convey exactly that feeling of being an elite pilot. The campaign, the variety of aircraft, the progression, and spectacular audiovisuals come together to form a very solid package. Yes, ACE COMBAT is back, and it maintains an outstanding standard.

A strong campaign and exhilarating combat help Wings of Theve rise above its turbulence.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers the thrilling dogfights, rewarding progression and cinematic spectacle the series is known for, backed by impressive visuals, strong audio design and excellent performance. While a steep learning curve, occasional mission frustrations and an underdeveloped multiplayer component hold it back from reaching greater heights, fans of the franchise will find plenty to enjoy, while newcomers willing to learn its systems will discover an exciting aerial adventure.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivered one of the best aerial combat experiences in the series, thanks to enjoyable gameplay, diverse missions, and a weather system that adds real depth to the battles. However, it fails to fully utilize its story ideas and characters the way they deserve. Despite the clear improvement in gameplay and missions, it remains a strong and enjoyable experience for military flight fans, proving that the series is still capable of delivering unforgettable aerial dogfights.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is, without a doubt, everything the fans were hoping for. The campaign delivers spectacular dogfights, an engaging story and some of the most stunning skies ever seen in a game. At the same time, the online mode ensures that dozens of hours of gaming fun await you even after you’ve completed the campaign. Are you interested in aeroplanes or have you always wanted to take part in dogfights? Then you simply must get your hands on Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve. Roger that?

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is another brilliant release in the series that brings together pulse-pounding dogfighting with sublime mission design. I found myself hooked into the narrative from start to end (weird bits and all), whilst the satisfying sense of progress, varied gameplay, and rewarding mechanics ensures that there’s a high standard across every aspect of the game’s design. I simply cannot praise it enough, and whether you’re a long-time fan of the series or a newcomer that wants to scratch that dogfighting itch, you’re going to love Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve pushes the series’ arcade formula further with deep combat, dynamic weather and missions that demand careful management of speed, positioning and weapons. Its surprisingly human story also turns the squadron into far more than simple wingmen.

Wings of Theve is the best entry in the franchise and one of the most beautiful games released this year. It's accessible, tremendously exhilarating, and so much fun that any complaints feel minor compared to what you get.

After years away from Ace Combat, returning with Wings of Theve feels like rediscovering an old favorite in spectacular form. Its gorgeous skies, accessible arcade dogfighting, stirring soundtrack, and massive battles make the series’ familiar formula thrilling again. Yet uneven pacing, repetitive objectives, and story interruptions keep its new ideas from feeling revolutionary. Still, when the action clicks, Ace Combat 8 delivers an exhilarating comeback.

The latest entry in the long-running series is another win for Bandai Namco. While it doesn’t bring anything particularly innovative to either the genre or the series itself, it ultimately succeeds thanks to its excellent blend of gameplay, presentation, and soundtrack.
Bandai Namco wants to introduce its airplane series to the whole world, and with each new installment, it continues to raise the bar to make that happen.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a gem of an action flight sim worth every penny and time spent on it. A complete package, if you will. A new standard bearer not just for Ace Combat games, but those involving aerial combat in general. The genre is truly back and we can't wait to see more of you get your grubby hands on this.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of those games that remind you why you love video games. It's not perfect, and its story is the weakest link, but the overall experience is excellent.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is everything I wanted from the next game in the series - a full-blown return to form.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers a strong arcade flight campaign, with missions that keep things fresh, an aircraft tree that's satisfying to climb, skies worth staring at, and a genuinely excellent soundtrack. The story has some great moments, and the flying is a blast from the first mission to the last.

Even if you’re not a fan of the franchise or simply haven’t jumped on board yet, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve serves up some incredible gameplay, wedged in between stunning visuals and a memorable story.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a love letter to military aviation, with a massive variety of iconic aircraft, a corny yet action-packed campaign full of brilliant set pieces, and gorgeous backdrops throughout. Whether you’re a casual fan or an aviation geek, there’s plenty of fun for everyone.
One of the most breathtaking aerial warfare spectacles crafted for video games to date. An absolute must-play for any combat aviation enthusiast.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is, in many ways, the pinnacle of a series that is no stranger to excellence. Adrenaline-fueled, breathtaking, and incredibly fun, Bandai Namco Aces’ latest title doesn’t reinvent a formula that already worked perfectly well, but it takes it to its absolute peak thanks to controls that are more responsive than ever, top-notch cinematic direction, and a cast of characters capable of stirring emotions far beyond expectations. The soundtrack, once again, is spectacular. There are still some issues with PC optimization that need addressing, a few narrative elements that feel too superficial, overly verbose briefings, and a certain reluctance to innovate in the gameplay—but these are minor flaws that do little to detract from what, all things considered, is one of the most successful titles of the year.

It is difficult not to highlight how much the wingmen contribute to this experience. Their presence during operations, the commands we can give them, the ability to configure their aircraft and, most importantly, the personalities presented in the cinematics make them much more important than simply occupying space in the sky. Combined with the variety of the 30 missions, the preparation before each operation, the different aircraft classes, upgrades and battles against major targets, the campaign maintains a very high level of quality throughout almost its entire duration. My favorite mission was the first attack on the land battleship, precisely because it brings several of these elements together and requires a different approach compared to conventional combat.

Ace Combat 8 gave me the most enjoyable aerial combat experience I have ever had. The night missions accompanied by a memorable soundtrack, the constant progression in difficulty, the large-scale battles, the presence of the wingmen and, above all, the ability to play with a flight stick made a huge difference to my experience. The game is accessible enough for someone who is not a simulator specialist to learn, while also offering enough depth for that same player to notice their own improvement as they progress. I started out needing to adapt to the controls and ended up much more comfortable with the flight stick, making decisions about aircraft, weapons, allies and positioning almost naturally. With an exceptional campaign and an impressive variety of possibilities in each operation, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve establishes itself as a landmark for the franchise and as the most complete and enjoyable aerial combat experience I have ever had.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve ultimately does exactly what a new installment in this series should do. The flying feels fantastic, the missions are spectacular, and unlocking increasingly better aircraft ensures you constantly want to play just one more mission. Graphically, it is also a significant step forward. The aircraft are highly detailed, the enormous cloud formations really add something to the gameplay, and small details like water droplets on the cockpit window do a lot for the feel.

Bandai Namco, you beautiful, beautiful people, you did it. You nailed Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, creating one of the most compelling war games that I have played through. This is coming from somebody who wasn’t a big fan of the last one either. The narrative is engaging and compelling, even when playing out with six different players in the middle of explosions and absolute chaos. And that gameplay? Engaging, whether you have been playing these games your entire life or are looking to try one for the first time. This is a big, bold Mission Accomplished.

It’s very rare for me to have high expectations for a game and then have it exceed them, but Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve was one of those cases. An incredibly fun game that expands its universe in interesting ways and manages to tell a relevant and human story, but is imperfect due to an online mode that embodies the worst aspects of the medium. Still, it’s a title that will certainly vie for a spot among the series’ top favorites—a spot where competition is fierce. And, living up to its subtitle, this is a game that gives me great hope for the future of this series.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is the installment the series deserved after years of silence: richer, more polished, and more refined than its predecessor—and perhaps the entire series—in every aspect.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve feels like a modern continuation of a formula that already knew what it wanted to be. It takes the fundamentals that have worked since the series' earlier days and surrounds them with a larger campaign and production values that let the concept breathe.

If I had to summarize Ace Combat 8 in a single word, I’d initially struggle to do so, as the game deserves pretty much every praiseworthy adjective I could throw at it. But if I had to pick just one, I’d go with “epic.” It completely immerses you in its world thanks to a thrilling story, great visuals, intuitive controls, lovable characters, and a series of missions that almost always manages to one up whatever came before.

While it has a few shortcomings, such as repetitive missions, audio mixing issues, and aggressive multiplayer microtransactions, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve successfully recaptures the magic of aerial combat. With strong visuals, an innovative cloud system, and an ambitious story, it delivers the authentic Ace Combat experience that fans have been missing for so long.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve delivers thrilling aerial combat with responsive controls, cinematic battles, and engaging large-scale encounters, while its story explores heroism and identity amid a devastating war.
While the story gets bogged down with prior knowledge of the world, it’s backed up by a fun cast of characters that makes it worth investing time into.

«Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve» offers little innovation, instead refining the proven formula with frantic jet action. Varied missions, adrenaline-fueled dogfights and an epic soundtrack create unique action moments, while the new online modes add some variety. Microtransactions are a bit annoying, and stutters in Fidelity mode hurt the presentation. Still, the single-player campaign delivers jet action in perfection.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is not the niche hardcore game you think it is. It’s an impressive, accessible aerial combat fighter with visuals and sound design that really seal you into the cockpit. Accompanied by a story that, although it has a few missteps and a lot to take in at first, is a story full of passion that tackles a lot of great ideas and layers on anime-inspired moments. This entry is a great time to step into this respected franchise.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve marks a spectacular return for the franchise, delivering intense aerial combat, a memorable campaign, deep tactical options and a stunning visual upgrade. Its mix of strategy, cinematic moments and explosive dogfights makes it an impressive evolution of the series.

ACE COMBAT 8: Wings of Theve delivers some of the series' finest aerial combat, spectacular skies and wonderfully varied missions. Uneven pacing and underdeveloped themes hold it back slightly, but this is Ace Combat flying near its very best.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a triumphant return for one of gaming’s most enduring aerial combat franchises, delivering an exceptional package that excels across nearly every category. Longtime fans will simply relish this moment, and newcomers stepping into the cockpit for the first time are in for a hell of a ride. Its heartfelt war story, memorable cast of characters, exhilarating arcade-style flight mechanics, deep aircraft customization, and varied mission design come together to create an experience that is both accessible and rewarding. More importantly, it never loses sight of what has made Ace Combat special for decades: the thrill of taking to the skies and emerging victorious against overwhelming odds.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the biggest surprises of the year, delivering exhilarating aerial combat alongside an unexpectedly emotional story, memorable characters, varied missions, satisfying aircraft management, gorgeous visuals, and an outstanding soundtrack. A late tutorial, initially confusing Aircraft Tree, one overly drawn-out boss encounter, and occasional crashes hold it back slightly, but the sheer joy of flying and the strength of its campaign make this a fantastic return for the series.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is, in many respects, the most accomplished version of a series formula that has worked for decades.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve soars with thrilling dogfights, a grounded yet explosive story, standout cinematic moments, and online modes that keep players flying long after the credits.

Ace Combat 8 is the best the series has ever looked and felt, providing gamers with an opportunity to command your crew and flight at top speeds to down the enemy. The gunplay and flight takes a little time to acclimatise, though once in the groove you’ll be successfully navigating the danger zone. With plenty of missions, music tracks and skill tree options, the game houses enough meat to keep you flying for the FCU alongside Joker Flight for countless hours.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is undoubtedly one of the most comprehensive and ambitious entries in the franchise's thirty-year history. Bandai Namco has successfully refined the flight mechanics to perfection, offering highly accessible gameplay backed by stunning visuals and audio, as well as a wide variety of missions. While it suffers from minor pacing issues in the campaign's narrative and occasional frustration regarding target locking, the game's strengths far outweigh its shortcomings. It is a solid experience that not only satisfies series veterans but also sets an incredibly high standard for the genre once again. Now, it remains to be seen how the multiplayer component evolves, but that is a story for another time.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve doesn't try to reinvent the franchise—and that was the right call. It understands what works. It expands the campaign, improves character interactions, and gives greater weight to your squadron. Missions feature far more variety, weather systems are used in more compelling ways, and the visual leap is massive. To top it off, it delivers a much more ambitious multiplayer mode than I expected.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve made me feel like an idiot for the first few hours, and I’m grateful for it. Once I stopped expecting Top Gun and started flying the way the game wanted me to, it turned into one of the most immersive flying experiences I’ve ever had, backed by a grounded, surprisingly emotional story about a scared pilot wearing a dead man’s helmet and a presentation that comes very close to perfection.
Epic, deeply satisfying, and visually stunning, Ace Combat 8 is the true embodiment of the greatest aerial combat films brought to life in video game form!

One one hand wish for more bravery to try something really new with the series, on the other hand I enjoy that Ace Combat 8 delivers exactly what fans can expect, just prettier and a bit more dynamic.

For all of its quirks, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve ultimately delivers exactly the sort of ridiculous aerial spectacle I was hoping for. There are a few rough edges here and the story borders on melodrama at times, but when everything comes together, there’s very little that compares to the feeling of pulling off some ridiculous high-G manoeuvre, watching your target explode, and immediately looking for the next enemy to shoot down.

Ace Combat 8 is a fun and exciting experience that will satisfy fans of the series and warplane games. While the story mode offers only a small improvement over the previous game, the online mode is a big step forward for the series thanks to its variety and content. This also makes it a promising entry point for newcomers to Ace Combat.
ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE is an incredible experience, but I still find it difficult to recommend it without reservations to those who have never had contact with the franchise.

Ace Combat 8 surprised me in almost every possible way. Its arcade-focused flying remains incredibly easy to pick up while providing enough depth to make mastering its aircraft and dogfights immensely satisfying.
Ace Combat 8, as a whole, is a lot of “two steps forward, one step back.”

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a worthy heir to one of the longest-running sagas in video game history and fully embodies what Ace Combat has always been: its gameplay remains impeccable, fast-paced and visually rewarding. Some components, however, now need the courage to change their form without losing their substance. A must for fans and pleasantly vintage for veterans, it still shows its age to newer generations.
Ace Combat 8 delivers another excellent flight campaign by refining what already works, even if its ambitions rarely extend beyond the runway the series already knows.

"A Powerful Return for the Kings of the Sky"
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve offers a clear evolution of the series' formula rather than attempting to alter its identity. It blends accessible, enjoyable flight mechanics with greater depth in control and customization, alongside more varied missions and massive battles that leverage current-generation capabilities. Despite some technical issues and the limited impact of narrative choices, the strength of the aerial combat, visual variety, and sound design make for a comprehensive and ambitious arcade flight experience—one that preserves the spirit of Ace Combat while significantly expanding upon it.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve may not reinvent the series, but it delivers the most comprehensive overall package to date and presents its story more impressively than any previous entry. With a 30-mission campaign, immersive first-person cutscenes, and a stronger bond with your crew members, it offers one of the best campaigns the series has seen so far.

For veterans, the new additions are somewhat limited, with only a handful of quality-of-life features and additional animations. However, if you enjoyed the previous entry, you really can’t go wrong with Ace Combat 8.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve proves the series is still soaring high after three decades. With a strong campaign, engaging narrative, rich aircraft roster, and refined gameplay, it delivers an impressive experience for veterans and newcomers alike. Outstanding visuals and sound elevate every dogfight, and despite a few multiplayer question marks, this is a triumphant return. For anyone ready to take to the skies of Strangereal, takeoff is highly recommended.

​Ace Combat 8 is precisely what hardcore arcade flight combat fans have been waiting years for: an ambitious, worthy sequel that stays fiercely loyal to its roots while dramatically elevating the franchise’s visual and technical standards. While Strangereal’s tangled narrative web and mid-mission radio chatter might still alienate newcomers—and a couple of tedious escort objectives slipped past the cutting room floor—the electrifying gameplay, superb aircraft and mission variety, and jaw-dropping next-gen fidelity far outweigh any turbulence. Project Aces has once again proven that when it comes to white-knuckle, cinematic dogfights, no competitor can contest their dominance of the skies.
