The tasks feel like they might be helping to prepare kids for more challenging games. I do think some design choices, like characters’ eyes not moving and the handling for some event segments, aren’t the best. But this does feel like it could be one of the “good” games to pick up for a younger child.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps is quite clearly built with a younger audience in mind, but don’t let that fool you into thinking it’s little more than a lazy cash-in on a popular franchise. There’s a notable level of care taken in bringing Bluey’s world to life here, and with plenty of things to snap and activities to try, Bluey’s Happy Snaps is a wonderfully fun time for kids and their parents alike.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps is neither particularly special nor an unforgettable experience, as certain episodes of the Bluey series can genuinely be. But clearly, it didn’t need to be. My son was utterly captivated by its simplicity, charm and visual fidelity. And no matter how much I try to push Super Mario Odyssey on him, the sparkle in his eyes tells me there’s room for both.
94.1% of OpenCritic critics recommend this game (136 reviews).

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls has been the most fun I’ve had playing a fighting game in recent years. Looking forward to seeing how they expand the roster and which new characters they will introduce in the near future.

Marvel Tōkon Fighting Souls is a super fun, very accessible and utterly gorgeous fighter with enough content to keep both the hardcore and casual fighting game player busy. As revered as the Marvel vs Capcom series is, Arc System Works have done a fantastic job in taking the Marvel Tag Fighter mantle from Capcom.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is an incredible fighter that captures the high-octane, frantic fun of a superhero battle. Each character is distinct with unique abilities that add personality to every member of the roster. With a focus on assembling your team to unleash mighty combos and huge assists, this team-based battler adds a fresh spin on the genre. While there is plenty of support to aid newcomers, the number of systems in play can become overwhelming and may take time to fully understand. However, once everything clicks, the depth provides an incredibly rewarding experience that encourages experimentation and mastery.

Accessible to players of all skill levels but offering a high ceiling for pros, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is one of the best fighting games currently available. From its great selection of modes to its stunning presentation, this is a must-have for Marvel fans and fighting game enthusiasts alike.

With Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Arc System Works delivers its best work in years, creating a fighting game that will win over Marvel fans. Its gameplay strikes the perfect balance between accessibility and depth, resulting in a captivating formula that sets a new benchmark for the genre.

A new mainstay in the fighting game community has arrived. ARC SYSTEM WORKS and Marvel combine for an excellent tag-team fighter with a gorgeous art style and roster full of iconic characters in one of the better games released in the genre in recent memory.

Fresh gameplay paired with unprecedented production values make for an all-star pairing in Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls. An accessible gameplay loop paves the way for impressive depth, hopefully securing this tag fighter’s place in the FGC scene for years to come. The dodgy PC port is affecting the crossplay experience at launch, but the PS5 version is flawless and comes highly recommended – with excellent DualSense integration. Meanwhile, the offline experience isn’t quite up to the same level as genre frontrunners like Street Fighter 6, but its various comic book storylines are beautifully illustrated and excellently voiced, with writer Keiron Gillen doing a great job with the scripts. This title is a triumph on the PS5, and a reminder that Sony is capable of greenlighting compelling live service games when it puts its mind to it.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a breath of fresh air for both Marvel and the fighting game genre. Rather than recycling ideas we’ve been playing for decades, it takes a completely fresh approach that successfully blends the Marvel universe with Arc System Works’ signature brand of madness.

Marvel Tôkon: Fighting Souls is exactly the comeback Marvel fans have been waiting years for. Arc System Works once again demonstrates its mastery of the fighting genre with a game that is visually spectacular, deep in gameplay, and surprisingly accessible to new players.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is an excellent tag fighter that strikes a fantastic balance between accessibility and depth. Its 4v4 system is surprisingly approachable thanks to its emphasis on assists, while a diverse roster, excellent tutorials and plenty of unlockable rewards provide plenty of incentive to keep playing. Add in gorgeous comic-book visuals, a superb soundtrack and smooth online performance, and Arc System Works has delivered one of the strongest Marvel fighting games to date.

With MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls, Arc System Works not only brings Marvel back to the fighting game genre, but also reignites a flame that seemed to have been extinguished. Although the online mode still has some kinks to work out, its frenetic, precise, and strategic combat—coupled with spectacular visuals—makes every match a true spectacle. Marvel is back, and it’s doing so with one of the best fighting games of the year.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls sees Arc System Works take a bold gamble by reworking a familiar formula. That gamble pays off with a fighter that's both accessible and competitively deep. The limited roster and stage count barely matter due to strongly distinct characters. This is a highly capable fighting game with something to offer newcomers and veterans alike, one I expect to see plenty of on the competitive circuit in years to come.
Every match feels like it could be ripped fresh from the pages of a comic

While uncompromising in its vision and design, Arc System Works also makes sure to give beginners all the tools they need to succeed. Coupled with a killer aesthetic and a variety of enjoyable modes, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a fighting game triumph.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is everything it needed to be. The character designs and roster are fantastic, with deep skill expression for those willing to put in the time while being approachable to new players. It’s stuffed with content that actually rewards you with different colorways for playing.
Tokon is definitely the next big thing in versus fighting. The kind of game you want to keep learning, playing and watching evolve in the years to come.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a fighting game that’s difficult to explain and, for that very reason, surprisingly easy to love. Arc System Works has taken the chaos of Marvel crossovers and transformed it into something personal, capable of welcoming those who’ve never played a fighting game before without sacrificing the complexity needed to win over veterans. Its accessibility is no shortcut to banality: once you get past the surface, Tōkon demands study, muscle memory and the ability to read what’s happening on screen. Underpinning it all are an original combat system, extraordinary art direction and a love for Marvel evident in every detail. There are still a few undeniable rough edges, from the clarity of the fights – which practice can help overcome – to the difficult launch of the PC version, an issue that needs to be resolved as soon as possible for a title that relies on cross-play. But the most important impression remains: Tōkon has forged its own unique path. If Arc System Works can provide the right support, this strange and irresistible experiment could become one of the most interesting fighting games of its generation.

I may have started a little colder on Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls than I thought I’d be considering its legacy, but that very quickly faded after I spent more time with it and understood what it was trying to do. Its gorgeous style, incredible roster, and genuine evolution of the tag-fighting genre make me confident in finally being able to crown 2026's best fighting game.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is the fighting game revival Marvel absolutely needed, with its enthralling story, exhilarating anime style, and robust number of modes that will keep players coming back for more again and again. It has an incredible roster of familiar and lesser-known fighters that all play distinct from one another and are all absolutely fun to play, who may even encourage players to read some comics to learn about their pasts and current adventures. Despite its notably few flaws, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is one of the best fighting games of the decade and I cannot wait to find out which new characters will join its roster in the near future.

Arc System Works has outdone itself here, releasing another strong fighter with a real sense of dynamism, style and flourish in its delivery. It’s perfect for Marvel fans, and lays a foundation that easily involves more casual comic book fans and game players as well.

It delivers a frantic, deeply strategic 4v4 tag experience that masterfully balances accessibility for newcomers with the complexity veteran fighters crave. The stunning visual presentation and rocking soundtrack cement its status as an instant classic, although the launch roster feels slightly lean and the PC version faces optimization hurdles.

Arc System Works reaffirms its mastery of the genre with a title that succeeds on multiple fronts. Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a love letter to fans of the House of Ideas, but it is also a top-tier fighting game that appeals to a wide range of players, from casual gamers who can have fun simply using the simplified controls and gradually learning all the nuances of an original and engaging combat system, to seasoned experts who will spend hours coming up with new combos and synergies to win in the inevitable tournaments.

The latest in a long string of hits for Arc System Works, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls isn’t just the next must-have tournament fighter for esports pros, but also an essential offering for Marvel and fighting game newbies alike. Put simply, this is the finest brawler featuring Marvel characters to date, period. Your turn, Capcom.
This is the ultimate Marvel fighting game. I thought we had already peaked with MvC3, but Marvel Tokon proved me wrong.

I played a handful of matches in each offering, joining up with some friends in a custom room, challenged random players in ranked and casual matches, and explored the Open Lobby. Online connections were strong thanks to the rollback netcode under the hood, and I rarely saw any technical hiccups at all while playing on PlayStation 5...It’s here where the PC version of Tokon must be mentioned, as its launch has been, to put it lightly, disastrous.

This is not how any of us expected Marvel fighting games to come back, but I sure am glad it happened this way. Arc System Works knows what they’re doing, and it shows in every single corner of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls. At pretty much every turn, I saw polish, depth, and quality design, from the roster and story, to the wide variety of gameplay modes, to the tools to learn and grow. I wish the PC version had gotten a better start, because we’ve learned now that crossplay means that affects PS5 players, too, and nobody wants to cut their player access in half because of a bad platform experience. That and some very small gripes about mechanics and menus aside, Marvel Tokon: Figting Souls feels like a powerful new chapter in Marvel fighting, and it looks to continue to get better from here. When’s Mahvel? Mahvel is now.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is the optimal fighting game for newcomers. It’s not only visually pleasing, but it’s also filled with impressive systems that come together to create an experience that’ll keep you coming back. Each round is unique, and each fighter has a lot of potential as a main. Arc System Works found a way for veterans and newcomers to play together and, more importantly, to play to their strengths, whether through intricate combos or simple button inputs.
Marvel Tōkon is bold, beautiful and brilliant, even if the combat feels somewhat lacking in terms of variety and player agency.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a triumph across the board, at least for the PS5 version. Arc System Works has managed to craft a truly excellent fighting game, combining monumental art direction with impeccable fluidity. The introduction of the shared health bar and dual control scheme make the learning curve accessible to anyone, without compromising the extraordinary technical depth required for high-level matches, which is essential for a title that relies almost entirely on multiplayer. A great title for all fighting game fans and fans of the Marvel Universe.

When it comes to the combat system, Arc System Works set out to create an experience that anyone can enjoy, regardless of their level of experience with the genre—a goal the studio achieved brilliantly. While some might find fault with the selection of fighters, stages, or game modes, there is no denying that Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is one of the most entertaining experiences of the year, and I can't wait to see how professional players take this title to the top at EVO in the future.
Arc System Works had a big task to live up to the Marvel Vs Capcom series, but Marvel TOKON: Fighting Souls offers the strongest foundation possible to become a new FGC pillar.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a visually impressive palate cleanser after Marvel vs Capcom Infinite, delivering the kind of style and energy Arc System Works is known for. While the PC version struggled at launch, the PS5 version shows plenty of promise for this new chapter of Marvel fighting games.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is another masterpiece from Arc System Works. The Japanese developers, who specialize in fighting games, have created a title brimming with love for the Marvel universe, featuring meticulous attention to detail in the design of each hero and an incredibly layered combat system that adapts to any type of player—from beginners to experts, as well as those who prefer to fight with a single character or manage an entire team.

It’s been a while since Marvel took another serious shot at the fighting game genre, and handing the reins to Arc System Works initially seemed like an interesting pairing. As it turns out, it simply works. Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls manages to be approachable enough that newcomers can start throwing out spectacular attacks within minutes, while its 4v4 system hides an impressive amount of depth for those willing to put in the time. Combine that with a varied roster, gorgeous anime-inspired presentation and a clear affection for the Marvel Universe, and both fighting game enthusiasts and Marvel fans should find plenty to enjoy here.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a deeply complex tag fighter that uses the vast library of Marvel characters to its benefit. As mechanically deep as it will be for veteran fighters to explore and hone their craft, it still has the systems in place to ease newcomers in, providing them with a comfortable springboard to enjoy and improve. It’s hard not to imagine a rich community growing around yet another effort done by Arc System Works who continue to prove their mettle.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is one of the greatest fighters of this generation, with superb, layered combat and visuals that continue to impress.

Arc System Works has done it again, delivering an excellent fighting game, this time greatly benefiting from the inclusion of some of the most recognisable characters in pop culture. The tag-team system provides great strategic depth, while the fighting system is on par with the best in the genre, accompanied by beautiful visuals. The lacking story mode is a bit underwhelming, but the well-functioning online mode will surely keep you busy for a long time.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a visually stunning, comic-authentic masterwork that swaps tag-fighter panic for pure, visually stunning combo fun – cementing itself as a reverent successor to the Marvel vs. Capcom legacy.

Marvel’s Tōkon overcomes its troubled launch to become one of the most enjoyable modern fighting games. While our review was conducted on PS5, the PC version’s early technical issues also affected the console experience through crossplay and matchmaking. After several updates, Arc System Works delivers spectacular visuals, excellent netcode, and an accessible four-character team system with a clever emphasis on assists. A simplistic story mode and some questionable Brazilian localization choices are minor drawbacks in an otherwise excellent package.

Arc System Works has crafted a title that respects Marvel's legacy in the genre while daring to set its own rules, bolstered by stunning visuals, a delightful story mode, and a carefully calibrated balance between accessibility and a high competitive ceiling. On-screen chaos and a roster that feels somewhat lacking are the shortcomings of a game that otherwise excels.
Marvel Tokon is a place to stop and admire the fighting game genre for what it is—an entertainment product where animation and art direction serve as the primary hooks.

With Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, Arc System Works proves once again why it is one of the world’s leading fighting game studios. The visually stunning superhero battles are accessible, yet soon reveal an enormous depth of gameplay that rewards creative and tactically clever fighting.

MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls is an incredibly enjoyable fighter that's impressively accessible and has a ton of potential to be expanded upon down the road. If you enjoy colourful fighting games with diverse casts then you need to play this one, chums.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is an electrifyingly fun, stylish fighter that has earned its place as a highlight of the Marvel fighting game lineage. It succeeds both as a gorgeous love letter to Marvel Comics and the stories, characters, and worldbuilding that has made it such an enduring force in pop culture and as a deeply intricate fighter for newcomers and veterans to break down and enjoy. There are some unfortunate caveats, particularly with a few strange system mechanics, roster omissions, and, most importantly, the frustrating PC performance, that bring the experience down a bit across the board. Nonetheless, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls has laid the console groundwork for a glorious reunion between Marvel and fighting games, and the result is marvelous.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a solid and highly entertaining experience, featuring outstanding presentation, extensive fan service, and excellent localization. Its 4v4 system built around a single shared health bar adds strategic depth and a distinctive flavor to combat, although it also carries several familiar Arc System Works conventions, including autocombos, repetitive patterns, an uneven learning curve, and some balance issues. It does not reinvent the fighting game genre, but it fully succeeds at delivering an enjoyable experience, particularly for Marvel fans and fighting game enthusiasts.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is an extremely technical, frenetic, and beginner-friendly fighting game, featuring a solid roster and variety of modes for player progression, along with great incentives to play online. If you are a fan of Arc System Works' work or are looking for a new fighting game to call your own, this is a great choice.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a solid 4 vs. 4 fighting game with some of the most fun and spectacular mechanics. Furthermore, it stays true to the Marvel essence by offering several interesting modes, especially the Episode Mode. Although 20 characters feels like too few, they are well-balanced and defined. Marvel vs. Capcom now has a new rival.

A fighting game's impact is difficult to determine at launch due to balancing updates and the community's approach to it. Given the package Arc has delivered here, though, Marvel Tōkon is a more than worthy successor to Marvel vs. Capcom and Dragon Ball FighterZ. I believe it has the potential to become a fighting game mainstay for years to come.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is fast-paced and deep, yet readable and accessible. The game didn’t have an easy launch, but it has now stuck the landing – with a superhero landing.

Is Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls better than Marvel vs. Capcom? It is hard to give a definite answer, but Arc System Works’ new game stands out on its own thanks to its excellent combat system, which is both accessible to newcomers and deep enough for veteran fans. It also has a beautiful visual style and plenty of single-player and multiplayer content. While the technical issues are a real problem and some design choices did not fully convince us, overall, this is a must-play for fighting game fans.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls manages to bring its own identity to a classic genre. Interesting mechanics, well-developed characters, and excellent graphics. However, problems with the online modes, few interesting offline modes, and a relatively small cast prevent the title from shining as it should.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a top-notch fighting game. Easy to learn, complex to master, and gorgeous in action, it's pretty much everything I could have expected from a combination of Marvel and ArcSys. A surprisingly robust single-player campaign and comprehensive tutorials also help it shine, even if you're not interested in multiplayer. The game's notable online crossplay issues are the biggest thing holding it back, but patches have already started to address some of those problems. If you're a fighting game fan, Tokon is well worth checking out. For newcomers, it could be one of the best introductions to fighting games available.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers excellent gameplay designed to accommodate both newcomers and veterans, ensuring that victory often hinges on the finer details. The blend of unique concepts for iconic characters, elaborate animations, artwork by renowned comic book artists, and a fantastic soundtrack hits the mark for fans.

With its easy-to-learn but challenging-to-master combat system, visually appealing art style, cast of highly chosen Marvel characters, and well-crafted and resented story, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls could be the best Marvel-themed fighting game ever.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls turns its ambitious 4v4 format into a surprisingly approachable and strategically rich fighting game. Arc System Works delivers spectacular comic-book chaos, a varied 20-character roster, and a flexible assist system that rewards experimentation, while Episode Mode gives its Marvel cast plenty of personality. Its forgiving campaign does little to prepare players for the much tougher realities of online competition, but the depth of party building and fast-paced battles make finding the right team consistently rewarding.

There were plenty of reasons to be skeptical about Marvel Tōkon Fighting Souls, from Marvel’s history with Capcom to the huge expectations surrounding Arc System Works. And then there was the 4v4 concept: how do you fit eight characters on screen without overwhelming the player? Surprisingly, it works. Sharing a single health bar across the team makes the game approachable while leaving plenty of room to master your entire roster, a philosophy that fits Marvel perfectly. There are still some rough edges, especially with assists, screen readability and the relatively small 21-character launch roster. Solo content is also limited, although the Episodes are a pleasant surprise. But the important thing is that Marvel Tōkon Fighting Souls is genuinely fun, and delivers what you want from a good fighting game. It’s not the new Marvel vs. Capcom, and that’s probably for the best.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls arrives at a moment when the fighting game genre seemed to have stopped surprising anyone. Arc System Works tries to fit into this balance with an operation that, on paper, looked impossible: take a notoriously difficult license like Marvel, historically unable to produce a truly long-lived fighting game since the failure of Marvel vs. Capcom Infinite, and build on top of it a system that is both accessible and layered.
Marvel Tōkon is the complete package as a fighting game, with extremely varied training mode options that are perfect for players who've never touched the genre before.

While this isn’t quite the genre defining hit like Street Fighter or even a top-level Mortal Kombat, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls delivers a strong side-scrolling fighter game with a cool 4vs4 gimmick that means the action on-screen is chaotic, brutal and brilliant fun to play.

Marvel Tokon shines thanks to the electrifying gameplay from Arc System Works. Combined with its visual and audio elements, it creates a fast-paced, accessible, and incredibly fun experience. However, the offline modes are underwhelming, the stages are few and far between, and no one would mind having more characters.

While there's fun to be had in All-Star Arena, solo players likely won't get much out of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls. It's the multiplayer where the game shines, with the focus entirely on the exciting, action-packed 4v4 tag battles, gorgeous art and animation, and stellar roster of fighters. Over time, as some of the technical issues are ironed out and new characters are added as DLC, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will become an even easier recommendation for fighting game fans.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a different animal. The fighting design allows for spamming in battle, but there is room for mastery and cohesion. While not complicated, the flow of the matches will take some time to learn and establish a direction of attack on how to play the game. The variety of game modes provides the opportunity for different exposure to different characters while eliminating the idea of anything stagnant. The art design of the characters is beautiful, and the soundtrack is fantastic for battle. At first, it was difficult to determine what Marvel Tokon was trying to be. However, spending more time in the Episodes allowed Marvel Tokon to grab some traction and provide an idea of how the game needs to be played.

Marvel Tokon is a blast to play as a fighter. The game looks fantastic, its combo system is fun and it pays great respect to the rich lore of Marvel with how the characters are designed to fight. While a couple things do hold it back from perhaps standing with Arc Sys all time great fighters, it’s another good game in the current line up of fighting games that doesn’t seem to stop growing.

Marvel Tokon Fighting Soul combines Arc System Works' excellence with a universally appealing franchise—one of its greatest strengths. It is a stunning game with finely tuned gameplay. However, be aware that it demands commitment; while the gameplay is highly accessible, the game remains challenging for beginners to grasp, particularly given its tedious tutorial mode. The lackluster story mode and the lack of single-player content for casual gamers are downsides. Nevertheless, Marvel Tokon is a title not to be missed if you are a fan of Marvel and, above all, a fan of fighting games.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls attempts to offer something for every type of player. From the story mode and arcade challenges to training, tutorials, and both casual and competitive online modes, the package is far richer than it might appear at first glance. It is this variety, above all, that allows the unique 4-on-4 system to shine in different contexts, giving players the freedom to learn, experiment, face off against friends, or dive into online competition. However, the PC version suffers from significant issues that require major fixes if it is to match the quality of the console release. In short, the score below applies only to the PS5 edition; we currently advise against purchasing the PC version. That said, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a solid, reasonably deep fighting game that largely satisfies both target audiences, even if it makes certain compromises that prevent it from standing tall alongside the genre's titans.

Marvel Tokon Fighting Souls is a great game, but definitely not a perfect one. While it delivers plenty of excitement, offers a wide range of options for both single-player and multiplayer, and clearly shows a great deal of attention to many aspects, it still feels somewhat underdeveloped—both in terms of balance, but above all in the chaotic way it handles on-screen battles.
An impressive start to a new fighting game franchise, that has a few rough edges but also plenty of new ideas and some gorgeous animation for its varied roster of superheroes and villains.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is the complete package for Marvel diehards and tag fighters alike. Top-tier presentation, incredibly rewarding single-player modes, and a welcoming onboarding system that makes learning the ropes feel genuinely fun. While launch-window netcode hiccups, unoptimized crossplay, and clunky PC performance keep it from achieving immediate must-buy status, the foundational gameplay underneath is solid enough to stick with it. Once ArcSys irons out the online kinks, Tokon has all the makings of a mainstay that will keep the FGC hooked for years to come.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a strong fighter that manages to channel the chaotic energy of Marvel vs. Capcom while also carving out its own niche in the genre. While the roster feels small for the kind of game that it is, and the single player offerings feel underwhelming, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls provides a strong foundation on which I have no doubts Arc System Works will build for years to come.

This is another way in which Marvel Tōkon succeeds Marvel vs Capcom: it’s not just mechanics or characters, it’s cultural exchange, as American superheroes are once again reinterpreted by Japanese game developers in a genre that facilitates international competition. Marvel Tōkon is built to show off how fun it can be to participate in that evolving conversation. Won’t you go a few rounds?

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls arrives with a number of interesting new features. This time, it introduces 4v4 battles with a much fresher approach through the use of the Assemble mechanic, combined with frantic combos and the signature visual effects of Arc System Works. It features a story mode that is not particularly deep, but is presented through comic book panels, giving it a very distinctive visual identity. The launch roster includes around twenty iconic Marvel characters, a somewhat limited number. It is a title that will need continued support from the community in order to establish itself.

Even with a few weak spots, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, in many ways, is the redemption Marvel fighting games have needed for almost a decade. It’s not exactly Marvel vs. Capcom, but it’s not trying to be. Tōkon has its own eye-catching visual style and given famed developer Arc System Works the space to flex its mechanical muscle in a different arena. Time will tell how well this game matures and evolves, but it’s clear Tōkon has a sturdy base and demonstrates Marvel — and maybe even “Mahvel” — is back in the fighting game space.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls delivers excellent, highly addictive fighting mechanics that make it one of the year's strongest fighters. Its four-character tag system feels fresh, the roster is varied, and the game offers a solid selection of single-player and multiplayer modes. However, the story campaign becomes repetitive very quickly, while the PC version's technical problems negatively affect the crossplay experience even on PS5. Despite these flaws, the outstanding gameplay makes Marvel Tokon a very easy game to recommend to fighting game fans.
Eurogamer's review of Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, the latest fighting game from Arc System Works - and one of the best of its kind we've played in years.
The anime paradigm of Marvel Tokon means the overarching framework of the game is ridiculous even by fighting-game standards.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a fantastic fighting game by one of the genres greatest developers, with that said, it's network state is far from great, and while Arc Sys worked hard on the PC port itself, the netcode still requires some fixing.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls proves that fighting games don't have to be intimidating for newcomers. Arc System Works has crafted a smart combat system where "button mashing" actually yields immediate results, yet hides immense mechanical depth for those willing to put in the time to learn. The single-player content could be a bit more robust, but the visual excellence and incredibly accessible learning curve make Marvel Tokon a stellar fighting game.

Now that I'm sitting here, about to put the finishing touches to my final verdict, I find myself keen to carry on playing, to keep honing my skills and to play more online matches against real opponents. That's a good sign, after all. So I tip my hat to ArcSys - not bad at all.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a surprisingly robust 4v4 tag fighter whose inventive team mechanics and varied single-player and party modes make it far more than just another Marvel-branded crowd-pleaser.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls comes pretty close to hitting the bullseye for me. It is absolutely stunning from an audiovisual standpoint, while its story mode is also top-notch in terms of both writing and style, despite its repetition in different episodes. Its mechanics are engaging and fun, but the game is also fairly complex and consequently rather frantic – fortunately, there are plenty of incentives to learn its intricacies. And no, this certainly isn’t Marvel vs. Capcom, but then again, it doesn’t need to be.

Marvel Tokon is a lot when it comes to learning the basics and mastering each character. Despite being a challenging title for players that are not that used with the genre, it instigates you to become better and better. Of course, having some of the most famous characters in the pop culture helps a lot with that.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is one of those games that manages to appeal to a wide audience. Marvel fans will have fun putting together their dream team and spotting references in each stage. Fighting game fans will recognize Arc System Works’ heavy-handed yet talented touch in the combat system. The downsides include the shallow campaign, the lackluster boss, the requirement to use PSN on PC, and the odd decision to keep character names in English despite an otherwise meticulous Brazilian localization. Aside from that, it’s the most solid Marvel fighting game in a long time.
Despite its previous custodian threatening to make its legacy a footnote, this tag fighter still has plenty of soul. [Issue#428, p.108]

Arc System Works has managed to create a game that looks like an anime series, features spectacular battles, has a good balance of difficulty, a fairly deep combat system, and engaging modes. If you love Marvel, team-based fighting games, and have been missing high-quality arcade-style brawlers, Marvel Tōkon is worth a try. Just don’t play through the "Episodes" story mode. Or maybe play through one episode and that’s it — you’ll thank me later.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is an engaging fighting game with many impressive features. Despite some flaws, it accurately portrays several beloved Marvel characters in many ways and makes them fun to control through gameplay that Marvel fans would love.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls truly stands out thanks to its graphical quality and roster of playable fighters, making it one of the most interesting current projects featuring the comic book publisher's heroes and villains. The decision to feature four-on-four battles is bold, yet executed well enough to avoid overwhelming players while still offering options for beginners.

Will Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls be able to eclipse Capcom's games? No, probably not. They are far too iconic. But Arc System Works imposes its style in a rather nice way by opting for 4v4 battles, leveraging all the creative firepower of its artists, and offering a story that is ultimately pretty well crafted—at least for Playmobil fights (because, let's face it, this is also about opening your toy chest to pit Spider-Man against Magneto). A nice additional feather in PlayStation's cap... provided we overlook the PC launch, of course. Which might actually suit Sony just fine.

The result is a game that doesn't yet appear to fully satisfy the hardcore or the newcomers, but there's absolutely potential here for it to blossom into something really special. If that doesn't come naturally through dedicated players picking apart the systems on offer, then patches can fix plenty of this. That's a cop-out, I know, but that's the modern fighting game reality. As of right now, Tōkon is simply a good fighting game, but hardly something to marvel over.
Performance anxiety.
A gorgeous and innovative fighting game that can appeal to all skill levels.

Marvel Tōkon is a near-ideal fighting game. Between meaningful layers of complexity, a solid amount of welcoming modes, and absolutely phenomenal presentation, Arc System Works has bent over backwards to make an accessible tag team fighter that could make anyone fall in love with the genre for the first time.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls impresses due to its unique 4v4 tag mechanics that are easy to learn but difficult to master. Combine that with spectacular graphics, an incredible roster, and mighty gameplay modes, and you have a truly uncanny fighting game.
 $59.99 at Amazon $59.99 at Best Buy $59.99 at PlayStation Direct US

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a deep and incredibly fast-paced fighting game that manages to breathe new life into the familiar team-based formula with its 4v4 format. It has a satisfying combat system and fantastic art direction, but all of that is held back by a lack of content variety.

If it weren't for the frustrating online issues, Arc System Works' latest creation would be easy to recommend to just about anyone - whether you're a fighting game fan or simply looking to spend a few enjoyable evenings with your favorite superheroes.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is not Marvel vs Capcom and it was never trying to be, despite how desperately many people seem to want it to be. While the issue with inputs, pc performance and a lackluster roster had a lot of people bouncing off the game in the first week of release, I’m glad I stuck around and gave it more time as I’ve discovered that it’s a solid foundation that could become something truly special with a few iterations.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a highly accessible 4v4 tag fighter that manages to offer deep combat without overwhelming newcomers. Its phenomenal character design, impressive learning tools, and solid single-player modes establish it as one of the best fighting games of the generation, but a flawed PC version and long matchmaking times drag the experience down
Marvel Tokon Fighting Souls isn’t reinventing the wheel here, but it does answer the question, “What could another company do with a Marvel based fighting game?”

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is another excellent fighter from Arc System Works, able to capture casuals and veterans alike thanks to a refined, simple control scheme while retaining cavernous depths. Outside of that, it can feel pretty bare bones though, so you better be willing to hop online and put your dukes up.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is by no means an awful fighting game, but this PC version does it no favours. It’s a game held back by shockingly poor optimisation and performance issues that affect everything from menu navigation to gameplay, and while its core Marvel fanbase might not necessarily care, fighting game players like myself do. It will take some time, but until the developers manage to patch everything up, Tōkon is a miss on PC.

I’d hoped for more from Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls. Arc System Works created a gorgeous and well-crafted fighter, but there are too many aspects here that leave me with mixed feelings; the mediocre storyline and slow matchmaking are things I can get over, but issues with the combat system are something I simply cannot overlook. Tokon offers a dozen or so hours of solid entertainment, but it’s really best suited to casual games with friends – it won’t take the fighting game scene by storm.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a dream come true for many fighting game fans, even if its nuances can take a while to warm up to. If only the PC version could have received the same love and care as almost everything else.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a striking, very accessible (at first), and incredibly deep fighting game that brilliantly utilizes Marvel's heroes and Arc System Works' expertise. The stunning visuals, excellent 4v4 system, and wide variety of fighters provide plenty of fun, though the campaign could be longer, the roster larger, and the selection of modes even more extensive. However, the foundation is strong enough that with the right support, the game could sustain an active community for a long time.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a fighting game that focuses heavily on the presentation and technical aspects of its gameplay.

Arc System Works has struck a good balance between accessibility, spectacular visuals, and challenging gameplay. The 4 vs. 4 battles sounded risky, but they're handled without much difficulty. Visually, it's a real eye-catcher, with some more or less successful "Japanese-style" redesigns.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a team-based, yet at its core a traditional fighting game, offering fun for beginners and depth for veterans of the genre. Expect beautifully animated visual treats. The game is suitable even for children; in fact, it’s the exact opposite of Mortal Kombat. Here, fights are fair and only go as far as knocking your opponent unconscious. It’s a fast-paced, arcade-style and entertaining fighting game. It’s just a bit of a shame that the story mode isn’t more elaborate and, instead of one epic ending, features five similar ones. The beautiful animations don’t deserve to be repeated over and over again. However, there’s still a multiplayer mode – both local and online – with the ambition of creating an eSports league.

Arc System Works' highly anticipated team-based fighting game exceeds expectations and is shaping up to be one of the genre's most significant competitive titles. Arc System Works once again raises the bar and sets a new standard within the fighting game niche. An ideal title for both fans of the genre and Marvel Comics fans.

It’s surprising to say that a fighting game can tell a great typical story five times over, and Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls has managed to do so. With such an accessible way to enjoy combat alongside tools to bridge the gap between newbie and pro, players of all skill levels will enjoy round after round as long as support for the game persists in the years to come.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers an impressive new take on Marvel fighting games with beautiful manga-inspired storytelling, deep 4v4 combat, excellent tutorials, plenty of single-player content, and smooth online play on PS5. The PC version needs additional optimization, but the core fighting experience is fantastic and gives Tōkon a strong foundation to grow for years to come.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a high-quality 4v4 tag-team fighting game. It features excellent animation and plays very well, though it takes some time to truly master the combat. It includes a variety of modes, as you would expect from the fighting genre. If you’re a fan of fighting games, Marvel, or comics, this title will draw you in completely in no time.

Ultimately, Tōkon is a game for those willing to invest time, lose, return to training, and try again. And if Arc System Works keeps its promise to continue adding characters and content, I believe MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls has everything it takes to maintain the competitive spirit of gamers for a long time.
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a fantastic return to superhero fighting games, and I enjoyed everything Arc System Works has brought to the table.

Marvel Tokon has succeeded in introducing a fighting experience that fits the legacy of Marvel characters in the fighting genre. Much of that is thanks to its distinct art style, alongside its packed content, a healthy variety of mods, and its fast, fun combat system built around 4v4 showdowns. To be a standout in the genre, has a clear identity of its own, and proving that Marvel still has a prominent place in the fighting game scene.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is proof that it’s still possible to reinvent the wheel in an established genre. The shared health bar completely changes the way you think strategically during a match, while the assist and tag mechanics are packed with nuances. The story mode, despite being tied to the genre’s traditional formula, stands out thanks to its comic-book presentation and different artists for each team. The extra modes are there for some temporary fun, the roster could be larger, and the Portuguese voice acting, while inconsistent, is a fantastic gift to Brazilian players. In the end, Tokon’s issues are minor compared to an extremely solid, creative, and addictive experience. If you’re a Marvel fan, a fighting game fan, or both, Tokon deserves your full attention.
Marvel Tokon combines spectacular anime-inspired visuals with fast, deep combat that makes mastering its four-character teams the main reason to keep playing.
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is an interesting mix of mainstream appeal and Arc System Works unique style. However, the launch of it was crippled by significant issues that are still not fixed.
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls really comes into its own where it matters most.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is not perfect, but its strengths are much more important than its shortcomings. It feels fresh without losing the bits of fighting games you know. And it has enough depth that you can keep discovering new possibilities long after you learn the basics. For a new fighter, it makes a strong argument for itself on the PS5 as one of the more enjoyable entries in the genre.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a competent fighting game, and given Arc System Works’ pedigree, I would expect nothing less. The flashy and over-the-top moveset genuinely makes you feel like you are a superhero smashing up the city in a life-and-death fight for justice. The combat system is robust with plenty of variety once you start exploring off the game’s standard combo paths, but given the structure, this might not be the most friendly fighting game to cut your teeth on.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is exactly the kind of collaboration that could easily have been visually spectacular without necessarily offering enough depth behind it. Fortunately, Arc System Works manages to pull off both almost perfectly. The universe works surprisingly well with the studio’s signature style, and the combat is accessible, fast-paced, and extremely deep. That said, newcomers will need to be patient to fully master all the game’s nuances, especially if they want to play online. Personally, I also would have liked the various story episodes to offer more distinct adventures. However, the game has the foundation to improve over time and pays perfect homage to the Marvel franchises.

From the anime-inspired character models, stages, down to the special attacks, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls embodies the vibe of reading a comic while playing a next-gen game. The story mode, while not topnotch and limited in roster, offers enough to flesh out different characters’ motivation and background. In a world where Street Fighter 6 and Tekken cater to its loyal fanbase, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls approach is both admirable and welcoming to both new and competitive fighters.

A successful and entertaining new fighting game that serves as the spiritual successor to Marvel vs. Capcom. Thanks to its easy to learn hard to master gameplay, it’s perfect for fighting game enthusiasts of all kinds.

We tested the game on the standard PlayStation 5 and found that Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls offers a generally smooth and stable experience at 60 frames per second, both offline and online. The visual presentation is excellent and does not require the usual choice between Quality and Performance modes, an understandable decision for a fighting game where consistent frame rates are essential. Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is not the new Marvel vs. Capcom, and it probably does not even aim to be. Arc System Works’ game takes that tradition as a starting point, but develops its own formula based on a progressive 4-versus-4 structure, a shared health bar, and an extremely important assist system. The result is a spectacular, accessible, and surprisingly deep fighting game. Newcomers can start with simplified controls and auto-combos, while more experienced players will find plenty of depth in team building, synergies, and managing the pace of the fight. The main reservations concern the readability of the action, some potential roster imbalances, and a single-player mode that, while polished, does not reach the same level as the online experience. In conclusion, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a title that is hard for Marvel fans and anyone who enjoys anime-inspired fighting games to ignore. It is a production that respects its source material, is technically impressive, and manages to offer a formula that is simple enough to understand, yet complex enough to support an entire competitive scene for a long time.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls proves that the right studio with the right approach can breathe new life into the genre - and if you’ve never understood why people love tag fighters, this is the game that will make it click in an afternoon.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is one of the biggest surprises of 2026 for me, simply due to how good it feels to play.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a successful fighting game of the current generation. The title looks phenomenal, has a great atmosphere, and delivers on the positive side.
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls achieves a true miracle: breaking free from the cumbersome shadow of Marvel vs. Capcom to find its own brilliant and distinctive identity.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls works for both newcomers and competitive players, thanks to a team system that evolves throughout each fight. Its modes offer plenty of content, the campaign does its job and every character bursts with personality on screen.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is one of the most enjoyable and well-crafted fighting games of the year and, above all, a game that manages to take an already familiar universe and give it its own fighting identity.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls has everything it takes to become one of the best fighting games of recent years, capable of filling the void left by Dragon Ball FighterZ and, more importantly, Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers a fast, deep and spectacular fighting experience that combines Arc System Works’ expertise with Marvel’s iconic heroes in a remarkably stylish package.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls surrounds its 4v4 team battles with story content, training tools, alternate modes, and online play. Its biggest strength is how quickly the combat becomes understandable before assists, team building, and traditional commands add more to learn. Full-team fights can become harder to follow, and I would've liked more stages. If you want a Marvel fighter that lets you start having fun quickly and then rewards the time you spend learning a four-character squad, this is a great one to dig into.

With a highly creative roster and phenomenal visual flair, Tokon delivers a deeply satisfying fighting game experience. Arc System Works introduces clever tweaks to the tag-fighter formula, offering great and strategic depth without demanding grueling execution. It's a fantastic Marvel brawler that just needs its netcode ironed out.

After a few hours of gameplay, we can say that Arc System Works has succeeded in delivering a product of exceptional quality, with great attention to detail in both gameplay and visual design. The single-player mode could have been expanded a bit further, but in fighting games, these modes are often secondary to matches with friends or online multiplayer. But what makes Marvel Tōkon memorable—beyond its combat—is precisely its unmistakable visual style, which blends Eastern and Western influences, Marvel comics, and anime aesthetics. These are two sides of the same coin—contemporary pop culture—which has been fueling the passions of generations around the world for decades. Marvel Tōkon pulls off this combination with remarkable ease, while also succeeding in creating a fighting game that speaks the same language to both newcomers and veterans of the genre.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls isn’t the next MvC, and that’s okay. It’s doing its own thing, and it’s doing it pretty damn well. There’s a lot to love with what ArcSys is doing with Marvel Tokon, and I can’t wait to see how the game evolves from here.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls succeeds in its bet: to offer a 1v1 fighting game disguised as 4v4 with deep mechanics, but accessible enough to please all audiences. Arc System Works has been able to take advantage of their previous projects to offer a solid experience. Only downside, a roster that may seem light given the number of fighters on the floor, but will be strengthened over the months and DLCs already planned.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is, without a doubt, the best treatment a Marvel-based game has ever received. It successfully combines an accessible combat system that is easy to learn with genuine depth for players who want to master it, while also delivering an excellent variety of game modes and a strong launch roster.

Arc System Works nailed Tokon and showed once again why they are one of the best in the genre. While it’s too soon to know if this game will perfectly fill the tag team Marvel void in the fighting game community, it launched with a respectable package perfect for everyone.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is an accessible and highly entertaining fighting game. While its launch roster feels a bit limited and seems poised to rely heavily on paid content, its gameplay and impressive visual presentation make it a thoroughly enjoyable title for fans of the genre.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls really took me by surprise. The anime style is stunning, the Marvel characters are brilliantly rendered, and technically the game runs exceptionally smoothly. Even when the screen descends into utter chaos with attacks, assists and combos, everything stays neatly in place. The accessible combat is also a major asset. You don’t need to be a fighting game expert to enjoy it straight away, whilst there seems to be plenty of scope to develop your skills further. The short Episode mode is undoubtedly a downside. An hour and a half is simply not enough. Whether the game remains engaging in the long term will depend mainly on the online community and how deeply players can delve into the combat.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is an excellent fighting game that needed only one attempt to establish itself among the very best the genre has to offer. The talented development studio has transformed years of experience into an outstanding title that will appeal to both casual fighting game players and true fans of the genre.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls' ultra-vibrant presentation, relentlessly satisfying combat and impressive degree of depth easily make it one of the best fighting games of the generation.

Arc System Works has poured an incredible amount of passion into the project, and that enthusiasm is evident in nearly every aspect of the game. Its ambitious combat and obvious affection for Marvel come together to make Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls one of the standout games of the year.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls really doesn't make it easy for me to rate it. So many design choices are questionably poor, and the online mode is terrible. The whole game is brimming with wasted potential, … but otherwise, it's really good. It's fun, it has great characters, outstanding presentation, nice modes, and even the story is good.

Marvel Tokon is a brilliantly executed tag team fighter that just works perfectly for newcomers and veterans alike. Each character comes with a fighting style group and a unique set of abilities, making each fight a fresh situation to tackle. The art style does great justice to the universe, along with voice-overs that do much better in the Japanese version. The matchmaking is quite good in terms of skills, but it’s hard to find players, possibly because of the network bug or maybe a low player count. Overall, the PS Store price of 3,999 is definitely better than the launch price of Tekken 8 at 4,799 for the disc edition.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls manages to carve out its own space among Marvel fighting games. The 4v4 system works very well, and Arc System Works’ art direction perfectly matches the characters. The single-player content could be more robust, but especially online, there is a solid foundation for those who plan to spend many hours learning and refining their teams.

MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls really nailed pretty much everything it needed to get right out of the gate, and most of the aspects that are floundering can still be tuned up to the high standards of the rest with updates. This is a hell of a fighting game that stands up to the storied greats in the tag fighter subgenre, many of which were built with the help of Marvel anyway.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a team-based fighting game that delivers an accessible, fast-paced, and extremely fun experience, featuring impressive visuals, a strong roster, and excellent Brazilian Portuguese voice acting. Although the short campaign eventually becomes repetitive and the auto-combo system slightly limits freedom during combat, the overall package works very well and provides highly satisfying matches.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls comes highly recommended because it successfully combines spectacle, accessibility, and depth, offering one of the most engaging fighting game experiences available today. Its combat system has a lot of potential, the roster is put to great use, and both the single-player content and online options provide plenty of reasons to keep playing. However, it’s true that some of its mechanics can feel overwhelming during the first few hours. All in all, I’m confident that this is the next fighting game that will define an era in competitive gaming.

Capcom’s Marvel games will always be all-time classics, but Arc System Works and Marvel have made something truly special with the first-ever 4v4 tag fighter and more characters soon to join the fray. MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls has finally arrived and is ready to rock this universe!

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is different in the best ways possible, blending Arc System Works' stylistic approach to a beloved roster of characters. It may be smaller than most offerings, but it absolutely makes up for that with originality and gorgeous visuals within.

It should be clear that 'Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls' is a successful tag team fighter. Casuals can hold spectacular battles perfectly well with auto combos, and the Tony Starks can go wild with all the bizarrely named mechanics. The game looks great, sounds good, feels good, and plays wonderfully. Fortunately, developer Arc System Works is not averse to supporting games for a long time, so there will likely be enough unique characters to make the current roster of “only” 21 even stronger.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is chaotic and complex, yet still a highly entertaining fighting game with one of the most beautiful portrayals of superheroes we’ve ever seen.

In terms of gameplay and presentation, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers an excellent experience. Both Marvel fans and fighting game enthusiasts should find plenty to enjoy here. The single-player modes are also fun and serve as a good introduction to the characters, after which you can hone your skills in the well-equipped training mode and across the vast online world.

Unfortunately, the severe performance issues on PC have only been partially resolved after a week, which detracts from what is otherwise an extremely polished overall package for this 4v4 fighter.

Arc System Works has made a tag team fighter whose best ideas sit in its unique structure rather than its roster. Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls asks a lot of your memory and time, but the payoff is worth it in the end.

MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls is not just a game that capitalizes on Marvel’s characters and heroes; it offers a fresh take on the fighting game genre through the unique style of Arc System Works, with a distinctive art direction and a fast, enjoyable combat system. It’s an exceptional experience worth diving into, especially for Marvel and fighting game fans.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a great fighting game, one of the best this generation, with flashy combat and easy to play but hard to master gameplay, that is unfortunately a bit held back by a lackluster single-player offering.

I feel like Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls had a lot to prove to live up to similar fighters that came before it, but it absolutely nails the licensed fighting game formula with its deep combat, rewarding mechanics, welcoming approach to newcomers, and stunning visuals. Arc System Works have truly delivered an exceptional brawler here, proving that Marvel’s heroes and villains don’t need to be part of a crossover to make their mark on the fighting game genre.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls combines stunning Arc System Works artistry with an accessible yet remarkably deep 4v4 combat system. A few chaotic moments aside, its excellent roster, learning tools and surprisingly strong single-player content make it one of the most complete fighting games in years.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls unquestionably establishes itself as an absolute masterpiece of the fighting game genre and as the perfect embodiment of the modern vision championed by Arc System Works over the past decade. The game achieves the incredible feat of combining immediate, spectacular accessibility with a layered, deep, and multifaceted combat system. We’re willing to bet it will become a benchmark for the global competitive scene. The only real cloud hanging over the game remains the optimization of the PC version and its impact on the stability of cross-play matches. However, this issue does not stem from inherent flaws in the product or the netcode itself. Rather, it stems from a series of questionable decisions by Sony (a general trend that has been recurring a bit too often lately, but which is beyond the scope of this review). For this reason, we do not feel it is appropriate here to penalize an otherwise excellent development effort in our rating. We sincerely hope that the situation will be resolved as soon as possible through dedicated fixes. Setting aside this technical issue, we’re looking at an extraordinary game that’s visually stunning and incredibly fun.

When combat is at its best, and you succeed in summoning your team members at the right time, starting a combo of attacks that combines your characters' abilities, the game delivers some of the most enjoyable and thrilling combat moments in fighting games of this generation.

"Marvel Fighting with a Distinct Identity: Arc System Works"
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls succeeds in building its own identity rather than simply imitating other Marvel fighting games, thanks to a deep combat system, four-fighter squads, and support elements that add a clear strategic layer. This is complemented by exceptional visuals, diverse content, and a polished PlayStation 5 experience.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls hooked me despite being a fighting-game novice with little interest in Marvel these days. Its striking audiovisual presentation, fresh anime-inspired takes on iconic characters and excellent haptic feedback make every chaotic fight feel impactful. The accessible yet deep combat system and diverse roster are the game’s biggest strengths. However, online play still has technical issues, Arcadia Rumble is a complete misfire, and the otherwise enjoyable story mode could have benefited from a more creative narrative. Despite these shortcomings, the overall package works. Fighting-game and Marvel fans can jump in without hesitation. And if you’ve lost touch with Marvel over the years, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls might just reignite your love for it – it certainly did for me.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers some of the most electrifying team-based combat the fighting game genre has seen in years, with a roster where every fighter feels genuinely distinct and a shared health bar system that reinvents what 4v4 battles can be. It's not perfect, the onboarding curve is steep and its premium price tag paired with a paid Year 1 character pass is a real barrier for a genre that lives or dies by its player base, but once everything clicks, this is one of the most rewarding fighters in recent memory.

As a Marvel fighting game developed outside its longtime Capcom partnership, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is an extremely solid, deep, flashy, and fun fighting game that can stand up to current titans like Street Fighter 6 and Tekken 8. The ambitious 4‑vs‑4 system proves manageable with practice, offering depth without overwhelming players, and on the PS5 it delivers a smooth, visually striking experience.

The drawback lies in its limited offline single‑player features, making it best suited for those who thrive in competitive online play, along with a currently shoddy PC port that will hopefully receive patches to improve its performance.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls arrives as one of the best surprises for those who enjoy fighting games. The mix of frenetic brawling, charismatic characters, impeccable audiovisual presentation, and a generous amount of content makes it very easy to recommend the game.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls delivers exactly the fighting game Marvel fans have waited over a decade for — Arc System Works' team-based system and stunning art direction more than earn the Marvel vs. Capcom torch.
Tōkon puts four Marvel fighters in your hands, then makes figuring out what they can do together the most fun part.

With a plethora of features, immaculate art style &a; sounds, huge love &a; respect of the source material from Arc System Works, and a solid fighting game engine that caters to both beginners and expert, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a triumph. Even the most jaded and stubborn of tag fighters will admit that there's a lot of "sauce" and depth in the devs' take on Marvel superheroes.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a very good fighting game that, despite a few missteps in the narrative, delivers phenomenal and dynamic gameplay, a diverse cast of characters, and a wide variety of content that will keep fans of the genre and Marvel fans entertained for hours on end. If fighting games are your thing, Tōkon is a must-buy.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls delivers a matchup as spectacular as it is ambitious, bringing together the Marvel universe and Arc System Works' distinct identity. Its four-character team system introduces original mechanics and remarkable depth, while its artistic direction is simply brilliant. However, performance and fluidity issues on the PC version prevent all that potential from fully unfolding. For this reason, the score is provisional, and we will return later to check if this promising fighting game manage to unlock its full power.
93.8% of OpenCritic critics recommend this game (16 reviews).
Metacritic user score 6.8/10 (12 ratings).

Station to Station is often hilarious, often mortifying, and perpetually honest. As Perfect Tides so wonderfully depicted incredible specifics of adolescence, this sequel speaks as truthfully and intricately about the emerging of adulthood. It captures those moments of profound bliss and shattering devastation, alongside the beauty in the mundanity between. And it makes me miss those times with that magical girl from university, and so unbelievable grateful it’s so long in the past and never to be repeated.

Station to Station is as worthy a follow-up to the brilliant original Perfect Tides as anyone could have hoped, continuing Mara’s story with the same insight, compassion and immersive writing while deepening and expanding its narrative through interesting new mechanics.
A wonderfully written examination of what on earth it means to be an adult. Gameplay and art both feed back into the central themes, creating a heartfelt story, with a dash of pretentiousness.

An indie gem where every pixel breathes love for its characters. An old-school point-and-click adventure whose story starts slowly but then develops an irresistible pull. Perfect Tides: Station to Station is great storytelling on a small screen.
This is a story about finding your voice, but it also grapples with an uncertain time, when some outcomes are beyond our control or experience. [Issue#420, p.104]

Mara Whitefish's new adventure is sometimes irreverent, at other times sentimental, but it's always genuinely true. So much so that you find yourself getting angry at one character or another, only to realize that, as teenagers, we probably behaved the same way.

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is more somber than wistful, more grounded than nostalgic, and more realistic than fanciful. The 2003 setting feels circumstantial rather than deliberate as a storytelling device, and the autobiographical piece of it bleeds from every word of text.

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is a superb second chapter to an incredibly underrated point-and-click adventure, taking advantage of real-life stories and struggles to paint a beautifully moving and engaging story about a creative trying to make it big while making sense of the world. It too is a perfect time-capsule game of the early 2000s, filled with laser-sharp wit and references. Within is profound prose that uses an unconventional approach to game narrative to tell a divine coming-of-age tale that’ll be relatable to many. Bolstered by gorgeous pixel work, striking on-two’s animation and unique mechanics for the genre, Mara’s tales of love and loss as a creative in New York are quintessential storytelling for those who value game narratives. Come on in, the water’s damn fine.

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is a messy, disjointed and incredibly uncomfortable window into the life of a writer who still needs to find their way in the world, but all of this comes together to build an amazing narrative that engulfs the player, showing them to embrace discomfort and learn to be their best self. Sadly, a lack of meaningful accessibility options does lose the game half a star.
An impeccably written, and brutally honest, adventure that explores the anxieties of trying to transition to adulthood

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is one of those games that's so relatable it sometimes hurts. What's been created here is a game based on real life for real people. It's a game that says a lot about Mara, but it can also say a lot about ourselves and our relationships with others, whether friends, romantic partners, or family, but also about what we think of ourselves and how all these mundane experiences shape us.

"A deeply human and moving narrative"
Perfect Tides: Station to Station offers a narrative adventure experience focused on college life and creative ambition, presented in a deeply personal and moving way. The strong writing, innovative mechanics, and polished art design make it a successful sequel and a title in its own right. Despite its relatively slow pace and limited world, the depth of the emotional experience and interactive choices make the game a valuable addition for fans of interactive storytelling.

I went into Perfect Tides: Station to Station not entirely sure what to expect, but I can honestly say this is a gem of a game. Mara is an entertaining main character that you can easily connect to even though you’re thrown into the middle of her story. Everything works in perfect tandem to create a truly fun experience. My favourite thing about this game is that your choices actually feel like they have some weight to them, unlike other choice-based games where things feel inconsequential.

Perfect Tides: Stations to Station is an easy winner of the Thumb Culture Gold Award as it is an enjoyable little game, definitely worth the amount that it’s listed for. Check out the trailer below to get a better look at what’s in store for Mara.

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is the perfect point-and-click adventure for millennials but also appeals to younger audiences who are just turning 18 or are at least not too far off. Meredith Gran manages to paint a relatable picture of a young woman coming of age and I'm quite sure there are situations everyone out there will initially shake their head and ask, "Mara! Why?!" only to realize a moment later that they probably would have reacted the same way when they were younger. The writing tasks and books offer a bit more gameplay variety than its immediate predecessor, but it never gets truly difficult, which I didn't really mind. The dialogues and the story entertained me so well throughout the entire game and I hope that we will see more of Mara someday.

"Perfect Tides: Station to Station" is not a game that overwhelms me. It accompanies me. It challenges my patience, my compassion and my willingness to think in small steps. This story of an uncertain year is told in cautious pixels and whispering sounds. It is a quiet, honest look at growing up. Those who engage with it will experience a game that is not spectacular, but deeply moving.
But there’s more here than just the pieces I connected to. Perfect Tides: Station to Station is filled with so much life that I think anyone can find something to relate to.

Station to Station doesn’t require that you have anything to do with writing, schooling, or even the time period it’s set in. The only thing it wants from you is to remember what it was like to doubt yourself while the world went on. In this way, it turns small, everyday moments into something deeply meaningful.

Perfect Tides: Station to Station is a coming-of-age story filled with moments of real happiness, and just as many moments of self-doubt. There are times where Mara, the protagonist, is fully depressed, and the game doesn’t shy away from exploring that. It digs into relationships and intimacy, along with everything that comes with them: heartbreak, hurt feelings, and broken friendships. And choosing dialogue options during those moments truly put me right in the thick of it with Mara.

I also love that Mara is a writer, and that part of the experience involves writing papers. It pushes me to explore, learn, and gain experience so I can write better, which is a clever mechanic that fits the story perfectly. The art is phenomenal too, adding even more weight to the emotional rollercoaster the game delivers.

But at the end of the day, it’s the writing that makes Perfect Tides: Station to Station stand out. Mara is flawed, but she’s also incredibly relatable, and it’s hard not to get pulled in and root for her through the entire journey.

Stepping into Perfect Tides: Station to Station felt like being a teenager again: angsty, emotionally heavy, and stuck in that strange limbo of a summer holiday where everything feels too big. Consuming a story about another angsty, emotionally heavy girl trying to navigate the world, I felt seen in a way I hadn’t since my teen years.

I enjoyed Perfect Tides: Station to Station far more than I expected I would. It’s gritty, entertaining, and painfully relatable. It’s also very likely changed my opinion on point-and-clicks forever. For a simple, somewhat emotionally exhausting, story-oriented game, it definitely hits the mark. There are areas where I felt it could have been improved mechanics-wise, and I doubt I’d play through it again, but I do absolutely think it’s worth a try for anyone with an appreciation for storytelling, art, or comically large eyes.
