Fails to live up to its potential and the expectations created by being associated with The Witcher series, but one I could recommend giving a chance during a quieter period.
A new and intriguing action RPG that doesn's stray far away from The Witcher III's template, but delivers an engaging narrative experience full of memorable characters in a fascinating setting.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a great game, one that I will probably make multiple runs through to get all the endings, or heck just to get through the intro without anyone dying at the church! The combat is one of the more unique systems I’ve played and really enjoyed. The game looks great and plays smoothly. This is one of the better action RPGs I’ve played this year. I would highly recommend giving this one a try!

The Blood of Dawnwalker can’t escape a certain label, but the longer you spend in the Sangora Valley, the less you’ll care about it. You pay for power with your humanity, for help with time, and for certain decisions with consequences that cannot be undone. At first, this may seem like a limitation, but you’ll gradually realise that it allows the world to carry on even when you’re not part of it. Your adventure therefore doesn’t feel like a well-trodden path, and further detours await you on your next visit. Whilst the game has flaws that cannot be overlooked, it also features ideas you won’t soon forget.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a brave debut. Rebel Wolves shows it knows the grammar of narrative role-playing games very well, but does not merely rehash the model of The Witcher. The thirty-day system, Coen's dual nature and the need to live with missed quests and irreversible consequences give the adventure a recognizable personality. Not all components work at the same level. The combat needed greater precision, the open world could have made better use of the verticality of vampiric powers, and the technical performance needs further work. However, when the game puts its characters, its choices and its quests in the foreground, it manages to be intense, adult and surprisingly engaging. It is a role-playing game that gives its best when the player stops looking for the perfect playthrough and accepts missing something. Saving one person may mean giving up another quest; using vampiric power may simplify a fight but change your relationship with the world; chasing one goal may mean arriving too late for everything else. In this imperfection lies its most successful idea. Ultimately: it is a solid and ambitious narrative adventure, recommended above all to those looking for a role-playing game rich in atmosphere, choices and consequences. It is not without flaws, but it has enough character to represent one of the most interesting surprises in the contemporary action-RPG landscape.

A stellar opening bite from Rebel Wolves, The Blood of Dawnwalker demonstrates it can claw and battle with the toughest of the vrakhir. While it's not quite at the level of the very best in the genre, it delivers a superb open world adventure, filled with intrigue and compelling combat. Give it enough time to feed and this Dawnwalker could grow into a titan, and I can't wait to see what blood feast will come next.
If you like games like The Witcher 3 or Elden Ring, Blood of the Dawnwalker is a must-play experience.

If you're willing to overlook the gameplay uncertainties in order to be captivated by a mature, complex, and masterfully orchestrated narrative, Blood of Dawnwalker is an adventure you absolutely cannot miss.
While the game may have suffered slightly from a slow narrative pace and some performance and combat issues, it's undeniably a fun experience throughout.

The Blood of the Dawnwalker is a familiar yet inviting dark high-fantasy world inlaid with gameplay systems that stand out among the action-RPG pack. While it does have its setbacks, the overall product was a solid first impression that left me itching for more.

The Blood of Dawnwalker puts a fresh spin on the open world RPG by making every decision matter against a 30 day countdown. With a dark fantasy world to explore, human and vampire abilities to master, and choices involving allies, equipment, and the fight against the vampires, Coen's journey challenges players to decide what truly matters when saving their family is the priority. Rather than encouraging players to complete every side quest before progressing, the game makes time itself part of the challenge, creating an adventure where preparation must be balanced against the consequences of waiting.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark fantasy action RPG in which you play as a human by day and a vampire by night. The combat feels great, and each fighting style offers a distinct experience. Furthermore, your choices have genuine consequences—quests won’t simply wait for you. If you want to experience everything the game has to offer, you will need to play through it multiple times.
Playing The Blood of Dawnwalker is like attending a live rock concert: it's often uncomfortable, the music is sloppy, it's incredibly loud, but the energy and passion knock the walls down.
The Blood of Dawnwalker has a lot to offer to anyone looking for the dark side of RPGs and honoring the “Rebel” in the studio’s name, as it truly rebels against triple A development.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark open world action RPG where vampirism, family and relentless passage of time collide. With a time limit, a dynamic day &a; night system, engaging combat, meaningful exploration, memorable characters and a world filled with vampire lore and a great story, the game offers a refreshing take on the genre. The Blood of Dawnwalker, in the end, succeeds in creating a compelling world where every choice matters and the line between humanity and monstrosity is never quite clear.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an ambitious vampire RPG that stands out thanks to its 30-day time limit, the tension between humanity and vampirism, and systems that attempt to make your choices matter. Unfortunately, repetitive combat, camera issues, limited enemy variety and an inconsistent open-world design prevent the game from reaching its full potential. Still, there is a genuinely interesting RPG underneath those problems, especially for players who enjoy games that force them to accept that they cannot see and complete everything in a single playthrough.

In spite of the discrepancies between what the developers appeared to want this game to be and what actually made it to store shelves, The Blood of Dawnwalker is a pretty good time. The vision is present throughout the game and the obvious shortcomings often feel far more like a material consideration than outright mistakes.

If you enjoy Kingdom Come: Deliverance and The Witcher, and appreciate an RPG that expects you to learn its systems with relatively little hand-holding, Dawnwalker is worth your time. It certainly earned mine.

An incredible debut from Rebel Wolves, The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a refreshing twist on open-world RPGs with its dynamic day/night mechanics and compelling time-management system. Despite rough UI edges and a missing stealth system, its consequence-driven dark storytelling and punchy combat make it a must-play shot in the arm for the vampire genre.
Rebel Wolves doesn't need to prove that it can make an RPG. *The Blood of Dawnwalker* already proves it.
The Blood of Dawnwalker feels special in how it makes what could have been repetitive open world filler feel like core steps of a wider and more overarching narrative.
The Blood of Dawnwalker represents a bold, multi-layered undertaking that dares to foster a focused, responsible player rather than constructing an endless, passive playground.

Rebel Wolves' debut proves to be a baptism of fire, overcome with great authority and visceral passion, offering an unforgettable dark fantasy adventure to all lovers of great role-playing stories. Despite some technical and mechanical flaws, we are faced with a solid, courageous, and wonderfully written title. If you're looking for an experience that will captivate you and make you reflect on the consequences of your actions in a world devoid of hope, this journey into darkness is unreservedly worth your attention.

Blood of Dawnwalker exceeded all expectations. A great story and memorable characters combine with superb combat that is a joy throughout. This is one of my favourite RPGs in recent memory and I can't wait to see what Rebel Wolves do next!

Dawnwalker’s timer certainly wasn't something that initially sat well with me, but after seeing its execution, and the amount you can accomplish, when certain paths have been removed, I've turned around it, at least somewhat. Regardless, Rebel Wolves has crafted a stunning world to explore, with characters, lore, and a story worth caring about. While they have oddly shown their cards as to Coen's future adventures, I still find reasons to revisit and scour every nook and cranny this world provides. It's worth sinking your teeth into.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is an ambitious, dark and surprisingly refreshing RPG that doesn’t quite achieve everything it sets out to do, but gets enough right to make its debut difficult to ignore.

The main issue that bothered me during my playthrough was combat against multiple enemies. The directional attack and blocking system works very well individually, but the camera and aiming system end up significantly hurting the experience when several opponents surround Coen. The stealth could also have been much more developed. For a game starring a vampire, with all the importance given to nighttime and hunting, I found the stealth possibilities far too simple. Basically, we crouch and try not to be detected, while certain actions, such as opening a door, can immediately alert enemies to our presence. The AI has some good moments during combat, but its limitations become obvious in certain chase situations.


Even so, it is difficult to ignore how well the time structure works to create constant tension. Having only 30 days to save our family makes every decision feel important, even when we realize that there is enough time to build a very satisfying adventure. Before accepting a quest, I often found myself wondering whether that activity was really worth spending several hours of the calendar. Combined with the day and night cycle, activities exclusive to each period, vertical exploration, and the different skill trees, the system creates a dynamic that makes the world feel much more interesting than simply an open map filled with question marks. The ability to use a sword and vampiric claws, switch between different ability styles, and walk across walls also reinforces the feeling that Coen is becoming something different from a conventional medieval warrior.


And it is precisely this combination that surprised me most about The Blood of Dawnwalker. The vertical exploration, vampiric movement, directional combat, dark atmosphere, and time-based quest structure create an experience I did not expect to find at this level in a vampire game. The influence of The Witcher is evident in several details, from the structure of certain quests to the presentation of characters and the object inspection system, but this did not bother me because there is a very natural evolution of these ideas within its own proposal. The combination of urgency in the story and the freedom to decide what to do creates a dynamic that works extremely well throughout the adventure. At any moment, there is a feeling that we could be doing something else, following another quest, or exploring a different path, and that uncertainty ends up being one of the most interesting and distinctive aspects of the experience.

The Blood Of The Dawnwalker is an absolute treat for fans of deep, atmospheric vampire RPGs who can look past the rough technical state of the Xbox Series S version. If you love tense directional combat, rich investigation mechanics, and a world packed with secrets, the sheer depth here easily outweighs the performance bumps. It is a must-play game!

The Blood of Dawnwalker es, en definitiva, el primer paso de Rebel Wolves. Un paso que nace inevitablemente de los mismos barros que dieron forma a The Witcher, pero que poco a poco empieza a encontrar su propio camino. Y si este es el punto de partida de lo que está por venir, quizá lo verdaderamente interesante no sea preguntarnos cuánto recuerda Dawnwalker a The Witcher 3, sino hasta dónde será capaz de llevar Rebel Wolves todo lo que ha aprendido.

For a debut, The Blood of Dawnwalker is remarkably ambitious. The story rivals the genre’s best, the time mechanic reinvents how an open world can feel, and the vampire power fantasy delivers exactly what it promises. It’s held back by a camera that fights you and an enemy roster that runs out of ideas early, but Rebel Wolves has built something worth paying attention to, and I’ll be first in line for whatever comes next.

The painful part is I really wanted to love The Blood of Dawnwalker, not have this lukewarm emotion towards it. The best aspects of the game are so unique compared to everything else out there and, with enough commitment, are very fun to play. It’s the other side of that coin that muddies the water. That great combat has to contend with technical hiccups, and those are the only things where maybe I would feel differently. Progression is the best example of how great Ideas just keep having minor directional choices hold them back profusely. There is a series here; developer Rebel Wolves has a great concept here that works when it works but doesn’t when it doesn’t.

The Blood of Dawnwalker particularly impressed us with its dark atmosphere, vast open world, and compelling duality between human and creature. The Witcher’s influence can certainly be felt, but the game manages to carve out an identity of its own thanks to its 30-day system, meaningful choices, and nighttime transformation. Despite an occasionally confusing interface and a few graphical and technical issues that can break immersion, the overall experience remains highly compelling. With a higher level of polish, The Blood of Dawnwalker could have set the bar even higher.

There is just so much to this world, to this story, and I am so impressed that Rebel Wolves was able to tell such an intriguing story within it. Being able to blend vampires, religion, and witchcraft together while also having great written characters for all of this it so impressive. Not being afraid of putting unique mechanics into a game that could scare off some players I absolutely applaud. The Blood of Dawnwalker is a masterclass in keeping to a theme, a setting, and idea, and it’s absolutely one of the best RPGs I’ve played not only this year, but ever.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is gripping right from the get-go. A well-paced, emotionally charged story, a unique and fleshed out time mechanic, and a dark, fascinating world all combine to make something genuinely brilliant. If you have any interest in RPGs, you absolutely must check this one out. Arguably one of the best games I’ve played this gen.

Therefore, The Blood of Dawnwalker earns a rare, well-deserved Thumb Culture Platinum Award!

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a passion-driven RPG from former CD Projekt RED talent. Despite a few minor technical issues that are easily fixable with updates, Rebel Wolves has crafted a rare experience: a role-playing game that truly respects your choices, your time, and the way you build your hero.

Sangora stands out through its decaying art direction, excellent sound design and an atmosphere that changes dramatically between day and night. The Blood of Dawnwalker has technical imperfections, but its narrative and distinctive use of time successfully separate it from other RPGs.

The Blood of Dawn walker is a beautifully dark world, with a refreshing freedom in how your story is told and a rather unique method of becoming a vampire. It is a true successor to both the Witcher and Vampyr, and a perfect choice for fans of either.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is undoubtedly my biggest surprise of the year. Not only did I not have high expectations for this game, but I actually wrote it off as a failure from the start. Despite all that, I decided to give it a chance, and I absolutely don’t regret it. I managed to finish the whole thing in exactly 40 hours, and I already know that I’ll be returning to the Vale Sangora many times in the future. It’s a great RPG that pulls you in like quicksand. Its unique approach to gameplay, the constantly stressful time-pass mechanics, a superbly written story, phenomenal characters, stunning audiovisuals, and a strongly felt Slavic atmosphere are among its greatest strengths. It’s all the more disappointing that the game doesn’t quite live up to the same high standard when it comes to combat, controls, and camera work.
The Blood of Dawnwalker still has a few rough edges, but its blend of storytelling, time management and vampirism gives it a distinct identity.
The Blood of Dawnwalker offers a genuinely interesting approach to both time and choice that makes it difficult to put down.
“The Blood of Dawnwalker” is a game that does everything well. Whatever it mixes together, it does so with flair.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is not perfect, but it's a really great RPG you have to play. When the credits roll, it doesn't demand a replay, you desire it. Bugs and technical issues on PC really hold it back from being more, but it's still one of my favorites of the year. It's well-written, with an interesting world, and fun systems to sink your teeth into. Rebel Wolves has made a memorable and earnest game, and I'm genuinely excited for the sequels that are already planned. Simply put, The Blood of Dawnwalker has stakes, and unlike vampires, doesn't suck.

Drawing inspiration from various video games while also following its own philosophy, *The Blood of Dawnwalker* stands out as one of the most interesting open-world RPGs of recent years. It isn't perfect, but it offers an adventure unlike few others in the genre.

In some ways, The Blood of Dawnwalker feels a bit old-school in its design, but once we settled into its rhythm, we found a satisfying, if slightly clunky RPG that is well worth a recommendation from us. The time limit means we can’t be the all-in-one hero, and there’s a story here that…ahem..sank it’s fangs into us early on.

Despite its severe optimization issues, the courage to create mechanics that challenge modern industry standards honors the legacy of its main influences. The Blood of Dawnwalker stakes its claim among the great open-world RPGs.

For a debut project, Rebel Wolves aimed high—very high. Perhaps a little too high, even, given the numerous technical issues. Still, I consider The Blood of Dawnwalker to be an exceptional RPG with an intriguing storyline. One of its greatest strengths is the vast freedom of action it offers, to the point where an adventure that would normally take about ten hours can easily stretch to three times that length, depending on how much you want to explore. To get the most out of the game, it’s best not to overthink things and just go with the flow. Little by little, minor quests turn into major events, leading, among other things, to duels against Brencis’s generals. The combat and loot system is also very enjoyable, with great responsiveness, despite a limited roster of enemies. Unfortunately, the whole experience is weighed down by technical execution that lacks polish and a few missed opportunities in terms of consequences. If you’re willing to overlook a technically uneven game, *The Blood of Dawnwalker* should be a treat—even more so if you enjoy the vampire theme, which is very well executed here.


Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

When it comes to vampires, gaming has been a little short on options lately. So, if you’ve been looking for a great vampire-themed RPG since the days of the underrated Vampyr, you absolutely shouldn’t miss The Blood of Dawnwalker. Hell, you shouldn’t miss it if you love RPGs in general, because it’s an engaging, well-written game packed with compelling stories and memorable characters.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a game the writer was overlooking, but one that, once experienced, isn't easily forgotten. The world created by Rebel Wolves is incredible, and it manages to fight on equal terms with masterpieces like The Witcher 3. The narrative is certainly one of the production's strengths, even though it's tied to the time mechanic, which will need significant refinement for the next chapter.
A haunting narrative that explores the psychology of monstrosity through personal reflection and moral decay.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a great attempt at creating a much-needed new IP and despite some issues with its quests, the superb divergent storylines and real-time directional combat will keep you thoroughly invested.

The Blood of Dawnwalker comes highly recommended because it’s an RPG with its own distinct identity, thanks to several ideas that work very well together. The protagonist’s duality, the time system, and the weight of the decisions players make set it apart from many other open-world games. It’s not without its issues, but its strengths outweigh its flaws. This is a dark fantasy adventure with personality, great ideas, and a more than promising foundation.

As someone who went with little to no expectations, “The Blood of Dawnwalker” is an very much welcoming surprise, with good writing, impactful choices and a very fun combat system — even if sometimes flawed or undercooked in certain areas, like stealth mechanics.
“The Blood of Dawnwalker is a remarkable dark fantasy RPG where meaningful choices, a gripping narrative and a deep combat system come together to create an unforgettable adventure.”

The Blood of Dawnwalker brings innovation to modern open-world RPGs by introducing a 30-day system in which every choice consumes time and actively shapes the story. Despite featuring combat that is merely functional and noticeable visual compromises in the PS5 Performance Mode, the game stands out thanks to its impeccable writing and memorable side quests. The result is a memorable and highly recommended RPG that turns time management into its greatest strength.

The Blood of Dawnwalker combines time pressure with exploration and meaningful choices, constantly forcing you to decide what to prioritize. Despite its shortcomings, its human-vampire dynamic, moral ambiguity, and bold RPG choices make for a distinctive experience.

It's easy to see why Rebel Wolves feels confident this will be a massive multimedia franchise. There is a rich foundation to build from, and Coen is an immensely compelling tragic hero whom I would follow into any adventure. It isn't perfect, but it is the perfect start to something greater.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an ambitious and remarkably confident debut, carried by a strong story, memorable characters, difficult moral choices, and a beautifully atmospheric world. Its time-management system creates meaningful consequences and replayability, while the day-and-night combat offers plenty of build variety, even if some progression systems feel overly complicated. Repetitive side activities, occasional technical issues, and familiar open-world design hold it back, but Rebel Wolves still delivers a compelling RPG that left me eager to see what the studio does next.

The Blood of Dawnwalker combines technical combat, investigative RPG elements, and a compelling day-and-night system that lets players shift between human and vampire abilities, creating an ambitious adventure despite some launch optimization issues.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the most interesting experiences of 2026. Whether you’re a fan of vampires or simply an RPG enthusiast, Rebel Wolves’ title has everything it takes to entertain all kinds of audiences, delivering a serious and mature story, an incredible world to explore, and razor-sharp gameplay, all built around its deep choice system that shapes the experience. With the confirmation that a follow-up is already in development, I’m rooting for the success of the Dawnwalker Saga. Here’s hoping we get a modern-day Coen!
Despite its flaws, Rebel Wolves' debut game is undoubtedly one of the most interesting and inspired Action RPGs we've seen in recent years.

The Blood of Dawnwalker represents a bold new step forward for a fresh studio, clearly making a statement with a world enriched in deep lore, filled with memorable characters and a story you won’t soon forget.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is at its best when it trusts its vampire fantasy, its choices, its time limit, and Coen’s internal conflict. It’s not a perfect RPG, but it already has something many games take years to find: an identity of its own.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a gripping experience that balances out the stress of time management with excellent storytelling and exciting RPG gameplay. By forcing players to treat time as a finite resource, every single decision carries genuine weight – and with a narrative that’ll hook you from the word go (and that will keep you on your toes with the consequences of your actions), it’s easy to find yourself wholly invested in its world right until the very end. Once the combat clicks and the world opens up, it is incredibly difficult to put down, with The Blood of Dawnwalker a triumphant, dark, and highly replayable adventure that breathes fresh life into the genre.

The Blood of Dawnwalker aims to position itself as a Game of the Year contender—an RPG packed with grand ideas that clearly shows the studio's pedigree. However, by trying to blend so many disparate concepts, it ultimately runs a bit out of steam, even if its innovative playtime limit stands out as one of its strongest pillars.

For those with the patience to overlook some rather dated gameplay moments, The Blood of Dawnwalker offers glimpses of a masterpiece, and I am very excited to see what Rebel Wolves have in store for us in the future.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has its share of scars, but beneath them beats the heart of a bloody good RPG. Its excellent story, convincing world, and meaningful player freedom give it an identity of its own, while Rebel Wolves proves with its very first bite that it has a serious appetite for the genre
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a truly solid experience in almost every respect, winning you over with its narrative identity, nocturnal pacing, and bold design choices.
The Blood of Dawnwalker has a great story and ideas, but repetitive combat and frustratingly undercooked systems leave it feeling less than the sum of its parts.

The Blood of Dawnwalker turns its brilliant day-and-night duality and limited-time structure into meaningful choices at every step. Memorable characters, rewarding combat and remarkable replay value make Rebel Wolves' debut one of the finest open-world RPGs in years.
The Blood of Dawnwalker's rough edges and technical issues hold it back, but its 30-day time system, meaningful quests, satisfying combat, and vampire-human duality make it a compelling debut.

The Blood of Dawnwalker will suit gamers looking for a serious, immersive dark fantasy role-playing game with choice-making elements and a vampire-themed environment, rather than one that simply includes vampires. There will be no denying that the game has some flaws, in particular, in terms of combat diversity and traversal. However, the game's best mechanics work together rather than separately.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a game with tremendous potential. Whilst it’s impossible to ignore the significant influence of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, The Blood of Dawnwalker has established more than enough of its own identity to stand out. It’s a must-play for fans of the (dark fantasy) RPG genre.

I'm having a blast with the skills and directional blocking. The time limit doesn't rush me, but the meaningful day-and-night-cycle enriches the quests. And when I think I know what to expect in the open world, The Blood of Dawnwalker uses it's nonlinear structure for great surprises.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an impressive start to a new RPG saga by Rebel Wolves. With veterans of the genre behind the game, I went in with high hopes. The many systems introduced in this new adventure had me worried at first, but the game introduces everything naturally and at a steady pace, leaving plenty of room for the excellent narrative to shine. Those still having doubts can safely invest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Just know that you won’t only be investing Time Segments in-game, but likely plenty of your own time in real life as well.
The Blood of Dawnwalker's story kept me captivated, but it was the world and its characters that made me reluctant to put the controller down.

"It is impossible to experience everything in The Blood of Dawnwalker in a single playthrough, and because so many things are time-sensitive, you’ll come across different results. There really is no wrong way to play this game, and that in and of itself is remarkable.

This world doesn’t want you to live in it, but instead, the compelling nature of it makes for another playthrough after beating the main story. It’s an outstanding victory for Rebel Wolves as it's an incredible first outing for them. The Blood of Dawnwalker is a day 1 purchase for any gamer out there.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a gorgeous, ambitious RPG that gives you an incredible world to explore, meaningful choices to make and a fantastic vampire fantasy that feels genuinely different from anything else out there. While the lack of New Game Plus, no post-game free roam and the possibility of rushing through the story hold it back slightly, this is still an exceptional RPG and one of the biggest surprises of the year.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a very specific RPG title. A game that was genuinely just a step away from effortlessly ranking among the best projects of this year. With future patches and updates, it might still get there. Until then, however, it remains a game held back from the top by one fundamental flaw: the developers' fear of taking their risky ideas and diving headfirst with them into the unknown. Dawnwalker ultimately teases players with the cool concepts hidden up its sleeve without ever truly playing its hand. This is evident whether you look at the fundamentally great combat system - dragged down by poor enemy and equipment variety - or the time mechanic, which doesn't impact the gameplay nearly as much as it could nor should.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is both what we expected and what we feared: an RPG rooted in familiar structural mechanics that tries to branch out with a couple of fresh design ideas. The touch of Rebel Wolves, a team largely made up of former CD Projekt Red employees, is most evident in the writing: the world-building, lore, and plot are compelling and satisfying, keeping you glued to the controller for hours. Centered around Coen are the sandbox element and the 30-day mechanic, two bold choices that pay off in replayability and a sense of consequence, even if the promised freedom is only partially realized. The result is a debut that’s at times captivating and enjoyable, but with the typical flaws of a first effort.

With their debut title, Rebel Wolves were able to craft an outstanding and unconventional RPG rooted in granting player freedom and variety across most of its elements. The studio also built an intriguing world backed by masterfully told lore; however, a few flaws in open-world design and enemy variety kept The Blood of Dawnwalker from reaching excellence.

The Blood of Dawnwalker feels like a visitor from an alternate universe, where all of the energy, creativity, and craftsmanship we associate with The Witcher instead went into the creation of this weird, unique vampire tale. Despite the obvious Witcher influences, it feels unlike anything else I’ve played, and is easily one of the year’s finest RPGs.

While the bar isn't exceptionally high bar, it's worth saying that The Blood of Dawnwalker is undoubtedly the best vampire game ever. Some systems perhaps promise more depth than they can actually deliver. But, as a whole, Dawnwalker is an intriguing open-world RPG, with more than enough unique ideas to sink your fangs into.

One thing is clear: The Blood of Dawnwalker definitely doesn’t suck. In fact, after over 50 hours with The Blood of Dawnwalker, I’d go as far as saying it’s one of the best RPGs I’ve played this year. It just has some teething problems…

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an easy recommendation whether you come from The Witcher 3 or any other RPG from the modern era. It delivers on many of its promises, offering excellent combat, a dense open world with a lot to seek, and an interesting story that presents a likeable protagonist. However, it’s underdeveloped villains, 30-day mechanic, and glaring technical issues prevent it from hitting the mark.

It’s not The Witcher 3. It doesn’t need to be. Dawnwalker has its own blood type and a unique RPG-ing taste that’s anything but vein-illa. Despite the occasional technical anaemia, there’s enough life in it to suggest Rebel Wolves could eventually sire a truly monstrous series from this.

Devs, Rebel Wolves take the typical RPG formula and infuse their own unique take on a vampire game into a dark fantasy that stands on its own. I can see The Blood of Dawnwalker enduring the test of time, and I’m keen to see where Rebel Wolves take players next.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a great first step by Rebel Wolves. With well-written characters, a mature story, and a fascinating lore, the game is entertaining and leaves a huge taste of 'wanting more.' Unfortunately, it just isn't better due to a problematic technical side that shows the game needed more time in the oven.
The former Witcher 3 developers show how a dark fantasy setting should be handled.

The Blood of Dawnwalker makes an impressive debut with compelling writing, meaningful day night mechanics, and versatile combat. Repetitive enemies, awkward traversal, and technical roughness undermine its ambitious open world, but Rebel Wolves establishes a promising foundation for the new IP.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a fantastic open world RPG with a sharply written story, great characters and meaningfull choices throughout. It wears it's Witcher 3 inspirations on it's sleeve, but isn't afraid to add some twists to keep it fresh.
"The Blood of Dawnwalker" is the first big hit of a crazy second half of the gaming year 2026.

We loved the fact that you can just give in to the feed and kill main characters along the way, and that there were many different ways to end the story. It was great to hear that this is just chapter one of Coen’s story, as we can see Rebel Wolves growing and becoming a real powerhouse in this genre.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an excellently written ARPG whose roots in The Witcher are unmistakable. The consistently high quality of the voice acting and sound design contributes greatly to an atmosphere that makes the player genuinely care about the fates of its characters and the world they inhabit.

Unfortunately, the gameplay—particularly the combat—becomes rather repetitive and tedious after a short while, while the crafting system feels somewhat tacked on and is rarely, if ever, actually necessary. On the other hand, we really enjoyed the concept of time as a resource, which has been implemented in a very player-friendly way.

Despite its gameplay shortcomings, we will definitely embark on a second playthrough, because the stories Dawnwalker has to tell are absolutely worth hearing. They ultimately rise far above any of the game's shortcomings and are easily its greatest strength.
Rebel Wolves’ debut action role-playing game is one of the most unique and ambitious games to come out in 2026.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, Rebel Wolves gambled on a new IP and didn’t hold back in their ambition. Thankfully, it has paid off in spades, and from the looks of it, this is the start of a new RPG franchise. It might not have the same notoriety as The Witcher series for now, but if Rebel Wolves can produce the sequels with the same level of quality, then The Blood of Dawnwalker might just be the next great RPG series.

Simply put: The Blood of Dawnwalker is an all-new, AAA action-RPG that manages to impress in every way, and one that’s our frontrunner as the Game of the Year. We might possibly be witnessing the birth of a new powerhouse IP, and I, for one, am all for it.

While I played through The Blood of Dawnwalker, I had a fantastic time exploring the game's open world as I fought the numerous monsters and humans in gruelling combat with fantastic abilities that look as cool as they feel. I was also able to enjoy the large story with its numerous consequences and choices that lasted the entire game. Although the gameplay is fun it can get repetitive doing the same side content, but it is very far and few between allowing a break between them.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is considered an excellent Action RPG experience that delivers a wonderful, poetic story alongside carefully written characters and a meticulously crafted protagonist, while introducing a new and distinctive time system that serves the experience in a dark world full of secrets and mystery. It features an enjoyable and addictive gameplay system with two different forms—as a human by day and a vampire by night—backed by deep RPG elements that grant you complete freedom in building your character and shaping your story's path through masterfully crafted, unforgettable quests. This blend is completed by a enchanting soundtrack and a stunning art direction to deliver an epic experience that leaves a clear mark, despite a few flaws in enemy variety and side content.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an amazing first effort from Rebel Wolves, proving that open‑world RPGs can still surprise us. By stripping away genre bloat and focusing on meaningful mechanics such as the use of the day and night cycle, a gripping narrative, and morally complex characters, the developers have delivered a dark fantasy experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly new, making it a must-play for fans of the genre.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a triumphant and uncompromising action RPG that brilliantly combines mature storytelling with ferocious vampire gameplay. The contrast between the human day and the monstrous night works flawlessly, while the breathtaking city of Svartrau will captivate you from the very first moment. If the developers manage to iron out the inconsistent optimization with a Day One patch, we have an undeniable Game of the Year contender on our hands.

Comparisons between The Blood of Dawnwalker and The Witcher 3 are inevitable, but it has nothing to fear -even when faced with Geralt's best adventure- because Rebel Wolves' game is excellent. It offers an open world full of secrets and quests—all of them interesting—and the ability to forge a narrative however we want to navigate this world of horror, fantasy, and political intrigue. It has some technical issues, and not all of its mechanics work as well as they could, but it is undoubtedly one of the best games of the year.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a true narrative sandbox with a malleable and flexible structure that allows you to play your way and see where the wind takes you. While its combat isn’t as strong, the game’s narrative framework is consistently mesmerizing.

The Blood of Dawnwalker does a lot of things we've seen before. The influence of other major RPGs is frequently noticeable, and comparisons to The Witcher, in particular, are easily made. Yet, Rebel Wolves has added enough of its own ideas to ensure that Dawnwalker doesn't feel like a copy. The time system, in particular, makes a big difference.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a familiar take on the RPG genre, but its dense human-Vrakhiri dual gameplay loop and time management, accompanied by a banging story, make this one of the best RPGs of the year.
Sharp writing, forgettable combat: The Blood of Dawnwalker is a solid vampiric RPG worth playing for its story and quests alone, if you can stomach the gameplay jank.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a game that has been hovering near the top of my 2026 anticipation list. While it has some issues in its package, there are components in story and the vampire abilities that provide exciting moments across 40-60 hours of play. Your enjoyment will depend on your connection to a solid story, combat feel and the use of time segments to progress across 30 days. The sounds can be visceral and stumbling across random occurrences always enhances the lived-in vibe of an open world. There is something here that may just need a few updates to realise its best form, yet I can’t help but be excited for where Rebel Wolves decides to place their time next.

The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a dark and thrilling journey through a rich open world filled with exploration, featuring an exceptional day-and-night cycle that meaningfully impacts quest design, abilities, and gameplay. Despite several technical issues, including frame-rate drops, inconsistent visual quality, and lengthy loading screens, these shortcomings do not diminish the fact that we experienced a distinctive and bold adventure with plenty of room to improve.

From key parts of the team that brought us The Witcher 3, The Blood of Dawnwalker turned out to be a disappointing letdown. Repetitive combat, forgettable quests and frequent crashes leave its promising vampire adventure feeling like a major missed opportunity.

The Blood of Dawnwalker isn't perfect by any means, but its attempts to merge The Witcher's grungy world with an intense time limit make it stand out from Geralt’s masterpiece. Its story is riveting, its characters are expertly written, and its combat combined with the 30-day time limit is utterly unique, making for a thrilling adventure that is as bloody as it is good fun.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is well worth playing for those who enjoy narrative RPGs, dark fantasy, vampires, difficult choices, and open worlds populated and created with personality. It has the kind of adventure that makes the player think about a quest while away from their PC or console.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is more than an attempt to replicate The Witcher’s success, depending on its own unique charm and atmosphere. Its time-limited story system and freedom of choice work exceptionally well, while the gameplay delivers two distinct experiences. Despite some repetition, it lays a strong foundation for what could become a remarkable series.

The Blood of Dawnwalker nearly strikes a successful balance between classic open-world design and fresh ideas. Its day-night cycle and time pressure are intriguing additions, but neither is used consistently enough. Fans of open worlds and vampires will find plenty to enjoy, although the game offers few major surprises. Technical issues and the lack of a performance mode (in my review build) also hold it back. On the other hand, the charming story is particularly strong at the beginning and end, while the lively world is a joy to explore. Rebel Wolf's debut is far from a masterpiece, but it shows plenty of talent and leaves me hoping for a sequel.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has an interesting identity thanks to its combination of human and vampire gameplay, the day-and-night cycle, the time system and meaningful choices. However, the empty open world, awkward blood and health system, time pressure, uneven combat and several visual and technical bugs keep the experience from reaching its full potential. I enjoyed my time with it, but I often found myself thinking how much stronger the game could have been with a livelier world and a better balance between freedom and time pressure.

Despite its open-world technical issues and certain aspects of its combat, you're in for a bloody good time with this vampire-laced role-playing tale. The Blood of Dawnwalker is this year's spotlight CRPG entry that hit all the right notes with its story, characters, world-building, and overall adventure &a; capstones.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is by no means a flawless experience, but the developers’ ambition in storytelling and in creating a world that responds meaningfully to the player’s choices has ensured that its gameplay shortcomings do not overshadow the overall experience. With its debut title, Rebel Wolves has shown that it has plenty to say, and one can only hope that some of this game’s shortcomings will be addressed in future installments.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an excellent dark fantasy RPG that shines thanks to its strong sandbox elements. As a debut title, Rebel Wolves has done a terrific job of finally doing justice to vampires in video games.
The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers layered narrative depth, dense worldbuilding, and excellent dual combat that keeps exploration and battles equally engaging in a way that truly shines in today’s age.

"When time is more precious than blood"
The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a highly ambitious vision of the Action RPG with a compelling time system, real-world choices, a dual identity that shifts gameplay between day and night, and an atmospherically rich and detailed open world. 
While the combat and some technical aspects could use some polishing, the interconnections of the game's systems and the strength of its quest design make it a very promising experience, and it could well become one of the standout Action-RPGs of 2026.

The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a captivating RPG experience with its rich atmosphere, unique mechanics built around the day-night cycle, and a freeform quest structure in which player choices shape the course of fate.

Blood of the Dawnwalker is an impressive debut from Rebel Wolves that, despite flaws such as problematic lip-sync and technical issues, manages to overcome and even surpass the initial skepticism carried over from the Cyberpunk 2077 era. For fans of deep storytelling, dark Slavic atmosphere, and thoughtfully implemented vampire mechanics, time spent in Vale Sangora comes highly recommended.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a high-quality action RPG, built around a unique combat system, a very convincing "dual" gameplay, and an open narrative structure that stays rich and coherent even while leaving almost every choice in our hands. The time limit and the tangible weight of every decision make the whole experience deeper, within a beautifully detailed world; it's just a pity that the technical side and some production limits are not always up to par.

lego-batman-legacy-of-the-dark-knight.title: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight

reviews.excerpt: Metacritic user score 8.3/10 (808 ratings).

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the best love letter to Batman we’ve ever seen. The way it handles the history of the World's Greatest Detective is incredible. With great combat mechanics, a fun and fantastical story that gives the cornerstone eras their turn, this is, hands down, the best LEGO game to date.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is impossible to put down. It manages to imbue the intensity of Gotham with just the right level of whimsy and humour. The game’s perfectly crafted open-world and varied mission design don’t simply just make it a blast to play; it also makes the game very good value for money, and that goes a long way these days. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight deserves to stand proud as one of the best games of 2026 and within LEGO and Batman’s history.

The end result is a fun, funny, and self-aware homage to the Dark Knight that is equal parts LEGO wackiness and phenomenal Batman Arkham successor. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is one of the best LEGO games of all time. Heck, it might just be THE best LEGO game ever. And it'll certainly give your favorite Arkham game a run for its money.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t just another iterative entry in the franchise; it's a new vision defined by varied gameplay, gorgeous upgraded graphics and clever storytelling. Whether you’re gliding across Gotham's skyline, piecing together detective puzzles or laughing at a perfectly timed gag, the game delivers a rich, polished experience that honors the Dark Knight in a way only LEGO can.

LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight’s Legacy manages to go beyond the classic formula of other games in the franchise, offering a fully immersive experience in the complex city of Gotham and unraveling Batman’s legacy through an original, epic, and entertaining story. It is a “love letter” to fans of the Caped Crusader and a tribute to the Dark Knight’s legacy.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the perfect love letter to the Caped Crusader, with fun gameplay, great writing, and tons of surprises every step of the way.

LEGO Batman: Legacy Of The Dark Knight knows its audience of Arkham fans, and youth, and strikes an exceptional balance of meeting the gaming needs of both. It is the Arkham game you never knew you needed.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is extremely ambitious in scope compared to previous LEGO/mega-IP combos, and it succeeds tremendously in nearly everything it has set out to accomplish.

Appearances can be deceiving - especially when it comes to grown adults willingly sinking hours into this phenomenal LEGO game. This is easily one of the best, if not the best, pieces of Batman fan service ever made, and a must-play for anyone who grew up with the films, games, and animated series. It also stands as the most ambitious, and arguably the best, LEGO game ever created.

Legacy of the Dark Knight goes beyond LEGO's classic lighthearted tone and nostalgia. It builds a vast Gotham City with meticulous attention to detail, celebrates the legacy of the Dark Knight, and expands on the foundations laid by a legendary video game trilogy. TT Games finally decided to push its formula to the limit, and the result could be the best LEGO Batman game yet—and the closest we’ll get to reliving the golden days of Rocksteady.

As we wait for the Dark Knight's next big game, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight steps in and delivers a lovingly crafted, satisfying entry. It pulls from the best Batman entries while going beyond expectations in every aspect. This one’s by the fans, for the fans.
Legacy of the Dark Knight’s excellent combat and stealth systems, fun open world, and clear reverence for the World’s Greatest Detective bring it close to plastic perfection.

Whether as a first Batman game or a revisit of franchise lore, Legacy of the Dark Knight presents a rich adventure of layered twists, complete with solid and approachable gameplay, along with that well-balanced, laugh-out-loud humour. As an ode to such a prolific franchise, there’s so much the game gets right.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a fresh improvement on the Lego series formula, trimming down the massive bloat. It’s focused, reworking years of Batman media into a mostly connected, large-scale story that covers years of the Dark Knight’s career. Feeling like one big comic book combined with an improved, if only slightly, combat system makes this the best Lego game in years. You might not be blown away by anything Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight has up its sleeves, but any fan of Lego or Batman would be doing themselves a disservice by not answering the call.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a monumental step for the franchise, delivering the definitive LEGO Batman experience. Gotham City itself is a highlight, a vibrant open world filled with distinct districts, crimes, Riddler puzzles, and collectibles, encouraging extensive exploration. Overall, it's a delightful surprise and a must-play for both LEGO and Batman fans, balancing nostalgia with deeper mechanics.
It’s a masterful tribute to the Dark Knight's history, treated with the utmost respect, packed with sharp wit, and delivering stellar quality across the board.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is an incredible celebration of the Caped Crusader, and if you've encountered any of his adventures across comics, film or gaming, you'll find joy in every reference and aside.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight upholds the high standards of this particular series and stands as one of the best examples of adapting a franchise into the world of colorful bricks. Its flaws are minor and do not detract from the gameplay experience. Designed for the whole family, the game will entertain and thrill you—at times making you forget it’s a parody—so you’ll be ready to kick some villainous butt and serve as Gotham City’s guardian with plenty of attitude (and even the "Batitwist").

Legacy of the Dark Knight delivers TT Games' most ambitious, cohesive and authored LEGO title by cutting the content bloat and filtering it all through the lens of Rocksteady's Batman Arkham games. It's an adventure steeped in nostalgia but packed with plenty of open-world fun, fantastic level designs and set pieces, and brilliant humour.

LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight's Legacy is a must-have game for fans of the DC hero, and for anyone looking for a game to enjoy with family and friends on the same console. The idea of ​​using the character's classic films, without the obligation to follow their respective plots exactly, or even the order in which they were released, creates a unique and incredibly rich story full of references to its universe, which fits perfectly with the game's concept.

Legacy of the Dark Knight is the best Batman game in over a decade that takes us back to the good old days of the Arkham trilogy with plenty of humor, but it also has a lot to offer in terms of gameplay.

I am utterly delighted by Legacy of the Dark Knight. Its story is charming and effective, its combat is engaging, and its open world is top-notch. It's a no-holds-barred approach to the revered character, and though there are spots where the execution could have been better, TT Games included everything I could have asked for in one wholly entertaining package. The Dark Knight has a storied legacy, and this adventure does it justice.

Legacy of the Dark Knight skillfully blends the signature style and humor of the Lego games with numerous gameplay elements borrowed from Rocksteady's Batman: Arkham series. The result is a truly excellent action-adventure – and so far one of the best Lego titles released by TT Games.

Layering LEGO's playful freedom over the Arkham series' proven gameplay foundation, this is the most Batman-feeling game in years. Its chapter-based structure weaves together homages from across Batman's vast media history, while an open world built around each Bat-Family member's distinct identity both honors the Arkham legacy and elevates the LEGO series to a new high.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the perfect game for Bat-fans, in all forms of media. It manages to keep the spirit of its original stories while putting its own comedic spin on them and adding every memorable reference to the franchise that any fan would recognize, no matter how small. On the gameplay side, it successfully combines two different identities into an enjoyable experience, instantly making it one of the better Batman games out there.

And even with those restrictions, they’ve managed to create a fantastic game. Because when you’re soaring over the city, you hear the police radio warning that a crime is in progress, and you plummet at full speed right into the middle of a group of criminals—who go flying due to the force of the impact and the sheer terror your mere presence inspires—the only thing you can think is: "I’m f*cking Batman."

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a highly entertaining title that successfully combines the charm expected from Lego games with gameplay reminiscent of the Arkham series, delivering a great tribute to the Dark Knight that can provide hours of fun. However, frequent graphical issues keep it from reaching perfection.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight embraces the Dark
Knight’s 86-year legacy with iconic stories, classic suits, and modern
story arcs. Inspired by the structure of the Arkham trilogy, the game
builds its own identity through lighthearted gameplay, charming humor,
and consistently entertaining moments.

In a way, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is easy to evaluate: if you're willing to be captivated by either LEGO or Batman, or even if you just want to enjoy the simple fun of playing together with a dear one, there are plenty of reasons to join in the romp of defending Gotham on the Bat's long life journey. On the other hand, those expecting in-depth character and gameplay development should look elsewhere.
The best LEGO game in years, even though not as revolutionary as anticipated. Gotham is glorious and the gameplay is smooth. TT Games at their finest.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight might be the best LEGO game yet, delivering a fun, family-friendly take on all of the brooding bat’s biggest moments, plucked from every medium, and lovingly recreated brick-by-brick in an epic open-world capable of matching even Rocksteady’s best. It’s the Batman game Gotham deserves, and it absolutely is the one it needs right now.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is not only the best LEGO game TT Games has ever made, the most complete and focused in every aspect, but it's also a great Batman game, able to stand up to Rocksteady's Arkham games and hold its own, despite the obvious differences related to their target audiences. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is and aims to be a universal game, suitable for everyone as is tradition for LEGO games, but it would be a grave mistake to dismiss it for that reason and not enjoy a celebration of so many years of adventures of a timeless hero, in a Gotham City that has never been so beautiful to explore in a game. Close your eyes and leave your fear behind, it's time to be Batman again, this time in cape and bricks!

Ultimately, LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight’s Legacy is a must-have for anyone who loves LEGO games and the Batman universe. Its generosity and ingenuity in drawing on the best elements of the Arkham series elevate this installment to a higher level, making it far from “simplistic.” Its longevity is unquestionably among the best you’ll find in this genre, and the variety of gameplay options keeps things fresh enough to prevent boredom. Not to mention all the events involving Bruce Wayne and the Dark Knight that we relive, along with the usual shenanigans of the LEGO series, which give this new game a very unique flavor and identity.

LEGO Batman: L'eredità del Cavaliere Oscuro is an extremely entertaining adventure, both because of its lighthearted gameplay, which appeals to players of all ages while still offering a certain degree of complexity, and because of its engaging campaign, which pays tribute to movies, comics, and animated series with surprising consistency. Hopefully, Traveller’s Tales has overcome the problems of recent years as well, because this is certainly the cleanest game we’ve had the chance to test at launch, at least on the PlayStation 5 version, and it undoubtedly represents the direction to follow in order to renew video games inspired by the world-famous Danish building bricks.

All things considered, LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight's Legacy succeeds in the arduous task of paying tribute to the legendary figure of one of comic book history's most iconic characters, delivering a comprehensive product that encapsulates practically every facet of Gotham City's Caped Crusader. Added to this is a well-crafted gameplay system—largely borrowed from Rocksteady Studios' *Arkham* trilogy—and a rich, well-balanced open-world design that could keep you engaged for hours on end, even after you’ve completed the main adventure. Aside from a few minor gameplay blemishes and boss fights that are less thrilling than one might reasonably expect, TT Games' latest creation stands as a heartfelt love letter to the legend of Batman—one enriched by a witty sense of humor that is never cliché. If you are a fan of the Bat, this is a title you simply cannot afford to miss.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is both the culmination of a formula TT Games has refined over twenty years and the moment that formula stops being enough on its own. The game doesn't simply reproduce what has always worked: it dismantles it, rebuilds it with new materials, and attempts something the LEGO games had never genuinely tried before. To be a Batman game in the fullest sense of the term.

The integration of “Arkham-style” gameplay provided the boost that LEGO titles had been missing. *The Dark Knight’s Legacy* is undoubtedly one of the finest entries in this multifaceted saga, which has now been running for 30 years. It is a fresh and entertaining title that masterfully blends immediacy with variety, creating a Batman multiverse brimming with surprises. Once again, however, the absence of an online option for co-op mode—which TT Games stubbornly continues to omit from its games—is a sore point.

This ambitious title delivers an exceptional tribute to the Dark Knight, blending deep fan service with a vibrant open-world Gotham. It successfully incorporates Arkham-inspired mechanics and rewarding co-op play, although the combat eventually feels repetitive. Despite slightly clunky vehicle handling and simple boss encounters, it stands as an essential experience for fans.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the kind of game we thought we’d never see again. A title that successfully revives the spirit of the Batman Arkham series while keeping the accessible, chaotic charm of classic LEGO games intact. What could have been a lazy nostalgia trip instead turns into a sincere, ambitious, and surprisingly polished love letter to the Dark Knight. Behind its LEGO humor and family-friendly tone lies a game that genuinely understands Batman: his mythology, his villains, his films, his comics, and his video game legacy. TT Games blends all of these influences together with impressive confidence to create an adventure that feels both like a celebration of the character and a genuinely great action-adventure game. Sure, the low difficulty, basic enemy AI, and a few technical hiccups hold it back from true masterpiece territory. But despite those flaws, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight captures something special: the fantasy of soaring across Gotham at night, striking fear into criminals, and truly feeling like Batman again. TT Games hasn’t just made its best LEGO game in years, it’s delivered one of the best Batman tributes ever made.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight may not reinvent the classic LEGO formula, but it combines it surprisingly well with an atmospheric open world set in Gotham City. The mix of varied missions, countless secrets, and strong Batman fan service constantly motivates you to keep playing. While the simple combat and repetitive activities can become a bit tiring over time, the game still stands out as one of the most entertaining LEGO adventures in recent years.
Featuring sharp writing, accessible gameplay, and plenty of discovery opportunities, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is another strong entry in the LEGO franchise perfect for younger players.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes up the mantle of the Arkham franchise, combining its simple gameplay and adding the already famous mechanics from Rocksteady's titles. It is a game with a strong story component that covers the key moments of the character throughout his history. It is still a LEGO game (too easy) but even so, it is entertaining.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a spectacular celebration of the Caped Crusader, masterfully blending the charm of plastic bricks with the thrill of Arkham-inspired combat. Driven by a breathtaking maximalist Gotham City and a deep respect for Batman's history, it delivers an immensely rewarding odyssey for fans of all generations.

It probably sounds ironic to call a LEGO game a near must-play of the year, but LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight absolutely deserves that acclaim. Brilliant world design, heartfelt humor, and concentrated scale all coalesce for a meticulously crafted adventure that’s well worth your time regardless of your affinity or history with Batman as a brand. Despite its combat and storytelling not shining nearly as brilliantly, they don’t ruin what is otherwise a wonderful experience that I hope becomes a cornerstone of LEGO titles moving forward.

Traveller's Tales' latest LEGO game could well be considered the pinnacle of the studio's LEGO legacy. What it lacks in challenge (being aimed at younger audiences, after all) it more than compensates for with beautiful visuals, imaginative use of the beloved brick aesthetic, and a world packed with charming and entertaining activities. Additionally, the trademark humour that has become synonymous with the developer is consistently effective, while the countless references to Batman films, comics, and video games are both clever and rewarding for fans.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is one of TT Games' most compelling productions, combining the irony and accessibility typical of the LEGO brand with the timeless charm of the Dark Knight. Gotham works, the combat system inspired by the Arkham series surprises with its fluidity and immediacy, and the campaign effectively condenses decades of Batman imagery. Some limitations remain, such as the limited number of playable characters and the side activities that lack long-term impact. However, nothing that truly compromises a rich and engaging adventure, designed for both longtime Batman fans and those looking for a light but refined action adventure.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a Batman Arkham for kids, for better or for worse. If you were expecting this game to be an Arkham City 2, you might be disappointed by the game's lack of depth, but it's fun and will certainly appeal to its target audience; you just might not be part of that audience.
Every Batman game that comes out for the rest of eternity will be measured against the Arkham titles, and Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight knows it

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the most complete LEGO Batman yet, packed with fan service, gorgeous visuals, and plenty to collect. Its darker open-world approach won’t appeal to everyone, but Batman and LEGO fans will still have a blast exploring Gotham together.
The closest thing to a new Batman: Arkham game there’ll be for many years and a great co-op adventure in its own right, that somehow manages to be unpredictable all the way through.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the culmination of two decades of stellar development from one of gaming's most underrated studios. It's funny, it's witty, it's vast and engaging, full of love for the world of Batman and above all else, it's so much fun. At the end of the day, isn't that what it's all about?

A referential and joyful deep dive into the world of Batman, the latest LEGO effort from TT Games is elite brick gaming. Legacy of the Dark Knight just wants to be an enjoyable time, and it refuses to falter from that commitment. This new LEGO Batman will be some of the best fun you have all year.
A strong open-world Gotham and trademark slapstick humour powers a fantastic plastic parody of the Caped Crusader's greatest hits. Our review of Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a love letter to not just Batman, but the history of Batman media. While it's a very easy game, that doesn't take the shine off of an experience that left me smiling constantly. Rocksteady's legacy is given the recognition it deserves, and proves there's still a huge demand for the Arkhamverse to rise again.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the most ambitious Lego game to date, blending stories from nearly 90 years of Batman comics, films, and games into a visually stunning open-world adventure set in Gotham City. The game delivers a fluid combat system clearly inspired by the Arkham series, and a city packed with secrets, puzzles, and collectibles.

LEGO Batman: The Legacy of the Dark Knight therefore perfectly achieves its goal: to serve as the culmination of everything great about Batman. It refines the gameplay of the Arkham series, packs in references to the best Batman films, and ties it all together within the playful LEGO universe. The title even affords itself the luxury of being fully playable in co-op and proves incredibly generous, featuring an open world brimming with content. This makes it the most ambitious LEGO game ever released—and perhaps even the best; dare we say it! However, this standard LEGO game formula also constitutes its biggest flaw, due to levels that are far too conventional, predictable, and repetitive—especially when playing solo. If you are a Batman fan—whether you plan to tackle the adventure in co-op or gift it to a child—it’s a resounding yes. But for those awaiting a true successor to the Batman Arkham games, this serves as a fun way to pass the time, though you’d be better off waiting to see what Rocksteady has in store for the future.

There are games that surprise you simply because they didn't have to exist—at least, not in this form. LEGO Batman: The Legacy of the Dark Knight could have been just another spin-off, another box of bricks sitting on an already crowded shelf. TT Games decided otherwise. It is neither a mechanical rehash of the Arkham series, nor merely another licensed LEGO title; rather, it is a universal work that pays tribute to a character who has endured through the ages—and seems to understand exactly why. It isn't flawless. The stealth mechanics sometimes feel like a half-remembered echo of Rocksteady's games, while the combat constantly reminds you that the game refuses to become too intimidating for its intended audience. Yet, TT Games has delivered its most ambitious title in a long time. It is also its most polished. And, above all, its most honest. An immense love letter to Batman, radiating a contagious sincerity. Ten years after Arkham Knight, that felt almost like a forgotten sensation.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a charming tribute to the DC icon that isn't afraid to take things with a sense of humor, inviting us on a journey through a less “dark” version of Gotham—but one that's just as memorable.

Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t just one of the best LEGO Batman games—it’s one of the best Batman games and one of the best LEGO games, an experience that delivers on virtually every level. It’s even better when played in co-op.

It's practically impossible to get bored in the new TT Games title. The British developer delivers one of the most fun Batman titles, honoring the legacy of a memorable character with striking visuals and the unique humor of the LEGO universe.
The new Lego Batman takes a step forward and is a terrific tribute to the character’s recent mythology through Nolan and Rocksteady, but it still falls short of being the definitive Lego game.

The game certainly has its limitations, but all of that pales in comparison to how much fun it is to step into the shoes of Batman and his friends—even if it’s in a blocky version full of charming Lego humor. Gliding and soaring above the dark streets of Gotham may not feel as epic as web-slinging in Marvel’s Spider-Man, but it’s so enjoyable that you’ll hardly ever use the built-in fast travel to get from point A to point B in the blink of an eye. Developer TT Games has already released three Lego games starring Batman: Lego Batman 1, 2, and 3. Well, the fourth time’s the charm, because Legacy of the Dark Knight is perhaps their best Lego game to date.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes 87 years of Batman history and crams it into one plastic package. The result is a joyous love letter to the Caped Crusader that feels like every classic Batman movie rolled into one.

Broadening the scope of Lego’s licenced games – certainly in the wake of 2024’s half-baked Lego Horizon Adventures – Legacy is a darkly enjoyable plastic romp through Bat-history leaving little out and cramming a huge amount in.
The resulting product doesn’t just make for one of the best Batman games over the past decade, but is an experience that virtually every Bat-fan will love.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a wonderful homage to the history of the franchise. Fans of Batman are in for a treat, as each moment references iconic elements from the movies, comics, video games, and television while piecing together its own story. While the difficulty is low, every aspect of the gameplay is delivered with care, making this an engaging adventure. Charming and confident, this tribute breathes new life into Gotham.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is everything a Batman fan would want. It honours the character, his rogue gallery, allies, and world with success. Whatever your favourite iteration of the Caped Crusader is, you can play as them. As a LEGO game, it is easily the most advanced and impressive we've seen yet. I haven't had this much fun with a LEGO game in a long, long time, and here I am, over the moon, elated by how coherent and fleshed-out Legacy of the Dark Knight is.
If you want to have a fun time remembering the most iconic moments of the bat, you should definitely try it, since it doesn't matter what generation you're from.
More so than the ill-fated Lego Dimensions, Legacy of the Dark Knight may be the ultimate Lego game, not just drawing on a single series but nearly every popular iteration of Batman.
Look for enjoyment rather than challenge and you’ll find a colorful, fun, funny and brimming with content adventure that is sure to satisfy any Batman and LEGO fan.

Applause should be given Traveller's Tales, as they've conjured up the ultimate LEGO Batman game in the series' fourth outing. Retelling the origins of Bruce Wayne as Batman has been well-trodden ground, but witnessing his storied history play out with LEGO's joyful jokiness and whimsy is exceptionally pleasing.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight creates a clever throughline between the imagination of the brick-building video games and the mechanical genius of Rocksteady’s Arkham series, resulting in the strongest LEGO game yet. Full of endearment to its source material and approachable for audiences of almost all ages, regardless of whether your childhood Batman was Adam West or Robert Pattinson. It may not be quite the hardcore video game comeback we wanted from the Dark Knight, but it’s a surprising win nonetheless.

While more enemy variety and better playspaces for stealth would have been nice, what's given works well enough, especially when paired with all the characters. Finally, the game is wrapped in a beautiful presentation that serves as a love letter to Batman. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight does Batman proud and is a rare case where the Dark Knight deserves to step out of the shadows.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a unique experience set in the Batman universe that delivers on its promises and offers plenty of content for both adults and children to enjoy, setting a new standard of quality for LEGO.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn't just another Lego game. It's the best Lego game to date, and the best Batman game since Arkham Knight (and it's been 11 years, Karl!). Sure, it's not as deep as the Arkham games, and not as charismatic as The Lego Batman Movie. But it's made with passion, love, and an understanding that players want more than just button mashing.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is one of the best entries in the LEGO series in years. Visually striking and atmospheric, which makes all the difference when we're talking about Gotham City, with spectacular graphics, dynamic combat, sharp humor, and a genuine celebration of decades of Batman lore. Solo or in good company, it's a hard game to put down, whether for long-time fans or for those discovering the Dark Knight for the first time.

At the end of the day, while a hardcore Batman fan may take issue with some aspects, the joy that the game provides more than makes up for those problems. If you love the character as much as I do, then you owe it to yourself to play Legacy of the Dark Knight for yourself, as it is the ultimate love letter to one of the best characters ever created. For kids and families, this is even more of a no-brainer, as this is the best possible way to introduce new audiences to the Caped Crusader. All in all, while this may not have been the Batman game I needed, it was the one that we deserved as an experience that truly captures his iconic legacy.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight represents the biggest evolution in TT Games' Lego formula to date, seamlessly blending their signature British humor with mechanics inspired by the Batman Arkham series. While held back slightly by weaker stealth elements and classic developer-typical technical bugs, the fantastically detailed Gotham, refined gameplay, and clever tribute to Batman's entire history make this one of the best Lego games ever made.

Lego Batman: The Legacy of the Dark Knight remains a Lego game, with all the usual strengths and weaknesses that come with that, but this also makes it highly accessible to everyone. The game especially shines in the sheer amount of love for the character that Traveller's Tales has poured into it, both through the all‑encompassing story and the Arkham‑style combat.

Fans of the Dark Knight can’t really complain about anything missing from this release. It’s an exhaustive journey through the legacy of one of comicdom’s most famous characters that manages to incorporate both Batdance and cries of “Martha!” It is playful, clever, and consistently something that (in an era of serious storytelling influencing the form) so many games forget to be: fun.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a pretty entertaining and comedic experience for all fans of Batman especially when it has many deep references to the movies, comic lore and TV series. However, it lacks innovation because the LEGO game series still follows the same comfort zone formula with its repetitive activities.

Legacy of the Dark Knight tries to honour many legacies at once, and struggles to serve them all effectively. A familiar but fun LEGO game, a functional and simplified continuation of the Batman: Arkham series’ mechanics and an unambitious and only intermittently funny Batman story all sit alongside one another in a final build of a game that will still be enjoyed by many, but is never quite the sum of its bricks and will unlikely have much of a legacy of its own.

This LEGO Batman : Legacy of the Dark Knight is a true love letter to DC’s massive franchise. If you’re a fan of the Caped Crusader, you’ll be delighted to find all these iconic references that have endured through the decades. And if you’re less of a Batman fan, then this LEGO game is a great way to discover Bruce Wayne’s story, LEGO-style, while having a great time...Unlike the older LEGO Batman titles, this one offers a larger world, a wider variety of enemies and bosses, even if the combat can sometimes feel repetitive, and above all, a story that almost completely retells everything from A to Z. In short, it’s a really enjoyable game to play, with, of course, plenty of side quests and collectibles to hunt down, just like any good LEGO-branded game.
