LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight Legacy is a safe bet—perhaps even too safe. It checks all the expected boxes without ever taking any risks. Worse still, it tries to have it both ways without ever fully satisfying players on either front. Fans will undoubtedly find something to enjoy, thanks in particular to the richness of the universe and the numerous references. But those hoping for a more significant evolution of the formula may be left wanting. This new installment of LEGO Batman thus fulfills its purpose with diligence. Accessible, generous, and faithful to the spirit of the franchise, it offers a pleasant and familiar adventure—for better or for worse... Another brick in a solid edifice, but one that could certainly use a bit of a refresh.
Filled to the brim with content that will excite every Batman fan, Legacy of the Dark Knight ist yet another fun Lego romp that slightly misses the mark by relying too much on boring combat sections.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a lovingly crafted nostalgia trip that could do with a tighter focus to really spread its leathery wings.
When Legacy of the Dark Knight finds its focus, there's still plenty of zen-like charm to enjoy here. And if you crave the chaotic? Well, beanbag begins. [Issue#425, p.112]
"Young and old, gather round / Everybody hail the new king in town."
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is an endless parade of references and gags that's difficult to resist. Our review.
Legacy of The Dark Knight has set a new plastic mold for TT Games, and is easily the studio’s best work since the golden age of Batman, Indiana Jones, Star Wars, and Marvel Super Heroes.

It's still simple, but not quite as simple, it's bursting with even more secrets, and it's another playful take on a mythology that I love. It's the most fun I've had with a Lego game since 2005, and a template for how Lego games can rebuild into something greater, piece by piece.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. Whether you're a fan of Batman or Lego games, there's a lot to love in this charming adventure.

It would be easy to get caught up in LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight's pitfalls and dunk on the repetitive combat and performance, but truthfully, the game is far too fun to warrant too much negativity.With a frequently hilarious script, endless callbacks, and a cracking open world to explore, TT's love for the Caped Crusader always manages to shine through. And hey, love like that is infectious.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a catch-all Batman experience that takes liberal inspiration from everything tied to the Caped Crusader.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a great experience overall, and will likely find a passionate audience among those who love this series, but it also won’t do much to convert people who simply don’t enjoy the silly simplicity of the genre.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is an outstanding return to the formula. Fans of the Dark Knight will be pleasantly surprised at all the suits, songs, and storylines included.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight truly deserves to be recognized as a "love letter" to Batman. TT Games has delivered an engaging adventure for the whole family, albeit one incapable of offering any serious challenge to players.
Having reached the end of this analysis, I can say that LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a masterpiece in every sense of the word and in everything it sets out to be.

Regarding the LEGO M.O., the cliché can ring true: what you see is what you get. Thankfully, in Legacy of the Dark Knight's case, you see a lot of great things. Despite the bugs, this is a refined entry in many ways. Don't be surprised if your play sessions run longer than expected and if your interest holds well after the credits roll. If it's been a while since you've played one of these LEGO Batman games, now is a great time to hop back in. "Like a growing addiction that I can't deny," Legacy of the Dark Knight is "the new king in town."

I'm pretty sure everyone on the LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight dev team could beat the rest of the world at Batman trivia. Sometimes that makes for fantastic jokes and cool recreations of iconic scenes, and sometimes it results in an overabundance of references without the substance to back it up. The Arkham gameplay is a great new spin on the LEGO formula, and this brick-built Gotham may be one of the city's best interpretations yet. If you go in with the right expectations, this could be your new favourite LEGO game.
It's been eleven years since the last Batman: Arkham game and almost twelve years since LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham. The Caped Crusader's...

This is a really great game for all Batman fans. It can be a bit rough around the edges technically, and the gameplay is a bit too basic at times, but it’s hard not to appreciate just how much the developers love the Dark Knight in all his incarnations.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight builds on strong LEGO foundations by incorporating the Arkham games and LEGO City Undercover. It’s become more sprawling and more engaging through combat, stealth and driving. But its accessibility has not been lost: anyone can dance with the devil in the pale moonlight, not just adults.
Fun celebration of the Batman mythos, now in LEGO form

Here’s the thing: with everything said, this is simply one of the best Lego games ever created. Frankly, if the conversation is "Top 10 Batman Video Games", it needs to be included there as well. A slick and wonderful exploration of the history of Batman and crew that has some rough edges, but is ultimately so smart and well created that it’s hard not to smile the whole time it’s on.
If anything I kept lamenting what we lost in Rocksteady and Batman games from the last decade. Save your 60 dollars and buy yourself a cool LEGO set. I can guarantee you'll get more fun from that.

Legacy of the Dark Knght is a charming tribute to the legacy of the Dark Knight, putting you in control of Bruce Wayne/Batman from his childhood all the way to his prime as the Caped Crusader. By drawing from various sources, including the films and blending them with an original approach and a touch of humor, the game delivers an entertaining and engaging narrative. Its combat system, inspired by the Arkham trilogy, offers a seamless flow in battles and provides a more structured gameplay experience compared to previous installments. Finally, the developers' admirable finesse in crafting a dark yet vibrant Gotham City makes Legacy of the Dark Knight a must-play for Batman fans that absolutely shouldn't be missed.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is both a very good LEGO Batman game and a very good overall Batman game. The focus on a small set of characters makes everyone feel like they're more than just a skin swap. The use of an open world is well done, since it actually feels like a living place. The combat is more fluid but feels natural, while the kid-friendly humor is retained to keep the game feeling light-hearted, even during the more serious scenes. This is a game meant for every kind of Batman fan, and it is a title well worth playing.
If you've missed LEGO humor and love Batman, this is a game you'll enjoy. However, remember that this series is ultimately "aimed at children," so adjust your expectations accordingly.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is proof that TT Games is ready to evolve as they made the bold move to ditch tired, old mechanics in favor of a mature, story-driven, and genuinely fun experience; and even though the game's "Lego nature" slightly limits how deep the combat and storytelling can go, it still manages to impress, proving just how much untapped potential this franchise has.

This isn't just another LEGO game thrown out for a quick buck. It's an ambitious, mature, and incredibly atmospheric project that brilliantly combines Gotham's dark cinematic history with the playfulness, insight, and typical humor of the Danish construction set.

Legacy of the Dark Knight is at its best when it lets you alternate, unhurriedly, between a main mission full of clever ideas and a spontaneous detour through the streets of Gotham. TT Games does not reinvent every LEGO mechanic and the combat cannot carry the weight of the entire adventure on its own, but it builds a surprisingly cohesive tribute to Batman. On Switch 2, portability is a concrete advantage for those who accept some technical compromises and a less polished city than in the other versions. The Chaos Collection rounds out the picture well, especially for those who want a more frenetic alternative – though shorter in length – to the main campaign.

While Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight’s implementation of its Arkham-inspired systems might leave much to be desired, its simplified nature does little to dampen the joys of collecting that Lego games are so well-loved for.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight successfully combines the atmosphere of the Arkham games with classic LEGO humor in a way that works surprisingly well. Gotham is fantastic to explore, the combat system feels fluid and satisfying, and the more focused character roster gives the gameplay far more purpose than in older LEGO titles. While the lack of online co-op remains the game’s biggest drawback, Legacy of the Dark Knight easily stands among the best and most ambitious LEGO games released in recent years.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight was a blast. Exploring Gotham City felt like a family-friendly Grand Theft Auto, and that’s not a bad thing at all! The story was engaging and the humour spot-on, meaning I was rarely left without a smile on my face. Everything is awesome? Pretty much!

Lego Batman: The Legacy of The Dark Knight blends sharp humor, excellent writing, rich combat, and a beautifully crafted Lego Gotham into a wildly entertaining experience that shouldn't be underestimated.
For LEGO fanatics and lovers of all things Batman, this is a strange but entertaining amalgam of Batmans from every form of media and generation brought to life

I absolutely loved my time with LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight. The game has great visuals, a storied past that wraps and intertwines decades of Batman tales, a traversal and gameplay out of the Arkham series, all in a well-built Gotham City. If you love Batman or LEGO games, this is a must buy.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the best LEGO game ever made and a true love letter to Batman. The story is a fantastic combination of every era of the character; the smaller pool of characters is enjoyable to play as and customise; and it’s one of the best-looking games of the year. If you’re a fan of Batman, LEGO, or just fun games in general, do yourself a favour and play Legacy of the Dark Knight.

Despite its cute art style, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is an entertaining action-adventure game that will keep players entertained for hours, even with its simpler combat system, occasionally clunky controls, and a somewhat annoying number of bugs. Thanks to its amazingly crafted levels, rich open world, and great story, the game can proudly stand alongside the successful Batman: Arkham series. And it can certainly be considered one of the best LEGO games.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes two opposite ends of the spectrum, Lego comedy and accessible gameplay with Batman’s darker tone and stealth-oriented sections, and meshes them together to great effect with only a few outliers. Visually stunning, inventive mission structure and an impressive open-world Gotham full of hilarious comedic writing. Some aspects that are made more accessible for a younger audience, such as combat, don’t hit as well, but if you adjust to this lighter, comedy-first Batman, then there’s something for both newcomers and veterans to enjoy.

It’s time, then, to draw our conclusions from this review of LEGO Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight, stating that this is a game we highly recommend. It doesn’t break any new ground in terms of gameplay, but everything it does, it does very well. As much fun as all LEGO games are, this is the closest we’ve come in years to a new game in the Arkham series. Recommended for all LEGO fans, Batman fans, or anyone who loves open-world action-adventure games.
It's not only the best LEGO game ever, but the grand return of the Gotham legend we've all been waiting for. An essential masterpiece to experience down to the last brick.

A fun LEGO twist on the iconic caped crusader’s tale, this game mixes solid combat with Gotham’s charms. Great for Batman fans seeking a lighthearted adventure. Legacy of the Dark Knight is TT Games’ most ambitious and most successful LEGO game in years — a genuine Batman experience wrapped in the LEGO brand’s best qualities, with a campaign that earns its runtime and a Gotham worth spending time in. Its weaknesses — the thin roster, the post-game content drop-off, the performance wrinkles — are real, but they don’t diminish what the game does right. Which is quite a lot.
Legacy of the Dark Knight doesn’t just feel like another Lego Batman game. It feels like the future of the Lego franchise, and it’s one I thoroughly enjoyed from beginning to end.

Who could have thought that, after the surefire disaster that was the Suicide Squad game, the salvation to the cherished Batman Arkham gameplay loop would arrive in the form of a Lego game? Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t just “a good Lego game”, or “a fun diversion if you like Batman”. It’s an impressive new direction for the TT Games Lego formula, focusing on quality over quantity, deeper gameplay over mindless collectability, and an even deeper level of polish and writing.

Only seven playable characters, a lack of mini kits and skins posing as rewards instead of real gameplay advantages? Compared to earlier Lego outings from TT Games this feels like a downgrade to me. On top of that the activities tend to be to samey while also happening always in the same setting as opposed world hopping former Lego adventures. Still: Lego Batman - Legacy of the Dark Knight has ignited my collectathon fever once more, the animations are endearing and the dark atmosphere in Gotham City's eternal nighttime is crafted so well it is striking.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is far from a simple LEGO game — it's the best Batman title since the Arkham trilogy.

In many ways, a huge step forward across the board. It is not without a few stumbles, but the lingering repetitiveness is still masked well. The result is an entertaining game full of wild humor, likable characters, an excellent combat system, and vehicle handling that brings back memories of the beloved Arkham series. For DC fans, this is a must-play.

TT Games has dismantled decades of Batman and reassembled them into something fresh, built on the best combat system ever seen in a LEGO game. It's not Arkham, but it's the closest thing available today — wrapped in the humor and content generosity only the LEGO brand can deliver. For Dark Knight fans, it's unmissable.

I don’t know if we’re likely to see another Arkham game any time soon, but as long as we get something as inventive and as fun as LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, I’m perfectly prepared to wait a lot longer.

The game offers plenty of side missions as well as a free-roam style that allows for lots of play after completing the main story, and also allows players to spend time with some costumes and ability variants.

It's a game clearly built with affection for the character, packed with references for longtime fans and accessible enough for those simply looking for a fun adventure with friends. It's also commendable that Traveller's Tales, with its latest releases, has chosen to tailor the experience to the specific franchise they're working with, as was the case with The Skywalker Saga. Obviously, this has meant a much longer wait for the next game, but it's worth it. That's why, even though 12 years have passed since Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham (2014), the Dark Knight has proven he still knows how to make a comeback.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a worthy addition to the LEGO game franchise. After the rather lukewarm reception of LEGO Horizon Adventures, this latest entry once again delivers an experience that Batman and DC Comics fans will appreciate, while its charming presentation and humor are engaging enough to appeal even to players who are not particularly interested in superheroes.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t just a great LEGO game; it’s a genuinely fantastic Batman game.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is more than a nostalgic tribute: it is the most ambitious LEGO game in years, turning Gotham into a heartfelt playground for Batman fans.

Legacy of the Dark Knight is the biggest surprise of the year, and I didn't expect it at all. TT Games took a character who hasn’t had a game worthy of his legacy in over a decade, wrapped him in LEGO bricks, and delivered an experience that will make Batman fans feel right at home. The few minor missteps do little to detract from the overall package.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight celebrates decades of the DC hero’s history with a game that appears ambitious on paper, but ultimately falls into the traps of simplicity, repetition, and a few less entertaining excesses.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight mixes LEGO humor, Arkham-style combat, open-world Gotham, strong Bat-Family moments, and rich Batman fan service, but its easy difficulty, shallow stealth, smaller roster, and lack of online co-op hold it back.

I have played a few LEGO games, but the franchise has never clicked with me quite as much as LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight. Maybe it’s the fact that the title used Batman: Arkham as a base for its combat, or the well-designed open world. I don’t think so, though. So much of the experience feels like a more compelling version of what LEGO does. I remember playing LEGO Horizon with characters being random in every scene, an extension of the LEGO formula.

All in all, this is a solid overall package and a game that should delight fans of both Lego games and Batman adventures, but I do need to temper the hype somewhat, as I find too many shortcomings to join in on the most enthusiastic praise. The game is comfortable, charming and at times genuinely enjoyable, but never quite lives up to what it could have been.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight successfully celebrates the Dark Knight’s entire legacy while offering a modern, accessible adventure packed with content. Thanks to its excellent art direction, vast array of references, and open world that’s a joy to explore, the game easily ranks among the best LEGO titles of recent years. Admittedly, some side activities lack originality, and a few technical glitches occasionally slow down the pace of the adventure. However, these flaws remain relatively minor when you consider everything the game accomplishes. Although an online mode would have greatly enhanced the two-player experience. Ultimately, whether you’re a fan of the movies, the animated series, or the comic books, this title is well worth your attention.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a huge love letter to Batman, with an open Gotham, Arkham-inspired combat and the unmistakable charm of LEGO bricks.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is exactly what a fan of LEGO games would expect, without redefining the series, despite Rocksteady’s contribution and the clever additions to its combat system.
LEGO Batman put together a fun formula by blending Arkham‑style gameplay with bits of story pulled from various Batman films.

Lego Batman: Legacy Of The Dark Knight is a Lego game that uses the combat of the Arkham games. The game plays well and has different difficulty levels. Nevertheless, it is not too difficult. It is a celebration of Batman in Lego style for young &a; old.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight delivers a highly entertaining and affectionate tribute to the Caped Crusader's history, skillfully combining the atmospheric essence of the Arkham series with LEGO’s signature, lighthearted humor. While its stealth mechanics fall flat and the repetitive open-world police alerts can feel bloated, the game shines through its visually stunning rendition of Gotham City, satisfying combat, and a brilliant musical score heavily inspired by the films. It stands as a rich, deeply satisfying experience that any dedicated Batman fan will thoroughly enjoy despite its minor flaws.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is hard to knock. There are some hiccups, but generally, the game is a fantastic way to celebrate the impact of Batman in another way. Blending the movies was a smart move to tell a familiar but somewhat new story. The combat is familiar yet fresh. It’s the perfect balance of fun and broodiness that a LEGO Batman game should be.

Maybe one day Rocksteady will return and create the next great Batman game. But until then, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight reminds us that sometimes the one you least expect is the one who best understands what a dark city truly needs.

The best thing about Batman is definitely its insightful, genuinely funny script. The characters crack jokes, the game is full of references to the films, and the story moves naturally forward. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a comprehensive history of Bruce Wayne's life, deeds, and companions, with a family-friendly, fun twist from TT Games.

Overall, I think that's one of the game's biggest strengths; Batman has so much source material to draw from, It makes sense to mix and match to create a cohesive patchwork of gameplay,
story and visual elements that will appeal to both obsessive and more casual fans, as well as create new ones. I would love to see other DC franchises get this treatment, and I think there are plenty of other franchises that would fit the bill too, such as Marvel, and even Star wars, if the team can have creative permission to tell an all new story in a galaxy far far away.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is one of the best that TT Games has put out to date. This sets the standard of what LEGO games should be. Funny, engaging story, simplified combat, and plenty of references are to be found in this game.
A richly crafted tribute to Batman’s world, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight offers fun combat, deep references, and collectible‑filled stages fans will enjoy.

LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight’s Legacy is, without a shadow of a doubt, the finest brick-based incarnation of the Caped Crusader ever created. Traveller’s Tales has delivered an adventure brimming with personality, which celebrates decades of the character’s history through a reimagining that is both entertaining and, above all, faithful to the original material. However, those hoping to find the same depth and level of challenge as in the Arkham series may be disappointed.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a love letter to both Batman and the Arkham series. It successfully combines surprisingly deep combat, gorgeous visuals, and classic LEGO charm into one unforgettable adventure. TT Games delivers its most ambitious LEGO game yet, blending Arkham-inspired action with the heart and humour fans expect. Gotham has never looked better in plastic form.
LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight’s Legacy goes all out on fan service, and it works.

"Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight" is a tribute to 80 years of Batman. The game brings together Batman characters from a wide range of eras and tells a story of its own. It’s packed with Lego slapstick and humorous one-liners that make me laugh just as much as they do my five-year-old son.

TT Games didn’t just rebuild Batman here. Along with their last stellar showing, LEGO Skywalker Saga, they’ve slapped down a duplo-sized brick in a larger plan to rebuild my faith in the entire LEGO games formula.
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a love letter to the character, the fans and the Batman universe.

LEGO games are usually lots of fun to begin with, but this one is elevated by being a fantastic tribute to decades of Batman. If you’re a fan of Batman, you’re really going to love the storylines, costumes, and references.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight proves to be a massive, incredibly fun game, crafted with such attention to detail that every single Batman fan should experience it. Despite a gameplay system inherited directly from the Arkham series that falls short in polish (both in terms of gameplay and technical execution) and an underlying humor that, in rare moments of the campaign, feels overly pervasive and out of place, its encyclopedic scope, the extraordinary variety of main missions, and a spine-tingling audiovisual presentation make it an incredibly solid, massive, and satisfying product. If you’re looking for a total, reverential, and visceral journey into the history and immortal myth of Batman, this is practically a must-buy. TT Games has hit the mark once again, crafting a splendid and memorable declaration of love. We’re betting it will remain in the hearts of The Dark Knight fans for a long time to come.

While LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is what you expect from a LEGO action adventure game, kudos to TT Games for implementing Batman: Arkham quadrology mechanics in its retelling of the Batman mythos (albeit in all-ages family friendly form).

Lego Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight stands out as not only the finest Lego game we've ever played but also ranks among the greatest Batman titles of all time. Featuring numerous Easter eggs, sharp humor, and some of the most impressive combat mechanics seen in a Lego game, Lego Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight will undoubtedly be remembered as one of the most exceptional titles ever developed by TT Games.
LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight Legacy, despite some uncertainties, is without too many doubts the best LEGO game, and the greatest love letter, ever made by TT Games.

The LEGO Batman games have generally been good, but LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes things in a familiar yet new direction I hope we see more of, and across different properties. The improved combat feels weighty and impactful, yet whimsy as “CRACK!” and “POW!” pops up on-screen. The reverence for Batman by TT Games is truly felt, and is such a celebration of the character for nearly 90 years across comics, TV, and film. Legacy of the Dark Knight is the best LEGO Batman game to-date, but is also the best Batman game yet.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is without a doubt the most ambitious and mature LEGO Batman game to date. TT Games combines a stunning open world, more in-depth combat and a loving tribute to Batman’s entire history into an adventure that will appeal to both fans and newcomers alike. The story isn’t always perfectly tight, but the charm, humour and sheer joy of playing more than make up for it. As far as I’m concerned, this is the surprise hit of 2026.

LEGO Batman: The Dark Knight's Legacy is highly recommended because it's the most ambitious project TT Games has ever undertaken within the LEGO franchise. Their reinterpretation of the Batman universe is admirable; it's a true love letter to the Dark Knight. All of this comes together to make for a fun game to play, always with the studio's signature sense of humor. If you’re a Batman fan, this game is made by and for you.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a witty, brilliantly affectionate celebration of Caped Crusader history that masterfully balances sharp satire with fluid, Arkham-inspired combat. While repetitive enemy waves, shallow stealth, and overly simplistic puzzles check its momentum, the vibrant Gotham open world offers an incredibly rich co-op value.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is pure, unadulterated fun, delivering another excellent LEGO outing coated with the legacy of one of the most iconic comic book characters of all time.

Although Legacy of the Dark Knight did not reinvent the genre of “brick-built” games, it stands as undeniable proof of the decades of experience and brilliance that TT Games represents. This game is not merely a love letter to Batman, but to Batman’s legacy as well.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knights feels like the ultimate Batman fan game disguised as a LEGO title. TT Games somehow managed to capture everything that makes Batman such an iconic character, from the darker Gotham atmosphere and Arkham-inspired combat, right through to the humour, gadgets, and the ridiculous amount of fan service packed into every corner of the game. As someone who grew up obsessed with Batman, this honestly felt like stepping into a playable tribute to the Dark Knight’s entire legacy.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight has all the ingredients of a great Lego game: fun co-op gameplay, slapstick humour, puzzle solving, and constant chaos, all handled quite well. What pushes it beyond a typical Lego title, though, is Gotham City itself. The world feels massive, detailed, and genuinely enjoyable to explore, with enough side content and traversal options to keep things enjoyable even outside the main story. While the narrative is fairly straightforward, the writing and character interactions keep it charming throughout. More importantly, the game understands exactly what people want from a Batman Lego game and delivers on that setup with polish from the start to the finish.

After spending several hours in the city, it’s hard not to appreciate the amount of care that went into this adventure. Between the impressive visual quality, the particularly successful sound design, and the huge amount of content available outside the main missions, the game constantly makes you want to keep exploring the city. Every district hides a secret, a reference, or something new to unlock, and that’s exactly what makes the experience so enjoyable over time.
Warner Bros. and TT Games bring us a new adventure featuring the Dark Knight, based on the LEGO building blocks we all know and love.

LEGO Batman: El Legado del Caballero Oscuro is the best LEGO video game to date. The evolution of its combat and puzzle-solving mechanics, along with a more than substantial improvement to its open world, make this a title that truly transcends the classic formula we have experienced so far. TT Games has done a stellar job of turning this brick-built world into a universe with its own distinct personality.

Iconic scenes covered, ultra present humor (you only have to see how Harvey Dent becomes Double Face), staged almost cinematic and solid gameplay but which does not stand out from the Rocksteady production, LEGO Batman: The Legacy of the Black Knight will bring a lot of pleasure even if the sharp collectivity side and the immensity of the tasks to be accomplished will be able to tire.

Batman makes a triumphant return to video games, paying homage to the legacy of previous titles while incorporating all the humor and charisma of LEGO that the experienced Traveller's Tales developers have accustomed us to. A gift for all fans of one of the most important superheroes in pop culture.

Legacy of The Dark Knight is the ultimate love letter to everything Batman, from the original comics to the films and everything else surrounding this cornerstone of the DC universe, serving as a spiritual successor to the original Arkhamverse adventures. With an adventure spanning various eras, packed with jokes and references that pay homage to the original material, a superbly realised Gotham City brimming with content, and the return of Arkham-style combat—which I’d missed terribly—this title is a safe bet for anyone seeking quality action, whether playing solo or with friends, for both LEGO fans and Batman fans alike.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is one of the most complicated LEGO games ever. Instead of just replicating what had already been done, TT Games wanted to mix the accessibility and personality of LEGO with the dramatic narrative, exploration, and combat depth of current Batman games.

The game is certainly not perfect; the combat and puzzles are too easy, the vehicles could have offered more freedom, and those prompt bugs are just annoying. But there is a lot to compensate for that. Gotham City looks beautiful, the Batcave is surprisingly fun to build out, and there is a huge amount to do in the city. The story might not be very long, but the amount of side content and unlocks ensures that you won't be nearly done with it when the credits roll. For Batman fans, this is an absolute must-have and the best Batman game since the Arkham series. For anyone in the mood for a large, accessible open-world game with plenty of humor, many unlocks, and a wonderful atmosphere, this is also one to keep an eye on.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight feels like a return to form for TT Games in many ways. It follows Arkham's lead, pulls in decades of Batman history, and slathers it all in the well-trodden LEGO formula that values accessibility and charm.
It's not just the references that make it work, but also the gameplay and the thrill of exploring Gotham. Whether someone is a LEGO fan, a Batman fan, or both, there's something here to enjoy.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a very enjoyable open-world adventure that celebrates Batman with great care and charm, honoring iconic films while expanding the series' gameplay with new mechanics and deeper combat. Technical flaws and limited side-content hold it back slightly, but it remains an outstanding tribute for Batman fans of all ages.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a love letter to the character, making any Batman fan very happy. It changes the LEGO formula a bit by focusing on the Bat-family instead of having many playable characters, and it feels like a spiritual successor to the Batman Arkham games.

Describing a game as "a love letter" to something is a cliché, but the truth is, there's no better way to describe this work than as "a love letter to Batman's history." Fans of the character will enjoy a fun journey through the cinematic history of the Dark Knight, filled with entertaining puzzles and plenty of objects to find. However, those who haven't seen the movies and won't understand the references and might not forgive the numerous technical issues, the repetitive combat system, or the many minor flaws it has.
TT Games delivers an adventure worthy of the legacy of one of the greatest characters in entertainment, easing a bit of the nostalgia left behind by the Arkham trilogy in the gaming world.

It’s not often I find myself being blown away by a LEGO game. In general, they’re games geared towards a much younger audience of players, and while LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight still maintains much of the playful, blocky heart and soul that makes the LEGO universe so enduringly charming, it also does something very impressive with the Batman IP, both narratively and mechanically, that makes it feel like one of those big blockbuster AAA Batman game that we would get from Rocksteady Studios. 

With it pulling from 85 years of Batman history, this feels like a worthwhile tribute to the Caped Crusader. It’s a reminder of why we love him so much, whether we first met him through the gritty lens of modern cinema, the animated classics of our childhood, the comics, or a pile of plastic bricks on the living room floor. 

Without a question, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a must-play for all Batman fans out there.

LEGO Batman: The Legacy of the Dark Knight masterfully delivers on its proposal to celebrate more than 80 years of the hero’s history, bringing a story packed with references and GREAT humor, alongside a lively Gotham City that invites exploration, marking the beginning of a new era for the franchise, despite stepping on a few LEGO bricks with a somewhat repetitive combat system and little enemy variety.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight stands as one of the most complete titles in the LEGO franchise. Its combination of open world, variety of content, and adaptation of one of the character's most popular stories results in an engaging and accessible experience.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight brings the spirit of the Arkham games into the LEGO universe in a way that clicks. Gotham is a joy to explore, the combat feels great, and the humor keeps the darker Batman lore light without losing its charm. The lack of online co-op is a shame, but this is easily one of the strongest LEGO games in years.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a superb remake of an already excellent adventure game, and is utterly essential for fans.
Replaying Black Flag after 13 years and witnessing how well it aged and how perfectly it was adapted to the current generation is a delight.
Everything you loved about Black Flag is there but just refined, polished and re-wrapped with the biggest changes coming in the smaller mechanics to make the whole story feel more fluid.
The Golden Age of Piracy may be over, but Black Flag Resynced seems intent on reminding us why it's one of the most romanticized time periods of the modern age.

One of the best games in the franchise receives an impeccable treatment. With stunning visuals and technical brilliance, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced already stands as one of the best remakes ever made and a necessary modernization that we hope to see in more games in the future.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a fantastic remake that adds meaningful changes and quality-of-life improvements that make an already stellar swashbuckling adventure an absolute must-have for PS5 owners.

Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced is the definitive way to experience one of the greatest Assassin's Creed games ever made. With its stunning visual overhaul, meaningful accessibility features, and thoughtful story additions, it fully delivers on the fantasy of living life as a swashbuckling pirate. Even without the modern-day storyline that once raised the stakes, and despite the occasional bugs and glitches, Edward Kenway's unforgettable voyage across the Caribbean never feels rudderless. Resynced sets a new blueprint for the series while making the original pale by comparison, proving itself to be well worth its weight in gold.
After all these years, Edward Kenway’s story is still the best virtual pirate experience out there, and this version only confirms that. A top-tier remake of a top-tier classic.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag: Resynced is the best possible tribute Ubisoft could have paid to one of the saga’s most beloved and iconic entries. More than just a remake that lives up to expectations, it is a carefully crafted return that leaves no room for doubt. The addition of new scenes and an expanded storyline featuring familiar faces adds an extra layer of immersion and enjoyment. Thanks to the graphics engine used to recreate the game’s environments, along with its countless improvements, it stands as one of the best remakes of the year. It may even encourage Ubisoft to revive other classic entries, such as the one starring Altaïr.

Black Flag Resynced marks the return of a great Assassin’s Creed game, but more importantly, the return of a true adventure. It is the kind of game that makes you want to set sail, explore, hunt for treasure, watch the sun go down over the ocean, and remember why Black Flag remains such a special entry in the series even today.
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has been remade from the ground up using Ubisoft's in-house Anvil Engine, using the same technology that brought forth Shadows.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced nails what mattered most: the visuals are stunning, naval combat has never been better, and the expanded story finally gives Edward, Caroline, and the rest of the crew the depth they deserved. A few rough edges won't stop veterans from feeling the wind at their backs again — the Jackdaw is back, Edward is back, and in fine style.

Black Flag might be Resynced, but its heart remains. In many ways this remake is a one-to-one carbon copy of the original, with some annoying bits shaved off and the good parts improved. With a few caveats, it remains that same great game from 2013, upgraded with flashier graphics, a snappy combat system, and added depth it desperately needed even 12 years ago.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is an absolutely fantastic remake. Not only does it maintain what made the original so great in the first place, but every new addition only builds upon its foundation, each of which lends itself to a gameplay loop that never gets old and a visual style that frequently had me stunned with awe. Despite some problems here and there, this is still an absolute must-play, regardless of whether you are a new fan of Assassin's Creed or you've been following it since the beginning.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is everything I wanted from a modern remake of one of the franchise’s most beloved entries. It respects what made the original so special while smartly refining the areas that needed improvement, such as combat and ship gameplay.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is like discovering a lost treasure. So much could have gone wrong in bringing this behemoth back from the depths, but Ubisoft does so with tremendous care and respect.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced proves that some classics only needed modern technology to shine even brighter. With stunning visuals, refined naval combat and meaningful additions to its original story, Ubisoft successfully modernizes one of the franchise's best entries without losing its identity. While minor issues with AI and Brazilian Portuguese lip-sync remain, the adventure of Edward Kenway is as captivating as ever, making this an essential remake for both longtime fans and newcomers.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced improves on the original game in various ways, resulting in an experience that feels more rewarding, immersive and dynamic. It looks bloody lovely, too. Whether you're an Assassin's Creed fan or simply want to be a pirate, consider this a must-play.

Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced successfully justifies its return with meaningful new story content, a refined combat system, and stunning visual upgrades that elevate one of the franchise's most beloved adventures. While some pacing issues from the original remain, the remake modernizes the experience without losing what made Edward Kenway's pirate journey so memorable, making it an easy recommendation for both newcomers and returning fans.

The red "X" marked the spot. And for Ubisoft, it was a treasure that
turned out to be real. After years of navigating rough seas, the company
has finally found solid ground, bringing Edward Kenway's legendary
adventure back in great fashion. It's fair to say that Assassin's Creed
Black Flag Resynced is everything fans were hoping for.

I’ve come away from Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced remarkably impressed, as it’s a top-notch remake of an already excellent game. Though there are a few little bumps throughout on the technical side, the revamped mechanics and expanded story, supported by the updated visuals, do more than enough to validate this remake’s existence. Whether or not you’ve played the original Black Flag, Resynced is certainly worthy of your time.

Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag remains one of the best video games ever made, with a beautiful, moving and action-heavy story worth experiencing. Resynced updates and modernises it, with clever tweaks to streamline its story and ensure the original game's legacy is never forgotten.

While I have my gripes with some of the new content that's been introduced here, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a stellar remake of one of the best games the long-running series has to offer. Ubisoft Singapore has brought the pirate dream back to life with Resynced, and I think longtime fans will be very pleased with their efforts here.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced does far more than enhance the visuals of an already captivating game. It also improves key aspects such as combat and the user interface, delivering an experience that is well worth revisiting. In addition, it introduces a substantial amount of fresh and varied content designed to entice even seasoned sea dogs who have already sailed through Edward Kenway’s adventure.

A great remake of a great game. It doesn't ruin what was good, improves
what needed fixing, and adds new content at the same time. It can be
overly simplified at times, but it's still the best option for fans of
pirate stories.

With modern controls and some smart changes, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced brings the classic into the current AC era, smoothing out the wrinkles of the original game. With its sprawling and beautiful Caribbean ocean, Resynced wisely doesn't overwhelm the player with tasks, instead leaning into a fun but unobtrusive story that can be ignored for hours in favor of some rewarding exploration. While I bounced off the original, I can now see why so many people love this game.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is an absolute must-play. It’s a remake that may not take a lot of risks, but when you have such a legendary foundation to work with, the new quality-of-life upgrades make this an easy Game of the Year contender. I wish the combat were a bit more fleshed out and that side activities like Assassin’s Contracts weren't so bare-bones (they're barely worth mentioning), but overall, Resynced is a treasure well worth hunting down.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced takes one of the most beloved Assassin’s Creed games and overhauls it to a degree that absolutely justifies its existence. Ubisoft Singapore has brought the Caribbean to life like never before and improved combat and parkour at a foundational level. While enough is cut from the original Black Flag to prevent it from being the “complete” package, the core experience is a feast for the eyes and has never felt better to play, giving players the perfect excuse to fondly remember a classic in a new way.

At its best, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced firmly establishes the formula for new remakes in the franchise, if not what all new Assassin's Creed games in 2026 and beyond should feel like. At its absolute bottom-of-the-ocean worst, it's a reminder of what made the Assassin's Creed franchise the beloved game series it was in the first place.
De perfecte zomertrip.

In almost every way, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a better-looking and better-playing experience than the original. Melee and naval combat have received outstanding updates, and the newly minted open world is a joy to explore. Both the main and side missions provide excellent opportunities for exploration. The original game’s story and characters are among the best in the series and remain a solid foundation on which to build the world. Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced strikes a near-perfect balance between preservation and improvement.
Even after 13 years, no game has managed to surpass Black Flag as the ultimate pirate simulator.

Assassins Creed Black Flag Resynched is a rare remake in today’s age. It actually feels like the developers have sunk passion and time into the project and made this a worthy addition to the franchise. Sure, there are some missteps, with bugs and glitches and the uneven combat system, but, for the most part, this is a beautiful journey. It’s a wonderful story with new characters and content, stellar naval combat and exploration and some of the best visuals this year. Black Flag Resynched is what makes this franchise so beloved. It will always be, a pirate’s life for me.

Still, even with these minor narrative missteps, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a standout remake, taking the best bits of the original and sprucing them up for the modern era. From its stunning visuals and revamped combat to new characters and redesigned missions, it’s a must-play for anyone who’s looking to replay through Edward Kenway’s pirating journey. And for those (like myself) who never gave the original a go, this one’s a no-brainer.
Edward Kenway returns in a truly spectacular remake that feels like a modern game but doesn't lose its essence. Pirate songs, intense naval battles, and unforgettable adventures are guaranteed.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag: Resynced modernizes a series classic without losing its unmatched pirate atmosphere. The definitive version of one of Assassin’s Creed’s finest entries.

The mix of the good memories and the new improvements works like a charm. This is a big (but not TOO big) adventure, full with action, surprises and great characters. The déjá vu factor is there, though.

For those who are already fans of the original or have always wanted to experience Edward Kenway's journey, I think it is well worth it. Even though it isn't perfect, in my opinion, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resyned reminds us just how good the franchise can be and remains one of the series' all-time highlights.

Resynced is a worthy remake of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag. Ubisoft has sensibly streamlined and modernised the game, and added new content. Despite offering little in the way of challenge, the whole pirat adventure has plenty to offer.

Black Flag: Resynced is a strong remake that reminds us why the original is still so beloved. Its appeal comes less from being a classic Assassin's Creed game and more from being a thrilling pirate adventure with a fantastic Caribbean setting, spectacular naval battles and highly motivating progression. Some typical series weaknesses remain, including repetitive structures and occasional control issues, but the overall experience still captures the unique charm that made Black Flag special.

A faithful and beautifully crafted remake that proves Black Flag remains one of the best pirate games ever made. While not every mechanic has aged gracefully, Ubisoft has delivered the definitive way to experience Edward Kenway's adventure.

While there is a glaring omission to the content in this package, Black Flag Resynced feels like the definitive pirate adventure that Ubisoft Montreal wanted to tell more than a decade ago. All of the improvements make this one of the best looking (and playing) Assassin's Creed adventures to date.
Veterans are going to enjoy revisiting the golden age of piracy, and newcomers get to experience what was still arguably one of the best games of all time.

Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced remains an excellent game, just like its predecessor was. Honestly, I can't say whether it's an unnecessary remake, because it definitely improves some aspects of the original, but makes others worse, such as the resource grind required to upgrade the Jackdaw. In the end, it's always great to replay a good game, especially in a newer and better-looking version, so yes, Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced is worth it.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced successfully modernizes one of the best titles in the series thanks to impressive audiovisuals and new content. However, beneath that revamp lies a design inherited from 2013 that shows its age. Even so, it remains a fun, solid pirate adventure that comes highly recommended for both veterans and new players.

Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced is a good but very safe remake. I still had a shocking amount of fun just sailing around and doing pirate things on the wide ocean, but the game lacks a certain confidence, and that keeps it from being a truly exceptional remake. It's a great way to revisit Edward's adventures with fewer rough patches, better graphics, and some extra content. Fans of the original will have a grand old time.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a refreshing reminder of the franchise's glory days. Charged with an infectious love for the original, Resynced is the best way to play the best Assassin's Creed game. If the Ezio trilogy is soon to get the same remaking, we can only hope it's treated in the same fashion.
Black Flag Resynced is the ultimate way to experience this fantastic adventure, even if some crack show through the new coat of paint
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is an excellent, revamped version that respects the most important aspects of the original adventure. Ideal for both veterans and new players.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a successful remake that modernizes a classic with improved visuals and expanded gameplay, serving as a solid action-adventure for both veterans and new players. While minor, aged flaws remain, the title successfully elevates the 2013 original and sets a strong foundation for the future of the series.

More than a decade after its original release, Assassin’s Creed IV Black Flag still stands apart as one of the most memorable entries in the franchise. At a time when the series has moved toward massive open worlds and RPG mechanics, Black Flag remains special because of its focus on adventure, exploration, and the simple joy of sailing across the Caribbean. That is also what made Resynced such a challenging project: modernize the experience without losing the identity that made the original so beloved. Ubisoft Singapore mostly succeeds by improving the visuals, refining certain mechanics, and adding new content while keeping the heart of Edward Kenway’s journey intact.It is not a perfect remake. The updated combat system can feel inconsistent, some choices like removing the modern-day Abstergo sections may divide fans, and a few new features could have been pushed further. But these issues never overshadow what made Black Flag great in the first place. Edward’s story remains one of the strongest in the series, the Caribbean is still a joy to explore, and the Jackdaw remains one of the best additions ever made to an Assassin’s Creed game. Whether you’re a longtime fan looking to return to the open seas or a newcomer discovering Edward Kenway’s adventure for the first time, Resynced proves that some journeys simply deserve to be experienced again. The treasure was already there, Ubisoft Singapore just polished it and brought it back to the surface.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a fun way to become a pirate assassin who loves to go around grabbing all the gold and stabbing everything that moves. Go be a pirate!

For me, a lot of the joy and excitement of Assassin’s Creed comes from visiting a new era in history and rediscovering the series’ conflict through the lens of that time and place. This return to a familiar locale lacks that, but it should still offer it for newer players who never experienced the game more than a decade ago. But even without that sense of newness, Black Flag Resynced is an impressive rework, setting a high bar for how to return to an older action game and make it relevant once more. I’d prefer to sail to new horizons, but I’m also happy to rediscover a journey that reminds me why I embraced the franchise in the first place.

One of the most visually striking games of 2026, Resynced reminds gamers of a certain age why “Black Flag” felt like such a bolt of lightning while also slipping into a few of the traps that would define the lesser entries in this series that would follow. In the end, “Black Flag Resynced” is a consistently entertaining piece of storytelling that sails through modern gaming waters despite its open-world ballast.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced does exactly what a great remake is supposed to do: replace the original as the definitive version of the game in the minds of fans. It looks, plays, and sounds better than the OG in every way, and makes up for the exclusion of the old modern-day segments with many hours of additional gameplay that round out Edward Kenway's story. Best of all, it feels like the classic AC adventures I love; simpler due to the lack of complicated action-RPG mechanics, but no less enjoyable.

If we're judging the game based on the parameters of a remake, it must also be said Ubisoft has done a fantastic job, serving up a tight and technically sound product with glossy and striking visuals, a wonderful attention to detail, and with the same beloved story and narrative at its core. Resynced is a top-of-the-line remake but quite an archaic action-adventure game at the same time.

Black Flag Resynced proves that Ubisoft still understands why this became one of the most popular Assassin's Creed games ever. The revamped gameplay and stunning Caribbean setting make getting lost in the open world a joy once again. The new additions are a fun but superficial complement, and rarely manage to evoke the same feeling and quality that made Black Flag so strong thirteen years ago. Ultimately, this remake is above all a tribute to a world that has stood the test of time remarkably well.
Black Flag Resynced is an extremely fun return to an old favourite, with some of the crunchier edges sanded off for a modern-day sensibility.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a triumph. Whilst I was nervous about such significant changes, they are mostly for the better. Combat in particular is a bit more challenging now, whilst also still allowing quick assassinations, naval warfare now has more options and is still the best ship-to-ship combat in gaming, and the removal of the modern day sequences makes space for more historical story and missions. It can get a little muddled and has the classic Ubisoft quirks and issues, but it’s hard not to enjoy this remake.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced successfully builds on the strong base established by the original release, but makes a few missteps.

Black Flag Resynced is a restoration born of a genuine love for its subject matter, and this is both its greatest strength and its most obvious limitation. On a technical and artistic level, it is a joy—the sea, the light, and the Caribbean once again cast their spell, perhaps even more potently than before—and the wealth of new content proves there was no shortage of daring talent. It is a shame, then, that this boldness didn't extend to the game's very foundations, leaving behind combat that feels (perhaps) too tame and a storyline that time has inevitably faded. Nevertheless, it remains a fantastic way to hoist the sails again—or to do so for the first time, if you missed out on Edward’s Caribbean back in the day.

Like a captain going down with their ship, Ubisoft has remained loyal to the classic Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag experience in this new Resynced version. It’s as you remember it, except better, bigger, and markedly flashier in all the right ways. Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced demonstrates there’s still a charm to staying faithful.

A skilful remake of one of the best loved Assassin’s Creed games, that retains an impressive diversity of tasks, complemented by gorgeous new visuals, streamlined systems, and perfectly pitched additional content.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a warm bath of fond memories, wrapped in an entertaining pirate adventure. Once again, the setting stuns thanks to its beautifully revamped world. While not without its flaws, this is a worthy remake of one of the most beloved Assassin's Creed titles.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a great remake of a game that probably didn't need to be remade. Of all the games in the AC franchise, Black Flag holds up better than many, but that doesn't change the fact that I had a wonderful time going back. The cast, setting and atmosphere are still some of the best ever realised in the series, and the new content feels right at home.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a great remake of a classic game and does a great job of walking the tightrope between respecting the original source material and introducing new content and modernizing aged features. Cut content is a shame, and the game’s more repetitive elements don’t age well, but there’s a lot to love here for new and returning players. The overhauled combat, beautiful world, and chock-full map truly got the game’s hooks in me — all over again.
A polished, faithful revival, AC Black Flag Resynced enhances, develops and improves upon the original while remaining structurally a 2013 game.

The developers at Ubisoft have clearly gone to great lengths to ensure that this remake deserves to exist, and it’s very clear after spending many hours with the game that it’s a love letter to the fans and the developers. The folks at Ubisoft have made one of the best games ever, even better. Whether you’re a returning veteran or a newbie, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is the definitive way to experience this all-time classic.
Beautifully crafted, this remake remains us how fun is to be a pirate within the Assassin's Creed universe.

If you enjoyed the original adventure, chances are you will love Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced. It keeps everything that made that game so special and adds more than enough new content to make revisiting it worthwhile. Unfortunately, the splendid new visuals aren’t enough to hide cracks in the open world foundation, lacklustre side activities, and a combat system that refuses to offer any depth before the first few hours. Somehow, though, all of this ceases to matter when your crew breaks into a shanty as you sail off into the sunset. These moments made me forget about the behemoth this series would become and enjoy my time spent as a legendary pirate trying to find his place in a changing world.

The Dark Animus rifts stand in deep opposition to how naturally every other change in Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced gels with the rest of the experience. From small additions like the cute cat or monkey that hangs near the Jackdaw’s wheel to sizable alterations like the overhauled stealth mechanics, Resynced does an excellent job of touching up a classic with features that feel like they were there in the first place. Ubisoft didn’t slowly swap out every board of the Jackdaw and turn it into something else; it’s no Ship of Theseus. Instead, the team cleverly fortified its existing foundation in order to ensure this famous pirate ship will stand up a little more accurately to the lofty tales that precede it.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced works because it represents an excellent synthesis of the saga's past and present. Not everything flows smoothly: the narrative additions are interesting on paper and introduce fun gameplay elements, but they lack in terms of the production. The gameplay formula, however, suffers a bit from some elements borrowed and carried over from the RPG era, particularly the combat. Everything else, from the graphics to the stealth, from the parkour to the exploration and naval phases, is the result of a consistent evolution and modernization that respects the original experience. All in all, Resynced is a victory for both Ubisoft and the players: because, after so many years, we have in our hands a game worthy of the name Assassin's Creed.

Thanks to its seafaring adventures, thrilling naval combat, tight and varied combat encounters, thoughtful stealth, plenty to discover, a top performance from the lead, and glorious visuals, Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag is an easygoing joy of a game. How much it retools the original, I’m not sure, but this remake feels right at home in 2026. I never understood why Black Flag got the remake treatment first, but now I get it. This is a pirate adventure for the ages.

Thirteen years later, Black Flag still proves what was already clear back in 2013: it's a far better pirate adventure than it is a traditional Assassin's Creed, and that's arguably its greatest strength. Resynced improves almost every aspect of the original, adds a fair amount of new content, and makes exploring the Caribbean more immersive than ever. Technical issues and a handful of questionable design decisions keep it from reaching true greatness, but it's still an solid remake and one of Ubisoft's strongest releases in recent years, delivering dozens of engaging hours on the high seas.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag: Resynced plays it safe—and it’s a good thing. The changes it introduces are necessary, and the visual overhaul will leave fans speechless, especially if they decide to take the plunge underwater. A few repetitive side activities and tedious boss fights take some of the shine off the game, but they don’t manage to overshadow the quality of this remake.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is a gorgeous, bittersweet reminder of the days when Ubisoft actually fired on all cylinders. Getting back under the Havana sun and living the pirate fantasy looks better than ever, but the illusion shatters the moment the new content kicks in. The added cutscenes and dialogue are shockingly subpar—or, frankly, exactly the kind of mid-tier quality we’ve come to expect from modern Ubisoft. It’s a trip down memory lane that proves how incredible this studio used to be, and how great they could be again if they’d just stop standing in their own way.

Between its strengths and weaknesses, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced makes it very clear that Ubisoft’s brilliance has never faded—it was merely overshadowed by aspects that weren’t as satisfying as they had been in the past. The new features are very welcome and make the game better and more fun, while the removal of the Abstergo segment creates damaging narrative gaps. Just as Ubisoft’s brilliance returns, that lingering shadow of “Bugsoft” still haunts certain moments, but without ruining the experience.
An ambitious remake of the iconic 2013 pirate game that more than does justice to the original.

The game’s old strengths hold firm. The depth and variety of Edward’s day-to-day life still delights – one day he’s upgrading the manor at his private cove, the next he’s clambering Incan ruins for Templar treasure. Primary quests are well-paced, well-acted, and have a knack for making you feel heroic. But in the end, it’s the moments in between that make this game special. It’s when you’re sailing your ship at night, watching the lanterns sway, listening to the crew sing a shanty. This game gives you enough space to feel a pirate’s freedom, now more than ever. It may be a case of Ubisoft plundering its own library for riches, but players get their fair share of the booty.

Where 2020’s Sea Of Thieves sets you and your mates up for multiplayer, grog-chugging hijinks, Resynced cements Black Flag’s place as the quintessential story-driven pirating epic. By being a plunder-led adventure first and an Assassin’s Creed game second, it remains a treasure-nabbing triumph, even with a few flaws. Put simply: this rum-soaked remake is a swashbuckling good time.

Black Flag Resynced isn’t a revolution—it’s a tribute. But sometimes, all it takes is to revive a legend to remind us just how great it was. In this particular case, the journey is still just as worth taking—or even more so, depending on what you’re looking for—without completely smoothing out its rough edges.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced accomplishes the seemingly impossible: it modernizes what many consider a near-perfect game with more epic naval battles, expanded story content, revamped visuals and a host of quality-of-life improvements. The combat and stealth systems still aren't perfect and leave room for improvement, this ambitious remake instantly reminded us why Edward Kenway's adventure remains, and always will be, one of the most beloved entries among Assassin's Creed fans.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced serves as a great lesson in how a classic should be masterfully adapted to modern standards. Without ever compromising the original structure we love so much—the one that warms our hearts—it breaks free from the series’ recent clunky design and succeeds in delivering a pure, fluid, focused, and seamless action-adventure experience. Minor issues with the parkour mechanics or the lack of a modern storyline might give die-hard fans pause at first, but the visual feast provided by the Anvil engine and the seamless, open-sea experience—free of loading screens—more than make up for these shortcomings. If you’ve been missing the warm breezes of the Caribbean and that unique sense of freedom, you now have a great excuse to take the helm of the Jackdaw once again.

This remake delivers a stunning visual overhaul of the Caribbean, particularly through its incredible water simulation and organic progression. Yet, the modernized combat sacrifices the classic power fantasy for clunky realism. Despite its technical ambition, persistent crashes and outdated AI frequently disrupt the experience, preventing this beautiful voyage from reaching its full potential.

While the simpler “classic” Creed formula may surprise those used to the modern, grind-heavy RPG entries, I’m guessing that they’ll quickly adapt and have a great time sailing the high seas and living out the ultimate pirate fantasy, now easily accessible and polished up. For those who seek a treasure of a an experience this year, Resynced is the perfect choice.

One of Ubisoft’s greatest adventures is back, remade with modern polish while preserving everything that made the original so beloved. Sure, some outdated mission design and mechanics show their age, but the charm of emulating the pirate life still shines bright.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced breathes new life into a beloved pirate classic. Breathtaking visuals, zero loading screens, and thoughtful gameplay tweaks more than compensate for the weaker new content and lukewarm first impressions of the Animus hub. A must-play for veterans and newcomers alike.

In addition to a fantastic graphical update and a much-needed overhaul of the combat system, there’s a long list of new features: from new types of cannons to special officers you need to recruit for your crew. While these aren’t usually major changes, just about every aspect of the game has been scrutinized to see if it could be improved. Some weaker elements, such as the incredibly boring scenes set in the present day, have simply been cut—and that, too, makes the game better. All of this makes “Resynced” the perfect entry point for anyone who’s never played “Black Flag” before. For those who already experienced the adventure back then, this game might not be a must-have at full price.

Returned to us with its seams concealed and its ropes tightened, Black Flag feels not like a relic from an earlier age, but a reminder of a path the genre might profitably rediscover: breadth without bloat, and an ocean of possibility that rarely asks you to sail too far to find something worth doing. [Issue#427, p.106]
With a fresh coat of paint, superlative tweaks, and a renewed narrative structure, Black Flag Resynced is a stellar showcase of how to update a classic title.

In some respects, the foundation of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynce shows its age, given that the overhaul is primarily graphical—and yes, the combat overall disappointed me—but the fact remains that the core game was and still is excellent today! So for long-time fans who already know it by heart, its appeal will be limited beyond the visual treat but for those who never set sail alongside Edward Kenway, you'll feel like you're playing one of, if not the best, Assassin's Creed games of recent years. Proof that sometimes the old classics are still the best but also that it's high time Ubisoft drew inspiration from its past glories to bring new gems to life that can carry on this legacy, unless they're doomed to shine only in the shadow of a glorious past.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced succeeds in its mission to modernize the game's presentation, yet struggles to hide the aging cracks in its core open-world formula. The pirate immersion in the heart of the Caribbean is fantastic, elevated by a cast of supporting characters—both new and returning—who remain as engaging as ever. However, a camera that often goes haywire during combat, occasionally tedious repetition in the action, and a lack of improvements to the main campaign prevent this first remake from reaching true greatness—at least for now. That said, Black Flag Resynced did succeed in making me imagine what a remake of Altaïr’s or Ezio’s adventures might look like, and I would certainly love to revisit those eras with this level of polish. This new version offers a great summer adventure for newcomers and a sweet dose of nostalgia for veterans. But if you are already burnt out on the Assassin’s Creed formula, Resynced isn't going to be the game that redeems it for you.
A competent yet very safe remake that will satisfy both fans and newcomers.
Strong pirate adventure foundations and roguish charm keep this remake afloat
With being one of the best looking games of this generation, Black Flag Resynced is a faithful remake whose brilliance is occasionally clouded by technical bugs.

Pitched as Ubisoft’s flagship and bounce back title for this year’s AAA open-world experience, it is perhaps, and this isn’t meant harshly, not essential gaming in 2026; also in light of other AAA open-world experiences that may be also coming out in 2026. There is a stipulation on this comment, however, that rests somewhere on a sliding scale of whether or not someone has played the original back in the day or not. For a fan of the original, it’s a pleasure to revisit its characters and world and it will be surprising to them just how much variety of content there was in the original that is now carried over into a much shinier remake. Whether that would be the case for someone who has never played the original, it would be interesting to hear about because it doesn’t dare to push toward any new ground really. The question it asks, though, is does it have to? What Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced does do, and what Ubisoft has generally been good at creating over the years, is the perfect casual experience, and it is hitherto priced as such. Oft’ a casual experience is preferred to pushing envelopes, taking names and breaking new ground. Oft’ a casual experience can end up being your favourite world to be immersed in. Pirates are great and being a pirate is great.

For all its flaws – its lackluster combat system, clumsy naval combat and genuinely horrible AI – Black Flag Resynced is also easliy one of the prettiest games in the series to date, and Edward Kenway's story is still a joy to partake in.

Black Flag Resynced brushes a modern coat of paint onto an ageing classic, bringing the best and worst of the series' history into focus. It's beautiful, messy, and dissonant, but above all else it's still delightfully fun.
There is an ebb and flow to Black Flag Resynced: for every positive change the remake offers, it feels like there's a negative just beneath the surface.

Black Flag Resynced shines with its spectacular graphics, but just about everything else falls short. The animation and logic glitches—including getting “stuck” in the environment—the lackluster narrative, and the extreme simplification of combat mean it isn’t a very fun game.
Metacritic user score 8.3/10 (1517 ratings).
Newer, not better.
Metacritic user score 9.2/10 (2184 ratings).

Splatoon Raiders of-fish-ally earns our seal of approval as a fantastic game in the franchise. Whether you go it alone or get help from other players, searching for loot and mining ore has never been so fun, thanks to the amount of weapons and gadgets you can equip to blast enemies out of existence. Plus, you get to hang out with Deep Cut, which is always a fun time.

Splatoon Raiders is a wonderful solo reinvention of the popular multiplayer series filled with smartly designed missions and endlessly engaging progression systems. Underpinned by the franchise’s fantastic shooting mechanics, it’s a fresh and exciting adventure that should be in every Nintendo Switch 2 owner’s library.

Splatoon Raiders doesn't take itself too seriously and knows its audience. It's not trying to redefine gaming, it's just a fun, lighthearted ride that doesn't underestimate the audience or hold back on its mechanics.

You know you’ve hit gold when your biggest criticism of a game is that you just wanted more. Between the fast-paced, technical gameplay, the depth of the build mechanics, and the irreverent design that underpins the Splatoon series, this is an experience that’s shockingly hard to fault. Go play it.

Splatoon Raiders successfully twists the Splatoon formula into a slick, satisfying single player-focused looter shooter that's incredibly difficult to put down. Surprisingly deep loot game, some absolutely hectic encounters and a bleakly-beachy vibe all its own, there's plenty here for fans as well as anyone previously put off by the series' multiplayer focus.

Splatoon Raiders marks an excellent entry to the Splatoon franchise I’d wager, and anybody that enjoyed the previous  games but might’ve wanted a more fleshed out solo experience is gonna have a blast here. It might be a little repetitive if you’re not familiar with this style of looter gameplay, but otherwise it’s a fantastic experience. From the blend of stick aiming and gyro aiming to the fun soundtrack these games always offer and all the way down to the core gameplay, Raiders is an addictive title well worth playing. Personally, I’d wager I like it just a little more than the standard Splatoon titles if not solely for the fact I’m definitely not as good at Splatoon than other kinds of shooters. Existing Splatoon fans will have a great time with Splatoon Raiders, but for new fans or anybody interested in Splatoon it’s probably the best way to get into the series in a solo environment before you decide to make the plunge into the main games.

Smart progression, perfect balance, a charismatic story and characters, lots of post-game content and mechanics that will make you sink hours into without even noticing the time go by. Splatoon Riders is here to stay, proving that its campaign mode, whether played solo, in local co-op, or online, is just as fun as the previous PVP focused titles.

Splatoon Raiders offers excellent value for money, with plenty of variety to cater to different types of players. The main campaign delivers a more curated adventure with a steady learning curve that’s made even more enjoyable by teaming up with friends or strangers online. Once the credits roll, the post-game content shifts gears, giving hardcore players an endless chase for increasingly difficult scenarios and better loot that’s genuinely hard to put down. Splatoon Raiders, in my opinion, was a very risky move for a franchise that’s still growing its playerbase, but Nintendo has managed to defy expectations by delivering a solo Splatoon adventure with plenty of bait on the hook. Rather than simply serving as another Side Order, Splatoon Raiders inks its own identity in spectacular fashion, and it’s safe to say this adventure has me hook, line and sinker.

Splatoon Raiders is a gamble that paid off. Nintendo takes one of its most recognizable franchises and has the courage to steer it in a completely different direction without betraying its identity. Ink, movement, and chaotic combat remain at the heart of the experience, yet a surprisingly deep progression system emerges around these elements—one capable of winning over even those who usually view looter-shooters with skepticism.
