Endless Ragnarok makes a good game better as it brings forth tons of quality-of-life improvements as well as brand new modes and a new story to fight through. While still suffering from some of the same narrative issues Relink had, the plethora of challenges and new playable characters will give long-time Relink players a reason to come back. New players will be able to experience the most complete Relink package, highlighting the game's satisfying combat first and foremost.

Endless Ragnarok is an unexpected, but extremely welcome expansion that builds upon the foundations of Granblue Fantasy: Relink with plenty of fun, meaty content for fans to sink their teeth into. Be warned that there is a rather steep difficulty curve to get to grips with, especially for returning players who haven't touched this game in ages. Once you get past that, however, Relink will have its hooks in you all over again before you even realize it's happening.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a worthwhile expansion that prioritizes meaningful gameplay additions over storytelling. While its narrative rarely leaves a lasting impression, the Conflux roguelite mode, excellent new playable characters, rewarding progression systems, and satisfying combat enhancements breathe new life into an already stellar action RPG. Fans looking for more reasons to master ReLink's endgame won't be disappointed.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is an excellent expansion given its relatively short two-year development turnaround. It capitalizes and expands on what made Relink’s endgame loop compelling, but it does so at the cost of a lackluster narrative. There are a myriad of new ways to build its now 28 playable characters, and the moment-to-moment action is even more addictive than the base game. I hope that a full-fledged sequel to Relink will come eventually, because I crave more, but I want one to be built from the ground up with the lessons they learned from the first Relink, rather than another expansion that tries to apply additional band-aids over it.

Final impressions of Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok are heavily tied to how you feel about the original game. Liked it and enjoyed clearing the endgame content? Then grab the DLC without hesitation — another 50–100 hours of fun monster-slaying action are guaranteed. Enjoyed the story but not a fan of grinding? Then it's better to skip it.

A little over two years after the game's release, Granblue Fantasy Relink: Endless Ragnarok stands out as a model of generosity and an essential expansion for action-RPG enthusiasts. By intelligently tweaking the difficulty and introducing the "Chaotic Void" mode, Cygames demonstrates its willingness to listen to the community and address the shortcomings of the original experience. Admittedly, the expansion doesn't eliminate the structural stiffness of the base game, nor its understated storytelling or battles that occasionally clutter the screen. Yet, with its massive roster and colossal amount of content offered at an attractive price, this return to Zegagrande serves as a reminder of just how underrated Granblue Fantasy Relink is. In short, it is a sure bet for both longtime fans and newcomers alike.
Grandblue Fantasy Relink Endless Ragnarok ressemble finalement à l’aboutissement d’un titre déjà riche et généreux, venant approfondir chacune de ses mécaniques sans bouleverser sa nature.

Endless Ragnarok isn’t a game changer for Granblue Fantasy: Relink, but it does stock the base game with better-balanced and deeper endgame gameplay. There’s not much new in terms of story, and there’s a fair bit of reskinning and rehashing going on, yet this is a smart expansion for a relatively breezy RPG experience.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink's major expansion, Endless Ragnarok, greatly expands the game with an impressive amount of new content. The time and effort required to fully build a character have now increased several times over. New characters, the summon system, new bosses, and the solo roguelike mode all offer substantial, high-quality additions. While the Chaos difficulty features too many reused enemies and the story presentation leaves something to be desired, Endless Ragnarok still delivers 20 to 50 or more hours of additional gameplay.

Endless Ragnarok makes Granblue Fantasy: Relink feel like a more complete game thanks to its various additions, including harder boss fights and a simple roguelite mode for mindless currency grinding.
Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a great new expansion with a few flaws. However, those flaws don't hinder the otherwise enjoyable new pile of content.

Endless Ragnarok has a lot to offer. New difficulty, new mechanics and characters, on top of a very replayable roguelike mode, mean that this is a worthwhile addition to a game already brimming with content.

Endless Ragnarok brings a lot of cool fights and content to Relink and, if you haven’t jumped into this ARPG, this expansion effectively joins the base game at a great price. If you’re an existing player and were a fan of the base game, Endless Ragnarok will be for you! If you enjoyed your time with Relink and felt as though you’ve had enough of its loop, this expansion ultimately might not really do much for you.

For players who are fans of the base game and wanted more, Endless Ragnarok is exactly that. For the rest of us, this expansion does little to address the problems of gatekeeping content behind grind, and limiting the amount of content available to play with my friends. Further, the hours of grind required to see this new content outweigh the enjoyment offered by the new stuff. with choices like this, Endless Ragnarok feels like it’s a great fit for one specific type of player, and a poor one for everyone else.

Endless Ragnarok operates in a unique spot. While there is quite a bit of volume to the content, it is purely locked as a late-game expansion. It is not even accessible unless the player has beaten the first game, but it adds new characters, weapons, and other systems for the late-game boss rush. Ultimately while the combat can be fun, the grind and length of battles wears on a player, and the lack of any interesting character development or expansion story makes this a very limited niche of DLC.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok brings more of what’s in the base game, and not much else for new or returning players. As a co-op experience, I could see Endless Ragnarok as a group of up to four friends game of choice, especially with crossplay implemented, but the generic fantasy characters, repetition to a fault, and lack of any clear guidance make this hard to recommend. The accessibility features still put the responsibility in the player’s hands, making me question why this is even offered beyond as a tool for players looking to learn bosses. I don’t consider binging CBS’s Cold Case while keeping a hand on the controller to grind for hundreds of hours a peak gaming experience anymore, but maybe you need a new podcast game, and Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok might be a good fit.
Granblue Fantasy: Relink's Endless Ragnarok Expansion introduces 6 new playable characters, a roguelite mode called the Conflux, and more.
Riveting, rewarding, and endlessly replayable, Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is one of the best action RPGs on Nintendo's system.

If you played and loved the original release of Relink, then Endless Ragnarok is going to be an amazing time. It’s a heaping helping of new battles, new bosses, and new characters. Between that, the summon system, and some new progression mechanics, there’s so much to dive into.
While the story isn't groundbreaking, anyone who enjoys anime-style action and epic battles will have a blast.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is one of the more unique, attractive, and immediately enjoyable JRPGs available for the Switch 2. The main story is not very long, but the game offers more than enough peripheral content to keep players busy for quite some time.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok eschews story for brutally hard bosses. It's more of a gauntlet of tough challenges for veteran players rather than the casual crowd, though its new characters and less tedious grind are welcome inclusions.

Endless Ragnarok is a must-play for those who have conquered Granblue Fantasy: Relink, offering players a new roguelike gauntlet, new playable characters, new levelling systems and a ton of new battles.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok answers a lot of the complaints I had with the base game and adds a ton more to do in the game. If you haven’t played Granblue Fantasy: Relink before, this is the perfect time to get the game and the expansion, as it is still an amazing experience.
Endless Ragnarok doesn’t reinvent Granblue Fantasy: Relink. It’s the same core game, just with some extra content tacked on to keep veteran endgame players grinding for a few more weeks.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a truly well-crafted Expanded Edition of the highly sought-after JRPG released almost two years ago. Admittedly, the emphasis on the story isn’t particularly strong here, but fans of pure action and epic battles against gigantic beasts, all set against a backdrop of phenomenal anime graphics, certainly won’t need much persuading to give this new game a go.

Reviewing this version is no easy task, as there are two different perspectives. Considering the whole picture, Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is the definitive version of a modern classic and one of my favorite games of this generation, expanding and refining everything that was already great. However, viewed solely from the perspective of what it adds to the base game, it's a robust content, but it has high re-entry barrier, relies on repetitive endgame elements, and doesn't bring enough new features to transform the game, making it bigger, but not necessarily better.
A solid expanded and revamped take on Grandblue Fantasy: Relink with a ton of new content

I appreciate that the DNA of a free-to-play property is the Granblue name, obviously, but the console titles should be an opportunity to build the name into something meaningful. Not just continue to churn out endless content to keep people playing.

If there is a JRPG equavilent to Monster Hunter, then Granblue Fantasy Relink have always been one. Just for Endless Ragnarok to blow things out of the water and provide a post game that is worthy to be called as one of the most addictive JRPG titles this generation

Granblue Fantasy: Relink isn't a game that I'd suggest for everybody, but if you're a JRPG fan looking for something new to try and enjoy I'd say you can't go wrong. With a fun roster of characters, beautiful art, and fast, energetic gameplay, I can't wait to revisit Relink.

While the game is far from being bad, there are some problems that manifest really quickly during the gameplay. The grinding required to beat the strongest enemies and bosses is simply too much of a chore and the new story isn’t very shallow and lacking in depth. In the end, too much was promised, and too little was proposed.
Endless Ragnarok offers plenty of challenging endgame content, strong new characters and fresh mechanics for veterans, but it is aimed squarely at players with a strong appetite for grinding.

Endless Ragnarok expands *Granblue Fantasy: Relink* with a new story, six playable characters, novel progression systems, and abundant endgame content. It is an expansion that builds upon the existing foundation rather than reinventing the game, aiming instead to enhance its greatest strengths and offer fresh challenges to both veterans and newcomers embarking on the adventure for the first time.

The final impression is this: not only is it an excellent action RPG, but it’s also a platform designed to grow over time, capable of rewarding both those who simply want to complete a spectacular campaign and those who enjoy spending hundreds of hours searching for the perfect build and taking on the most challenging trials.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok reimagines the game’s endgame with a roguelike mode, six excellent new characters, deeper progression, and challenging encounters that reward strategy over raw damage. Its grind-heavy structure, visual clutter, and modest story hold it back, but mechanically it’s an exceptional expansion for dedicated players.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink is a fast-paced and highly enjoyable action JRPG built around an excellent combat system, a likeable cast, spectacular boss fights, and gorgeous audiovisual presentation. Its story moves a little too quickly and some side content leans heavily on grinding, while Endless Ragnarok focuses more on expanding the endgame than delivering another major narrative campaign, but together they offer a substantial and rewarding package for both newcomers and long-term players.

Going into the review, I had nerves and uncertainty. Coming out of it, I believe I found a new passion. That is a very hard standard for a game to set and speaks to the level of enjoyability. I believe this is the sort of release that is very rare recently, a truly masterfully crafted DLC.

Fans of MMOs and loot driven games will feel right at home here. There’s an enormous amount of content to sink your teeth into, and the additional Endless Ragnarok expansion only adds to that. The addictive Conflux roguelike mode is an absolute highlight, providing yet another compelling reason to keep coming back for “just one more run.”

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is an entertaining twenty-five to forty-hour expansion that stretches the complete package out to over a hundred hours.  The new bosses are worth the trek to get there, but the repeated fights needed make taking breaks preferable to a marathon.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is a title suited mainly to those who love Japanese video games in their fullest expression, one where farming plays a major role, paired with fresh gameplay and numerous unique characters.

Granblue Fantasy Relink Endless Ragnarock is a great example of an Expansion made for the fans. It does do anything incredible, but it hones in on the specific content the fanbase loves the most, being the endgame boss fights.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok, folks, is a pretty cool expansion for a game that was already strong in its most basic form. I really enjoyed the improvements and new features, and I think the title manages to deliver what we expect from a quality DLC.

Endless Ragnarok revives the game with new characters and roguelite content. Master Skills fix base game issues and add deep build variety for all. While Summon Stones feel a bit shallow, the overall experience is excellent.

Endless Ragnarok certainly entertains, even without a strong emphasis on its narrative, which I feel is a very noticeable blemish here. Combat, new encounters, or remixed ones, and the added features to kit out your characters are the strongest elements that make this DLC really worth it. Summons and the Conflux feel fairly thin on function, but can certainly entertain from time to time, it's just a shame the roguelike addition is solo only, otherwise I would have put more time into it. Regardless, Endless Ragnarok is a damn good addition to Granblue, even if it doesn’t soar quite as high as the game it is added to.

Endless Ragnarok doesn’t try to reinvent Granblue Fantasy: Relink. Instead, it expands on what the base game does best: its exceptional combat. The six new playable characters are a joy to use, and the challenging boss encounters provide plenty of rewarding endgame content for veteran players. However, the expansion’s biggest drawback is its limited story, which lacks the emotional depth and memorable moments that made the original adventure so compelling. While it doesn’t quite reach the same heights as the base game, Endless Ragnarok is still a worthwhile expansion for players looking for more of Relink’s outstanding action-packed gameplay.

The gameplay is generally fun and, given the large number of characters, offers a fair bit of variety despite the game’s accessibility. It looks good and the varied soundtrack is brilliant. The main story, right up to the end credits, is rather short – it took me 20 hours – but it’s entertaining.

It's fair to say that Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is a great example of how to expand a good game. The DLC adds a lot of content to the action RPG, including new missions, new characters, and interesting gameplay mechanics. Although much of the new content is available after the campaign, the fun and quality of the title are present from the start, making it a great suggestion for both newcomers and veterans of the franchise.

Endless Ragnarok is a substantial expansion that significantly expands upon the combat systems, character build options, and advanced quest offerings of the 2014 game. However, the narrative weight of this DLC is not comparable to the number of quality-of-life improvements and new advanced quests. Thanks to this, Granblue Fantasy: Relink is more appealing than ever to new players, and its DLC provides a new reason for those who have already completed the game to return—once again—to Cygames' universe.

Cygames has delivered a product that will be very well received by longtime fans of the franchise, those who joined in Relink, and new players hopping in with the DLC. The level of gameplay quality, the spectacle of the fights and animations, the satisfying grind, and the content that delivers dozens and dozens of highly entertaining hours make Granblue Fantasy: Relink and Endless Ragnarok an easy recommendation on my part.

Endless Ragnarok delivers a robust, content-heavy expansion packed with impressive endgame modes and thrilling summon combat that expands the action-RPG's best ideas. While handheld play on Nintendo Switch 2 looks fantastic, inconsistent frame pacing, a locked 30 FPS, and heavy narrative gating leave this rich expansion feeling alienating to newcomers and visually compromise its portable premiere.

The thing is, Granblue Fantasy Relink: Endless Ragnarok feels heavily geared towards hardcore players who were already there, grinding it out past the credits, and doesn't really feel like an entry point for players looking to try it.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink delivers an extremely enjoyable action RPG experience, featuring fast-paced, deep, and highly addictive combat. The Endless Ragnarok expansion builds upon that experience with a new campaign, additional characters, new game modes, and progression systems that make the endgame even more robust. Even without revolutionizing its storytelling, the overall package impresses with its wide variety of content, excellent art direction, and gameplay that stands out as one of the best in the genre. It is an easy recommendation for action RPG fans and anyone looking for a game packed with dozens of hours of content and strong replay value.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a purrfect expansion that rewards dedicated players with new features such as summoning, crossplay, and quality-of-life improvements. Players will have a lengthy road to unlock the new content, but the journey is well worth it for fans who want a fun and challenging action RPG.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is an excellent expansion that prioritises what the base game already excelled at: spectacular combat, satisfying progression, and addictive replayability. It's an easy recommendation for anyone who loved Relink and thrives on a good action RPG grind.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a really good expansion to this great game. My only thing is the heavy amount of monster quests that need to be done in order to start the content. With a wall like that, it slightly killed my momentum next to the grinding needed to continue. Luckily, we can get early access to the Conflux Surveys and can start the smooth grinding. But to me that’s just like using a coaster on a wobbly chair.

I hope that if they make another DLC to this size or larger…please let us start the story before making us have to drag the grinding fest.

I give Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok the Thumb Culture Gold Award

“I know that the PlayStation 5 has a few high-profile RPGs releasing in early 2024, but honestly, if you’re a fan of the genre, you REALLY won’t want to skip Granblue Fantasy: Relink,” I said in my original review. Two years later, that sentiment stands stronger than ever. Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok isn’t just an expansion, but instead feels like the definitive version of an already fantastic game. It addresses the grindy nature of the endgame, adds meaningful new mechanics, and provides a wealth of challenging new content. If you’re a returning player who enjoyed the base game, this is an absolute must-play, and if you’re jumping in for the first time, you’re in for a spectacular adventure with Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok.

Granblue Fantasy Relink returns after two years with Endless Ragnarok, an expansion that lives up to the game that inspired this action RPG, where the grind never stops, and continues to be the game with the best combat system of recent years.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink is an action RPG developed and published by Cygames, Inc. Aiming to reach Estalúcia, a legendary island, the crew of the Grandcypher, an airship that flies through the Sky Realm, arrives in the celestial space of Zegagrande, home to numerous floating islands. Upon arrival, our crew becomes embroiled in a larger conflict involving the Church of Avia, which threatens the very existence of Zegagrande. Assemble your team of four characters, choosing from a wide variety of unique characters, both in appearance and gameplay. With the new expansion Endless Ragnarok, in addition to several improvements implemented in the game, a continuation of the main story unfolds, with new challenges and more epic battles. Climb aboard the Grandcypher and explore the mysteries and adventures of the Sky Realm.

Granblue Fantasy Relink Endless Ragnarok is a meaty expansion with 30+ hours of content that makes an already great game even better and easy to get into for newcomers, although the new roguelite mode is repetitive and could use a bit more content.
A JRPG with engaging active combat, and plenty of terrific characters to enjoy, even if perhaps the scope of the story seems limited

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is the kind of expansion that is bound to get Granblue Fantasy: Relink fans coming back again and again. Gorgeous, glorious and gratifying, I’m looking forward to conquering whatever Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok throws my way next.

For first-timers, there are already 28 playable characters, each with their own unique gameplay, making for an enjoyable adventure. I wouldn't recommend it to everyone, but if you enjoy the genre, I suggest you check it out.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is a rather excellent game as a whole package as long as you’re looking for gameplay over story in your JRPG. That said, the Endless Ragnarok content is only really exciting to heavily invested players, who really want to farm the endgame. The new roguelite mode is certainly a standout feature, but you will need to grind those quests for quite a while before unlocking it in full.

The story is the one place Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok falls short of the original, feeling thinner and more like an epilogue than a proper continuation, but everything wrapped around it, the combat, the characters, the grind changes, and the new modes, makes a strong case that this is exactly the kind of expansion longtime players were hoping for.

Granblue Fantasy Relink – Endless Ragnarok brings Cygames' action-RPG to Switch 2, bundling the base game with its expansion in one package. Real-time combat mixes melee and magic well, and new additions like Chaos difficulty, summons, Primal Bursts, and Mastery traits add welcome depth to the endgame.
The story is solo-only, but the roughly 20-hour campaign is tightly paced, while the Konflux mode and online quests offer strong replay value for those chasing loot solo or in crossplay co-op. Visually the game runs smoothly, though the locked 30 FPS and lack of a performance mode may bother PC/PlayStation veterans. The soundtrack, blending Nobuo Uematsu and Tsutomu Narita's styles, is a definite highlight.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok works because it understands what people want more of. The game's combat depth, character variety and smarter progression aspects were all given serious attention over a rather short production cycle. The Conflux itself is worth much of the price of the expansion, as it allows you better and more varied options to create your characters than the original grind ever offered.
Between great Quality of Life additions, a good roguelite mode and an exceptional endgame, “Endless Ragnarok” is a must have for “Granblue Fantasy: Relink” be it newcomers or veterans of the genre.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok is a fantastic experience for action-RPG fans, offering tons of extra content to sink your teeth into. While the Endless Ragnarok expansion adds an impressive amount of depth, it demands a level of grind that might push it past what the general audience is willing to tolerate. That said, the base game is absolutely worth a purchase on its own, and if it leaves you craving more, Endless Ragnarok will easily provide enough high-end content to keep you busy for a very long time.

Between the frenetic battles across various islands in the sky, the heart-pounding action at key moments, and giant monsters that seem impervious to even the most over-the-top attacks, Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok has a lot to offer fans of this specific type of action RPG!

At first glance, Granblue Fantasy: Relink appears to be an RPG with a relatively modest story, yet it delivers an excellent gameplay experience and stunning visuals; by combining a diverse cast of characters with deep narrative and character-building elements, it earns a place alongside the great RPGs of recent years.

Endless Ragnarok doesn't reinvent Granblue Fantasy: Relink, it simply gives you more reasons to love it. The Conflux stumbles early on, but once it opens up, this expansion becomes the best argument yet to pick up the controller again.

Open Critic:
Whether you are a veteran skyfarer returning to optimise your builds and challenge the new content, or a newcomer looking for a fun and mechanically satisfying coop action RPG, Endless Ragnarok is the perfect package for you. Dozens, if not hundreds, of hours of playtime await you in the skies of Zegagrande.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a generous, vibrant, and seamlessly integrated expansion that successfully reinforces everything that already made Cygames' action RPG so special. While its story works better as a framework than as a major emotional driver, the combat, the new systems, The Maelstrom, the summons, and the endgame progression turn the return to Zegagrande into an immensely satisfying experience. For veterans, it offers a clear reason to return, and for newcomers, it serves as a more complete and appealing version of an adventure that continues to shine through its characters, art direction, and that JRPG energy that always invites you to look toward the next horizon.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink – Endless Ragnarok is the expansion that respects the veteran player's intelligence without shutting the door on newcomers. Master Traits reinvent familiar characters, the six new fighters cover distinct playstyles with mechanical generosity, and the summoning system adds a layer of spectacle that the base game had never touched.

Granblue Fantasy Relink – Endless Ragnarok is a massive and fantastic expansion, adding more value and content to an already massive world introduced by its predecessor. With additional story content and new Chaos Levels, returning players are given a treat to continue their skyfaring adventures to a whole new level, despite some boss recycling.

Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok offers dozens of hours of additional content for solo players or multiplayer enthusiasts who want to return to the skies of Zegagrande for a little more grinding.

Endless Ragnarok DLC adds a new adventure while building upon what made Granblue Fantasy: Relink a masterpiece. Its defining aspects, such as its worldbuilding, rich characters, and easy to learn gameplay, are all present, now paired with new adventures.

Casual players should think twice (or thrice) about committing to a purchase, but for the diehards who have been finding new ways to turn Relink on its head and smash into its boundaries for the last two years, this expansion hands you the keys to nigh-boundless adventure, as expansive as the skydom itself. Enjoy responsibly, and I won't think any less of you for wanting to tap out.

Granblue Fantasy Relink players and sweaty action RPGers who want to continue getting more buff than jacked-up meme Vyrn will find a lot to love in Endless Ragnarok's plethora of endgame offerings. That said, people starting on the base game may want to wait until they're powerful enough to tackle all the Endless Ragnarok challenges. It's a lot to ask, but veterans and players who have waited for a worthy follow-up will be immensely satiated.
Metacritic user score 8.5/10 (180 ratings).
Rhythm Heaven Groove is not only incredibly fun, backed by an amazing soundtrack, but it's so unbelievably accessible practically everyone can play it.

Rhythm Heaven is fundamentally different to other rhythm games, and Rhythm Paradise Groove is no different. It might seem both whimsical and bonkers from the aesthetics and general energy of the game, and it is that, but it’s also an enormously clever project that subtly helps you develop very real rhythm skills. I love it when games entertain while also teaching like this.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is Nintendo at its handheld best, and that also happens to be my favorite kind of Nintendo. It is essential for rhythm game fans, and I'm going to go back to replaying older stages literally after sending this review in. The wait for a new Rhythm Heaven was long, but Tsunku and Nintendo have delivered what I consider a tie for my favorite game of 2026 with Forza Horizon 6, and I'm not just saying that because both feature Ado.

There’s no rhythm game quite like Rhythm Heaven, and Groove is a triumphant return for a series that has been gone for far too long. It's one of the only rhythm games to truly bring music and gameplay together, and it's fantastic.

Rhythm Heaven Groove lives up to the expectations longtime fans have had for the series. With higher-quality songs, familiar yet flexible stage formats, and highly replayable bonus modes, it brought back memories of grinding for medals on the Nintendo DS and Wii. For rhythm game fans, it is undoubtedly the most fitting first-party send-off for the Nintendo Switch generation.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a fantastic return to form from Nintendo and Tsunku, filled to the brim with fresh beats and funny characters, with plenty of modes to explore alone or with friends while you work on perfecting your skills.

This new installment preserves the essence that made the series a defining title in the rhythm game genre while introducing a broad selection of brand-new content and game modes that significantly expand the overall experience, with Beatspell standing out in particular thanks to its originality.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is a kooky, superb rhythm game that has loads of reasons to come back to play time and time again.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a superb sequel that expertly capitalizes on the captivating energy of its excellent music across a series of joyfully animated minigames. The solo campaign is well-balanced and stuffed with genre-shifting earworms you won’t forget fast. The new Beatspell RPG mode and more straightforward Toybox levels don’t quite reach that same impressive bar, but the co-op mode does stand as a great addition with a solid range of competitive and collaborative games that quickly got me and my friends laughing. Even so, this irreverent return to Rhythm Heaven hits all the right notes, solidifying itself as an unmissable addition to the series.
If you are new to rhythm games, this would be the ideal way to get started in the genre. This game is the perfect way to bid farewell to the Switch when it comes to first-party releases.

Rhythm Paradise Groove marks a spectacular comeback for the series: quirky, humorous minigames, groovy music, and a solid selection of unlockable content make the game a real blast—despite its minimalist visuals—and a must-have for fans and newcomers alike.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a classic Rhythm Paradise game: colorful, fun, and musically outstanding, keeping you glued to the screen until you’ve completed every single minigame. Yet, setting aside the welcome additions, I expected a little something more—especially after waiting so many years for a new installment. I wanted something that would satisfy both my completionist streak and my emotional side. As it stands, however, it remains nothing more than an incredible, beautiful toy.

Rhythm Paradise Groove doesn’t miss a beat. Whether getting in the groove with friends and family or honing your skill to accumulate Medals playing solo, this game deserves its chance to shine in the spotlight and a place in your Nintendo Switch collection. Its kaleidoscopic colours, hypnotic soundscape and flawlessly addictive formula make for an uplifting experience that you won’t want to put down all summer.
Rhythm Heaven proves that plastic guitars and complex controls aren't needed to excel in its niche: all it takes is dancing to your own rhythm —preferably in a clumsy way— to see the magic happen.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is an impressive rhythm game that manages to offer a lot of variety in its minigames. With a whimsical style to its visual and audio choices, the game is vibrant in a way that sets it apart from many titles of its genre. It lives up to the legacy of the franchise and is an experience worth getting to know for anyone curious about the sort of variety that can be explored in rhythm games.
Rhythm Heaven Groove is an excellent new entry in the beloved series, introducing several great features, with fun gameplay, incredible visuals, and a fantastic soundtrack.

Rhythm Heaven Groove quickly won me over. The beginning requires some time to adjust and grasp the rhythm of each challenge, but as the minigames progress, the sense of improvement is incredibly rewarding. With an excellent variety of challenges, music, and highly entertaining multiplayer, the game serves as a great entry point for new players.

You might be sad that Rhythm Heaven Groove is the last big Nintendo Switch game, but just like the system itself, it’s full of surprises and quirks that’ll likely catch you off guard. Groove might appear to be a tough and demanding cookie on the surface with its emphasis on precision timing, but the way the game teaches and rewards you for playing are boundless, and it’s a breezy pick up and play game with a treasure trove of extras that’ll keep you wanting and craving more of it. Yeah you’ll need dedication and will incur bouts of frustration, but with all that’s stuffed into it-you’ll keep on coming back for more.

Even though Beatspell falls a bit short of the mark, Rhythm Heaven Groove is still a triumph through and through, offering up some of the best rhythm-based antics the series has seen to date. I can only hope that Nintendo doesn’t decide to lay it to rest for another couple of console generations before it decides to revisit this criminally underrated franchise.

The game arrives on the portable console after 10 years, with more than 100 levels across both solo and multiplayer modes. This new installment stands among the best in the franchise, with unique designs that burst with charisma and, above all, originality. Rhythm is at the heart of the experience, and while some minigames can feel a bit unfair, with time and practice, the dopamine rush is just perfect.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a silly, addictive rhythm game that brings the same weird energy that fans of WarioWare will recognize. As my first experience with the series, I was surprised by how much fun its odd challenges and catchy gameplay offered.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is an outstanding experience on the Nintendo Switch that I’d easily recommend to anyone. Whether you have a previous affinity for the series, or this is your first Rhythm Heaven experience, I think you’ll easily fall in love with the toe-tapping, beat-driven music and quirky animations that Rhythm Heaven Groove excels at.

Rhythm Paradise Groove carries a kind of creative electricity that is hard to fake. Every mode, every song and every odd little scenario feels touched by a team that genuinely enjoys the craft of rhythm, and that enthusiasm seeps through the screen. It is not flawless, yet its spirit is so strong and its execution so assured that the imperfections never manage to dull its glow. This is the sort of game that quietly raises the bar for what a rhythm title can be, not through spectacle, but through an unshakeable commitment to making every beat matter.

But above all, what is most impressive is that Nintendo continues to champion concepts as unique and offbeat as this series—at a time when the vast majority of publishers are merely looking to cash in on their big-name franchises. Here, however, the game stands out by offering a form of fun that is so pure, simple, and hypnotic that it’s impossible to resist... provided you have at least a little rhythm in your veins. If that doesn't apply to you, you might not find it quite as entertaining.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a delightfully eccentric experience: wonderfully weird, exceptionally creative, and built around such precise audio design that nearly every minigame becomes a small obsession. Its Remix stages and delightfully chaotic spirit elevate the experience considerably, although the inconsistent Dpad controls and timing issues while playing on a TV slightly diminish its polish. Even so, it stands as one of the most unique and instantly endearing titles in Nintendo's catalog.

Rhythm Heaven Groove delivers a huge collection of creative rhythm minigames that are easy to learn but rewarding to master. Its quirky humor, memorable music, and simple controls make it a fun game to pick up whether you're playing alone or with a friend. While its repetitive structure makes it best enjoyed in shorter sessions, its charm and addictive gameplay make it easy to keep coming back.

Rhythm Paradise Groove doesn't reinvent the series, but it doesn't need to. It's another excellent rhythm game on Switch, offering hours of lighthearted fun while putting your sense of timing to the test. A polished, budget-friendly package that will appeal to both longtime fans and newcomers alike. Another evergreen addition to Nintendo's already outstanding hybrid console library.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a breath of fresh air and a fantastic way to revive a highly original and groundbreaking franchise that has already been a hit in past generations. Its minimalist controls prove once again that a great idea needs very little to work when it’s executed with talent. The creativity of its mini-games, the excellent soundtrack, the constant humor, and the inclusion of exciting new features like the brilliant Beatspell make this new installment one of Nintendo’s most intriguing comebacks.

Rhythm Paradise Groove earns its crown as the king of rhythm games on Nintendo Switch. It has catchy songs, wonderfully absurd humor, and multiplayer that’s just as chaotic as it is hilarious. It’s one of those weird, wildly original gems that only Nintendo could make.

Rhythm Heaven Groove delivers a double album's worth of content, including a bumpin' new collection of minigames, a fully fleshed-out multiplayer option, mini RPG mode, and various other quirky odds and ends. The game's idiosyncratic approach to the rhythm genre means your experience may be somewhat uneven -- you'll like some minigames more than others -- but most folks will find plenty here to get their hearts beating.

Like its predecessors, Rhythm Paradise Groove may not be the most demanding rhythm game in the strictest sense—the kind you occasionally see in YouTube videos from Japanese arcades (though be careful not to underestimate it)—but it remains a pillar of the genre. It achieves this through an extraordinary blend of intuitive gameplay and a "pick-up-and-play" style, the quality of its musical tracks, and the sheer variety and creativity of the scenarios and situations used to get us tapping our feet and keeping the beat. The record-breaking number of minigames and the addition of new "side challenges" are merely the icing on the cake for an experience that would have been compelling even with fewer scenarios, given the evident quality, originality, and attention to detail. We are thoroughly pleased with this return to the stage—and to our consoles—and highly recommend that you test your skills, have fun, and unwind with this new must-have title if you own a Switch 2.

If you’re someone like me who fears rhythm games due to their challenges, then Rhythm Paradise Groove is the perfect cushion to soften the blow; it’s accessible, friendly and offers just the right amount of challenge, without being too overwhelming or intense. There’s a whole heap of unlockables and different game modes that keep things fresh and entertaining, and the rhythms and songs throughout the game are bound to have you toe-tapping all the way through. Some may be put off by the latency between the TV and controller input, but even after a while its something that you can adjust to, so there’s always positives to play off.

Rhythm Paradise Groove never overcomplicates things. It’s all about feeling the rhythm, reacting at the right time, and trying again when you mess up. There are no sprawling skill trees, endless checklists, or unnecessary progression systems designed to artificially extend the experience. Instead, Nintendo places complete faith in a deceptively simple idea: if the music is catchy, the gameplay satisfying, and the presentation charming enough, players will naturally want to improve. And turns out, Nintendo was right. Looking back, I realized something that genuinely surprised me. I never became particularly good at Rhythm Paradise Groove. Even after dozens of completed minigames, countless retries, and more than a few bruises to my musical ego, I still wouldn’t describe myself as someone blessed with impeccable rhythm. The results screen continued to remind me of that often enough. Yet somehow, I never really cared, because somewhere along the way, I stopped worrying about chasing perfect scores. I started enjoying the process of getting a little better each time. That’s a difficult feeling to manufacture, and it’s one Rhythm Paradise Groove captures beautifully. Perhaps that’s the biggest compliment I can give Nintendo’s long-awaited return, since it didn’t transform me into someone with perfect rhythm (sorry to my family). It transformed someone with absolutely no rhythm into someone who couldn’t wait to press “Retry.” And if a rhythm game can accomplish that, it’s doing something very, very right.

After more than a decade of silence, Rhythm Paradise Groove is not just a highly nostalgia trip, but it immediately establishes itself as an absolute must-have for the genre. The formula proves to be a true fun machine, capable of combining visual humor with surgical rhythmic precision, all elevated by the tracks composed by Tsunku. Despite a Beatspell mode that could have dared a bit more in terms of depth, and a few less intuitive minigames, the overall package is magnetic and, most importantly, perfectly keeps time with the music, providing total fun for the player.

Rhythm Heaven Groove takes the series' signature, easy-to-pick-up rhythm gameplay to the next level. It offers incredible accessibility, including a TTS option that reads out almost all on-screen information, alongside a great volume of content. However, it's a shame that the input delay in docked mode isn't fully resolved across all play modes.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is an extremely successful sequel that manages to modernise the series whilst retaining its essence. Thanks to its superb music, creative mini-games and strong rhythm design, it offers a fun experience that stays fresh for a long time.

Despite the issues with some parts of the presentation, Rhythm Heaven Groove is a great entry in the series, featuring a ton of catchy tunes and fun scenarios. It’s a welcome return to one of my favorite series and an easy game to recommend to just about anyone, regardless of their familiarity or skills with the genre.

This rhythmic masterpiece marks a triumphant return, delivering eighty inspired minigames and a surprisingly deep RPG mode. It blends quirky visuals with infectious beats, yet frustrating latency issues in TV mode and occasionally unintuitive patterns hold it back. Despite these technical hiccups, it stands as an ambitious and content-rich series benchmark.
Rhythm Heaven Groove is not my favorite in the franchise, but it makes me just as happy, proud, anxious, and angry as all the previous games in the series.

Even after its hiatus, Nintendo’s weirdest rhythm series still hasn’t missed a beat. Rhythm Heaven Groove's infectious soundtrack and delightfully absurd minigames make it almost impossible not to smile while playing, even if its biggest new idea, Beatspell, leaves you wanting more. It doesn’t push its 20-year-old formula after a decade away, but it’s such a joyful game that you’ll gladly keep coming back for an encore.

Rhythm Paradise Groove offers excellent value for completionists and perfectionists alike. There are dozens of inventive mini games to master, plenty that I still haven’t perfected, and I can easily see the multiplayer alone providing hours of laughs with friends and family. For me, I finally understand the fans on social media. Rhythm Paradise Groove is a wonderful experience that thrives on rapid-fire gameplay, hilarious absurdity, and a soundtrack that will happily lodge itself in your brain for days. What initially looked like a simple rhythm game quickly revealed itself to be one of Nintendo’s most charming and addictive experiences. Rhythm Paradise Groove is an absolute gem and, much like our girl Stella, it helped me get my groove back.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a super-fun time with its simple gameplay that's impressively challenging and oodles of content which is all set within such imaginative and colourful scenarios that it's a constant joy to play.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is weird and wonderful! Packed with character, each minigame delights with its unique take on the premise. This bleeds into the multiplayer experience, which is a highlight. Each activity brims with hilarity, leading to moments of joy. Due to the straightforward gameplay loop and simple controls, it’s extremely accessible, which encourages engagement from players of all skill levels, making it easy to pick up and endlessly entertaining. Put simply, it’s a blast.

Infectiously charming, Rhythm Heaven Groove's simple musical mini-games are buoyed by smart game design that becomes more than the sum of its parts, inviting you onto the stage to master its odd-ball antics. Loaded with side-modes, Beatspell is a surprise RPG triumph that deserves more investment, but is a great first step.

Rhythm Heaven Groove has a lot going on, with over 80 minigames, tons of bizarre moments, and a whole lot of heart. The series itself feels like it hasn't changed much, but that's exactly why I find it so endearing; it's basically the same sort of experience that permeates through the Nintendo ecosystem, and one that I feel rightfully celebrates the return of Rhythm Heaven. The series is timeless and continues to be a franchise that fans often clamour over online. Thankfully, this entry is diverse and memorable, with so many fun minigames to keep you busy despite a couple of frustrating additions that do not exude the same joy as the rest of the game offers.

A decade after the last Rhythm Paradise, Groove feels like the series never skipped a beat, delivering razor-sharp gameplay, irresistibly catchy tunes, and charm in spades. While not every side mode hits the right note (Beatspell aside) and the new multiplayer minigames can grow repetitive, the core rhythm action is as addictive as ever. It may take newcomers some time to find the beat, but once it clicks, Rhythm Paradise Groove becomes impossible to put down and a spectacular swan song for the Nintendo Switch era.

Groove's tracklist feels inspired and the Japanese songs are especially good, though I expect criticism in some countries where localised lyrics were part of the charm. But the game feels as funny as ever, with its cast full of the usual suspects (naturally frogs, robots, aliens and the occasional hairy onion imported from WarioWare). It might not be peak like 3DS' Megamix with its unbeatable selection and the good 'ol stylus touch controls, but it's the best entry for new-newcomers, provides more ways to play than ever, and introduces the most engaging multiplayer mode so far.

Tomodachi Life was a late-cycle winner, but if Rhythm Heaven Groove is to be its swansong, Switch 1 is going out on a high note. Beatspell didn't hit for me, personally, and the lag issues thrown up by playing on a modern TV are irritating, so be aware that you'll need to play in handheld or tabletop mode to get the best out of it…You shouldn't let that dissuade you from experiencing one of gaming's most infectiously fun-filled series, though. I was worried that we'd make it through the Switch generation without a Rhythm Heaven, but coming just over a decade after the last, Nintendo has snuck out one final hit for the old Switch. A surprise and a delight, indeed.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a perfect example of the wonderfully weird side of Nintendo. With its colourful presentation of wacky characters, upbeat soundtrack of catchy earworms, gameplay that's easy to learn but hard to master, and modes that surpass expectations of both quantity and quality for the price, heaven is a place on Nintendo Switch. As one of the most uniquely charming rhythm games on the platform, whether playing solo or with friends, everyone should get their groove on. If you wanna try out the game for yourself before committing to a purchase, a demo is available now on the Nintendo eShop.

As with its predecessors, Rhythm Paradise Groove is a wonderful little game that offers up joy and challenge in equal measure. At a time when the games industry seems single-mindedly focused on what's bigger and better, you can always rely on Nintendo to remind us that you can't have gaming without a little whimsy.
Rhythm Heaven Groove modestly brings the classic series back to the forefront.

Rhythm Paradise Groove has a lot to see and do. There are plenty of minigames across several modes of play, and with highly addictive music to tie the package together. The problem is that it is essentially just a minigame collection, so if you’re looking for a wealth of single-player replayability, this won’t be for you. However, if you are a score chaser by nature, or regularly have friends over, Rhythm Paradise Groove will be an excellent addition to your collection.
The great thing with Rhythm Paradise Groove [is that] the dance floor is open to us all. I’ll try not to step on your feet.

I’d wholeheartedly recommend playing Handheld over playing in Docked Mode, but Rhythm Heaven Groove is still a wonderful return full of all sorts of catchy minigames for players to test their rhythm against solo or with friends.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a joyful package of mini-games that is pretty fun for friends and family gatherings. It is jampacked with various insane ideas and offers a challenging experience for completionists as well.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is an enjoyable experience for players of all skill levels when it comes to rhythm games. Easy to pick up for short bursts of playtime, and with a smooth difficulty curve, this is a great instalment to the franchise, and one that can provide a great entry point into the genre. With over 80 new games to play and 30 unique co-op and competitive minigames to jump into at any time, plus a whole host of extra activities to check out, there’s no shortage of fun to be had.
This game gets me inside the music. It makes me pay attention. It makes me try to understand what's actually going on.

Rhythm Heaven Groove follows the franchise formula very closely, building a familiar but robust toy box for fans of the beat. Lag is the number one concern! We recommend playing in handheld mode, and choosing headphones carefully if necessary. Still, it’s worth the care.

Having played every single title in the series and mastered some of its hardest challenges, Groove feels like the perfect entry point for newcomers who want to see what the fuss is all about. It won’t have you going after high scores or singing along to chart-topping bangers like Guitar Hero or Singstar, but Rhythm Heaven Groove continues the series’ legacy of being a unique take on this beloved genre that is well worth your attention.

Rhythm Paradise Groove confirm all the series' long-standing strengths, translating the concept of rhythm into a collection of distinctly Japanese minigames that are irresistibly absurd. While its nature doesn't lend itself to long sessions, it is perfect for the quick, casual bursts of play that often define a gamer's summer, thanks to its simplicity without, however, being trivial in its game design. Nintendo has decided to remain faithful to the established formula of the series - with "Beatspell" serving as the new addition here - but then again, why go to the trouble of changing something that has proved to work so well?

Despite its simplistic control scheme, there’s an awful lot of fun to be had with Rhythm Heaven Groove's brilliantly unorthodox set of levels, characters, and tunes — all packed with tons of personality and vibrancy. The new Beatspell mode may not exude the charm of the core experience, and the basic nature of gameplay won’t be for all, but the game remains a blast whether you’re riding solo or competing against friends.

Nintendo is one of the biggest and oldest game publishers in the world, so it feels strange to say that something it made carries itself with indie sensibilities. But that’s always been true of WarioWare, and by extension, it’s true of Rhythm Heaven Groove. It’s such a strange, low-fi game that it comes off as if the team is getting away with something while the boss isn’t looking. But it’s also a genuinely welcome addition to my Switch collection, because it’s such an oddity. Whenever I feel the need to tap my toes while feeling the beat of a tadpole march, or invite my friends to compete in a foot race as lucha libre across giant bouncy balls, I’ll return to Rhythm Heaven.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is coming to home consoles with an installment designed to appeal to a wider audience. Although the multiplayer aspect has taken center stage with some very engaging mini-games, it still offers a very complete single-player experience. Not all the changes are a good fit for the formula, but it remains a unique, original, and charming title.
An avalanche of minigames, modes and brilliant ideas for the series' triumphant return.

It more than meets those lofty expectations, with its slick mix of mini-games and creative use of catchy tunes making it a must-play for rhythm game fans. While those without rhythm may find its many challenges frustrating on occasion, there is a real variety here, and a patience to teach those in need of more time and generosity. As a complete package, Rhythm Paradise Groove absolutely sings. It more than lives up to the legacy of its fan-favourite predecessors.

At €40, Rhythm Paradise Groove is Nintendo’s best chance to reintroduce itself, after more than 10 years, to those players who adore Osawa’s work, styles and playful influences. Twenty years of a distinguished, rhythm-filled career and it doesn’t feel a day old: the sheer volume of content, the gameplay ideas and the consistent dynamic minimalism that carries the series from game to game – including the additional modes that breathe new life into the core structure – are all elements that enrich a very substantial package, capable of delivering a great experience whether playing solo, in multiplayer or in a group. Now let’s just hope that WarioWare makes a comeback soon too.

Despite a few minor snags, though, Rhythm Heaven Groove is just plain fun. With an extensive library of single-player and multiplayer mini-games, every stage offers a unique and engaging challenge that ensures the game never feels stale. I often found myself muttering “just one more” during my play sessions because I just didn’t want to stop learning new rhythm games and challenging myself to make it to the remix stage. If you enjoy rhythm games or are a newcomer curious to give them a try, I think Rhythm Heaven Groove will feel well worth its $40 price tag for the amount of entertaining gameplay on offer.
While not all miniganes are created equal, there’s still a huge selection to choose from featuring charm and creativity by the truck load that you can’t go wrong.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a worthy successor to Rhythm Heaven and Rhythm Heaven Fever. It occasionally misses in terms of presentation, but it is far from charmless. And its endless parade of excellent tunes (and robust bonuses) will keep you bopping your head to the right beat.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a welcome earworm, bringing some much needed goofiness along with some fun music too. While the simple menus feel bare, there is plenty on offer here. There’s easily hours of minigame challenges for you to perfect your score, on top of a surprisingly-involved side adventure.

In short, Rhythm Paradise Groove is a competent and genuinely fun return of one of Nintendo's most original franchises. It is not the definitive reinvention that a wait of more than ten years might have deserved, but it offers enough content to justify dozens of hours of play. It could use a bit more polish and care in its overall presentation, along with a feedback system for those chasing perfection on every track. Even so, for fans of the series, and for anyone wanting a Switch 2 filled with catchy music and good-humoured nonsense, Rhythm Paradise Groove delivers on what it sets out to do.

Rhythm Heaven Groove doesn't reinvent Nintendo's beloved rhythm series, but it doesn't need to. Packed with hilarious minigames, outstanding music, and deceptively challenging gameplay, it's a joyful return that proves simple mechanics can still create unforgettable experiences. While some extra modes feel underdeveloped, the core rhythm action remains as addictive as ever.
A fun restatement of a game concept that started on the Game Boy Advance and yet is just as much fun to play today on the Switch 1 – especially with the greater variety of minigames and modes.

The mini-games in Rhythm Heaven Groove might not reach the same cohesive and triumphant highs as series classics Ringside or Hole in One, nor is the entire package attempting to reinvent the wheel like many of its contemporaries. But it doesn’t need to. After 11 years, it feels like being reunited with an old friend who has remained untroubled by the passage of time. Even if they ring a familiar tune, you’re still eager to hear what new stories they have to tell.

Rhythm Heaven Groove feels like a throwback to a classic era of Nintendo. If you were growing up during the time of Miiverse, Street Pass, and the 3DS, it will seem very familiar to you. The songs are outstanding, and the mood it can put you in is second to none. Not all the levels are winners, and I certainly found myself with a feeling of disappointment at how many of them end anticlimactically, but Rhythm Heaven Groove is still a neat little game that's worth diving into.

The WarioWare of rhythm games, Rhythm Paradise Groove offers up a series of joyful minigames that all test your ability to keep a rhythm. It's challenging, but the nature of the minigames means it's very easy to keep trying until practice makes perfect.

Rhythm Heaven Groove isn’t the kind of game that will generate a lot of buzz or make headlines, but it’s precisely the kind of game that helps the Nintendo side of gaming achieve its own unique charm. In an era of widespread cynicism and creative stagnation in the gaming industry, this game embodies all the brilliance and eccentricity of video games’ golden age.
Don’t let its cutesy graphics fool you, as Rhythm Heaven Groove’s difficulty is such that it’s tempting to call it the Dark Souls of rhythm games.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a fantastic return for the series, delivering over 100 delightful rhythm games alongside plenty of extras and secrets to discover. While it misses a few features from previous entries and its presentation can feel lacking at times, it’s still an easy recommendation for rhythm game fans.

Even though it is a little light on content, what's here is strong enough to recommend Rhythm Heaven Groove to the majority of Switch owners, especially if they are looking for a new local multiplayer option. The music is catchy as hell, the art style is adorable, and the mini-games are almost all winners. If Rhythm Heaven Groove is indeed the last first-party Nintendo game to be released for the Switch, it's definitely not a bad game to go out on.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a deceptively simple yet thoroughly entertaining game. It delivers an unapologetically straightforward experience, offering a delightful variety of rhythm challenges that make it hard to put down.

When I think about Rhythm Heaven Groove a year from now, or even ten, I won't think about a list of what it does or does not include. I'll think about the hours it had me pacing around my kitchen. I'll think about the years it had me reflect on and the memories it reminded me of. I'll remember how I came to terms with one of my biggest fears in life, the years that go by and never come back. Through it all, I'll keep tapping my foot to the beat, hoping to anchor myself to the moment, and remember to breathe every once in a while.

Rhythm Paradise Groove marks a joyful and substantial return for Nintendo’s long‑dormant rhythm series, offering a huge selection of quirky minigames and a polished audiovisual experience. Despite a divisive Beatspell RPG mode and a few uneven challenges, the game delivers hours of inventive, charming rhythm action both solo and with friends.

It's not without a couple of missteps, but Rhythm Heaven Groove is a fine return to a series that still has plenty of hits up its sleeve. It almost demands playing exclusively in handheld mode, but do so with some wired headphones to appreciate some of the catchiest tunes that Tsunku has ever produced.
While Rhythm Heaven Groove is a welcome return and a solid choice for newcomers, it misses the mark on becoming an absolute legend once again.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a charming rhythm game that thrives on creativity, offering a constant stream of inventive minigames that reward timing and musical instinct over visual cues. Its outstanding soundtrack and clever gameplay keep the experience fresh, while local multiplayer and the Beatspell RPG mode add welcome variety. However, the simplistic presentation, inconsistent visuals and lack of Portuguese localization prevent it from reaching greater heights. Even so, it's an enjoyable and refreshing experience for anyone looking for a unique rhythm game.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is a delightfully rhythmic game, but unless you feel like playing every level to perfection, you will get bored of it quite quickly.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a very likable rhythm game that doesn't necessarily try to reinvent the wheel, and that's a good thing - the great amount of content, the colorful graphics and sound style, and the overall experience it will provide you are good, even if on the way there you will sometimes encounter obstacles like the game's inability to handle wireless headphones and different models of televisions.

Rhythm Paradise is silly fun, playful beats and a surprisingly good way to improve your rhythm skills. The strange humor works, even though you might not really know why. The game does lose some points on the multiplayer, which rather than the promised 30 games, has only ten with three difficulty levels each. Still, this is possibly one of the most fun ways to improve your sense of musical timing.

Is Rhythm Paradise Groove the last great Switch exclusive? Probably not. Yet Nintendo's latest compilation of musical mini-games is great fun, split into 80 solo capsules and 30 multiplayer experiences, with a delightfully sunny and wacky disposition.

Rhythm Paradise: Groove is bursting with insane creativity and a huge amount of silly rhythm mini-games, but if you don’t have a sense of rhythm or a stomach for its specific kind of Japanese weirdness, it won’t keep you engaged for long.

Rhythm Paradise Groove beautifully channels the experimental, chaotic charm of the DS era with over 80 catchy solo tracks by Tsunku, unique multiplayer modes, and even a rhythm RPG. However, despite its vibrant visuals and creative variety, its unforgiving timing windows and brutal offbeat difficulty make it a punishing experience that prioritizes strict perfection over casual fun.
Even if this particular slice of "Paradise" takes a little longer to find its groove, there's comfort in realising that, for this most stately of companies, the (off)beat goes on. [Issue#426, p.116]

Rythm Heaven Groove is an entry that fits what is expected from the franchise, offering musical levels that are as absurd as they are fun. Although it is intuitive and has a well-tuned difficulty curve, the precision of some commands often fails for no apparent reason, which ends up being frustrating. It is geared more towards fans of the series than casual players.

The latest Rhythm Paradise is a one-two punch: at first glance appearing as a new episode without any major rough edges, relying on the solidity of its formula, it proves to be greatly generous. A hidden compensation for the game's extreme sobriety and the lack of truly catchy tunes. A nice summer treat as always.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a stern mistress that doesn’t suffer fools gladly and its mini-games sometimes feel like quantity over quality, which not what you want from what is probably Nintendo’s final release for the original Switch console.
Lots of content and plenty of ways to play. If you like this genre, it's made for you.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a fun and accessible new game of the Rhythm Paradise series and it delivers a pack of rhythm-based minigames dressed in cute and clean graphics to the tune of upbeat music. With that said, the game is inevitably more fun on multiplayer than single player, where it can get repetitive too quickly. The RPG-lite Beatspell mode is an interesting addition and a good side fun from the main objectives, though it too runs the risk of feeling that some instances last too long. Rhythm Paradise Groove is therefore a better option as a party game than as a solo experience.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is fun, diverting and unique, but unfortunately does not come without some unnecessary flaws.

Anyone who enjoys timing-based minigame collections might well find something to like in "Rhythm Paradise Groove." However, significant latency issues in TV mode, merely functional graphics, and limited content – combined with a steep price tag – make it impossible to offer a general recommendation for this Switch title.

Infectiously charming, Rhythm Heaven Groove's simple musical mini-games are buoyed by smart game design that becomes more than the sum of its parts, inviting you onto the stage to master its odd-ball antics. Loaded with side-modes, Beatspell is a surprise RPG triumph that deserves more investment, but is a great first step.
Rhythm Heaven Groove is as weird as it is fun and serves as a fittingly quirky swan song for the OG Nintendo Switch.

It might not do too much to stray from the music minigame formula it helped popularise some two decades ago, but Rhythm Heaven Groove is still exactly the kind of grand return for this beat-bopping series I was hoping for.

Rhythm Paradise Groove, like its predecessors, may not be the most challenging rhythm game in the strictest sense, the kind you occasionally see on YouTube videos from Japanese arcades (but be careful not to underestimate it, eh?), but it remains one of the genre's cornerstones thanks to its extraordinary mix of intuitive gameplay, a "hit-and-run" approach, the quality of the songs it offers as background music, and the variety and creativity of the scenarios and situations it uses as pretexts to get us tapping our feet and keeping track of our beats.

If you’re someone like me who fears rhythm games due to their challenges, then Rhythm Paradise Groove is the perfect cushion to soften the blow; it’s accessible, friendly and offers just the right amount of challenge, without being too overwhelming or intense. There’s a whole heap of unlockables and different game modes that keep things fresh and entertaining, and the rhythms and songs throughout the game are bound to have you toe-tapping all the way through. Some may be put off by the latency between the TV and controller input, but even after a while its something that you can adjust to, so there’s always positives to play off.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a triumphant return from a decade-and-a-half hibernation. While it struggles to abandon some of the archaic visual design the series has grown attached to, the juiced-up soundtrack, consistently strong rhythm games, and wonderfully intriguing Beatspell RPG have me believing that this series has the legs to carry the music into the modern age.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a perfect example of the wonderfully weird side of Nintendo. With its colourful presentation of wacky characters, upbeat soundtrack of catchy earworms, gameplay that’s easy to learn but hard to master, and modes that surpass expectations of both quantity and quality for the price, heaven is a place on Nintendo Switch.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a highly distinctive rhythm game that delights with its ideas, music and absurd humour, but doesn’t set out to appeal to everyone. Its simple controls conceal a challenging experience that demands full concentration, a sense of rhythm and a constant drive to improve your scores. Fans of the series and of Nintendo’s more unconventional titles will have a brilliant time, whilst others may lose interest after just a few minutes.
Rhythm according to Nintendo? A series of absurd yet fun minigames to try out this scorching summer.

Cementing its appeal in simplicity, Rhythm Heaven Groove packs an entertaining punch for both solo and co-op play. It makes sure to reward dedication and effort, and most importantly, proves that the spirit of fun hasn’t been eroded by time.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is proof that you don’t always need 15 buttons, a massive open world and 100 hours of content to make a great game. Sometimes, all you need is one button and the right moment to press it.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a lot of fun and can present quite a challenge. You will laugh and laugh either when you play solo or when you play with others. If you’re looking for a good party game, this will fit the bill. There is a huge variety in the minigames so you and your friends will find a game that suits you best. You can even enjoy it if you have as much rhythm as a scarecrow like me. If you’ve ever been to the arcade and enjoyed the rhythm games there you will love Rhythm Paradise Groove.

Rhythm Heaven Groove is a wonderful return for Nintendo’s rhythm series. Its short minigames reward careful listening, multiplayer creates memorable group sessions, and Beatspell adds a rewarding campaign with post-game content.
Rhythm Heaven Groove is weird, fun, musical, and unmistakably Nintendo. Whether you’re chasing Perfect scores or playing with friends, it’s an incredibly fun surprise.

Whether you're a hardcore enthusiast chasing perfect scores or simply a novice intrigued by the surreal situations on offer, you'll soon find yourself bobbing your head to the beat, trapped in an irresistible whirlwind of laughter and constant attempts to break your own records.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is Nintendo's best way to reintroduce itself, after more than a decade, to those who adore Osawa's work, styles, and gaming influences.
The title is okay for rhythm game fans. However, we certainly can't recommend "Rhythm Paradise Groove" to everyone.

Aside from the UI design, Rhythm Paradise Groove is a very creative experience with a collection of mini-games that'll have you humming and bumping your head to the beat as you try to do some exciting and at times mundane tasks to the beat.

Although I do think the first minigames in “Rhythm Heaven Groove” are a bit harder than they should be for a franchise that’s been dormant for so long, the complete package still shows why it’s still relevant after all this time. It’s filled with humor, charm, and challenge for those who seek those “perfect” in every minigame and or at the very least a gold medal.

If you’re looking for a pure rhythm game that’s lighthearted and truly challenges you to feel the music instead of just reacting to visual cues, Rhythm Heaven Groove delivers exactly what it promises. Even if it’s not the pinnacle of the franchise, it remains a feast for fans of the genre.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is fantastic from start to finish, offering single-player gamers plenty of challenges in both the classic minigame mode and the brand-new RPG. And for multiplayer, there are several additional games, both competitive and cooperative.

If you’re the type of person who doesn’t mind randomly playing a video game with a friend, family member, or loved one present, they probably already know that you’re someone into the medium and will likely not bother you for the rest of the session. Every once in a while, though, there’s a game that’ll get the attention of such people, likely to a point where they’ll want to join you or at least ask, “What are you playing?” 

That’s one of the best feelings in the world, and it’s a feat that I think Rhythm Heaven Groove accomplishes whenever it’s played around people. It’s a big part of what makes the series great.

Rhythm Paradise Groove returns without reinventing its formula, and proves it still has plenty to say. The result is a rich, immediate experience that challenges even players who think they already have rhythm in their blood.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is a solid and fun return that focuses on music. It does not innovate the formula but refines it for multiplayer sessions.
Rhythm Paradise Groove is an impressive return that delivers another wonderfully odd collection of rhythm challenges backed by fantastic music and endless charm.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a great game, one that you will absolutely love playing. I personally wouldn’t wait to pick this up and go and get it now. For me, this is an essential Switch 2 purchase.

Rhythm Paradise Groove gets the Thumb Culture Platinum Award.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a joyful and wonderfully creative return for the cult rhythm series, packed with imaginative minigames, excellent music, charming visuals, tougher remixed challenges, and a fun local multiplayer mode. A handful of minigames may not click with everyone, but the overwhelming majority are addictive, rewarding, and an absolute delight to master.

With its cheerful music, colorful style, and diverse minigames, Rhythm Heaven Groove is an accessible rhythm game for young and old. However, not every challenge is equally memorable, and the game will primarily appeal to children and fans of the genre.
Even though Rhythm Paradise Groove made me smile at times.... it's certainly not my favourite.

Rhythm Heaven Groove marks the triumphant return of one of Nintendo’s most beloved rhythm sagas. Thanks to its simplified controls, brand‑new RPG mode, and highly accessible design, the game makes coordination fun for audiences of all kinds.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is a rhythm-filled extravaganza that completely sweeps you away. That is, provided you’re prepared to put your ego aside and let your timing be put to the test. It’s charming, chaotic, musical and, at times, downright brutal. But when everything clicks, when you feel the beat and the mini-games become one fluid dance, this is exactly the sort of game that turns a dull evening into a rhythmic party.

When I think about Rhythm Heaven Groove a year from now, or even ten, I won't think about a list of what it does or does not include. I'll think about the hours it had me pacing around my kitchen. I'll think about the years it had me reflect on and the memories it reminded me of. I'll remember how I came to terms with one of my biggest fears in life, the years that go by and never come back. Through it all, I'll keep tapping my foot to the beat, hoping to anchor myself to the moment, and remember to breathe every once and a while.

Some games go viral, this one is a sound-shaped virus that finds a home between your ears and nests there for days.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is an amazing rhythm game full of silly ideas and sound effects that are impossible to forget. The controls are intuitive and the various minigames will keep you busy for days. This is an easy recommend for every Nintendo Switch owner of almost any age.

It’s hard for us to say whether Rhythm Paradise: Groove represents the pinnacle of the entire series. What we can say with certainty, however, is that Nintendo has succeeded in the difficult task of reviving a series that had been dormant for over ten years without betraying its identity—and, in fact, enriching it with a wealth of content and ideas that make it more unique than ever. In short, Rhythm Paradise: Groove once again proves itself to be a little gem, one of the most successful rhythm games of recent years, and a purchase that every fan of the genre—and, more broadly, every console owner—should seriously consider. And if this truly is the Nintendo Switch’s swan song, then it’s hard to imagine a better farewell.

548
Rhythm Heaven Groove was a long-awaited title for Nintendo's first Switch console, and it doesn't disappoint fans of the rhythm game series. Its difficulty remains consistent, if not increased, in the later levels compared to previous installments, while visually it retains its distinctive art style so familiar from WarioWare games. While unlocking the basic minigames takes a few hours, unlocking all the additional content demands truly honed skills, which encourages replayability.

Rhythm Paradise Groove is funny, fun, and even educational. It is just a shame that it falls short in a few places. But if you can look past the poor first impression, you will discover that it is a great little game for some entertainment and rhythm practice.
